title: Deep Learning-based Framework for Rapid, Precise and Fully Automated Localization of Cochlea Landmarks in 3D CT Images
text: Manual localization of anatomical landmarks within human cochlea structures in 3D computed tomography (CT) images is labor-intensive. However, despite progress in various studies on automatic localization methods, it remains challenging to jointly achieve rapid, precise, and fully automated landmark localization. Therefore, we propose a deep learning-based localization framework, called MEDICO-YOLO, which bridges speed and precision. It can automatically and simultaneously localize 6 human cochlea landmarks (apex, basal point, round window center of both left and right cochleae) in the full-resolution 3D CT images. The main contributions are: 1) MEDICO-YOLO learns from few manually annotated 3D CT images; 2) Within the framework, a 2D CNN-based network was developed to specifically localize cochlea landmarks in 3D single-scale medical CT images; 3) A novel loss function was designed; 4) The localization model achieved human expert-level precision while ensuring rapid inference. This study employed anonymized 3D pre-operative CT images (0.3 mm, covering the full head or temporal bone region). The evaluation involved comparing four models that were trained using 4 different training set sizes (n=4, 8, 12, 16). Each of them was evaluated on a distinct test set (n=16). The results show that the MEDICO-YOLO framework achieved strong localization performance by learning from few annotated 3D CT images. Trained on only 8 CT volumes, the model already attained a mean localization error of 1.30 mm (approximately 4 voxels). When trained on 16 CT volumes, the model achieved a mean error of 0.71 mm and a successful detection rate (SDR@3.0 mm) of 97.92%. Furthermore, on an Apple M1 laptop, the model achieved a real-time speed (32 ms) for inferencing each 2D slice (608 x 608) and an average latency of 25.43 s for inferencing the full 3D CT image (608 x 608 x 200, including post-processing). The complete methodology for the MEDICO-YOLO framework is presented in this article.

title: Methodological Adherence, Reporting Completeness, and Risk of Bias in AI-Assisted Systematic Reviews: A Matched Meta-Research Study
text: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to accelerate systematic reviews that inform clinical practice and policy. However, evidence on the methodological adherence, reporting completeness, and risk of bias of completed AI-assisted reviews is limited. ObjectiveTo compare methodological adherence, reporting completeness, and risk of bias between published systematic reviews with reported AI assistance and matched reviews with no reported AI use, and to assess AI-use transparency. MethodsWe conducted a matched-cohort meta-research study of English-language, peer-reviewed health systematic reviews. AI-assisted reviews published during 2023-2025 were matched 1:2 to reviews with no reported AI use using individualized MEDLINE searches targeting publication timing, clinical domain, review type, and meta-analysis status. When more than two eligible comparators were available, two were randomly selected. AI assistance was defined as reported use during searching, screening, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, evidence synthesis, or substantive drafting. Full texts and supplementary materials were examined to classify reported AI use. The primary outcome was a prespecified modified 13-item AMSTAR-2 methodological-adherence score (range 0-13; noninferiority margin -1 point). Secondary outcomes included PRISMA 2020 reporting completeness and ROBIS risk of bias; AI-use transparency was assessed descriptively. Adapted 13-item AMSTAR-2 confidence categories were summarized descriptively, while critical- and noncritical-domain adherence was examined in exploratory adjusted analyses. Multivariable regression models adjusted for journal impact tier, funding reporting, formal review-group affiliation, review-team size, and review-question type, using cluster-robust standard errors by matched set. Sensitivity analyses included matched-set fixed-effects models. The study was registered on the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/Q5JRW). ResultsThe cohort included 231 systematic reviews: 77 AI-assisted and 154 with no reported AI use. Mean 13-item AMSTAR-2 scores were 7.58 and 9.63, respectively. In multivariable-adjusted analyses, AI-assisted reviews scored 1.64 points lower (95% CI -2.37 to -0.91); noninferiority was not demonstrated. PRISMA adherence was estimated to be 4.7 percentage points lower among AI-assisted reviews in primary adjusted analyses (95% CI -8.9 to -0.6) and 6.4 points lower in matched-set fixed-effects analyses (95% CI -10.7 to -2.1). Among reviews with assessable ROBIS ratings, 75.0% of AI-assisted reviews and 65.6% of comparators were rated low risk (adjusted difference +17.8 percentage points; 95% CI 2.7 to 33.0). Among AI-assisted reviews, model version or date was reported in 42.9%, prompts or parameters in 55.8%, and data-governance or ethics considerations in 9.1%. ConclusionsReviews reporting AI assistance had lower methodological-adherence scores and had less complete reporting, despite more favorable risk-of-bias ratings. These findings provide an early warning that AI-assisted systematic reviews may require stronger safeguards, human verification, and transparency to support trust.

title: Diagnosis Journey and Future Outlook Among Young People Living with HIV in Bangladesh: protocol for a qualitative study
text: IntroductionBangladesh is a country with low HIV prevalence, but case detection has more than doubled in 2020- 24, reaching 1,891 cases in the most recently reported year, and the number of cases is growing in the 18-24 age group. There is little qualitative evidence that describes the journey from suspected exposure to diagnosis for young people in Bangladesh, and no comparative evidence of this journey between key-population and general-population youth. ObjectiveTo explore the pathway to HIV testing and diagnosis, what motivated testing, and the life outlook of people living with HIV in Bangladesh aged 18-30 years, and to compare these between key-population and general-population participants. MethodsThis qualitative exploratory study uses semi-structured in-depth interviews, guided by the theory of emerging adulthood and the HIV Stigma Framework. Purposive maximum-variation sampling (20-30 participants) will recruit people aged 18-30, diagnosed within that age range and currently on antiretroviral therapy, balanced between key and general populations. Participants will be recruited through Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital and Ashar Alo Society, Dhaka, and interviewed privately in Bangla. Recordings will be transcribed, translated into English, and analysed with the Framework Method in MAXQDA, with saturation judged within each group. Ethical concernsThe study is approved by the Ethical Review Board, Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Dhaka with written consent from Ashar Alo Society and PLHIV Network Bangladesh. All participants will be asked for written informed consent, identifiers will be removed and distressed participants will be referred for counselling and psychosocial support. Findings will be shared via a technical report, a policy brief for the National AIDS/STD Programme and partner organisations, conference presentations and peer-reviewed publication. LimitationsThe recruitment process via one gatekeeper organisation in Dhaka and the need for the participants to be on treatment may exclude young people not in care. (300 words)

title: On conducting diary-based social contact surveys to inform transmission models of close-contact infections: a systematic review and expert-informed questionnaire
text: BackgroundDiary-based social contact surveys are widely used to parameterise transmission models of close-contact infections. However, variation in study design, contact definitions, and questionnaire content limits comparability across studies. These challenges became particularly evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, when rapid and repeated data collection was urgently needed, often without harmonised instruments. To address these challenges, we aimed to develop an expert-informed questionnaire and update the recommendations on conducting diary-based social contact studies previously proposed by Hoang et al. (2019). Methods and findingsWe conducted a systematic review of diary-based social contact surveys published between 31 January 2018 and 25 September 2025 using PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection, extracting information on study design, survey methodology, contact definitions, and survey items from available questionnaires. Methodological quality and reporting were assessed using an adapted AXIS tool, with results summarised for each criterion. In total, we identified 129 studies across 62 countries, with most studies conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic (59.7% in 2021-2022). Retrospective reporting (86.0%) and non-probability sampling (77.5%) were largely adopted and became increasingly common during the pandemic, while non-paper-based data collection rose sharply from 2021 onwards. Across 36 retrievable questionnaires from general-population surveys, we identified 54 survey items. An online assessment involving 26 experts informed the classification of these items according to their perceived importance, resulting in an expert-informed questionnaire comprising 22 core items. Based on our findings, we updated previous recommendations on sampling, survey methods, contact definitions, behavioural change, essential contact information, and data governance. ConclusionsThis study provides an expert-informed questionnaire and updated recommendations to support harmonised social contact data collection, improve comparability across studies, and strengthen preparedness for future public health emergencies.

title: Perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation for the prevention of postoperative delirium: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
text: BackgroundPostoperative delirium is a common perioperative complication. Early randomised trials suggested that non-invasive brain stimulation may reduce postoperative delirium, whereas the recent MODEST trial found no preventive benefit. We synthesised the randomised evidence for perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation. MethodsWe searched eight bibliographic databases and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to 30 September 2026 for randomised controlled trials of perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation in adults undergoing surgery. The primary outcome was postoperative delirium. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated risk ratios (RRs), mean differences, or standardised mean differences. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. ResultsNine trials contributed data from 1451 participants. Postoperative delirium occurred in 72 of 750 participants receiving active stimulation and 166 of 701 controls (RR 0.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.31-0.56; I2=24.7%; moderate-certainty evidence). Estimates also favoured stimulation for hypoactive and hyperactive delirium, but not clearly for mixed delirium. Pain, anxiety, and sleep outcomes favoured stimulation but were highly heterogeneous and supported by very-low-certainty evidence. Length of hospital stay was not reduced. Adverse events could not be pooled because reporting was incomplete and inconsistent. ConclusionsPerioperative non-invasive brain stimulation may reduce postoperative delirium, but the evidence does not establish a class effect or support routine clinical use. Geographical concentration, methodological concerns, heterogeneous stimulation protocols, and discordance with the MODEST trial warrant independent multicentre sham-controlled trials. PROSPERO registrationCRD420261522168

title: Stressful life events recorded in 39.7 million clinical notes: associations with mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty
text: BackgroundDespite being harmful to both mental and physical health, stressful life events are not recorded in structured electronic health records. They appear sporadically in narrative clinical notes, where they are difficult to analyze at scale. Natural language processing (NLP) has made clinical notes more available for research, but applications to stressful life events remain limited, leaving their documentation patterns and prognostic value understudied. By applying NLP, we identified stressful life events from clinical notes and examined their associations with mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty. MethodsWe analyzed 39.7 million clinical notes, recorded between 2010 and 2023, from 202,988 patients in Central Finland Wellbeing Services County. NLP was applied to identify stressful life events in five categories: grief, divorce, financial distress, violence, and family problems. Associations with the risk of mental disorders (stress-related disorders, anxiety, and depression) were estimated using time-varying Cox proportional hazards models, and associations with physical health outcomes (comorbidity and frailty) using generalized linear mixed models. ResultsStressful life events were identified from clinical notes with high accuracy (F1 scores 0.81-0.95). Event prevalences ranged from 0.5% for family problems to 22.1% for grief. Most individual events were associated with mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty. The number of different life events was associated with a higher risk of stress-related (hazard ratio [HR], 1.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.58-1.67), anxiety (HR, 2.08; 95% CI, 2.03-2.14), and depressive disorders (HR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.94-2.03), and with higher comorbidity (rate ratio, 1.58; 95% CI,1.56-1.59) and frailty (mean ratio, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.56-1.58). ConclusionsStressful life events were accurately identified from clinical notes and were associated with a higher risk of mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty. Even so, violence and financial distress, the two events with comparable national estimates, were documented substantially less often than those estimates, suggesting underrecording of stressful life events in clinical settings.

title: Determinants of Digital Health Pre-Acceptance in Respiratory Care: A Quantitative Irish Study
text: IntroductionDigital health technology (DHT) is increasingly being integrated into healthcare delivery; however, limited research exists exploring the pre-acceptability of DHT among ageing respiratory patients. This study aimed to identify the factors influencing the pre-acceptability of digital health technology in individuals with chronic respiratory disease in Ireland. MethodsA quantitative study was conducted among respiratory service users attending two respiratory centres in the Midlands and West of Ireland. A convenience-based questionnaire was developed and distributed, which was informed by prior Phase 1 qualitative findings that adopted the Technology Acceptance Model and the Health Belief Model.Data were analysed using non-parametric statistical methods, including the Mann-Whitney U test, to explore differences between gender and geographical location (urban/rural). ResultsFifty-eight participants completed the study. Overall, participants demonstrated positive perceptions toward the use of DHT, particularly regarding support for self-management, hospital admission avoidance, increased symptom awareness, and enhanced engagement with healthcare professionals. Perceived usefulness emerged as a significant factor influencing acceptability. Concerns regarding privacy, data security, and digital literacy were less significant than anticipated. Statistical differences were identified between urban and rural participants in relation to perceived usefulness, technology design preferences, feedback functionality, and preference for reduction in face-to-face appointments. No significant differences were identified between male and female participants. ConclusionsThis study demonstrates that ageing respiratory patients in Ireland are receptive to the integration of digital health technology provided that technologies are perceived as useful, user-friendly, and supportive rather than replacements for healthcare professionals. The findings highlight the importance of involving service users during the design phase of DHT and recognising geographical differences in perspectives toward technology adoption. These findings may inform future policy, service development, and digital health implementation strategies nationally and internationally.

title: Knowledge and attitudes toward infertility and reproductive health among nursing and midwifery students from selected universities in Accra, Ghana
text: IntroductionIn sub-Saharan Africa, where high societal value is placed on childbearing, infertility prevalence is high and often leads to stigma and psychosocial distress. Nurses and midwives, as frontline reproductive health providers, need adequate preparation to support infertile couples, yet a literature gap exists regarding how well nursing and midwifery trainees are equipped with the knowledge and attitudes needed for this role. This study investigated the knowledge and attitudes regarding infertility among nursing and midwifery students, applying the Knowledge-Attitude-Practice (KAP) model. Materials and methodsA descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among a stratified sample of 263 final-year BSc nursing and midwifery students at four universities in Accra, Ghana. Data were collected via a structured questionnaire covering demographics, infertility knowledge, attitudes, and practice intentions; and were analysed using SPSS. ResultsRespondents demonstrated a high overall level of infertility knowledge (composite knowledge score: M = 18.25/23, SD = 3.17; attitudes toward infertility were largely favourable (composite attitude score: M = 3.812/5, SD = 0.654; female respondents scored significantly higher than males on both knowledge (U = 2800.5, p = .044) and attitude (U = 2777.0, p = .040). BSc Midwifery students demonstrated significantly higher knowledge than BSc Nursing students (U = 2868.0, p = .002). A statistically significant moderate positive correlation was found between knowledge and attitude scores (r = .400, p < .001), and knowledge score was the sole significant predictor of attitude in multiple regression (B = 0.080, p < .001, R{superscript 2} = .178). The large majority of respondents (86.3%) supported expanded infertility content in the curriculum. ConclusionThe significant association between knowledge and attitude supports the KAP framework and suggests that targeted curricular reinforcement of weak knowledge areas may further strengthen students attitudes. The findings will inform curriculum improvements and promote evidence-based practice in nursing and midwifery education.

title: Biological insights and methodological challenges learned from working with a diverse heterotrophic marine bacterial library
text: Abstract Organized collections of bacterial strains can help bridge the gap between studying model organisms and communities, through comparative experiments between genetically and phenotypically diverse strains. Yet, to date, few studies discuss in a detailed and systematic manner the processes of collecting and maintaining bacterial strain libraries. Here, we aim to address this gap by describing the establishment and initial characterization of a library of 62 marine heterotrophic bacteria, selected to represent a significant fraction of the genome-encoded functional diversity and a wide range of known phytoplankton-bacteria interactions. We systematically document the practical and methodological challenges of collecting, verifying, and phenotyping a diverse marine bacterial library; aspects of comparative microbiology that have received comparatively little detailed, systematic treatment to date. Cultured strains contain up to hundreds of mutations compared with the reference genomes, with non-synonymous mutations in rpoB and/or rpoC genes observed in ~15% of the cultures. Most strains grow well at 25°C, but the dependence of growth rate on temperature and the width of the temperature niche varies between strains in a systematic manner. We describe steps towards designing a universal, defined, minimal media for marine bacteria, revealing that growth inhibition on amino acids and peptides by carbohydrates is widespread. Cell counts obtained from flow cytometry and colony plating differ systematically, as do different methods to assess motility. Finally, we discuss traits potentially related to microbial interactions such as hemolysis, biofilm formation, and antibiotic resistance. Gammaproteobacteria such as Alteromonas, Pseudoalteromonas, and Vibrio reveal consistently robust growth, and activity, perhaps explaining why these clades are well-explored. Explicitly discussing the insights and challenges of working with strain libraries will pave the way to robust, reproducible, and generalizable mapping of bacterial traits across diversity.

title: Complexity-informed causal modeling of neurodevelopmental trajectories in pediatric high-grade gliomas: divergences from neural stem cell signatures
text: Abstract Pediatric high-grade gliomas (pHGGs) are lethal evolutionary disorders with stalled developmental pathways and disturbed differentiation hierarchies. We integrate transcriptional and algorithmic network complexity-based perturbation analysis to elucidate gene expression patterns and molecular divergence between Diffuse Midline Gliomas (DMG; previously DIPG) and glioblastoma (GBM), revealing shared developmental programs steering cell fate decision-making. Our complex systems approach supports the emerging paradigm that pHGGs are neurodevelopmental disorders with hybrid lineage identities and disrupted patterning. We identify dysregulated neurodevelopmental and morphogenetic signatures, alongside bioelectric and neurotransmitter signaling programs that alter synaptic organization, neuronal fate commitment, and phenotypic plasticity, regulating glioma phenotypic switching (cell state-transitions). In silico candidate transition-associated network signatures and regulators of plasticity were predicted as possible predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets, reinforcing the view that pediatric gliomas are disorders of cell fate decisions and collective cellular identity. Neuronal and synaptic enrichment is interpreted as a candidate neurodevelopmental network program emerging from disrupted cell fate decision-making. Across validation cohorts, these predictive signatures localized to progenitor-like, NPC/OPC-like, hybrid/ambiguous, immune, and extracellular matrix-associated compartments, supporting recurrence-associated plasticity dynamics. Decoded cell fate transition-associated signatures indicate recurrence-associated remodeling of neural progenitor, OPC-like, neurosynaptic interface, immune, and matrisome-associated programs, as computationally inferred network features. Using graph network-based complexity signatures, our algorithms identified candidate network-associated plasticity markers and interpretable regulatory drivers underlying latent glioma cell fate dynamics. These computational findings may help advance ‘differentiation therapy’ as a systems medicine strategy, discovering plasticity regulators to reprogram malignant fates toward stable lineages, offering complex systems-based targets for cancer reversion and predictive, preventive, and precision oncology.

title: DNAH14 Variants Are Associated With Asthenozoospermia and Impaired Mitochondria
text: BACKGROUND: Male infertility affects approximately 15%-20% of couples worldwide, with asthenozoospermia accounting for about 19% of cases. Nevertheless, the genetic basis of many asthenozoospermia cases remains poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether DNAH14 variants cause asthenozoospermia and to explore the underlying mechanisms related to sperm motility and mitochondrial function. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Whole-exome sequencing was performed on six Chinese individuals with asthenozoospermia. Dnah14-disrupted male mice were generated to assess fertility phenotypes. Comprehensive kinetics analysis, quantitative proteomics, Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis, transmission electron microscopy, and Seahorse assays were utilized to investigate sperm function, protein alterations, and mitochondrial bioenergetics. RESULTS: Six DNAH14 variants were identified in the affected individuals. Disruption of Dnah14 in male mice led to subfertility characterized by impaired sperm motility and fertilization capacity. Dnah14-deficient spermatozoa exhibited reduced flagellar beat amplitude but increased beat frequency. Quantitative proteomic analysis indicated substantial alterations in sperm protein composition, with GO analysis revealing associations with mitochondrial translation and mitochondrial inner membrane pathways. Transmission electron microscopy showed abnormal mitochondrial morphology, and Seahorse assays detected significantly reduced oxidative phosphorylation and glycolysis. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: DNAH14 is a critical regulator of sperm flagellar beat amplitude and mitochondrial bioenergetics, and variants in DNAH14 might be an important cause of asthenozoospermia.

title: Designing reproductive stage resilience to temperature extremes and water stress in food legumes: from physiology to translational genomics
Family screening and genetic testing in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis: Changing (not only) variant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis
text: With increasing awareness of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) as a cause of heart failure and the availability of disease-modifying therapies, the importance of early diagnosis has grown. Consequently, greater emphasis has been placed on genetic testing and family screening to identify individuals with variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) who are at risk of developing ATTRv cardiomyopathy (ATTRv-CM). To identify individuals with a genetic predisposition to the disease, all individuals with ATTR-CM should undergo genetic testing with subsequent cascade genetic testing in relatives when a genetic variant is identified. In asymptomatic pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) transthyretin (TTR) variant carriers, structured follow-up is recommended to enable early diagnosis, allowing timely initiation of treatment. Additionally, systematic family screening protocols may also help identify and detect ATTR-CM in general, including wild-type ATTR-CM.In conclusion, this narrative review provides clinicians with an overview of how to manage patients with ATTRv-CM and their families. Indeed, comprehensive genetic and cascade screening strategies are essential for early identification and optimal management of ATTR-CM. Future perspectives include refinement of risk stratification, optimization of diagnostic and screening pathways, improved timing of treatment initiation, and addressing health inequalities to ensure equitable access to care.

title: RAD52 is a therapeutic vulnerability for acquired PARP inhibitor resistance in ovarian cancer
text: Acquired resistance to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) limits their therapeutic benefits in patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC). Identifying therapeutic vulnerabilities that function across distinct forms of acquired PARPi resistance is an urgent need. In BRCA2-deficient PARPi-naive cells, targeting RAD52 can be synthetic lethal with a PARPi, making RAD52 an attractive therapeutic target. However, this approach has not been tested in HGSC models of acquired PARPi resistance. Here, we assessed the effects of RAD52 loss in 2 distinct Brca2-deficient mouse models of HGSC with acquired PARPi resistance. RAD52 loss suppressed homologous recombination and single-strand annealing DNA repair activity in both models. Genetic depletion and pharmacologic inhibition of RAD52 restored PARPi sensitivity both in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, RAD52 expression was elevated in a newly derived human model of BRCA2-deficient HGSC with acquired PARPi resistance. In this cell line, RAD52 inhibition synergized with a PARPi. Finally, elevated RAD52 expression was associated with poor survival in patients with HGSC. Collectively, these findings establish RAD52 as a clinically relevant therapeutic vulnerability in multiple models of HGSC with acquired PARPi resistance.

title: Retrospective single cell lineage tracing with highly mutable homopolymers
text: Retrospective reconstruction of cell lineages from somatic mutations holds substantial promise for understanding development, tissue homeostasis, and disease. Yet, current approaches are often constrained by low marker density, technical noise, and incomplete molecular readouts that limit the resolution and accuracy of inferred lineages. Here, we present RETrace2, a single-cell dual-omic method for simultaneous lineage tracing and cell-type identification. By identifying and targeting highly mutable homopolymers, which we show are approximately twice as informative as conventional microsatellite repeats, combined with technical improvements to increase marker coverage and reduce experimental errors of reading and amplifying homopolymers, RETrace2 can trace lineage continuously at an estimated resolution of fewer than five cell divisions in microsatellite-unstable organisms. Simultaneously, sparse methylation profiles are obtained from the same cells for cell-type identification. We validate the method using in vitro ground-truth models and demonstrate its utility in vivo by reconstructing multi-organ lineage trees from the brain, kidney and liver of Msh2-deficient mice. Cell lineage reconstruction can reveal developmental histories, but current methods are limited by marker density and accuracy. Here, the authors develop RETrace2, a dual‑omic single‑cell approach that combines highly mutable homopolymer markers with methylation profiling to enable high‑resolution lineage tracing and cell‑type identification.

title: Low‐Intensity Focused Ultrasound Enables Temporal Modulation of Human Midbrain Organoid Differentiation
text: ABSTRACT Controlling the precise timing of biosignaling cues in complex 3D models such as organoids is critical for guiding cellular differentiation and functional maturation. Ultrasound stimulation, a next‐generation neuromodulation modality, offers unique advantages due to its target specificity, ability to elicit mechanosensitive responses, and high spatial resolution. However, there is still a lack of precision stimulation platforms and comprehensive biomarker assays for selective control of organoid development. Here, we introduce a modular piezoelectric ultrasound stimulation platform that integrates seamlessly with conventional multi‐well plates, enabling selective neuromodulation of midbrain organoids (mBOs). We demonstrate that ultrasound can specifically modulate cellular differentiation by promoting dopaminergic progenitor markers while delaying terminal differentiation. Importantly, ultrasound stimulation did not induce cellular damage, as confirmed by the absence of apoptosis and DNA damage markers. This work demonstrates the potential of focused ultrasound as a safe, non‐invasive, and tunable biophysical cue for temporal regulation of organoid differentiation.

title: Identification of altered potassium channels for drug repurposing in long COVID patients
text: Introduction Long COVID (LC) is a complex condition characterized by persistent, chronic multisystem manifestations, with a significant proportion of patients exhibiting neurological symptoms. Human ion channels (HICs), particularly potassium channels, are abundantly expressed in the nervous system and are involved in key physiological processes, making them potential candidates for understanding LC pathophysiology and identifying opportunities for drug repurposing. Methodology Meta-analysis of RNA sequencing datasets from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients was performed. Differential gene expression analysis, functional enrichment analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed to uncover key genes, pathways, and co-expression modules consisting of HICs, lipid metabolism-, and immune signaling-related genes. Drug-gene interaction analysis was performed using the Drug-Gene Interaction Database and Connectivity Map to identify potential ion channel candidates for drug repurposing. Results A total of 715 dysregulated genes, including 18 HICs, were identified, among which seven were potassium channels. Three significant modules containing HICs, lipid metabolism-, and immune signaling-related genes were identified and found to be associated with antigen processing and presentation, complement and coagulation cascades, and cytokine-related pathways. Additionally, drug interaction analysis identified approved drugs targeting KCNA6 , KCNJ10 , KCNN3 , and KCNH4 . Conclusion These findings provide insights into a subset of molecular alterations underlying the multisystem dysregulation observed in LC. The identified drug interactions may provide opportunities for drug repurposing to address neurological manifestations of LC. Further experimental validation is required to establish their therapeutic efficacy and potential clinical relevance.

title: Microarray patches for transdermal drug delivery: a critical narrative review of technological innovations, CMC challenges, clinical translation, and global health implementation
text: Microarray patches (MAPs), alternatively known as microneedle patches, is a paradigm shift in the administration of pharmaceutical agents and vaccines. By utilising micron-scale projections to breach the stratum corneum, MAPs bridge the gap between the convenience of transdermal patches and the efficacy of hypodermic injections. This critical narrative review synthesises advances in MAP technology for transdermal drug delivery, focusing on technological innovations, chemistry, manufacturing, and control (CMC) challenges, clinical translation, regulatory considerations, and global health implementation. Special emphasis is placed on CMC challenges, including sterilisation and stability profiling, as well as the landscape of Clinical Trials, highlighting recent frameworks for pivotal Phase III studies in measles and rubella. We conclude by evaluating the programmatic suitability of MAPs for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), addressing critical barriers such as cold-chain logistics and trypanophobia. A coordinated evolution from product-by-product model to platform-industrialisation model involving vaccine, polymer and device producing companies, regulators, global-health agencies including World health organization (WHO), and technology enablers is necessary. The Measles-Rubella programme provides an important template. MAPs’ value is not about replacing a syringe but enabling equitable distribution of vaccination; a strategy to make vaccination less dependent on infrastructure. As scientific innovations, upscaling, unified regulatory frameworks and equitable access advance, MAPs will achieve global relevance.

title: A transient modified mRNA encoding Myc and cyclin T1 improves cardiac function after myocardial injury
text: Myc is an evolutionarily conserved transcription factor that is necessary for the restoration of tissues in multiple regenerative species. The adult mammalian heart lacks regenerative capacity and cardiomyocytes fail to divide following damage-induced signaling. Transgenic expression of Myc and cyclin T1 can drive substantial adult cardiomyocyte proliferation to replace lost cardiomyocytes. Here, using transgenic models and a prototypical mRNA therapeutic, we show that Myc and cyclin T1 require transient induction for cardiomyocyte proliferation that leads to myocardial repair and functional recovery after myocardial infarction in mice. This research provides a strategy to translate Myc-cyclin T1 coexpression for cardiac regeneration to address serious unmet needs in the treatment of cardiovascular disease.
