title: A strongly annotated passive acoustic dataset for tropical bird monitoring
text: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring enables continuous, non-invasive biodiversity assessment across diverse ecosystems. The scale of these datasets has driven the adoption of machine learning, with supervised approaches showing strong performance. However, supervised methods require time-resolved annotated datasets, which remain scarce, especially in complex tropical soundscapes. We present PteroSet, a curated dataset of strongly annotated Neotropical bird vocalizations recorded in Puerto Asís (Putumayo) and Pivijay (Magdalena), Colombia, between 2023 and 2025. The dataset comprises 563 recordings (73.62 h) and 15,372 time–frequency annotations, including 6,702 events identified to the species level across 168 species. We release the annotations in a COCO-inspired JSON schema that unifies audio files, taxonomic categories, and labels for machine learning workflows. Beyond providing annotated data, PteroSet serves as a realistic benchmark that highlights key characteristics of tropical soundscapes, including acoustic co-occurrence and domain shift across recording sites. We provide a deep learning baseline for binary bird detection, demonstrating PteroSet’s usability and the challenges it presents.

title: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
text: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching. This method integrates novel retrieval mechanisms, including LLM-based, vector-based, graph traversal-based, and hybrid techniques with advanced reranking schemes to extract the most relevant subgraphs from large external KGs. Our approach achieves superior results without requiring re-training, as evidenced by improvements of 39.79% in precision and 30.56% in F1 score over LLM-based state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods (e.g., Jellyfish-8B) on the MIMIC dataset, and enhancements of 69.20% in precision and 21.99% in F1 score over pre-trained language model (PLM)-based SOTA methods (e.g., SMAT) on the Synthea dataset. Additionally, KG-RAG4SM scales effectively across KGs from commonsense KGs to domain-specific ones, while its instruction-tuning knowledge exclusion component ensures truthful performance in end-to-end schema matching tasks despite the suboptimal relevance of KG context. Our empirical analysis and case studies from real-world scenarios show that the hallucination problem in LLMs for schema matching is well mitigated by our solution.

title: MultiSHAP: a Shapley-based framework for explaining cross-modal interactions in multimodal AI models
text: Abstract Multimodal AI models have achieved impressive performance in tasks that require integrating information from multiple modalities, such as vision and language. While existing model explanation methods, such as attention maps and Grad-CAM, offer insights into cross-modal relationships, they do not explicitly quantify fine-grained interactions between individual visual and textual elements and require access to model internals. Here we introduce MultiSHAP, an architecture-agnostic interpretability framework that leverages the Shapley Interaction Index to attribute multimodal outputs to pairwise interactions between fine-grained visual and textual elements, such as image patches and text tokens. MultiSHAP does not require access to model parameters, gradients, attention weights, or intermediate representations, but requires a query interface that permits separate perturbation of visual and textual inputs and returns a task-relevant scalar score, either directly or through a ranked output from which such a score can be deterministically constructed. Our approach provides: (1) instance-level explanations that characterize how specific visual and textual elements jointly affect a selected model output, and (2) dataset-level descriptive summaries of interaction patterns under a specified model, value function, feature partition, and masking operator. Experiments on multimodal benchmarks provide evidence that MultiSHAP captures behaviorally relevant input-level interactions, while pair-level evaluations provide partial evidence that the estimated patch–token correspondences contain information beyond unimodal saliency, and case studies illustrate its use for examining individual multimodal decisions. Although evaluated here on vision–language models, the underlying interaction formulation may in principle be extended to other modality combinations.

title: Evaluating LLMs on Italian through multi-prompt: the Evalita-LLM benchmark
text: Abstract We present Evalita-LLM, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on Italian tasks. The key innovation of Evalita-LLM is the use of multiple prompts for each task, which mitigates the model’s sensitivity to specific prompt formulations and ensures a robust and objective performance assessment. We propose an iterative methodology for selecting and validating multiple prompts, and metrics that capture both high performance and stability of a prompt given a set of LLMs. The resulting Evalita-LLM multi-prompt benchmark is based on ten native Italian tasks, eliminating translation issues and potential cultural biases. It includes a mix of multiple-choice and generative tasks, enabling more natural interactions with LLMs. We report experimental results from the benchmark’s development phase, along with performance statistics for several state-of-the-art LLMs. Evalita-LLM is publicly available with a leaderboard hosted on Hugging Face to support transparent evaluation and comparison of LLMs.

title: STAT+: Enforcement of stringent Medicaid work requirements delayed for six months
text: Enforcement of the Trump administration's stringent new Medicaid work requirements have been delayed for six months, until July 1, 2027.

title: STAT+: Democrats coalesce around ‘Medicare for More,’ ‘Medikids’ proposals
text: Democrats are coalescing around a plan to offer Medicare to more Americans, if not all of them.

title: Tex11 mutant mouse models of human azoospermia.
text: Do different patient TEX11 mutations lead to non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) when modeled in mice? A frameshift mutation in Tex11 leads to azoospermia in mice (Tex11D); a missense mutation had no impact on fertility (Tex11A); and a splice site mutation caused reduced testis weights and sperm counts with variable sub-fertility (Tex11L). Half of all NOA cases are unexplained but may arise from unidentified genetic mutations. Several variants in TEX11 have been identified in men with NOA; and Tex11 knockout in mice causes NOA. For fertility analysis of the different mutations, the sample sizes were as follows: n = 3 wild-type controls; n = 5 Tex11D; n = 3 Tex11A; and n = 3 Tex11L. Wild-type males and hemizygous mutant male mice in each Tex11 line were bred with two to four different wild-type females for fertility analysis. At 12 weeks, testes and epidiymides were then collected for histological analysis and sperm counts. Additional Tex11L mice (n = 3) and wild-type controls (n = 3) were bred for 52 weeks with 2 new wild-type females every 2-3 weeks, then testes and epididymides were collected for further analysis. Testes and epididymides from Tex11L mice (n = 3 for wild type and mutants) were also collected at 24 and 36 weeks of age for histological analyses. TEX11 variants identified in male patients with NOA were introduced into the orthologous region of the mouse genome using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. Lines were expanded onto a DBA/2 background by breeding female heterozygous carriers to wild-type DBA/2 males. Hemizygous males from the third generation and beyond were used for fertility studies, gross tissue morphology, sperm counts, and histological analysis. Compared to wild-type mice (145.0 ± 17.56 mg testis weight; 1.72 ± 0.50 million sperm/cauda epididymis; 6.42 ± 0.73 pups/breeding), Tex11D mice had reduced testis weight (28.33 ± 0.68 mg), no sperm in the epididymis, and were infertile with a maturation arrest testicular phenotype. We did not observe any spermatogenesis or fertility defects in Tex11A mice (145.0 mg ± 0 mg; 1.52 ± 0.11 million sperm/cauda; 5.83 ± 0.81 pups/breeding) compared to wild type. Tex11L mice had reduced testis weight (78.33 ± 16.41 mg) and reduced epididymal sperm counts (0.33 ± 0.13 million/cauda epididymis) but a variable fertility phenotype (5.42 ± 1.13 pups/breeding), with 2 out of 6 mice being subfertile. Tex11L mice also had variable testicular and epididymal defects, classified as mild or severe. Not applicable for this study. The sample sizes were limited for each mouse line. Our study shows the importance of validating NOA-associated variants in a mouse model. Our data suggest that different TEX11 variants produce a variety of phenotypes which could impact genetic counselling of patients with NOA. This study was supported by the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute for Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) grant HD096723 to A.N.Y. and K.E.O. G.R.A. was supported by NICHD grant HD114406. K.E.O. was an advisor to Paterna Biosciences. The authors declare that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.

title: Photoperiodic responses persist in DH-like neuropeptide gene mutants of the band-legged ground cricket, Dianemobius nigrofasciatus.
text: Seasonal adaptation is essential for the survival and reproduction of organisms inhabiting environments with predictable annual fluctuations. Photoperiodism is a key adaptive mechanism that enables most multivoltine insects to synchronize physiological and developmental processes with seasonal environmental changes, yet its underlying endocrine mechanisms remain poorly understood. Diapause hormone (DH) and DH-like neuropeptides, which belong to the tryptopyrokinin (TPK) family and are characterized by a conserved C-terminal WFGPRXa motif, play a pivotal role in photoperiodically regulated maternal embryonic diapause induction in several insect species. In some lepidopteran insects, DH has also been implicated in the regulation of photoperiodic responses beyond diapause induction, raising the possibility that DH/DH-like neuropeptides function as a common regulator of multiple photoperiodic responses across insects. However, whether this mechanism is conserved across insect taxa remains unclear. The band-legged ground cricket Dianemobius nigrofasciatus exhibits multiple photoperiodic responses, including maternal embryonic diapause induction, wing morph and rate of nymphal development. Here, we investigated the involvement of DH-like neuropeptides in photoperiodic responses in D. nigrofasciatus. Two genes encoding TPKs were identified from the genome sequence of D. nigrofasciatus. One corresponded to capa, whereas the other was designated Din-dh because it encoded seven TPKs (i.e., DH-like neuropeptides). We established three mutant lines carrying distinct Din-dh alleles derived from two G0 founders and investigated whether Din-dh is involved in photoperiodic responses. All mutant lines retained detectable photoperiodic responses. These results indicate that disruption of Din-dh does not abolish photoperiodic responses examined in D. nigrofasciatus.

title: Wine Yeast Engineering for Improved Polysaccharide Depolymerization and Reduced Urea Accumulation.
text: Engineering wine yeasts to combine efficient extracellular polysaccharide degradation with reduced urea accumulation may support improvements in winemaking. This study aimed to replace the arginase-encoding CAR1 locus in the genome of the triploid industrial wine yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae I-328 with an expression cassette for the endopolygalacturonase gene PGU1, placed under the control of the PGK1 gene promoter and terminator. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing was performed using an acetamidase-selectable plasmid followed by phenotypic screening and molecular genetic verification. Whole genome sequencing confirmed the replacement of all three CAR1 alleles by the PGU1 expression cassettes. The modified strain I-328-Y21 showed enhanced degradation of polygalacturonic acid relative to the parental strain. Consistently, RT-qPCR analysis showed that the transcription level of the PGU1 gene in strain I-328-Y21 was about 300 times higher than in I-328. Disruption of arginase-the enzyme that generates urea from arginine-reduced urea content in the growth medium by about ninefold. As ethyl carbamate is formed from ethanol and yeast-excreted urea, this strain could help lower ethyl carbamate in wine. Fermentation performance and other technological characteristics remained unaffected by the genome editing. The new strain, in which the arginase gene is replaced by an endopolygalacturonase expression cassette, is a promising candidate for winemaking.

title: Computational analysis of KLF6/PDE4B-associated ferro-aging signatures and candidate drugs in benign prostatic hyperplasia.
text: To identify ferro-aging-related molecular candidates associated with epithelial states in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and thereby prioritize drug candidates for experimental testing. Bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets were integrated. Differential analysis, comparison of 113 machine-learning combinations, external validation of a unified random forest, SHAP interpretation, BPH phenotype mapping, pseudotime analysis, cell-cell communication analysis, and in silico virtual knockout were performed. Primary analyses used complete available datasets, with a fixed computational subsample for virtual knockout. Drug prioritization was further conducted by combining reversal of the complete disease transcriptional signature with dual-target molecular docking against KLF6/PDE4B. 7 ferro-aging-related differentially expressed genes were detected in BPH tissues, including downregulated KLF6 and PDE4B, and cross-model screening identified PTGS2, KLF6, PDE4B, EMP1, and SNCA. The unified random forest achieved AUCs of 0.917 and 0.800 in GSE132714 and GSE119195, respectively, with KLF6 and PDE4B ranking first and second in SHAP importance within the selected five-gene model. The wide confidence interval in GSE119195 limited the certainty of external discrimination. Single-cell phenotype mapping localized BPH-related signals mainly to luminal and basal epithelial states. Both genes showed regional expression in spatial tissue and distinct predicted perturbation profiles after in silico virtual knockout in basal, Club, and luminal epithelial cells. Independent donor-level single-cell comparisons did not reproduce uniform epithelial downregulation: KLF6 was nonsignificant, whereas PDE4B showed positive estimates in basal and Club/hillock-like groups. Reversal of the complete disease signature together with dual-target ranking prioritized canagliflozin, filgotinib, and tadalafil. Their best KLF6/PDE4B binding energies were -8.7/-10.8, -9.3/-9.7, and -9.1/-9.5 kcal/mol, respectively. These computational findings prioritize KLF6/PDE4B as candidates associated with ferro-aging-related epithelial transcriptional states in BPH. Within this molecular framework, canagliflozin, filgotinib, and tadalafil were prioritized as candidates for experimental validation, with canagliflozin receiving the highest overall priority.

title: Microplastics (MPs)-associated chemical components are associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression via genomic instability and spatial microenvironment remodeling: A study based on integrated multi-omics analysis.
text: Microplastics (MPs) and their toxic components (BPA, DBP, DEHP) pose global health threats, with the liver as primary target. The mechanisms by which MPs may contribute to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and spatial microenvironment remodeling remain poorly understood. We employed an integrated multi-omics workflow combining bulk transcriptomics, WGCNA, ten machine learning algorithms combined into 101 candidate model combinations, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics (ST), inferCNV, CytoTRACE, and molecular docking with 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. We identified 22 hub genes at the putative intersection of HCC dysregulation and documented toxicological targets of MP-associated chemicals (BPA, DBP, and DEHP), enriched in cell cycle and senescence. A 6-gene (AKR1C3, AURKA, CCNB1, EZH2, FABP5, ESR1) risk model (glmBoost + SVM) achieved high diagnostic accuracy (mean external AUC = 0.965; internal bootstrap validation of the six-gene logistic model: bias-corrected AUC = 0.987 (optimism = 0.005). Single-cell analysis revealed risk genes localized in HCC parenchymal and myeloid cells, putatively positively correlating with CNV burden and stemness, while ESR1 showed inverse correlation. ST suggested spatial expression gradients of AKR1C3 and FABP5 with increasing malignancy. Molecular docking of all six hub targets against BPA, DBP, and DEHP, followed by 100 ns MD simulations of the AKR1C3-ligand complexes-the biologically most relevant sub-network-suggested structurally stable binding, with RMSD fluctuations (0.13-0.5 nm), maintained hydrogen bonds, stable Rg and SASA, low RMSF, and favorable free energy landscapes, supporting the structural plausibility of protein-ligand interactions. This study provides a multidimensional, hypothesis-generating landscape of HCC progression associated with MP-associated chemical exposure at single-cell and spatial resolutions, with dynamic and energetic evidence supporting the structural plausibility of stable plasticizer-target binding, offering novel toxicological targets and mechanistic insights for environmental and clinical intervention.

title: Multi-omics analysis highlights TM4SF4 + epithelial cells and the MMP14-associated signaling program in lung adenocarcinoma pathogenesis and microenvironment remodeling.
text: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression is shaped by aberrant cell-cell and cell-matrix communication within a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME). This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), genome-wide association study, and spatial transcriptomics to identify epithelial subpopulations associated with this crosstalk. Analyzing GSE196303 scRNA-seq data, we resolved 15 epithelial subpopulations. Using scPagwas, the TM4SF4 + subpopulation showed the highest trait-relevance score for LUAD genetic susceptibility (adjusted p < 0.05). BayesPrism deconvolution of TCGA-LUAD data revealed TM4SF4 + cell enrichment in tumors; high abundance was associated with poorer overall survival in the median-cutoff analysis (hazard ratio = 1.43, 95% confidence interval = 1.07-1.92, p = 0.016) and with TME remodeling features (reduced immune/stromal scores and increased tumor purity). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and multi-evidence intersection identified MMP14 as a candidate hub gene. Spatial transcriptomics supported the heterogeneous distribution of MMP14, and functional enrichment linked MMP14-associated transcriptional programs to ECM remodeling, migration, and Hedgehog/Notch pathways. Expression validation confirmed MMP14 upregulation in LUAD cells and tissues. Collectively, TM4SF4 + epithelial cells and the MMP14-associated program may contribute to LUAD progression and TME remodeling, supporting them as candidate biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for further validation.

title: CROST 2.0: an expanded repository of spatial transcriptomics.
text: CROST (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/crost) is a public spatial transcriptomics resource that offers curated datasets, standardized analytical results, structured spatial knowledge, and interactive exploration tools. In version 2.0, our collection has expanded to 544 projects and 3538 samples, nearly a three-fold increase from version 1.0 (182 projects and 1033 samples). We have also substantially expanded the derived resources for spatial colocalization and spatially variable cancer genes. To facilitate spatial microenvironment analysis, CROST 2.0 introduces an analytical framework comprising niche-associated differential expression, spatially resolved gene-set activity analysis, spatial interaction hotspot and topic analyses, and molecular and cell-type niche analysis. CROST 2.0 also provides the Spatial Compare function to compare spatial gene expression, cell-type distributions, and niche composition across samples. It introduces the Cancer NicheDE module to systematically characterize cancer niche-associated differential expression and integrates an online cell-type annotation tool, SCType, enabling the use of single-cell reference information in spatial transcriptomic analysis. These updates extend CROST into an integrated spatial transcriptomics resource for characterizing spatial microenvironments, investigating cancer-associated spatial features, and comparing spatial patterns across samples.

title: The Molecular Landscape of Placental Dysfunction in Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR): From Integrated Signaling Networks to Epigenetic Control.
text: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major pregnancy complication linked to placental insufficiency, resulting from defective trophoblast differentiation, impaired maternal-fetal vascular adaptation, and altered nutrient sensing. This review synthesizes current evidence on the interconnected molecular networks driving placental dysfunction. We map the reciprocal crosstalk between the pro-inflammatory shift, highlighted by NLRP3 inflammasome-driven trophoblast pyroptosis, and dysregulated extracellular matrix remodeling mediated by the MMP-9/TIMP system. This hostile microenvironment feeds directly into the angiogenic imbalance defined by the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, accelerating cellular senescence via p53 and disrupting survival hubs like the PTEN/PI3K/AKT axis. Consequently, downstream metabolic sensors, notably the mTOR pathway, are blunted, causing trafficking failure of essential amino acid (SNAT2, LAT1) and glucose (GLUT) transporters. Crucially, we introduce an original framework integrating emerging spatial transcriptomics and single-cell epigenomics, demonstrating that these pathomechanisms are anatomically regionalized rather than uniform. Finally, we provide a critical evaluation of translation-ready therapeutic targets, emphasizing that strict safety constraints against fetal teratogenesis render ligand-functionalized nanoparticles a non-negotiable prerequisite for placenta-selective drug delivery. Integrating molecular stratification with longitudinal biomarker profiling represents the next milestone for mechanism-based, targeted management of FGR.

title: Classic Hodgkin Lymphoma: Biology-Driven Disease Model.
text: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is a unique lymphoid neoplasm in which rare malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells orchestrate an extensive, spatially organized immune and inflammatory microenvironment that determines diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic sensitivity. This review summarizes recent advances in the biopathology, diagnosis, and prognostic stratification of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, with particular emphasis on the emerging molecular subtyping framework proposed by Aoki and colleagues, which is not yet clinically validated, and on the proposed concept of classic Hodgkin lymphoma as a systemic immunobiological disease. In this narrative review, we examined the literature on classic Hodgkin lymphoma biology, the tumor immune microenvironment, diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, and molecular classification, prioritizing studies published through to mid-2026 and distinguishing established evidence from observational associations, preclinical findings, meeting abstracts, ongoing trials, and hypotheses, including single-cell, spatial, and liquid biopsy technologies, and integrating the authors' own recent work on immune and inflammatory biomarkers and on the systemic immunobiological features of classic Hodgkin lymphoma. Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells sustain disease through constitutive NF-κB and JAK/STAT signaling, 9p24.1-driven PD-L1/PD-L2 overexpression, and secretion of chemokines and cytokines that recruit and functionally reprogram CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, macrophages, and stromal cells. Multidimensional profiling integrating malignant-cell genomics, spatial transcriptomics, and imaging mass cytometry has led to the proposal of four molecular subtypes of classic Hodgkin lymphoma (CST, CN913, STB, and CN2P), each defined by distinct genomic drivers and immune architecture, a hypothesis-generating framework that awaits prospective validation. Classic Hodgkin lymphoma has been proposed to be a systemic immunobiological disorder, with circulating tumor DNA, thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (TARC/CCL17), and peripheral immune signatures associated with disease activity beyond the lymph node; these markers are promising but remain investigational. Diagnosis is evolving from morphology-based assessment toward precision immunopathology integrating spatial and digital pathology, while prognosis is progressively incorporating tissue-based, circulating, spatial, and molecular biomarkers into integrated risk models that are, for the most part, still investigational and are being tested in biomarker-directed clinical trials. The convergence of molecular subtyping, spatial immunobiology, systemic disease biology, and liquid biopsy may reshape the diagnostic and prognostic landscape of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, suggesting a potential transition from anatomically defined, morphology-based assessment toward integrated, biology-driven precision medicine. This transition has unfolded stepwise, from tissue-based immunophenotyping and spatial biomarkers, through circulating markers such as ctDNA and TARC/CCL17, to genomically defined molecular subtypes now being linked to systemic immune readouts and tested in biomarker-directed trials. Prospective validation, assay standardization, and evidence of clinical utility are required before these approaches can enter routine practice.

title: Rapid identification of potent CD38 inhibitors via integrated AI- and structure-based methods.
text: CD38 is a multifunctional ectoenzyme and a clinically validated therapeutic target that plays critical roles in cancer, metabolic disorders, and inflammatory diseases. To accelerate the discovery of novel CD38 inhibitors, we developed an integrated computational framework that combines graph-based structure-activity relationship (SAR) modeling with high-resolution structure-based simulations for mechanism-guided molecular design. Large-scale compound libraries were first screened using artificial intelligence models trained on experimentally validated bioactivity data, followed by structure-based modeling to evaluate binding affinity and characterize protein-ligand interactions within the CD38 active site. Binding-mode analysis identified key pharmacophoric features, which were iteratively incorporated into the graph-based prediction framework to guide compound optimization. Importantly, integrating structural feedback into the generative process enabled enhanced target specificity and improved binding efficiency. Top-ranked candidates exhibited strong binding affinities and favorable bioavailability. This study demonstrates that the integration of AI-driven molecular design with structure-guided refinement enables efficient discovery of potent CD38 inhibitors, providing a robust framework for mechanism-informed drug discovery.

title: Comparative Reconstruction of Intrinsic Apoptosis in Clade V Nematodes Reveals a Conserved Execution Module and Heterogeneous Regulatory Architecture.
text: Intrinsic apoptosis is a form of programmed cell death, yet its regulatory architecture varies across Metazoa. In parasitic nematodes, this pathway is of particular interest because conserved components could represent candidates for anthelmintic intervention. However, pathway-level resolution across nematodes remains limited, and computational homology alone does not establish conserved biological function. Here, we assessed the evolutionary conservation of candidate intrinsic-apoptosis-associated proteins across a resource-defined set of clade V nematodes. Building on recent pathway reconstruction in the parasitic nematode Haemonchus contortus, we combined orthology inference, genome-guided homology searches, and structure-informed approaches. Homologs corresponding to the BCL-2-like, APAF-1-like, and CASP-3-like execution module were recovered from almost all species and showed high structural similarity among parasitic clade V nematodes. For BCL-2-like and APAF-1-like proteins in particular, structural similarity was greater among parasitic nematodes than between parasite proteins and their corresponding host homologs; these global comparisons inform target prioritization but do not establish drug selectivity. Regulatory components showed heterogeneous evolutionary patterns: FBXO-11-like homologs were comparatively well conserved, and PUM-1/PUM-2-like homologs showed intermediate conservation, whereas p53-like and especially EGL-1-like homologs were more divergent and variably detectable. No additional CED-13-like homolog was detected using sequence- and genome-based searches or, where structural coverage was available, structure-based searches. These findings support a comparatively conserved execution module embedded within a heterogeneous regulatory architecture and provide a framework for prioritizing apoptosis-associated proteins for experimental investigation in anthelmintic discovery.

title: Distributed event-triggered neural dynamics scheme for consensus motion of multi-robot arm systems with efficient communication.
text: To enhance the communication efficiency and reliability of multi-robot arm systems (MRASs) when performing cooperative tasks, a distributed event-triggered neural dynamics (DETND) scheme is proposed. To this end, the kinematics of MRASs is first established, and the consensus information interaction among robots is described via an undirected graph. Meanwhile, joint physical constraints are incorporated into the system model to prevent mechanical damage. Second, the event-triggered mechanism is integrated into the interaction network, and a distributed optimal control strategy is formulated based on the minimum velocity norm. Subsequently, a neural network solver is constructed to execute control strategies for the robot arms only at discrete triggering instants. By adopting the DETND scheme, limited communication resources and network bandwidth can be allocated more efficiently, thus enhancing the reliability and efficiency of the robots in performing consensus tracking tasks. Finally, computer simulations and physical experiments demonstrate that the proposed DETND scheme can effectively address the consensus motion generation problem of MRASs. Compared with conventional periodic time-optimal control methods, the proposed DETND scheme achieves superior performance in terms of communication efficiency and convergence performance.

title: Continuous 3D microscopic measurement via spatial-resolution compensation.
text: Extended-depth-of-field (EDOF) microscopy estimates surface height from axial focal positions, but elongation of the three-dimensional point-spread function makes axial resolution poorer than lateral resolution. We propose binocular oblique-view spatial-compensation microscopy (BOSCM), which uses two fixed, complementary oblique views to convert continuous lateral sample motion into simultaneous axial focal-plane scanning and lateral translation of the field of view. This geometry synchronizes focus-stack acquisition with large-area scanning and projects axial height variations onto the higher-resolution lateral direction. Global spatial calibration, constrained low-frequency residual compensation, and reliability-weighted fusion jointly recover dual-view height data and all-in-focus texture. Experiments show that BOSCM reduces spatial-resolution anisotropy, decreases the mean height RMSE by approximately 50%, improves the height-discrimination capability by approximately 18-fold, and improves reconstruction completeness on complex surfaces, enabling continuous large-area three-dimensional microscopic measurement.

title: Quantifying the localized electrical interface using a force-controlled scanning ion conductance microscopy.
text: The electrical double layer (EDL) at solid-liquid interfaces provides a natural transduction pathway for understanding interfacial electrical properties without physical signal conversion and convolution. However, the EDL's ultrashort characteristic length and complex signal decoupling pose challenges for conventional techniques in achieving reliable measurements. Moreover, a critical gap remains in the underlying measurement theory. We hypothesize that a measurement platform combining EDL-mediated localized charge characterization with quantitative electrokinetic modeling can open new avenues for advancing interfacial science. We developed a force-controlled scanning ion conductance microscopy (FCSICM) platform that enables high-resolution mapping of interface charge distribution. The ion current rectification (ICR) sensitivity was systematically evaluated across diverse interfacial conditions, including bias voltages, substrate polarities, and electrolyte concentrations. To bridge these observations and theories, a physically interpretable electrokinetic transport model was developed. Furthermore, the platform's versatility was demonstrated on diverse patterns and structures, where the high-aspect-ratio microgrooves are inaccessible to most conventional scanning probe microscopy tips. Force-feedback ensures stable probe-EDL engagement. The ICR results reveal a pronounced dependence of FCSICM on interfacial conditions, with the rectification ratio peaking (IPDL/IGlass = 1.5) at higher bias voltage (±1 V) and lower concentration (1 mM) due to Debye length expansion and enhanced ionic selectivity. The quantitative electrokinetic model faithfully reproduces current-voltage characteristics (RMS error = 0.009), transforming ion rectification from qualitative observation into a quantitative analytical tool. Synchronous topography and surface charge mapping across engineered substrates yielded excellent consistency, clearly differentiating distinct material interfaces. These findings collectively establish FCSICM as a promising tool for understanding interfacial science.

title: Integrated microRNA and mRNA Profiling in the Corneal Endothelium of Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy.
text: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are endogenous non-coding RNAs that post-transcriptionally modulate gene expression, playing roles in both development and disease pathogenesis. This study specifically investigates the differential miRNA expression in human FECD endothelium compared to healthy controls. By integrating this miRNAome profile with our existing transcriptomic background, we aimed to identify candidate miRNA-target gene regulatory relationships potentially relevant to FECD. NanoString nCounter miRNA profiling was performed on corneal endothelium from FECD patients and controls. Differential expression analysis was conducted, followed by correlation of miRNAs with transcriptomic data from matched samples. Functional enrichment was performed for negatively correlated miRNA-mRNA pairs to identify pathways relevant to FECD pathogenesis. We found 98 differentially expressed miRNAs between FECD and controls. Correlation analysis revealed negatively correlated candidate miRNA-target gene pairs, highlighting potential regulatory interactions. Enrichment analysis of target genes implicated PI3K-AKT, TNF, AGE-RAGE, and focal adhesion pathways as part of FECD molecular alterations. Several dysregulated miRNAs (e.g., miR-302 and miR-630) were associated with processes such as extracellular matrix remodeling, apoptosis, and inflammatory signaling, consistent with key pathogenic features of FECD. This exploratory study provides new insights into the pathogenesis of FECD by integrating miRNA profiling with a transcriptomic background. This combined analysis highlights candidate miRNA-target associations identified within the FECD group and places them into potentially regulatory pathways relevant to endothelial degeneration. The observed miR-29 expression trends are hypothesis-generating; however, the miR-29 family did not meet the prespecified FDR threshold and was not retained in the final correlation network, precluding confirmation of its contribution to ECM remodeling in our cohort. In parallel, comparison with earlier array-based studies revealed inconsistencies that may partly reflect differences in platforms and cohorts; these discrepancies warrant further investigation in independent cohorts. Finally, the analysis of mirtronic host genes uncovered unstable correlations, suggesting that array-based measurements alone are insufficient for reliable miRNA quantification. Together, these findings refine our understanding of FECD-related networks, resolve some earlier contradictions, and open directions for more robust validation and therapeutic exploration.

title: PVDive: the plant virus diversity database.
text: Plant viruses are a diverse class of infectious agents affecting agricultural crop production, plant health, and international movement of plant material. While availability and accessibility of scientific data related to plant viruses is essential for plant protection activities, scientific research, diagnostics, plant breeding, and beyond, publicly available data on plant viruses are at present not easily accessible; they are non-standardized, scattered across different resources, poorly interlinked, and not easily searchable by scientists or digital agents. We present PVDive (Plant Virus Diversity Database; https://pvdive.dsmz.de), a freely accessible resource providing high-quality, standardized, and integrated data associated with plant viruses. PVDive primarily offers information at the level of individual plant virus isolates and samples originating from the plant virus collection of the Leibniz Institute DSMZ (Germany). The data are integrated with information on plant virus species and host plants available in existing public resources and their access is centralized in a single platform. Through an intuitive, user-friendly interface with a number of search functionalities and a RESTful application programming interface, PVDive improves findability, accessibility, retrievability, and interoperability of plant virus data. To support data exploration, the platform also includes tools such as advanced search, sequence viewer, host gallery, and interactive data views.

title: Machine-Learning Derived Individual Risk Prediction in Congenital Heart Surgery: Development and internal validation of risk prediction models for in-hospital mortality after congenital heart surgery using data from the Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) registry.
text: Machine learning (ML) methods may improve prediction of individual risk of mortality risk after congenital heart surgery (CHD) by identifying nonlinear relationships/novel combinations of variables. Improved risk discrimination may improve outcomes by optimizing resource allocation and patient surveillance. Children and adolescents (age≤18 years) undergoing CHD surgery at Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium hospitals 9/1/2014-12/30/2019 were studied. Non-collinear potential predictors were identified empirically and used to create a logistic regression risk (LR) model (mimicking traditional risk-adjustment models) and ML (random forest and gradient boosting model) models. Model performance was evaluated using net reclassification index (NRI), the proportion of subjects in which either the absolute risk category or estimated risk relative to other subjects changed between each model and one composed only of STAT category as the primary outcome. This metric reflects how often a model changes how a clinician views the risk of a patient relative to a parsimonious model and provides some measure of the utility of these models. Secondary analyses compared overall model fit. In total 51,475 operative encounters from 52 hospitals were studied. Subjects were 45% female, 20% neonates, and 5% underwent STAT 5 operations. C-statistics and Brier scores did not differ significantly between ML and LR models. For absolute risk categorires, point estimates for NRI between ML-models and STAT category (0.76 95%CI: 0.68-0.83) suggested at best modest improvements compared to logistic regression model (0.75 95%CI 0.67-0.83), but the difference was not significant. Similarly, for rankings of risk within the cohort, NRI for ML models (0.26 95%CI: 0.19-0.32) was not significantly different to that for the LR model (0.24 95%CI: 0.17-0.33). ML derived models did not improve overall model fit. Magnitude of improvement in reclassification was at best modest and not statistically significant. Future research is necessary to evaluate the added values of incorporating more comprehensive data and/or advanced computational techniques and use of reclassification in risk prediction.

title: Data-driven cardiometabolic profiling in untreated women with Rotterdam-defined polycystic ovary syndrome: Unsupervised clustering and machine-learning profile assignment.
text: Cardiometabolic risk in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is heterogeneous and may not be fully captured by Rotterdam phenotypes. We aimed to identify data-driven cardiometabolic profiles at initial diagnosis and to evaluate supervised models for profile assignment. This retrospective, single-center, clinic-based study included 485 newly diagnosed, untreated women aged 18-45 years with Rotterdam-defined PCOS. Ten routinely available cardiometabolic variables were median-imputed, standardized, reduced by principal component analysis (PCA), and clustered using k-means. Profiles were characterized using variables withheld from clustering and evaluated in missing-data, anthropometry-excluded, age/body mass index-adjusted laboratory-only, and internal assignment-stability analyses. Patient-level cross-validated logistic-regression and random-forest models were used for profile assignment. K-means identified a metabolically favorable profile in 342 patients (70.5%) and a metabolically unfavorable profile in 143 (29.5%). The unfavorable profile showed higher adiposity, central obesity, fasting glucose, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol, transaminases, white blood cell count, insulin resistance, post-load glucose responses, C-reactive protein (CRP), platelet count, lipid-derived indices, and androgen bioavailability, together with lower sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG). Rotterdam phenotype distribution did not differ between profiles (P = 0.650). The profile structure was broadly robust to k-nearest-neighbor-imputed and complete-case clustering (adjusted Rand index [ARI] = 0.783 and 0.909, respectively), whereas age/BMI-adjusted laboratory-only clustering showed lower agreement with the primary partition (ARI = 0.307). Training-fold refitting with held-out centroid assignment showed high internal assignment stability (ARI = 0.909). The independent clinical-endocrine model showed moderate discrimination (receiver operating characteristic area under the curve [ROC-AUC], 0.718), whereas secondary cluster-recovery models showed higher discrimination (ROC-AUC, 0.889-0.942; random forest, 0.935). Routine baseline clinical and laboratory data identified a metabolically unfavorable PCOS profile that was not fully reflected by Rotterdam phenotype distribution in this clinic-based cohort. These exploratory findings require external validation and outcome-based evaluation before their clinical utility can be established.

title: Computed tomography derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in high-risk breast cancer using fully automated deep learning algorithms.
text: Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer. We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins. Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis. Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

title: Identification of Key Fatty acid Metabolism-Related Genes in Vascular Dementia.
text: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD. Single-cell RNA sequencing, intercellular communication inference, and in silico perturbation analyses were applied to define immune-stromal interactions. Potential therapeutic compounds were evaluated using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. We identified three VaD-related fatty acid metabolism genes (VaD-FAMRGs), namely PNPLA3, HSP90AA1, and ALB, which showed consistent diagnostic performance across multiple computational approaches and were associated with lipid metabolism, inflammatory processes, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Functional enrichment, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in silico gene perturbation analyses provided exploratory insights into the potential associations of these candidate genes with lipid transport, metabolic regulation, synaptic maintenance, and immune-inflammatory processes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed activation of the ANGPTL signaling axis, suggesting impaired endothelial-glial interactions driven by lipid metabolic dysregulation. Regulatory network analysis identified key transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulators, including REST, miR-155-5p, and miR-21-5p, which may coordinately modulate VaD-FAMRG expression. Drug repurposing analysis highlighted quercetin as a candidate compound with predicted interactions with all three hub proteins, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. These findings suggest that dysregulated fatty acid metabolism may be associated with the development and progression of VaD through coordinated metabolic, inflammatory, and neurovascular mechanisms. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes and establishes a theoretical basis for future mechanistic and experimental validation.

title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder.
text: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signalling, gut-brain axis, and rapid-acting antidepressant mechanisms, to construct a multi-systems framework of MDD pathophysiology and, as a secondary and explicitly scoped aim, to identify translational priorities for South Asian, particularly Indian, populations; the evidence reviewed is global in scope. A 2025 genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 688,808 cases identified 697 independent associations mapping to 635 genomic risk loci implicating glutamatergic, GABAergic, and neuropeptidergic systems. Environmental stressors converge on this genetic susceptibility through DNA methylation, histone modification, and non-coding RNA-mediated epigenetic reprogramming. An inflammatory MDD subgroup, characterised by kynurenine pathway disruption and microglial dysregulation, is of interest for patient stratification. Rapid-acting antidepressants proposed to act through TrkB-BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity offer a mechanistic account of their fast onset, although the direct-binding theory awaits independent replication. Gut microbiome dysbiosis, particularly among neurotransmitter-producing taxa, further extends the pathophysiological map beyond the brain itself. Together, these findings support a shift from a unidimensional monoaminergic model to an integrated, multi-systems molecular framework of MDD. Realising the clinical potential of this framework will require validated precision biomarker panels, dedicated South Asian GWAS cohorts, and longitudinal multi-omics studies.

title: Tumor-masked structural connectomics for assessing tract-specific white matter disruption associated with glioma aggressiveness: an interpretable machine learning pilot study.
text: To assess the feasibility of personalized tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable machine learning (ML) for differentiating low-grade gliomas (LGG) from high-grade gliomas (HGG), and to identify candidate tract-specific connectomic biomarkers of glioma aggressiveness. Thirty-five patients with histopathologically confirmed gliomas (20 LGG, 15 HGG) underwent preoperative diffusion tensor imaging and T1-weighted MRI. Tumor-masked probabilistic tractography was used to reconstruct individualized structural connectomes based on 50 white matter (WM) tract labels. We evaluated 296 graph-theoretical features using sequential feature selection and Random Forest classification within a strictly isolated nested cross-validation framework. We used SHAP analysis for model interpretation. Sensitivity analyses compared clinical-radiological, connectomic, and combined feature sets. The leak-free pure connectomics model achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.814 ± 0.327 (95% CI, 0.500-1.000), with a macro-F1 score of 0.786 ± 0.265. Restricting the analysis to non-zero connectomic features yielded a mean AUC of 0.833 ± 0.167. The clinical-radiological model achieved a mean AUC of 0.817 ± 0.149, while the combined clinical-radiological and connectomic model showed the highest point estimate (AUC, 0.933 ± 0.109; 95% CI, 0.798-1.068). SHAP analysis highlighted the sagittal stratum, medial lemniscus, and superior fronto-occipital fasciculus among the most informative WM pathways. Tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable ML demonstrated preliminary feasibility for identifying candidate imaging biomarkers associated with glioma aggressiveness in neuroradiological practice. These findings are exploratory and represent internal estimates from a single cohort; external validation in independent, multi-center cohorts is required before any potential clinical application.

title: Dynamic blood glucose trajectory is 28-day all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure: A survival prediction analysis.
text: BackgroundHeart failure (HF) is a global public health issue. Blood glucose influences HF progression, but research on its dynamic changes and mortglity remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the association of baseline admission blood glucose and its dynamic changes with all-cause mortality in patients with HF.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used data from MIMIC-IV and a tertiary hospital. We identified distinct glycemic trajectories using group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) and assessed their association with 28-day all-cause mortality via Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Machine learning models were applied to evaluate the predictive value of glycemia.ResultsA total of 6142 patients from the MIMIC-IV database and 391 local patients were included. Results showed that five dynamic blood glucose trajectory groups were identified. Among them, the moderate-to-high and high-level groups exhibited elevated mortality risk [HR (95% CI): 1.546 (1.231-1.942); 1.572 (1.140-2.168)]. Incorporating blood glucose trajectories into predictive models moderately improved the predictive performance for outcomes, and the Deepsurv model demonstrated better predictive accuracy and stability.ConclusionAlthough current retrospective design limits causal inference and warrants prospective validation, the present study provides evidence that dynamic blood glucose fluctuations demonstrate superior prognostic value compared to baseline measurements for predicting mortality in severe HF patients. Furthermore, machine learning based on glucose trajectory modeling enables early identification of high-risk individuals.

title: Mode-specific fetal heart rate signal dropout as a marker of perinatal asphyxia: A multicenter observational study using causal machine learning methods.
text: Cardiotocography (CTG) is the standard method for intrapartum fetal monitoring. Modern systems acquire fetal heart rate (FHR) using external Doppler ultrasound (US) or internal fetal scalp electrocardiography (ECG). We evaluated whether mode-specific FHR signal dropout was associated with perinatal asphyxia and whether it should be retained as an informative, mode-aware feature for downstream predictive models. We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study using routinely collected clinical and CTG data from Mercy Hospital for Women, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010-2021; Werribee Mercy Hospital, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010-2021; and the Czech CTU-UHB database from University Hospital Brno, for 2010-2012. A total of 46 662 labor episodes at ≥36 weeks' gestation with ≥15 min of interpretable CTG data in the final 60 min before birth were analyzed (32 242 in the model-development cohort, 548 in the Czech validation cohort, and 13 872 in the Australian community validation cohort). The exposure was mode-specific FHR dropout, classified as US low dropout, US high dropout (>30%), ECG low dropout, or ECG high dropout (>30%). The primary outcome was sustained perinatal asphyxia, defined using a Delphi-consensus composite of clinical, biochemical, and neurologic criteria. In the model-development cohort, 860 cases of perinatal asphyxia occurred (2.67%, 95% CI 2.49%-2.85%). Compared with US low dropout, ECG high dropout was associated with higher risk of asphyxia (inverse probability weighting IPW-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.14, 95% CI 2.20-4.48; targeted maximum likelihood estimation-adjusted OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.21-3.58), corresponding to an absolute risk increase of 2.27% (one additional case per 44 births). Survival analysis supported elevated hazards (HR 4.76, 95% CI 2.98-7.62). External validation supported the direction of association, although estimates varied across cohorts. In retrospective multicenter analyses, high FHR dropout during ECG monitoring was associated with increased perinatal asphyxia risk. These findings support evaluating mode-specific dropout as an informative signal-quality feature in future predictive models. Prospective validation of such models is needed before clinical implementation.

title: Multicenter Survival Analysis of Infectious Complications Following Breast Reconstruction: Healthcare Workers Versus General Population.
text: Breast reconstruction (BR) following mastectomy carries a risk of postoperative infection. Healthcare workers (HWs) may have increased exposure to nosocomial pathogens and occupational stressors, although their impact on postoperative risk remains unclear. We evaluated the association between HW status and postoperative infection and developed predictive models for infectious complications. This retrospective multicenter cohort study used a national database to identify female patients undergoing mastectomy with BR between 2010 and 2023. Patients were stratified by HW status. The primary outcome was postoperative infection. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models assessed infection-free survival and associated risk factors. Machine learning models predicted complications at 30, 60, and 90 days. Among 3115 patients, 304 (9.8%) were HWs. Overall complication (21.8%) and infection (7.4%) rates were similar between groups, with comparable infection-free survival across all time points. HWs had shorter hospital stays and fewer inpatient interventions, with a nonsignificant trend toward higher implant removal. Machine learning models showed modest discrimination, with procedural variables emerging as the strongest predictors. HW status is not an independent risk factor for infection following BR. Differences in reconstructive patterns and implant removal trends suggest that occupational factors may influence outcomes beyond infection. Predictive modeling remains limited using routine clinical data, highlighting the need for more granular variables to improve risk stratification.

title: Higher femorotibial width ratio is associated with knee injury and osteoarthritis: A UK Biobank study of 61,795 participants.
text: Soft tissue knee injury and knee osteoarthritis (KOA) are major contributors to long-term disability. Structural differences between femoral and tibial widths have been proposed as a risk factor, but population-scale evidence is limited. This study aimed to examine the associations between femorotibial width ratio (FTWR) and knee injury and KOA in a large imaging cohort. FTWR was derived for the whole knee and both medial and lateral compartments using a machine-learning pipeline applied to high-resolution knee dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans from UK Biobank. Outcomes were soft tissue knee injury, ligament injury, meniscus injury, hospital-diagnosed KOA, total knee replacement (TKR) and knee pain, identified using ICD (International Classification of Diseases) and OPCS-4 (Office of Population Censuses and Surveys Classification of Interventions and Procedures, Version 4) codes from Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) and questionnaires. Clustered logistic regression estimated associations. Odds ratios (ORs) are reported per standard deviation increase in FTWR, adjusted for age, sex, height, weight and ethnicity. Higher whole-knee FTWR was associated with increased odds of soft tissue knee injury (OR 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-1.13), ligament injury (1.07, 1.01-1.13) and meniscus injury (1.10, 1.05-1.14) in 61,795 participants. Associations were stronger for KOA outcomes, including hospital-diagnosed KOA (1.16, 1.12-1.21), TKR (1.27, 1.17-1.39) and chronic knee pain (1.08, 1.05-1.10). Medial compartment FTWR mirrored these positive associations, while lateral FTWR showed weaker inverse associations. Femorotibial width discrepancy is consistently associated with knee injury and KOA across clinical endpoints. Future work is justified to see if FTWR can serve as a scalable imaging marker of knee injury risk and provide opportunities for targeted prevention. Level III.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.
text: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.

title: Mapping the Evolution of T Cell Immunity in Coronary Heart Disease: A Bibliometric Analysis with a Focus on Inflammatory Paradigms (1991-2026).
text: Coronary heart disease (CHD) remains the leading cause of global cardiovascular mortality. T cell-mediated adaptive immunity, particularly Th1, regulatory T cell (Treg), and Th17 subsets, plays a pivotal role in atherosclerotic plaque formation and destabilisation, yet a systematic, quantitative mapping of this research landscape is lacking. Publications on T cell immunity in CHD from 1991 to August 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, restricted to English-language original articles. Bibliometric indicators were analysed with Microsoft Excel, VOSviewer (v1.6.20), CiteSpace (v6.4.R1), and bibliometric.com. Co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and burst-keyword analyses were performed. A total of 761 articles from 5,796 authors across 58 countries/regions and 299 journals were identified. Annual output increased markedly after 2010. China contributed the largest number of articles (n = 255, 33.5%), while the USA led in total citations (n = 8552), followed by China (n = 6,965) and Germany (n = 4,110). The most prolific and most highly cited author was Hansson Goran K. (14 publications; H-index = 13), while Becker AE achieved the highest average citation impact (248.0 citations per article). Circulation (IF = 35.5) was the leading journal by both article count (n = 33) and citations (n = 2,725). Keyword clustering revealed eight major research themes: clinical translation and computational approaches, T cell activation and immune cell interactions, classic immunopathology and plaque biology, inflammation and infectious triggers, Treg biology and T helper subsets, cytokine regulation and apoptosis, plaque vulnerability and ACS, and antigen presentation and extracellular vesicles. Burst analysis identified "machine learning", "monocytes", and "risk" as the most prominent emerging topics since 2023. Research on T cell immunity in CHD has grown markedly, with a clear shift toward the macrophage-T cell immune axis and immune-metabolic interactions, together with Treg-based therapeutic strategies and machine learning-assisted risk stratification. These findings provide a descriptive map that may help inform future translational research.

title: Prognostication of end-stage heart failure using a machine learning model based on haemodynamics and cardiac energetics data.
text: In the evolving landscape of heart failure treatment, clinicians face challenges in predicting which end-stage heart failure patients will require heart replacement therapies, such as left ventricular assist devices or transplantation, or are at risk of death. Traditional risk models often fail to accurately stratify patients due to complex interactions of guideline-directed medical therapy, individual responses, and haemodynamic or shock phenotypes. This study introduces a novel approach using machine learning to predict patient outcomes by analysing a comprehensive set of haemodynamic variables, including metrics tied to cardiac energetics-an emerging field focused on heart energy dynamics during failure. A dataset of 2904 patients across the spectrum of heart failure was used to train and test the models, which underwent rigorous model selection, cross-validation, and hyperparameter tuning on 70% of the data, using forward feature selection. Metrics for the remaining 30% used for testing resulted in an area under the curve of 0.81, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.35, and an accuracy of 0.74 to predict the composite endpoint of survival free from death, left ventricular assist devices, or transplant at 1 year. We also demonstrate consistency across the different patient databases used for training, validation, and testing, supported by an F1 score of 0.65 overall and 0.82 for patients who received medical management. The model shows a promising negative predictive value of 0.92, but external validation with a prospective database is needed before clinical application. This approach is novel in integrating haemodynamics and cardiac energetics with machine learning towards more individualized and effective treatment for heart failure patients.

title: Pre-Radiotherapy Risk Prediction of Grade ≥2 Radiotherapy-Induced Lymphopenia in Breast Cancer: A Single-Center Interpretable Machine Learning Study.
text: Radiotherapy-induced lymphopenia (RIL) is a clinically relevant hematologic toxicity in patients with breast cancer, yet early risk assessment before radiotherapy remains challenging because existing approaches often rely on dosimetric parameters or hematologic changes observed during treatment. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine-learning (ML) model using routinely available pre-radiotherapy clinical and laboratory variables to estimate the risk of grade ≥2 RIL in patients with breast cancer. We retrospectively studied 167 patients with breast cancer treated at Siyang Hospital between 2020 and 2025, including 56 with grade ≥2 RIL. Six predictors preselected from 20 routine pre-radiotherapy variables were used to compare seven algorithms through repeated nested fivefold cross-validation (20 repetitions; fivefold inner tuning). Performance was evaluated using patient-level mean out-of-fold predictions. The final model was interpreted using Shapley additive explanations and implemented as a research calculator. Irradiation extent and dosimetric parameters were excluded. Random forest achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.801 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.722-0.871), an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.750 (95% CI: 0.647-0.842), and a Brier score of 0.159 (95% CI: 0.128-0.193). Sensitivity was 60.7% and specificity 89.2%; this moderate sensitivity limits identification of patients who develop grade ≥2 RIL. The final model included age, absolute neutrophil count, absolute lymphocyte count, absolute monocyte count, lactate dehydrogenase, and prealbumin. This internally validated model showed moderate discrimination. Early predictor preselection may inflate performance estimates, and independent external validation is required. The calculator remains a research tool and should not guide clinical decisions.

title: Beyond covariate balance: statistical resilience of Machine Learning-Augmented Inverse Probability Weighting versus Entropy Balancing in clinical evidence translation.
text: Translating clinical trial evidence to heterogeneous community populations occupies a core mandate in modern drug lifecycle management. While Entropy Balancing (EB) is widely utilized to enforce exact covariate matching, its operational reliability under structural population separation and positivity violations remains insufficiently quantified. This study evaluates transportability inference risks using a dual-simulation framework, integrating theory-driven Monte Carlo stress tests with data-driven Plasmode architectures derived from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). We compared traditional parametric models, EB, and Machine Learning-Augmented Inverse Probability Weighting (ML-AIPW) across varying degrees of population overlap and functional non-linearity. Our results demonstrate that under severe representativeness gaps, EB achieves nominal covariate balance at the cost of a substantial 32% collapse in Effective Sample Size (ESS) and massive variance inflation with an RMSE of 1.701. This mechanical pursuit of strict distributional parity assigns extreme statistical weights to marginal clinical profiles, rendering EB estimates highly unstable and vulnerable to Type II errors. Conversely, the cross-fitted ML-AIPW framework achieved superior evaluative stability with an RMSE of 0.965 by non-parametrically mapping treatment response surfaces and utilizing cross-fitting to decouple nuisance parameter estimation from causal inference. By prioritizing the global minimization of Mean Squared Error (MSE) over superficial distributional symmetry, this architecture preserves inferential integrity even under sparse overlap conditions. These findings indicate that, under the overlap and misspecification conditions examined here, variance-aware estimation outperformed exact moment matching on total estimation error. Within this scope, EB is better suited to serving as a covariate-balance diagnostic than as a primary estimator, while ML-AIPW provided more stable point estimates under severe structural separation between trial and target populations.

title: Global Adoption of openEHR Clinical Data Repositories: A Vendor and Community Survey
text: The openEHR standard provides an open, vendor-neutral architecture for clinical data repositories (CDRs), yet its real-world deployment has not been systematically documented. We conducted a dual-perspective survey combining a vendor survey of openEHR CDR providers with a community survey of openEHR practitioners. Eleven vendor organisations reported deployments across 21 countries and over 100 institutions and health regions. A complementary community survey (n=29, 17 countries) provided context on regulatory environments, adoption drivers, and barriers. Combined, the surveys cover 28 countries, 25 of them with a reported openEHR CDR deployment. Three findings emerge: openEHR has achieved national-scale presence through two distinct channels. Through vendor-market convergence, openEHR-based systems cover the majority of regional health authorities without a national mandate, including 19 of 21 Swedish regions, 3 of 4 Norwegian health regions, and 16 of 21 Finnish wellbeing services counties. Through national health record adoption, governments have built or procured national systems on openEHR as their technical foundation, including Ireland, Malta, Greece, Slovenia, and, by community report, Iran. Across Europe, this constitutes an openEHR-based interoperability infrastructure already in place across multiple EU member states. We identified no country in which openEHR is named in binding national regulation, creating structural fragility and an unrealised opportunity for alignment with the European Health Data Space (EHDS). Second, 61% of deployments serve primary use only, and 12% support both primary and secondary use. Third, lack of openEHR-specific knowledge is the most consistent adoption barrier across all geographies and deployment tiers. Adoption is driven by practitioner need and innovation, not by regulatory mandate.

title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis
text: Background and AimsArtificial intelligence (AI) may help differentiate Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) on electrocardiograms (ECGs). We developed an ECG image-based model and evaluated whether AI assistance and visual explanations improved reader performance, overall and by reader background. MethodsA self-supervised three-architecture deep learning ensemble was developed and externally validated using 12-lead ECG images from two institutions, recorded [≤]14 days after onset regardless of reperfusion. A four-phase reader study compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and AI assistance (Phases 1-3). In Phase 4, readers were randomized to the reference sheet alone, AI predictions, or predictions with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Correctness was analyzed with generalized linear mixed-effects models. ResultsCohorts comprised 832 development and 95 external validation participants. External validation accuracy was 0.914, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.970 (95% CI, 0.938-0.992), or 0.958 using first recorded ECGs. Among 70 readers, the estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 unaided to 0.864 with AI (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference sheet (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95), and Grad-CAM added value (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25). In exploratory analyses, less experienced readers gained more; with AI, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. Mean AI-assisted reader accuracy remained below model accuracy. ConclusionsAn ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader performance, particularly with visual explanations. Experience-related differences emphasize the need for effective human-AI interaction. Seventy readers completed four phases. Phase 4 randomized readers to the reference sheet alone, with AI predictions, or with AI predictions plus Grad-CAM. Bars show mixed-model estimated probabilities of correct diagnosis (95% CI); the red dashed line indicates AI-alone accuracy on both 50-ECG sets.
