title: CNS-selective plasma p-tau217 accurately captures Alzheimer's disease pathology and progression
text: Blood-based biomarkers are transforming Alzheimers disease (AD) detection, with plasma tau phosphorylated at threonine 217 (p-tau217) being a leading candidate. However, circulating p-tau217 originates from both central nervous system (CNS) and non-CNS sources, limiting specificity. Here, we benchmark the performance of next-generation p-tau217 biomarkers that are selective for p-tau217 from predominantly CNS origin versus the conventional non-selective p-tau217. Across neuropathologically-defined, A{beta}- and tau-neuroimaging-characterized, and memory clinic cohorts, plasma brain-derived-p-tau217 (BD-p-tau217)-either alone or in ratio with brain-derived tau expressed as a percentage (BD-p-tau217%)-identified AD pathology and clinical AD with larger effect sizes, higher discriminative accuracies, and improved sensitivity and specificity, outperforming conventional alternatives. Furthermore, BD-p-tau217% and BD-p-tau217 demonstrated more robust prediction of future clinical progression up to two decades later. Importantly, diagnostic performance remained high in older adults with diabetes and cardiovascular disease, populations in which standard p-tau217 showed reduced specificity. The findings were independently replicated in a large multicenter cohort, demonstrating the robustness and generalizability of the observed improvements across clinical, imaging, and longitudinal outcomes. These results establish plasma BD-p-tau217% and BD-p-tau217 as biologically grounded and clinically robust biomarkers that advance early detection, diagnosis and prognosis of AD. One Sentence SummaryPlasma brain-derived p-tau217 and its ratio over brain-derived tau improve the specificity of the leading blood-based Alzheimers disease biomarker p-tau217.

title: Novel enzymes for amino acid biosynthesis in diverse bacteria and archaea: GapMind 2026
text: We previously described GapMind, an automated web-based tool for annotating amino acid biosynthesis pathways in bacterial and archaeal genomes. We used GapMind to identify gaps in biosynthetic pathways and systematically used comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics to identify candidate genes to fill these gaps. We confirmed the activity of ten of the proposed enzymes by using cross-species complementation assays. Highlights include a route to glycine via glyoxylate, two families that can replace phosphoserine phosphatase, an alternative N-succinyl-L,L-diaminopimelate desuccinylase, an alternative N-acetylornithine deacetylase, and a putative bifunctional MetB/MetC. We updated GapMind to include these additional enzymes. Across 208 prokaryotes that have high-quality genomes and can grow in minimal media, the average number of unexplained missing steps or gaps in amino acid biosynthesis dropped from 1.4 per genome to 0.7 per genome. The majority of remaining gaps involve the gain or loss of phosphate groups.

title: Multiparametric assessment of TNNI3 variant phenotypes in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes correlates with disease severity in patients
Mosaic ageing: from organ-specific decline to the cause of death
text: Ageing is often framed as a systemic, uniform process. However, growing evidence shows that ageing occurs unevenly across cell types, tissues and organs, generating heterogeneous within-individual trajectories. This mosaic perspective highlights the myriad cross-tissue ageing patterns that emerge from interactions among development, the genome and environmental and lifestyle exposures. The way these uneven trajectories play out may determine the emergence of specific ageing-related diseases and ultimately the cause of death. Here, we combine insights from molecular biology, biogerontology and evolutionary ecophysiology to develop an integrative view of mosaic ageing. We first describe the proximate mechanisms underlying organ-specific ageing variation. These mechanisms are moulded through age-specific natural selection, embodying trade-offs between maintenance, function and fitness. We then review tools for quantifying organ-specific ageing, ranging from classical measures such as telomere dynamics to high-resolution approaches including epigenetic, proteomic and multi-omic clocks, single-cell atlases and longitudinal imaging. Finally, we discuss how combining these tools with causal inference methods can help identify drivers of context- and species-dependent senescence and life-history variation and enable organ-targeted biomedical interventions. Overall, this perspective calls for moving beyond systemic models of ageing towards an integrative framework that places heterogeneous organ-specific processes at the centre of ageing research. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

title: DNA uptake and twitching motility are controlled by small RNA Arp through repression of pilin translation in Acinetobacter baumannii
text: Acinetobacter baumannii is a major opportunistic pathogen capable of natural transformation. This process is driven by type IV pili (T4P) facilitating horizontal gene transfer and accelerating the spread of antimicrobial resistance. While the transcriptional regulation of T4P is increasingly understood, post-transcriptional mechanisms controlling pilus assembly remain unexplored. Here, we identify and mechanistically characterise a small RNA, Arp ( Acinetobacter repressor of pilin), as a post-transcriptional repressor of T4P-mediated functions in A. baumannii . Previous proximity RNA-RNA ligation experiments using High throughput Global sRNA target Identification by Ligation and Sequencing (Hi-GRIL-seq), indicated interactions between Arp and the 5′ end of the pilA mRNA, encoding the major pilin subunit PilA. Here, in-line probing and translational reporter assays revealed that Arp represses pilA translation in A. baumannii by sequestering the Shine-Dalgarno sequence and the first seven codons of the pilA mRNA. Accordingly, deletion of arp increases DNA uptake and twitching motility, while overexpression of Arp depletes pilA mRNA from A. baumannii cells significantly impairing DNA uptake and twitching motility—two hallmark T4P-dependent phenotypes. Together, our study identifies a native A. baumannii sRNA that modulates natural competence by targeting pilin synthesis, revealing a new regulatory layer that could be exploited to disrupt horizontal gene transfer in multidrug-resistant strains.

title: Non-autonomous PMK-1/p38 MAPK signaling ensures homeostatic downregulation of germline stem cell proliferation in C. elegans
text: Stem cell underproliferation leads to tissue loss, while overproliferation can induce tumorigenesis. Stem and progenitor proliferation rates are therefore coupled to the needs for differentiated cells in the tissues they maintain, yet these homeostatic mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we used the C. elegans hermaphrodite reproductive system to understand how germline stem cell (GSC) proliferation is linked to sperm availability and oocyte usage. We designed a forward genetic screening strategy to identify germline homeostasis-defective ( ghd ) mutants that grow benign, differentiated germline tumors akin to hamartomas. We provide evidence that the TIR-1/sterile alpha and TIR-motif containing 1 (SARM1) metabolic sensor works together with the NIPI-3/TRIB1 pseudokinase to activate a canonical PMK-1/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling cascade in the somatic gonadal sheath, where it shuts down the oncogenic extracellular signal-regulated kinase MPK-1/ERK to cell non-autonomously couple GSC proliferation with oocyte needs. Similar PMK-1/p38-dependent inter-tissue signaling modules could underlie stem cell homeostasis in other systems and prevent differentiated tumors.

title: StrataChip: a microphysiological system to capture dynamic keratinocyte fate and mechanical transitions during human epidermal morphogenesis
text: Epidermal development and homeostasis require precise coordination between keratinocyte differentiation and mechanics. Still, the mechanisms integrating these processes remain poorly understood in part due to limitations of existing experimental systems. Here, we introduce StrataChip, a tractable microphysiological system that enables dynamic, multimodal interrogation of human epidermal morphogenesis. The platform integrates a media-perfused dermal tissue with human epidermal keratinocytes within a microfluidic device and supports rapid epidermal stratification following establishment of an air-liquid interface. High-resolution confocal imaging and single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrate that the StrataChip recapitulates key architectural and molecular features of the human epidermis, including distinct basal, spinous, and granular layers, as defined by canonical differentiation markers and adhesion molecule organization. Single-cell profiling reveals transcriptionally distinct basal and spinous subpopulations, including transitional states associated with suprabasal commitment. Live 3D imaging in situ captures keratinocyte morphodynamics, including basal cell delamination and asymmetric division in early stages of epidermal stratification. Altogether, StrataChip provides a robust platform that is capable of dynamic and mechanistic interrogation of how gene regulation and cellular mechanical changes are coupled during epidermal morphogenesis.

title: Evolution as fitness landscape navigation: concepts, measures, and emerging questions
text: Abstract Fitness landscapes are mappings between genotypes, phenotypes, and fitness that shape evolution. In recent years, empirical work and theoretical models have greatly advanced our understanding of how populations navigate rugged fitness landscapes. Here, we provide a timely review of the theoretical aspects of this field. Its rapidly growing literature employs a wide range of terms, which are sometimes used ambiguously or inconsistently. We therefore begin by defining the major concepts and the field’s vocabulary, highlighting our own terminology choices wherever needed. We then review key results on the relationships between epistasis, ruggedness, accessibility, and navigability for genotype–fitness maps, highlighting several complex and sometimes counterintuitive connections that have emerged. Further, we review how the conserved structural properties of the underlying genotype–phenotype map, which can lead to the formation of large connected neutral networks of genotypes, influence dynamics on fitness landscapes. We then compare the two levels to study landscape navigation: the level of genotype–phenotype maps and the level of genotype–fitness maps. Our review leads us to propose a new measure of navigability, based on evolutionary outcomes, which is broadly applicable and overcomes limitations of existing measures. Finally, we highlight examples from the smaller body of work that relaxes the common assumption of fitness-monotonic paths on static landscapes, and discuss how this can fundamentally change the nature of fitness landscape navigation. Throughout the review, we identify directions for future work to fill existing gaps and to synthesize the disparate strands of research within the field.

title: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
text: Abstract Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.

title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function
text: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

title: Chemical characterization, antibacterial activity, in vitro cytotoxicity, and selectivity of the lipid extract from Sargassum filipendula against multidrug-resistant bacteria
text: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria necessitates new therapeutic alternatives, and marine macroalgae represent an underexplored source of bioactive lipids. This study characterized the lipid extract (LE) of Sargassum filipendula and evaluated its antibacterial and cytotoxic profiles against MDR hospital isolates. LE composition was determined by GC-MS, and its thermal behavior by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the broth microdilution method (CLSI M07) against Acinetobacter baumannii , Escherichia coli , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Staphylococcus aureus , and coagulase-negative staphylococci, followed by determination of the minimum bactericidal concentration. Cytotoxicity was assessed in L929 and MDBK cell lines using MTT, Neutral Red, and Lactate Dehydrogenase assays; Hemolytic activity was evaluated using erythrocytes; and selectivity indices (SI) were calculated for each bacterial species. Palmitic acid (61.07%) and oleic acid (15.90%) were the predominant fatty acids. TGA revealed a total mass loss of 82% across two decomposition stages (296°C, 445°C), and DSC detected no phase transitions, indicating the absence of amorphous or crystalline domains. The LE exhibited bacteriostatic activity against all isolates, with MIC values ranging from 1.18 mg/mL ( S. aureus ) to 2.5 mg/mL ( P. aeruginosa ). Cytotoxicity assays yielded IC 50 values ranging from 0.16 to 1.25 mg/mL, and the hemolytic IC 50 was 12.81 mg/mL. However, the SI values remained below the safety threshold for all tested species (1.45–3.90). The S. filipendula LE is a candidate source of antibacterial compounds against MDR bacteria, although purification processes and in vivo validation are required to establish its therapeutic potential.

title: B7-H3-targeted natural killer cells are effective against atypical teratoid / rhabdoid tumors and extend survival in orthotopic xenografts
text: BACKGROUND: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumors (ATRTs) are the most common malignant CNS tumor in infants, and patients suffer from low survival rates and treatment-related morbidities. These tumors frequently overexpress the pan-cancer antigen B7-H3 (CD276), which can be targeted with immunotherapy. We hypothesized that adding a B7-H3-targeting cytotoxic chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) to NK cells can enhance killing against ATRTs. METHODS: We designed a library of variable affinity B7-H3-targeted CARs, which were transduced into primary healthy donor-derived NK cells. We verified B7-H3 expression in a panel of ATRT cell lines and further engineered luciferase and nuclear GFP-expressing ATRT (CHLA-04, CHLA-06, BT12, BT37) as well as a CHLA-06-derived B7-H3 knockout. We tested CAR-NK cell functionality using in vitro co-culture cytotoxicity assays. We delivered anti-B7-H3 CAR-NK cells intratumorally or intracerebroventricularly (ICV) to ATRT orthotopic xenografts and monitored for tumor growth and animal survival. RESULTS: B7-H3-targeted CAR-NK cells demonstrated target-specific cytotoxicity when compared to unmodified NK cells. Knockout of B7-H3 in target cells abolished the increased CAR-mediated target killing. When delivered intratumorally to CHLA-06 orthotopic xenograft-bearing mice, anti-B7-H3 CAR-NK cells eliminated tumor cells and prolonged survival. When CAR-NK cells were delivered ICV against a CNS disseminated tumor model of BT12, treated mice had significantly improved survival. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-B7-H3 CAR-NK cells effectively kill ATRTs in multiple pre-clinical in vitro and in vivo models in an antigen-specific manner. Evidence of efficacy in translationally relevant models provides support for using B7-H3-targeting CAR-NK cells in high-risk ATRT patients.

title: Digital twins for intelligent intersections: A literature review
text: Intelligent intersections play a pivotal role in urban mobility, demanding innovative solutions such as digital twins to enhance safety and efficiency. This literature review investigates the integration and application of digital twins for intelligent intersections, a critical area within smart urban traffic systems. The review systematically categorizes existing research into five key thematic areas: (i) Digital Twin Architectures and Frameworks; (ii) Data Processing and Simulation Techniques; (iii) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Adaptive Traffic Control; (iv) Safety and Protection of Vulnerable Road Users; and (v) Scaling from Localized Intersections to Citywide Traffic Networks. Each theme is explored comprehensively, highlighting significant advancements, current challenges, and critical insights. The findings reveal that multi-layered digital twin architectures incorporating real-time data fusion and AI-driven decision-making enhances traffic efficiency and safety. Advanced simulation techniques combined with sophisticated AI/ML algorithms demonstrate notable improvements in real-time responsiveness and predictive accuracy for traffic management. Additionally, the integration of digital twins has shown substantial promise in safeguarding vulnerable road users through proactive and adaptive safety strategies. Despite these advancements, key challenges persist, including interoperability of diverse data sources, scalability of digital twins for extensive traffic networks, and managing uncertainty within dynamic urban environments. Addressing these challenges will be essential for the future development and deployment of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable intersection management systems.

title: Safety in numbers: Tackling the deliberative, performative, and infrastructural roots of multi‐agent misalignment
text: Abstract Multi‐agent systems (MAS)—a uniquely important subset of the wider field commonly called “Agentic AI”—enable complex work processes involving distributed networks of multiple AIs, people, and technology tools. However, they also carry big risks. Root causes of catastrophic safety failures in multi‐agent collaboration (as in human collaboration) can be classed into three overlapping categories: 1. Deliberative —deviating from shared MAS commitments to fulfill explicitly expressed joint intentions; 2. Performative —inability to coordinate well or to adapt to changing circumstances; and 3. Infrastructural —safety, reliability, and trust in the operating environment. In the spirit of the international Multi‐Agent System Safety and Teamwork (MASST) initiative (Bradshaw et al., 2026), our multi‐disciplinary research team seeks to tackle the root causes of these three challenges through development, experimentation, and deployment of an integrated multi‐layered safety pipeline, enabling “safety in numbers” as increasingly powerful multi‐agent systems are deployed. Although this proposal is merely an initial sketch, it is our hope that sharing these ideas will inspire others to contribute to the discussion as we continue moving forward. We look forward not only to exciting discoveries within laboratory settings while also being committed to improving safe rollout of large‐scale MAS into the world to perform work in high‐consequence applications.

title: User Understanding of Robot Learning Evaluations through Task Success Rates and Beyond
text: Robot Foundation Models (RFMs) and related robot learning techniques represent a promising approach to developing general-purpose home robots. Given the broad capabilities of RFMs, users will inevitably ask an RFM-based robot to perform tasks that the RFM was not trained or evaluated on. In these cases, it is crucial that users understand the risks associated with attempting novel tasks due to the relatively high cost of failure. Furthermore, an informed user who understands an RFM’s capabilities will know what situations and tasks the robot can handle. In this paper, we study how non-experts interpret performance information from RFM and similar robot learning evaluations. These evaluations typically report task success rate (TSR) as the primary performance metric. While TSR is intuitive to experts, it is necessary to validate whether novices also use this information as intended. Toward this end, we conducted a study in which users saw real evaluation data, including TSR, failure case descriptions, and videos from multiple published robot learning projects. The results highlight that non-experts use TSR in a manner consistent with expert expectations and highly value other information types, such as failure cases that are not often reported in RFM evaluations. Furthermore, we find that users want access to both real data from previous evaluations of the RFM and estimates from the robot about how well it will do on a novel task.

title: AssemPlanner: a multi-agent based task planning framework for flexible assembly system
A human‐in‐the‐loop Bayesian optimization framework for constraint‐aware bioprocess development
text: Abstract We present Pareto Front Guided Sampling (PFGS), a human‐in‐the‐loop (HiL) Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework that reformulates surrogate‐model predictions as a multi‐objective optimization problem, allowing domain knowledge to be added intuitively to any BO problem. PFGS addresses constrained optimization by treating the posterior probability of constraint satisfaction as an explicit Pareto objective, and robust optimization via a Monte Carlo estimate of expected lower‐confidence performance under input perturbations, capturing likely degradation. The multi‐dimensional Pareto front makes trade‐offs between predicted performance, model uncertainty, constraint satisfaction, and robustness visible through pairwise two‐dimensional projections on an interactive dashboard, allowing selection criteria to be refined as the model and objectives evolve. The framework is showcased on a eight‐dimensional in‐silico fed‐batch Chinese Hamster Ovary cell culture case study. We showed improved performance over BO when the expert has perfect domain knowledge; however, PFGS is not designed to outperform BO, but rather to present a HiL acquisition function framework.

title: Unravelling groundwater's role in soil-plant-atmosphere continuum: integrated ecohydrological modelling approach using STEMMUS-SCOPE and MODFLOW 6
text: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum (SPAC) models are commonly used to investigate various components' role(s) in ecosystem functioning. Yet, in most SPAC models, groundwater is ignored or at best represented in an over-simplified manner, leading to misunderstanding of its critical role in simulating soil-vegetation dynamics. This study investigates groundwater's role in SPAC processes, in particular, the impacts of groundwater component (mass and energy) on: (1) regulating the soil profile, in terms of moisture and temperature; (2) the dynamics of the unsaturated/saturated zones and their further impact on water fluxes; and (3) the carbon fluxes and vegetation physiological processes (i.e. root water uptake and photosynthesis reflected by fluorescence). To address this, an integrated ecohydrological modelling (IEM) framework is developed by coupling the STEMMUS-SCOPE SPAC model with the MODFLOW 6 integrated hydrological model. The standalone STEMMUS-SCOPE (ST-SC) and the coupled STEMMUS-SCOPE-MODFLOW 6 (ST-SC-MF6) models were applied over an 8-year period (1 April 2016–31 March 2024) to three sites in the Netherlands (Loobos, Cabauw and Veenkampen). Various essential variables, including soil moisture ( θ ), soil temperature ( T s ), groundwater level (GWL), groundwater temperature (GT), evapotranspiration (ET), gross primary productivity (GPP), net ecosystem exchange (NEE), and sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) were simulated and then compared to corresponding in-situ observations. Performance of both ST-SC and ST-SC-MF6 was evaluated using the Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) and the root mean square error (RMSE) metrics. Results indicated that the groundwater contribution is spatially and temporally variable. The ST-SC-MF6 model showed better agreement with observations than the ST-SC, improving the KGE values for: (a) θ (+0.29), T s (+0.19), and ET (+0.35) at Loobos, (b) θ (+0.30), T s (+0.14), NEE (+0.18), and SIF (+0.15) at Cabauw, and (c) θ (+0.21) and ET (+0.15) at Veenkampen. Notably, benefits of ST-SC-MF6 simulation were particularly prominent during both wet and dry periods, i.e. improving the representation of: (a) the θ dynamics during wet conditions, when hydraulic connectivity between the phreatic surface and the unsaturated zone is strong; (b) the root water uptake and carbon assimilation during dry periods, when shallow groundwater mitigated vegetative water stress; and (c) the T s dynamics during both wet and dry periods, influenced by both GT and GWL, and further propagated to other T s -dependent processes/variables such as canopy temperature. Overall, the proposed ST-SC-MF6 IEM helped to: (1) incorporate groundwater as a key component of the water, energy and carbon cycles; and (2) define the important role groundwater dynamics plays in the SPAC for deepening the understanding of ecosystem functioning.

title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
text: Abstract High-numerical-aperture (NA) oblique plane microscopy enables noninvasive fluorescence imaging of subcellular dynamics without radical sample modification. However, performance degrades at depth in multicellular specimens as scattering and refractive-index heterogeneity raise out-of-focus background. We report a two-photon oblique plane microscope that improves resolution at depth by combining high-NA single-objective detection with multiphoton plane illumination. The microscope achieves ~ 300 nm lateral and ~ 650 nm axial resolution, with single-molecule sensitivity and < 60 nm localization precision in vivo. Compared with two-photon point scanning, the lower illumination NA delivers order-of-magnitude lower peak intensity, enabling > 5 × faster volumetric acquisition (up to 3.25 × 10 6 voxels s −1 ). In multicellular contexts, near-infrared nonlinear excitation enhances contrast throughout the illumination depth by ~ 2 × and restores volumetric resolving power by > 2 × relative to linear excitation. We demonstrate these capabilities through molecular imaging of epithelial tissue, stem-cell-derived gastruloids, and living fruit fly embryos, including multicolor transcription-factor dynamics, optogenetic subcellular control, and single-mRNA tracking, all using standard glass-based mounting.

title: A dual-modal fiducial marker with single-view x-ray pose recoverability for MR-guided surgical navigation
text: Abstract In orthopedic surgery, accurate intraoperative localization of implants and instruments is essential. Traditional surgical navigation markers rely on a fixed external reference frame, but in mixed reality (MR) surgical navigation the tracking camera moves with the surgeon’s head, making conventional markers unsuitable. This study proposes that markers for MR navigation must satisfy three design constraints: omnidirectional recognizability, X-ray recognizability, and dual-modal compatibility. Based on these constraints, we designed a marker consisting of a central cube and four cylindrical axes with unequal diameters, and proved analytically that its six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) pose can be determined from a single X-ray image. A pose estimation algorithm combining geometric optimization and deep learning-based feature extraction was used to validate dual-modal pose estimation, in which the marker pose is estimated independently from a single X-ray or optical image. On 100 X-ray and 194 optical images, the X-ray recognition error was 1.58° ± 1.26° (coronal plane) and 1.90° ± 1.50° (sagittal plane), with 94% of samples achieving a composite angular error below 5°; the optical recognition success rate was 90.2%, with an overall angular error of 1.52° ± 0.98°. Error distributions were symmetric and zero-centered (signed means within ± 0.02°); X-ray pose estimation remained solvable even at extreme sagittal tilt (up to ~ 40°), while rare optical failures (2.3%) could be reliably detected. These results provide preliminary evidence of dual-modal marker pose estimation from single-view X-ray and optical images; further validation is required before clinical translation.

title: Review of Machine Learning Approaches for Leaf Disease Detection in Rice Crop: Trends, Challenges, and Future Opportunities
text: Rice leaf disease is of important concern in developing countries, especially when the livelihood of a major population is dependent on agronomy. Rice is considered a staple crop in South Asian countries, foliar pathogens in rice cause substantial yield loss and economical burden. This review systematically examines the evolution of machine learning and state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for the detection of rice leaf disease. Unlike studies concentrated only on model performance, this review focused on the complete pipeline - spanning challenges observed during image acquisition, preprocessing steps, data characterization, features representation, classification methodology used, along with misused evaluation metrics leading to unsuccessful real-world deployment. This literature reveals a clear paradigm shift from handcrafted feature-based machine learning systems to deep learning architectures, because of their consistently high accuracy, learning discriminative representations directly from raw images without any human intervention. This review also highlights the growing demand for lightweight models for smarter IoT deployments. Overall evidence indicates that the future of automatic rice leaf detection depends on creating standardized benchmark datasets, robust cross-domain validation, and collaborating with smart agriculture frameworks combined with cognitive computer vision and domain adaptive learning, which are capable of accurate disease diagnosis under diverse field conditions.

title: Bio-inspired Self-Healing Concrete for Sustainable Structures: A Critical Review
text: Cracks provide pathways for water, chlorides, sulfates, and carbon dioxide to penetrate reinforced concrete, while conventional crack repairs are often costly, disruptive, and environmentally burdensome. Bio-inspired self-healing concrete incorporates bacteria, enzymes, fungi, or vascular networks to promote autonomous crack sealing and extend service life. This critical review addresses four research questions: (i) how bio-inspired healing compares with autogenous and non-biological engineered healing; (ii) how biological-agent selection, encapsulation and mix design influence trade-offs among healing performance, mechanical properties and cost; (iii) how reliable and comparable laboratory and field evidence is; and (iv) under which conditions self-healing concrete provides environmental and economic benefits. Literature retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science was screened using predefined criteria and critically synthesised, with emphasis on experimental and field evidence. Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) generally seals cracks 0.3-0.5 mm wide, although laboratory studies report closure of cracks up to 0.8-0.97 mm and reductions in water permeability exceeding 90%. However, healing-agent production can increase embodied carbon by 36% per m³ in one recent assessment. Environmental benefits therefore depend on achieved service-life extension, avoided repairs and targeted application. Reported life-cycle benefits range from approximately 12% to 75%, depending on assessment boundaries and assumptions. Major limitations include non-standardised testing, uncertain long-term bacterial viability and repeated-healing capacity, limited field evidence and regulatory uncertainty. Research priorities include standardised testing, long-term field monitoring, hybrid healing systems, predictive modelling and engineered living materials.

title: Technology-value symbiosis in digital values education: a conceptual framework for talent development
text: The digital and intelligent transformation of productive forces is changing the skills and ethical responsibilities expected of workers and creating new challenges for values education in Chinese higher education. Yet current practice often separates technology from values: instrumental uses of technology expand while value guidance is weakened. This study develops a conceptual framework based on the Marxist philosophy of technology. Its central contribution is the idea of technology-value symbiosis, presented as a double-helix framework. One helix traces technological development through data, algorithms, and immersive scenarios; the other traces value guidance through anchoring, goal alignment, and ethical constraint. Their interaction supports precise matching of educational supply and demand and embeds ethical regulation in value formation. These mechanisms work by reconstructing learner subjectivity to foster value identification, critical thinking, and digital competence, and to build longer-term capabilities. The framework also identifies four risks of imbalance: eroded subjectivity, diluted content and meaning, emotional superficiality, and value displacement. It responds with governance pathways addressing conceptual, methodological, ethical, and value-related concerns, six testable propositions, and an actor-based governance matrix. The main implication is that digital values education should be designed with technology and value guidance jointly, rather than treating technology as a neutral tool. The framework thus offers educators and policymakers a conceptual basis for pursuing digital innovation while safeguarding ethical and value-oriented education.

title: Where DNA data storage loses its bits
text: Abstract DNA data storage is judged by bits stored per synthesized nucleotide, yet it is rarely known where an experiment loses the bits it does not store. Here we fit position-dependent insertion–deletion–substitution channels to the raw reads of 17 public datasets, prove capacity bounds for them and measure information rates on the reads. A model-based accounting indicates that sampling dominates the losses of low-error array pools read by Illumina: at low sequencing depth, unread strands, uneven coverage and indexing cost 0.2–0.35 bits per nucleotide, against less than 0.01 for sequence errors. Error-prone chemistries leave 0.04–0.26 bits between genie information and achieved rates, and designs that forbid repeated bases cap density at 1.59 bits per nucleotide. In a prespecified, paired test on fresh files, an iterative soft receiver with sparse pilot bases needed 7–42% fewer reads than Trellis BMA, the best published method, on eight of nine datasets. The released software places any dataset against its own losses.

title: Artificial Intelligence in EGFR-mutated NSCLC: Reframing the Therapeutic and Biological Landscape
text: Despite advances in targeted therapy, acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a major challenge in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), owing to its biological heterogeneity, temporal evolution, and increasing therapeutic complexity. This narrative review critically examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to integrate clinical, molecular, imaging, and pharmacological data across the osimertinib treatment trajectory, with particular emphasis on resistance monitoring and clinical pharmacology. We discuss natural language processing for clinical data extraction and pharmacovigilance; digital pathology, radiomics, and multimodal learning for molecular pre-screening and risk stratification; longitudinal circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) modelling; and emerging applications of synthetic data, generative simulation, and digital twins. We also explore opportunities to integrate machine learning with pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling, exposure–response analyses, therapeutic drug monitoring, and model-informed precision dosing. Although selected AI approaches have demonstrated promising performance in retrospective studies and external or prospective silent evaluations, their ability to identify specific acquired resistance mechanisms and improve clinical outcomes through model-guided interventions remains unproven. Experience from other solid tumours provides methodological precedents, but disease-specific validation is required. Future progress will depend on multicentre longitudinal datasets integrating drug exposure, molecular evolution, treatment-related toxicity, and clinical outcomes, together with rigorous prospective evaluation. AI may complement established pharmacometric approaches to support more individualized, biologically informed treatment strategies in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

title: Beyond Conventional Culture: Integrating Rapid Molecular Diagnostics, Proteomic Technologies and Artificial Intelligence for Pathogen Identification in Clinical Microbiology
text: This research aims to optimize in vitro propagation techniques for ginger (Zingiber officinale Rosc.) by investigating the effects of plant growth regulators (PGRs) on shoot induction, root formation, and callus proliferation. Ginger is an economically valuable crop with medicinal, culinary, and industrial applications, but its conventional propagation through rhizomes is slow, prone to disease, and limits large-scale production, necessitating improved tissue culture techniques. The highest shoot induction (4.9 shoots) occurred at 3.0 mg·L⁻¹ BAP, while optimal shoot length (5.9 cm) was observed at 2.0 mg·L⁻¹ BAP. Root induction was most effective at 3.0 mg·L⁻¹ IAA, producing the highest root count (7.1), with the longest root length (5.3 cm) achieved at 4.0 mg·L⁻¹ IAA. Callus formation was optimized using 1.0 mg·L⁻¹ 2,4-D combined with 0.5 mg·L⁻¹ Kinetin and 0.750 mg·L⁻¹ IAA, leading to the quickest callus initiation (10 days), highest fresh weight (3.5 g), and largest diameter (2.3 cm). Acclimatization trials demonstrated high survival rates, with 93% in the growth chamber, 78% in the shade house, and 81% in open conditions. This study provides an efficient and reproducible tissue culture protocol for the mass production of disease-free, genetically uniform ginger plants, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional propagation methods and significantly improving cultivation practices, ensuring higher yields, better plant quality, and increased availability of superior planting material for agricultural and commercial applications.

title: PPanGGOLiN V2: technical enhancement and extended functionalities for prokaryotic pangenome analysis
text: The exponential growth of genomic data, particularly for microbes, has made pangenomic approaches a gold standard for large-scale comparative genomics. By capturing the full genomic diversity of a species rather than relying on a single reference, pangenomics has transformed microbial genomics, revealing the adaptive potential of bacteria and the evolutionary dynamics underlying functional diversity. Among available tools, PPanGGOLiN distinguishes itself through its graph-based model coupled with statistical gene partitioning. Here we present PPanGGOLiN v2, which introduces substantial improvements across three dimensions: new analytical features that expand what users can investigate, a comprehensive software architecture redesign that improves maintainability and extensibility, and performance improvements that address the computational demands of ever-growing genomic datasets.

title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention
text: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language model pre-trained on structural data, with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a cross-chain attention mechanism and a contact supervision head. Our method can detect both binding interfaces and pairwise contact matrices. We trained our model on very large datasets of non-redundant protein-protein pairs derived from the PPInterface dataset, the most comprehensive structural protein-protein database to date, and evaluated it on systematically filtered benchmarks at four redundancy thresholds (30%–90% sequence identity). We demonstrate that sequence redundancy inflates reported AUROC by up to 0.079 and MCC by up to 0.145 on identical models, representing a substantial methodological confound in the field. Even at 30% redundancy threshold, our results (AUROC = 0.811, MCC = 0.367, F1 = 0.45) exceed the best published sequence-only result on this convention. Our method also achieves comparable performance to existing partner-specific methods that use explicit structural information. The comprehensive training and evaluation dataset, in addition to the systematic redundancy inflation, can help gain insight into protein-protein interactions and the abilities and limitations of current detection methods.

title: Cloud computing for clinical next-generation sequencing testing
Comparative assessment of bacterial diversity in small water bodies of the Eastern Pamir mountains using amplicon-based and metagenomic approaches
text: Microbial diversity in remote extreme environments remains poorly understood. We investigated sediment microbial communities in small water bodies of the Eastern Pamir cold desert using V3–V4 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomics, to assess taxonomic and functional diversity. Amplicon data showed high Pseudomonadota abundance and taxa overlooked in the 2019 analysis, including Vampirovibrionaceae. Reanalysis of the amplicon data increased taxonomic assessment from 54% to 93% without changes in the number of unique sequences. Comparison of amplicon and metagenome-derived 16S profiles revealed limited overlap: only 15% of metagenomic V3–V4 sequences were detected in amplicons. Fourteen of 37 phyla were exclusive to ASVs, whereas three (of 20) to MAGs. Metagenomics recovered 86 MAGs spanning 26 classes, predominantly from Bacteroidota. Sulfur oxidation and sulfate reduction pathways occurred mainly in Pseudomonadota. Phototrophic potential was identified in 25 MAGs, largely Bacteroidota and established phototrophic lineages; most possessed complete nitrogen-fixation pathways. Eight genera detected with all methods belonged to halophilic or halotolerant lineages. These findings highlight salinity as an important driver of bacterial community composition in Eastern Pamir benthic communities and identify differences between methods. Integrating amplicon sequencing and metagenomics provides complementary insights into microbial diversity and metabolic potential in remote extreme environments.

title: Ericoid mycorrhizal fungi recover from nitrogen additions in a dry heathland experiment in southern England
text: 1. Ericoid mycorrhizal fungi are fundamental for heathlands’ establishment and functioning and contribute to the essential ecosystem services these endangered habitats provide, yet they are overlooked by environmental monitoring policies. As nitrogen pollution declines across Europe, policymakers need measurable indicators of habitat recovery encompassing above- and below-ground parts of the ecosystem. 2. We conducted a manipulation experiment simulating atmospheric nitrogen pollution on pioneer and mature heather (Calluna vulgaris) stands in a dry heathland to determine its impact on the functionality and composition of ericoid mycorrhizal communities, and to assess their viability as short-term recovery indicators in three substrates: heather roots, a common leafy liverwort (Cephaloziella divaricata), and soil. Additionally, we measured aboveground liverwort biomass, rhizoid colonisation and density, soil and heather leaf chemistry. 3. After an initial negative impact of nitrogen fertilisation, ericoid mycorrhizal colonisation in heather roots, ericoid mycorrhizal fungi of the genus Hyaloscypha in roots and soil, and symbiotic Pezoloma in liverworts, all recovered within seven months. Liverwort biomass, density and rhizoid colonisation were negatively affected, and did not recover. 4. The effect of nitrogen fertilisation and recovery trajectories depended on substrate, age of heather stands, and ericoid mycorrhizal morphotype and taxon. Pioneer plants were more sensitive to treatments than mature plants. 5. Policy implications: Our findings open new perspectives on the potential use of mycorrhizal fungi as indicators of recovery from nitrogen pollution in heathlands. The rapid recovery observed in pioneer heather communities suggests that ericoid mycorrhizal fungi can provide short-term measures of belowground recovery, but plant successional stage and fungal identity must be considered. Our results support the development of targeted and stage-specific belowground indicators to complement existing aboveground-focussed indicators, to improve assessment of recovery from nitrogen pollution in heathland conservation and restoration policy.

title: FGTD: a desktop application for GEO dataset discovery with sample-level metadata extraction and local semantic relevance scoring
text: Abstract The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) contains a large amount of reusable functional genomics data, but finding the series relevant to a biological question still requires the manual screening of heterogeneous metadata and linked publications. We present FGTD (From GEO To Dataset), a desktop application that automates the retrieval, filtering and ranking of GEO series and associated publications. FGTD organizes the extracted metadata, down to the sample level, in one table, reconstructing links to the Sequence Read Archive and BioProject, and ranks the series with a score that combines semantic similarity (computed locally with sentence embeddings), keyword and Medical Subject Headings matches, and citation and recency metrics. In a breast cancer case study FGTD produced the metadata table of 15 series in about 38 seconds, while manual curation (timed on two series and extrapolated to the cohort) was estimated at about 3.8 hours. In known-item evaluations on two published meta-analyses, FGTD ranked the reference series closer to the top than the date-ordered GEO listing (mean reciprocal rank 0.571 versus 0.020), although the gain depended on the keywords supplied, and its semantic component alone and its fusion with a lexical baseline performed at least as well. FGTD is freely available at https://github.com/SorenKK/FGTD.

title: An interactive spatio-temporal task computing framework with incremental graph reconstruction for remote sensing cloud platforms
text: In cloud-based environments, remote sensing computing platforms typically rely on executable scripts to orchestrate the invocation of spatio-temporal operators, thereby supporting the solution of geoscientific problems. However, existing task orchestration paradigms are primarily oriented toward monolithic end-to-end modeling, making it difficult to meet the requirements of scientific Workflow Management Systems (WfMS) for staged workflow construction, modular management, and iterative optimization. Moreover, in interactive analysis scenarios, repeatedly executed workflows with similar structures often lack effective reuse mechanisms, resulting in substantial redundancy in cloud computing resource consumption. To address these challenges, this study proposes an interactive spatio-temporal task computing framework tailored with an incremental computation approach based on graph reconstruction. We formally represent and dynamically construct spatiotemporal tasks using graph structures, then track the evolution of workflows during the spatiotemporal task modeling, and analyze the topological differences and dependencies between successive task versions. This enables us to systematically identify change operations and potential reuse opportunities during interactive orchestration, ultimately supporting fine-grained incremental computation. The proposed framework and methodology have been implemented on the Open Geospatial Engine (OGE) platform. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently reduces computational redundancy and execution time across different remote sensing tasks and data scales compared with conventional cloud-based geoprocessing workflows.

title: Aging reprograms the functional, epigenetic, and metabolic landscape of macrophages
text: Immuno-senescence is a dominant risk factor of chronic diseases, yet the impact of aging on macrophages remains understudied, despite their involvement in age-related conditions. Here, we examine bone marrow-derived macrophage aging by integrating transcriptomic and functional analyses across the lifespan. Besides aging hallmarks, we observed progressive changes in macrophages, including reduced responsiveness to both inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cues and an imbalanced secretory profile. This age-driven remodeling is reflected by changes in the expression of epigenetic regulators, particularly histone-modifying genes, alongside coordinated gene expression shifts toward lipid activation and trafficking at the expense of mitochondrial redox programs. Strikingly, these alterations differ between M1- and M2-like macrophages, indicating phenotype-specific aging trajectories. Functionally, aged macrophages exhibit enhanced phagocytic capacity against tumor cells, diminished migratory ability, and preserved antigen presentation. Together, our findings establish that aging drives an active transcriptomic reprogramming in bone marrow-derived macrophages, providing a framework to address inflammaging and age-associated diseases.

title: Next generation gene based therapeutics for cancer treatment and immune modulation
text: Recent advances in molecular biology, genetic engineering, and biotechnology have accelerated the development of next-generation gene-based therapeutic platforms in oncology. Despite substantial progress in conventional and targeted treatments, limited response durability, therapeutic resistance, and tumor heterogeneity continue to drive the need for more precise, programmable, and personalized therapeutic strategies. In this review, prominent current gene-based therapeutic approaches in the field of cancer treatment and immune modulation have been comprehensively evaluated. In particular, the potential of CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing technologies, RNA-based biotechnological platforms, mRNA and RNA interference (RNAi)-based therapies, and genetically modified immune cell approaches in cancer treatment has been discussed. In addition, the roles of CAR-T and CAR-NK cell engineering, macrophage reprogramming strategies and RNA-mediated immune reprogramming approaches in regulating the tumour microenvironment and enhancing the anti-tumour immune response have been examined. The combination of gene editing technologies, RNA biotechnologies and immune cell engineering is making significant contributions to the development of more targeted, effective and personalised approaches to cancer treatment. Unlike previous reviews that primarily discuss these technologies separately, this review provides a critical comparative evaluation of genome editing, RNA-based therapeutics and engineered immune-cell platforms with respect to their mechanisms, clinical maturity, delivery strategies, safety profiles and translational potential. This integrated perspective highlights complementary therapeutic opportunities and identifies current challenges that must be addressed for the successful implementation of precision oncology.

title: Immunosuppression as a hypothesized central pathological hub in andrological diseases: a hypothesis-generating framework
text: Male reproductive health disorders-including chronic prostatitis (CP), infertility, and genitourinary malignancies-are increasingly understood as resulting from sustained immune imbalance. While physiological immunosuppression is essential for maintaining immune privilege and reproductive function, its pathological dysregulation is an underestimated contributor to disease. Moving beyond the traditional view of immunosuppression as a mere bystander, this framework proposes it as a common and actionable hypothesized central pathological hub across the spectrum of andrological diseases. We synthesize evidence for how dysregulated immunosuppressive networks-including expanded regulatory T cells(Tregs), activated checkpoint pathways, immunometabolic reprogramming, and epigenetic modifications-shift from maintaining protective homeostasis to promoting chronic inflammation, tissue fibrosis, and tumor immune evasion. Importantly, this unified framework uncovers shared mechanistic foundations that connect inflammatory, dysfunctional, and neoplastic conditions of the male reproductive tract. From a translational perspective, we highlight emerging immunotherapeutic strategies-such as checkpoint inhibitors, metabolic modulators, and epigenetic drugs-that target this central hub. By reconceptualizing immunosuppression as a hypothesized central pathological hub, this framework suggests that (1) the transition from physiological protection to pathological promotion may be driven by chronic metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming; (2) shared checkpoint, metabolic, and cellular mechanisms may operate across CP/CPPS, male infertility, and genitourinary malignancies; and (3) therapeutic recalibration without disrupting testicular privilege may be achievable in principle, but remains unproven. This framework is proposed as a testable hypothesis, not a concluded model.

title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes attenuate fibrotic stricture remodeling through the let-7i -5p/TGFBR1 axis
text: Introduction Urethral stricture is a common and debilitating urological condition in which fibrosis narrows the urethral lumen. Recurrence after surgical repair is frequent, and no antifibrotic pharmacotherapy has been established. Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) show antifibrotic activity in several organ systems, but whether they act in urethral fibrosis, and by what mechanism, had not been examined. Methods We isolated and characterized hUC-MSC-EVs and tested them in primary human urethral fibroblasts (UFBs) stimulated with TGF-β1 and in a rat model of trauma-induced urethral stricture. Small RNA sequencing was used to profile the EV miRNA cargo, and the role of let-7i-5p was examined by gain- and loss-of-function experiments, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and let-7i-5p-depleted EVs (KD EVs), both in vitro and in vitro . Results hUC-MSC-EVs dose-dependently suppressed TGF-β1-induced UFB proliferation, migration and myofibroblast differentiation and lowered α-SMA and Collagen I expression, with reduced Smad2/3 phosphorylation. Periurethral injection in rats significantly reduced urethral wall hyperechogenicity, luminal narrowing, submucosal collagen deposition and profibrotic protein expression at the 4-week postoperative endpoint. Small RNA sequencing placed let-7i-5p among the most abundant miRNAs packaged in hUC-MSC-EVs, and this miRNA was efficiently transferred to recipient UFBs. let-7i-5p bound the 3′-UTR of TGFBR1 and suppressed TGFBR1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels. Depleting let-7i-5p from EVs with an inhibitor largely abolished their antifibrotic activity in vitro and in vitro , linking EV-delivered let-7i-5p to suppression of the TGFBR1/Smad2/3 signaling axis. Conclusion These results identify hUC-MSC-EVs as an injectable, cell-free antifibrotic candidate for urethral stricture and let-7i-5p as a cargo on which their activity depends.

title: Editorial: Innovative paths in targeted drug delivery: advances in precision and control
text: The Research Topic "Innovative Paths in Targeted Drug Delivery: Advances in Precision and Control" brings together four complementary contributions that illustrate this transition. Rather than representing a single technological pathway, the collection spans precision nanomedicine, smart biomaterials, programmable protein polymers for radiopharmaceutical delivery, and stabilized outer membrane vesicle (OMV) vaccine films. Together, these studies demonstrate that precision can be engineered through different mechanisms, but that meaningful translation ultimately depends on the same fundamentals: measurable control, biological relevance, reproducibility, safety, and practical manufacturability.Precision nanomedicine provides the broadest framework for this emerging paradigm. Sureshkumar and Balu 2026 review recent preclinical advances across lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, biomimetic, and hybrid nanocarriers. Importantly, their analysis moves beyond the traditional distinction between passive and active targeting and emphasizes spatial, temporal, cellular, and organelle-level control. Ligand-mediated targeting, stimuli-responsive release, multilevel targeting, combination therapy, and theranostic functionality are increasingly being integrated into single delivery systems. At the same time, the review highlights an important translational reality: greater engineering complexity does not automatically produce greater clinical benefit. The enhanced permeability and retention effect remains heterogeneous, active targeting depends on receptor availability and accessibility, and subcellular targeting introduces additional biological and manufacturing variables. These limitations underscore the need to evaluate nanocarriers not only by therapeutic efficacy but also by pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, safety, reproducibility, and scalability. AI-guided design, humanized models, and organ-on-chip platforms may help address these gaps, provided that they are supported by robust, and standardized datasets. Singaravelu et al. 2026 extend this concept through a broad examination of smart biomaterials for site-specific and controlled therapeutic delivery. Natural and synthetic polymers, hydrogels, lipidpolymer hybrids, and organic-inorganic systems can be engineered to respond to pH, redox state, enzymes, temperature, light, ultrasound, or magnetic fields. Such responsiveness provides an additional dimension of control: instead of relying solely on where a carrier accumulates, the system can be designed to determine when and under which biological conditions its payload is released. The value of these systems, however, lies in matching the trigger to a reproducible biological feature. Disease heterogeneity can weaken apparently precise mechanisms, while increasingly complex formulations create additional requirements for characterization and quality control. The review therefore places precision delivery within a broader framework that includes biomarker-guided targeting, standardized nanotoxicology, computational approaches, and emerging technologies such as organ-on-chip models. This perspective is particularly important for moving smart biomaterials from proof-of-concept demonstrations toward clinically meaningful platforms.A distinct but highly relevant route is presented by Tian et al., 2026 who examine elastin-like polypeptides (ELPs) as programmable carriers for radiopharmaceutical delivery. ELPs offer sequence-defined control over molecular weight, phase-transition behavior, functionalization, and self-assembly. These properties can be coupled with radioiodination, radiometal chelation, sitespecific conjugation, and thermally triggered or locally retained delivery. In radiopharmaceutical therapy, this level of control is especially important because carrier behavior directly influences radionuclide biodistribution, tissue retention, and radiation dose deposition. The ELP review also illustrates why programmability must be accomp

title: Gene therapy strategy to treat Cornelia de Lange syndrome due to Hdac8 Deficiency
text: Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS) is a rare, multi-system genetic disorder characterized by developmental and cognitive impairments with systemic manifestations. Among the genes associated with CdLS, loss-of-function variants in HDAC8 account for approximately 4% of cases (referred to as CdLS5), causing the dysregulation of the cohesin complex, a core pathogenic mechanism of the disorder. Currently, no gene-based therapeutic strategy exists to directly address CdLS resulting from HDAC8 deficiency. Here, we created a new CdLS5 mouse model by introducing a clinically reported HDAC8 p.Ile19Ser variant in the mouse Hdac8 gene using CRISPR-Cas9 technology. Comprehensive molecular, morphological, and behavioral characterization revealed that the new Hdac8I19S mouse strain exhibits a robust phenotype, including marked alterations in deacetylase activity and pronounced developmental and behavioral deficits. This model was subsequently used to evaluate a gene augmentation approach aimed at increasing HDAC8 protein levels and restoring cohesin function through delivery of human HDAC8 transgene. Two AAV vectors driving expression of human HDAC8 were assessed. Although efficient delivery and robust expression were achieved, only modest effects on Smc3 acetylation, a key HDAC8 substrate, were observed, and no significant improvement in cognitive or behavioral phenotypes was detected. Overall, these findings demonstrate that postnatal HDAC8 gene augmentation resulted in limited biochemical correction and minimal phenotypic improvement under the conditions tested. These results highlight important biological considerations, including target engagement and developmental timing, that should be considered in the development of effective therapies for cohesin-related disorders.

title: IL-6-Th17/IL-17 activation is linked to osteoclastogenesis in chronic gouty arthritis
text: Introduction The mechanisms of chronic gouty arthritis (CGA) and its progressive bone destruction remain poorly understood. The purpose of this study was to explore the potential involvement of interleukin (IL)-6 and T helper 17 (Th17)/IL-17 responses in CGA-associated osteoclast formation. Methods Fifty-nine patients with gout and 28 healthy controls (HCs) were enrolled in this study. Transcriptome sequencing, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) and flow cytometry were used to detect the levels of cytokines and Th17 cells’ response in CGA patients. Th17-enriched T-cell co-culture and IL-6/IL-17 neutralization experiments were used to assess the osteoclast formation in vitro . The effect of triptolide (TP) was evaluated in PBMC cultures, and the clinical changes following treatment with tripterygium glycoside (TG) were retrospectively examined in four CGA patients. Results CGA patients showed enrichment of IL-17 signaling, and the levels of CXCL1, CXCL2, IL-6 and IL-23 were cooperatively elevated. Also, the Th17-cell frequency, IL-17 production, and the capacity of naive T cells to differentiate into Th17 cells were also increased in CGA patients, which could be suppressed by anti-IL-6 antibody. Furthermore, CGA-derived Th17-enriched T cells increased osteoclast formation in co-culture, whereas IL-6 and IL-17 neutralization reduced osteoclast formation. And TP treatment in vitro showed lower IL-6 levels and reduced osteoclast formation in CGA. The four-patient treated with TG showed exploratory changes in inflammatory biomarkers and peripheral Th17 frequency after treatment. Discussion The findings support the potential involvement of IL-6/Th17/IL-17 responses in osteoclast formation in CGA, which links immune disorder to osteoclast activation, and provide a potential strategy for the use of Tripterygium-derived agents in CGA treatment.

title: Structure-based and AI-guided redesign of Sotrovimab for enhanced recognition of SARS-CoV-2 BA.2 and the E340G escape mutant
text: Introduction The rapid evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants has substantially compromised the efficacy of several monoclonal antibody therapies, including Sotrovimab, through mutations that disrupt antibody–antigen recognition. Developing antibodies with improved recognition of emerging variants and resistance-associated mutations is therefore essential for maintaining therapeutic effectiveness. Methods Here, we employed an integrated computational framework combining structure-guided antibody engineering, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sequence design, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and binding free-energy analyses to redesign Sotrovimab against the Omicron BA.2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) and the clinically relevant E340G escape mutant. Residue-level energetic profiling was used to identify destabilizing interface residues, followed by mutational redesign and ProteinMPNN-guided sequence optimization. The resulting candidates were evaluated through 500 ns all-atom MD simulations, complemented by conformational analyses, MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations, residue-level energy decomposition, and dynamic cross-correlation analyses. Results and Discussion The top-ranked redesigned Sotrovimab candidates retained the characteristic immunoglobulin fold while exhibiting improved structural stability, compactness, and reduced conformational fluctuations. Principal component analysis and free-energy landscape calculations further revealed more confined and energetically favorable conformational states, suggesting enhanced dynamic compatibility with the target RBD. MM/PBSA calculations indicated substantially more favorable binding free energies for both redesigned candidates against the BA.2 RBD and E340G mutant. Residue-level energy decomposition and dynamic cross-correlation analyses further demonstrated improved energetic complementarity and intermolecular communication across the antibody–antigen interface. These improvements were accompanied by enhanced hydrogen-bonding, hydrophobic, and van der Waals interactions, together with increased engagement of the conserved N343-linked glycan, potentially providing additional stabilization to the antibody -antigen complex. Among the redesigned candidates, Sotrovimab-design-2 consistently exhibited the most favorable structural and energetic characteristics. Conclusion Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of integrating AI-guided sequence optimization with structure-based antibody engineering to improve antibody recognition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and resistance-associated mutations. This framework provides a computational foundation for developing mutation-resilient therapeutic antibodies against evolving viral pathogens.

title: SEX DIFFERENCES IN SLEEP, CIRCADIAN RHYTHMS, AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PATHOLOGY IN THE APPXPS1 MUTANT KNOCK-IN MOUSE
text: Decades of research have demonstrated that sleep and circadian rhythm disruptions increase with age and are associated with increased Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) risk. Women experience more sleep and circadian disruptions with age, especially throughout the menopausal transition, and more women than men have AD. The molecular mechanisms underlying biological sex, sleep and circadian disruptions, and AD are largely unknown. Most research has focused on the build-up of toxic amyloid-beta (Aβ) in the brain [which is a cleavage fragment of the full-length amyloid beta precursor protein (APP)] alongside of loss of circulating gonadal hormones. To investigate these possibilities and others, we used an APPxPS1 knock-in (KI) mouse line to examine sex differences in baseline sleep and circadian rhythm patterns, response to sleep fragmentation (SF), AD-related neuropathology, and rhythmic expression of mRNA and proteins known to regulate circadian rhythms and AD neuropathology. Lastly, we determined the effects of gonadal hormones on these endpoint measures via surgical removal of gonads. We observed several consistent sex differences across multiple studies: females slept less and responded differently to SF than males; females had more Aβ and APP pathology than males of the same age; and circadian rhythm parameters and related genes were more broadly altered in females after SF. Interestingly, APP and not Aβ was correlated with sleep only in KI females, and this effect was abolished by SF. We showed for the first time, that not only Aβ, but also APP has a rhythmic expression in the brain throughout the 24-hour day. Only females with AD-related mutations showed a daily rhythm of both APP mRNA and protein. These rhythms were strongly correlated with core circadian rhythm regulating genes, and to a lesser extent with circulating estrogen levels. Removal of circulating gonadal hormones eliminated sex differences in baseline: sleep patterns, Aβ pathology, and circadian rhythm gene expression. Further, gonadectomy in combination with SF ameliorated sex differences in sleep in response to SF, and altered the relationship between APP and sleep in KI females only. Overall, these data show that APP and not Aβ may be a key driver on moderating sex differences in sleep and AD pathology with age in the presence of sleep disruptions.

title: Mars Seed: A Reference Architecture for Biomanufacturing Habitats from Martian Resources
text: Human exploration of Mars will require enormous quantities of materials for the first crewed missions and substantially more for permanent habitation, making flexible and scalable technologies for in situ resource utilization (ISRU), including biological ISRU, of significant interest. However, no existing mission architecture quantitatively evaluates whether in situ biomanufacturing can realistically deliver materials at the scales required for human settlement. Here, we present Mars Seed, an end-to-end reference architecture for using biomanufacturing to produce bioplastics at scale entirely from in situ resources on Mars. We provide a complete analysis of a space bioprocess in which feedstocks are generated entirely from Martian resources, converted biologically into polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) bioplastic, and purified to produce material suitable for constructing human habitats. We show that the upfront power and upmass costs of deploying the equipment required for this bioprocess are recovered within two synodic periods relative to Earth-shipped alternatives. Further, because the process relies entirely on feedstocks sourced from Martian materials, production can continue until equipment failure without requiring additional materials from Earth, enabling scalable conversion of local resources into useful materials. Mars Seed demonstrates that biological ISRU can be mass- and power-competitive with Earth-shipped alternatives, establishing biomanufacturing as a practical component of Mars mission architecture rather than an aspirational capability.

title: Digital twins for intelligent intersections: A literature review
text: Intelligent intersections play a pivotal role in urban mobility, demanding innovative solutions such as digital twins to enhance safety and efficiency. This literature review investigates the integration and application of digital twins for intelligent intersections, a critical area within smart urban traffic systems. The review systematically categorizes existing research into five key thematic areas: (i) Digital Twin Architectures and Frameworks; (ii) Data Processing and Simulation Techniques; (iii) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Adaptive Traffic Control; (iv) Safety and Protection of Vulnerable Road Users; and (v) Scaling from Localized Intersections to Citywide Traffic Networks. Each theme is explored comprehensively, highlighting significant advancements, current challenges, and critical insights. The findings reveal that multi-layered digital twin architectures incorporating real-time data fusion and AI-driven decision-making enhances traffic efficiency and safety. Advanced simulation techniques combined with sophisticated AI/ML algorithms demonstrate notable improvements in real-time responsiveness and predictive accuracy for traffic management. Additionally, the integration of digital twins has shown substantial promise in safeguarding vulnerable road users through proactive and adaptive safety strategies. Despite these advancements, key challenges persist, including interoperability of diverse data sources, scalability of digital twins for extensive traffic networks, and managing uncertainty within dynamic urban environments. Addressing these challenges will be essential for the future development and deployment of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable intersection management systems.

title: Reconstructing substitution histories on phylogenies, with accuracy, precision, and coverage
text: Ancestral sequences and substitution histories are usually averaged out in phylogenetic inference and are therefore not reported to the user. However, they can be recovered through ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic character mapping. By implementing and validating a new ASR and stochastic mapping package compatible with both single-locus and multispecies coalescent analysis, we show how reconstructing substitution histories can enhance the information gained about the tempo and mode of molecular evolution. We observe that known substitution histories (simulated and empirical) are recovered more accurately and precisely on time trees compared with unconstrained and non-ultrametric substitution trees that lack temporal directionality (maximum likelihood and Bayesian). We show that codon-partition models with site-rate heterogeneity, based on the four nucleotide characters, can effectively approximate the histories of synonymous and non-synonymous change, while requiring far less runtime than computationally demanding codon models that require 61 characters. In turn, this provides low-bias estimation of dN/dS that is robust to non-stationarity in GC content, codon usage bias, and nucleotide exchangeability rates. Lastly, using three case studies, we demonstrate how the approach can recover expected patterns in molecular evolution and pathogen transmission: that i) smaller-bodied mammalian species tend to have faster synonymous substitution rates than larger relatives, ii) amino acid substitutions are correlated with 3Di structural changes in aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and iii) influenza A virus spread more frequently to nearby locations than distant ones, in a major H3N2 outbreak in New Zealand. These three trends were more pronounced when based on count estimates derived from stochastic mapping, relative to parametric rates and distances. Our open-source code comes with a user-friendly graphical interface, as the BeastMap package for BEAST 2; supporting a wide range of clock, site, and tree models and data types - including insertions and deletions - within a Bayesian phylogenetic framework.

title: From Tool to Agent: How Worker Needs Reorganize Across the Agentic Roles of Workplace AI
text: As AI systems gain agency in workplaces, workers increasingly interact with systems that do more than support tasks: they make decisions, allocate work, and shape how workers communicate with others. We interviewed 16 workers in healthcare, finance, and management about their daily interactions with workplace AI systems. Across these domains, AI occupied three agentic roles: assistant, supporting worker decision-making; arbiter, making consequential decisions that workers had to explain to downstream stakeholders; and manager, directing work and displacing social structures through which work had been negotiated and learned. We find that worker needs depended on how decision authority and accountability were configured around the AI system. Explanation, control, accountability, and communication each took different meanings depending on whether AI supported, decided, or directed work. We contribute a role-based account of workplace human-agent interaction and identify accountability-authority asymmetry as a mechanism through which AI deployments can place responsibility on workers for outcomes whose authority has shifted to AI. We discuss implications for designing workplace AI around both the agent and its surrounding agency configuration.

title: Automated Intracranial Aneurysm Detection and Size Extraction from Imaging Reports Using a Dual-Model Transformer Framework
text: Abstract Background The unstructured and variable nature of radiology reports remains a barrier to automated extraction of clinically relevant information for large-scale research and AI applications, particularly for intracranial aneurysms (IAs). Objective We aimed to develop and evaluate a dual-model transformer framework for intracranial aneurysm information extraction and assess whether structured processing improved classification and size-extraction performance compared with unstructured text. Methods We analyzed 3,183 neuroimaging reports annotated by neuroradiologists and neurosurgeons.
