title: Multimodal public perception of Port City Heritage, a virtual reality study in Amsterdam
text: Public perception is recognised as a valuable yet underexplored dimension of architectural heritage conservation. This gap is significant for Port City Heritage (PCH), where many attributes have been rapidly changed through urbanisation. This study proposes a VR-based multimodal approach to examine how the perception of heritage attributes changes from visual attention to interpretation over time. Using Amsterdam’s 17th-century Canal Ring as a case study, 25 participants experienced historical scenes overlaid onto present-day panoramas. The findings reveal that heritage perception is an uneven cognitive process in which different heritage attributes follow distinct visual–verbal pathways. While architectural space and industrial structures attracted greater visual attention, PCH spatial and human-related attributes were more readily verbalised and interpreted. Historical comparison across the 16 th to 21 st centuries further reveals the declining perceptibility of Amsterdam’s port-city identity. The study identifies four visual–verbal patterns of heritage attribute recognition and translates these findings into a preliminary governance matrix for heritage interpretation.

title: Interferência Medicamentosa na Lactogênese e Implicações na Saúde Materno-Infantil: Abordagem Nutricional
text: Objetivo: descrever a interferência medicamentosa na lactogênese e as implicações nutricionais na saúde materno-infantil. Metodologia: revisão narrativa da literatura, de caráter descritivo e abordagem qualitativa, com busca realizada entre janeiro e abril de 2026 nas bases PubMed, SciELO e Google Acadêmico, priorizando estudos publicados entre 2020 e 2026, além de estudos clássicos considerados fundamentais para o tema. Resultados: diferentes classes farmacológicas, como analgésicos e anti-inflamatórios, antimicrobianos, psicofármacos e contraceptivos hormonais, apresentam características específicas quanto à segurança durante a amamentação. Determinados medicamentos podem interferir na regulação hormonal da lactogênese, promovendo redução ou supressão da produção láctea, como a cabergolina, a bromocriptina e a pseudoefedrina, enquanto outros são investigados por seu potencial galactagogo, como a domperidona e a metoclopramida, cujos resultados clínicos não demonstram eficácia equivalente. Identificaram-se, ainda, lacunas sobre as interações entre medicamentos e nutrientes no organismo materno e sobre os efeitos da exposição farmacológica pelo leite materno no crescimento e no desenvolvimento infantil. Conclusão: a necessidade de utilizar medicamentos não deve justificar, isoladamente, a interrupção do aleitamento materno, sendo fundamental a avaliação individualizada da relação entre riscos e benefícios. A atuação multiprofissional, especialmente a contribuição da Nutrição, é importante para o acompanhamento do estado nutricional materno e do lactente, e são necessários estudos com maior rigor metodológico e acompanhamento longitudinal.

title: Recent Advancements in Bio‐Derived Fuels: Technological Pathways and Data‐Driven Intelligence
text: Bio-derived fuel refers to biofuels produced from organic materials originating from biomass or biowaste, industrial byproducts, municipal wastes, and animal effluents. To date, no single technology utilizes biomass and biowaste effectively to maximize bioenergy generation, as these technologies are at varying levels of technical and economic maturity. This review critically compares direct combustion, pyrolysis, transesterification, fermentation, and anaerobic digestion, together with mechanical, physicochemical, chemical, and biological pretreatment methods. Technologies of converting biomass and biowaste into bioenergy were critically evaluated based on conversion efficiency, processing time, energy density, emissions, technological maturity, and economic feasibility. Conventional and modern technologies for bio-derived fuels were reviewed in terms of processing time, energy density, emissions, and cost. Biorefinery and bio-derived fuel properties were compared with those of non-renewable fuels. The review highlights advanced approaches for process optimization, bioreactor stability, and bio-product improvement. Integrated biorefineries capable of co-processing multi-biomass and biowaste represent key future opportunities for producing multiple fuels and value-added co-products.

title: Many Circles, One World? A Multidimensional Circle of Equivalence for the Local-to-Global Problem in Science
text: Scientific models often use locally established equivalences, admissible transformations, and preserved invariants to justify conclusions about larger mathematical or empirical systems. Yet valid local closure need not determine a unique global object, and correct mathematical composition does not automatically establish adequacy as a representation of reality. This conceptual paper investigates the Circle of Equivalence (CoE) as a multidimensional, claim-sensitive interpretation of the local-to-global problem in science. Building on symbolic closure, transformation contracts, and evidence-preserving invariance, it distinguishes local relational closure, mathematical composition, global structural identification, and scientific correspondence. Sheaf gluing, fiber bundles, the Hopf construction, and the Poincaré homology sphere provide established mathematical controls, while verification and validation, causal identifiability, and structured assurance supply competing methodological baselines. A minimal claim-specific qualification record is proposed to expose inferential bridges that exceed the supporting result, while recognizing conventional mathematical and scientific sufficiency. Prospective applications include cyber-physical engineering, computational biology, digital twins, and scientific AI. The paper offers no new topological theorem, independent proof of Poincaré, executed experiment, or validated improvement over existing approaches. Its contribution is a bounded conceptual synthesis whose further usefulness depends on critical comparative evaluation.

title: Integrating Biotechnology and Artificial Intelligence for Circular Food Systems: A Critical Review of Evidence, Trade‐offs, and Research Priorities
text: ABSTRACT Food systems remain largely linear, generating large amounts of food loss and waste and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while being increasingly exposed to climatic, geopolitical, and economic shocks. Biotechnology and artificial intelligence (AI) are supported circular food systems (CFS), but their combined benefits remain unclear. This narrative review, based on a structured search of five bibliographic databases, examines how biotechnological conversion routes (fermentation, enzyme‐assisted extraction, engineered microbial cell factories, crop biotechnology, and bio‐based packaging) and AI tools (machine learning, computer vision, soft sensors, and predictive models) interact across production, processing, packaging, and distribution. A four‐level integration framework is proposed, covering organism and enzyme design, bioprocess operation, feedstock and supply‐chain logistics, and product quality and traceability, and the maturity of the supporting evidence is assessed for each level. Most reported gains derive from laboratory‐ or pilot‐scale studies and from AI models validated on limited, single‐site datasets; techno‐economic and life‐cycle evidence for integrated bio‐digital systems is scarce, and trade‐offs in energy, water, cost and food safety are rarely quantified. Research priorities include open and representative datasets, externally validated and interpretable models, harmonized circularity indicators coupled with life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno‐economic analysis (TEA), and pilot‐scale demonstrations under realistic regulatory conditions.

title: UniMAG v1.0: A unified catalogue of metagenome-assembled genomes from human, animal, and environmental sources
text: Abstract We present 581,345 quality-controlled metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) compiled from published studies and public repositories, spanning the human gut ( n = 342,875), non-human animal gut ( n = 142,133), and environmental ( n = 96,337) habitats. Genomes were screened for exact duplicates and filtered on completeness, contamination, chimerism, and contiguity against MIMAG medium- and high-quality criteria. Retained genomes were taxonomically standardised according to GTDB and a species-level represent set was established for each habitat. Coding sequences were predicted for all genomes and annotated with KEGG orthologs and predicted defence systems. Whole genome, nucleotide, amino acid, general feature format (GFF), and genbank files are provided for each genome, as well as a per-genome metadata table linking assembly statistics, quality metrics, taxonomy, host and habitat metadata, and source publication. This collection represents a cross-biome genome set standardised under a common quality-control, taxonomic, and functional annotation framework, and is intended as a reference for cross-biome analyses of microbial diversity.

title: CROST 2.0: an expanded repository of spatial transcriptomics
text: CROST (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/crost) is a public spatial transcriptomics resource that offers curated datasets, standardized analytical results, structured spatial knowledge, and interactive exploration tools. In version 2.0, our collection has expanded to 544 projects and 3538 samples, nearly a three-fold increase from version 1.0 (182 projects and 1033 samples). We have also substantially expanded the derived resources for spatial colocalization and spatially variable cancer genes. To facilitate spatial microenvironment analysis, CROST 2.0 introduces an analytical framework comprising niche-associated differential expression, spatially resolved gene-set activity analysis, spatial interaction hotspot and topic analyses, and molecular and cell-type niche analysis. CROST 2.0 also provides the Spatial Compare function to compare spatial gene expression, cell-type distributions, and niche composition across samples. It introduces the Cancer NicheDE module to systematically characterize cancer niche-associated differential expression and integrates an online cell-type annotation tool, SCType, enabling the use of single-cell reference information in spatial transcriptomic analysis. These updates extend CROST into an integrated spatial transcriptomics resource for characterizing spatial microenvironments, investigating cancer-associated spatial features, and comparing spatial patterns across samples.

title: Integrative Genomic and Stem Cell Frameworks for Variant‐to‐Function Discovery in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Narrative Review
text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition shaped by de novo protein-truncating variants, inherited missense substitutions, recurrent copy number variations (CNVs), and distributed polygenic risk. These alterations converge on a limited set of neurobiological processes, including synaptic refinement, excitation-to-inhibition balance, chromatin state regulation, and glial-mediated neuroimmune signaling. Experimental paradigms now exist for systematic variant-to-function interrogation through CRISPR-engineered isogenic human pluripotent stem-cell libraries incorporating Cas9 nucleases, programmable transcriptional modulators (dCas9-KRAB and dCas9-VP64), base editors, and prime editing systems. Coupled with single-cell multi-omic platforms such as Perturb-seq, scATAC-seq, and CITE-seq, and with circuit-level phenotyping through multielectrode arrays, calcium imaging, and quantitative morphometry, these systems resolve ASD-relevant cellular states at single-cell and cell-type-specific resolution. In this narrative review, we distinguish deliberately between what these platforms have already established and what remains proposed. To date, a small number of studies constitute the demonstrated evidence base: in vivo Perturb-seq of 35 ASD/neurodevelopmental risk genes in mouse cortex, mosaic knockout of ASD genes in human cortical organoids, the CHOOSE organoid screen of 36 risk genes, assembloid CRISPR screening of 425 neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes, a 63-line mouse embryonic stem-cell CNV resource, and a CRISPRi screen of 102 ASD risk genes in human induced pluripotent stem-cell (iPSC)-derived microglia implicating ADNP in synaptic pruning. We summarized these in a dedicated comparison table. Against this, integration of polygenic and noncoding architecture, causal-inference frameworks, such as Mendelian randomization and do-calculus, and cross-laboratory reproducibility, remain aspirational rather than realized. We therefore frame the field's principal near-term requirement not as further gene discovery but as harmonized protocols, shared reference lines, arrayed validation capacity, and interpretable statistical frameworks capable of converting perturbation atlases into causal mechanism.

title: proMGE2—a planetary-scale resource of mobile genetic elements in microbial (meta)genomes
text: proMGE is a resource of prokaryotic mobile genetic elements (MGEs) that systematically catalogues MGEs from prokaryotes, their intercellular spread, antimicrobial resistance gene carriage, and MGE nesting interactions. We present proMGE2 featuring a 6X expansion, a total of >16.4 million MGEs from 670k high-quality isolate genomes, and 180k metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), spanning diverse MGE categories: transposons and insertion sequences, phages, phage-like elements, conjugative elements, mobility islands, and integrons. proMGE2 includes MGEs from MAGs derived from environmental microbiomes, encompassing ~50k samples across several major habitat types. proMGE2 provides a standardized MGE reference collection of >5 million non-redundant MGE sequences drawn from our curated database, and enables identification of MGEs in user-provided genomes. proMGE2 captures MGE diversity and their functional potential at unprecedented scale to support future research of mobile genetic elements and transfer of genetic material in microbes. The database is available at http://promge.embl.de/.

title: IDENTIFY AND SELECT NEW AI ALGORITHM FOR MULTIPLE SEQUENCE ALIGNMENT BASED ON SOME EVALUATION CHARACTERISTICS
text: This research paper opens new ways for multiple sequence alignments (MSA) that use artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. Where, Due to a lack of evaluation papers for MSA. Fulfilling this lack is a necessity in the bioinformatics field. To begin with, made a probe on MSA research papers. In addition, analyze these methods. Furthermore, evaluation metadata, then gathered data extracted from the research papers into the table of evaluation methods. Based on these characteristics or metadata, we select an AI algorithm called Augmented random search (ARS). As a result, an evaluation table that contains 8 features (objective functions (quality metrics), parameters or hyperparameter, assessment criteria, benchmark datasets, collect reference alignments, MSA algorithm, analyze and interpret results, and biological relevance) and mapped MSA problem on ARS. This paper adds new knowledge for artificial intelligence and multiple sequence alignment in the bioinformatics field. On the one hand, current research uses genetic algorithm (GA) and Reinforcement learning (RL) to solve MSA problems efficiently, on the other hand, there is an algorithm that beats GA and RL in a performance called Augmented random search (ARS)

title: Impact of the physico-chemical properties of surface-initiated polymer brushes on siRNA binding and transfection efficiency
text: Rational design of polycationic gene delivery vectors requires understanding how polymer chemistry governs RNA complexation, cellular uptake, intracellular release and, in turn, transfection efficiency kinetics.

title: 基于咪喹莫特重复刺激构建银屑病样炎症小鼠实验模型及其免疫特征研究
text: Long-term psoriasis management remains a major challenge worldwide. Although repeated imiquimod (IMQ) application has been used to mimic psoriatic inflammatory reactivation, it remains unclear whether this approach reflects amplified acute inflammation or the emergence of tissue-resident, memory-associated features. Here, we established a repeated IMQ-challenge model (IMQ-R) and compared it with a single-course IMQ model (IMQ-S) and human psoriatic lesions using bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (single-cell RNA-seq). During the final induction phase, IMQ-R showed a more rapid re-emergence of skin inflammation than IMQ-S and displayed features of inflammatory reactivation in previously challenged skin, including IL-17-related pathways, TRM-related T-cell features, and predicted multicellular communication patterns. Single-cell analysis showed that IMQ-R exhibited a cellular composition more similar to active human psoriatic skin than IMQ-S, with keratinocyte (KC) expansion, endothelial cell (EC) enrichment, and relative preservation of T-cell populations. T-cell subsets with memory-associated annotations, including central memory T cells (TCM) and tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM), were increased in IMQ-R. In particular, IMQ-R was associated with enrichment of TRM17-related transcriptional features and enhanced predicted communication among T cells, keratinocytes (KCs), and myeloid cells, including IL-17-related signaling pathways. In summary, repeated IMQ challenge generates a psoriasiform model with accelerated inflammatory re-emergence and TRM-related features during re-exposure that are not fully captured by the conventional acute IMQ model. This model provides a useful platform for studying inflammatory reactivation after repeated challenge and for evaluating interventions targeting cutaneous memory-associated inflammatory programs.

title: 肝豆状核变性的临床前模型：从发病机制到临床转化
text: variants, leading predominantly to hepatic and neurological injury. Extensive heterogeneity in genotype, age at onset, clinical presentation, and treatment response complicates both diagnosis and therapeutic development, highlighting the need for reliable experimental models that reproduce distinct features of WD pathogenesis. This review critically evaluates animal models, conventional cell systems, induced pluripotent stem cell models, and organoids of WD, with an emphasis on the phenotypes reproduced, experimental strengths and limitations, and translational applications of each platform. Rodent models have been instrumental in defining mechanisms of hepatic copper accumulation and toxicity and remain widely used for preclinical therapeutic evaluation, but existing models do not adequately reproduce the neurological manifestations characteristic of human WD. Patient-derived cells and organoids provide complementary platforms for investigating mutation-specific pathobiology, individualized drug responses, and genome-editing strategies, although incomplete maturation, limited cellular complexity, and insufficient standardization remain important constraints. Future progress will depend on models that more faithfully capture neurological disease, greater use of humanized systems, improved physiological fidelity of organoids, and standardized criteria for phenotypic assessment. Integrating complementary models across the preclinical pipeline should strengthen mechanistic insight and accelerate development of precision therapies for WD.

title: 从表达谱分析到功能验证：水生动物环状RNA的证据层级与生物标志物转化准备度
text: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence associating circRNAs with candidate biomarker potential for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. Overall, aquatic animals provide valuable non-model systems for expanding our understanding of circRNA biology, although many proposed regulatory mechanisms and translational applications remain to be further validated.

title: Precision genome modifications through CRISPR systems including base and prime editing for crop improvement
text: CRISPR-Cas technology has revolutionised genome editing in crop plants, enabling precise gene modifications to address critical agricultural challenges. Since its inception, CRISPR technology has advanced considerably, enabling diverse applications in crop improvement, such as enhanced stress tolerance and development of desirable agronomic traits. The emergence of base editing and prime editing has further expanded their potential for precise genome engineering in crops, offering greater accuracy and versatility. These advanced tools enable targeted single-base substitutions, insertions, deletions, and gene modification without causing double-stranded breaks or relying on donor templates, reducing off-target effects and increasing efficiency. These tools have successfully targeted important crop genes, advancing precision agriculture and crop improvement. In this context, this review focuses on the various classes and variants of CRISPR, along with their distinct mechanisms and applications in crop genome editing. We further discuss the recent technological advancements from CRISPR-Cas to base editing and prime editing, along with novel CRISPR systems that use alternative Cas proteins and compact TnpB nucleases. Integrating these advanced genome-editing technologies into current breeding programmes is pivotal for accelerating the development of climate-resilient, high-yielding, and sustainable crop varieties.

title: Identification of key programmed cell death-related hub genes for coronary artery disease complicated by metabolic syndrome via integrated bioinformatics
text: Given the high comorbidity and shared pathological mechanisms between coronary artery disease (CAD) and metabolic syndrome (MetS), this study aimed to identify and validate key programmed cell death (PCD)-related hub genes common to both conditions and to assess their therapeutic potential. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets and intersected with PCD-related genes to obtain candidate genes. Hub genes were screened using machine learning algorithms, and their diagnostic value, functional pathways, immune correlations, and regulatory networks were systematically evaluated through bioinformatics analyses. Potential herb-derived compounds were predicted via network pharmacology and examined by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, followed by absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity analysis. Finally, the expression levels of hub genes in clinical samples were detected by RT-qPCR. A total of 37 candidate genes were screened, from which Phosphatase and Tensin Homolog (PTEN), Heat Shock Protein Family A (Hsp70) Member 5 (HSPA5), and Cysteine Rich Protein 1 (CRIP1) were identified as hub genes with high diagnostic value and good nomogram predictive performance. The ssGSEA scores of mast cells differed significantly between CAD/MetS patients and controls. Quercetin was predicted to potentially bind to PTEN and HSPA5 and to have high gastrointestinal absorption. PTEN and HSPA5 were significantly upregulated, and CRIP1 was downregulated in CAD and MetS patients compared with controls, with a more obvious trend in the comorbid group. PTEN, HSPA5, and CRIP1 were potential targets for CAD and MetS, with quercetin as a promising intervening agent.

title: Dimethyltryptamine improves early graft hemodynamic performance in a heterotopic rat heart transplantation model
text: Abstract Preserving donor organ viability during cold storage is critical for successful heart transplantation, as ischemia–reperfusion injury (IRI) adversely affects graft function. N, N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT), an endogenous sigma-1 receptor ligand, has demonstrated cytoprotective effects under hypoxic and oxidative stress. This study evaluated the effects of DMT on graft recovery in a rat model of heterotopic heart transplantation. Hearts from male Lewis rats were preserved for 1 h at 4 °C in either Custodiol solution or Custodiol supplemented with DMT. Both donors and recipients in the treatment group also received DMT. After transplantation, graft function was assessed 60 min into reperfusion using preload-dependent pressure measurements, complemented by molecular and histological evaluations. DMT-treated grafts exhibited higher left ventricular systolic pressure, enhanced myocardial contractility and improved diastolic relaxation compared with controls. Gene expression analysis revealed significant modulation of Ddit3 , Hif1a and Vldlr , with trends in apoptotic and metabolic markers. A strong trend toward increased cleaved caspase-3 expression and significantly higher p62 immunohistochemical scores were observed, whereas cardiac troponin I and TNF-α levels remained unchanged. Overall, these findings indicate that DMT treatment improves early post-transplant graft contractile performance under the experimental conditions tested. The mechanisms underlying the observed functional improvement remain to be further elucidated.

title: Adaptive immune regulation of HSV-2 infection: from acute infection to latency and reactivation
text: Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) establishes lifelong infection through cycles of epithelial replication, neuronal latency, and periodic reactivation. While robust immune responses do not lead to viral clearance, they do play a central role in limiting the tissue impact of ongoing virus shedding that is part of the natural history of HSV-2. In sensory ganglia, CD8 + T cells suppress viral reactivation through non-cytolytic mechanisms, allowing persistence of latent viral genomes. At mucosal sites, tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM cells) provide rapid, localized responses that help contain viral spread. However, HSV-2 replication in epithelial tissues occurs rapidly and can outpace the activation and recruitment of circulating immune cells, creating a temporal mismatch that permits viral shedding despite immune surveillance. These findings suggest that HSV-2 persistence confers a kinetic and spatial advantage over immune responses, underscoring the need for next-generation vaccines and therapeutic strategies that enhance tissue-localized, early immune control and target latent viral reservoirs. This review examines HSV-2 infection as a continuous immunological process across epithelial and neuronal compartments and discusses its implications for vaccine development and therapeutic intervention.

title: G‐Quadruplexes and Z‐DNA: Non‐B DNA Structures in Genome Regulation and Molecular Targeting
text: G-quadruplexes (G4s) and Z-DNA are structurally distinct non-B-DNA conformations that have been extensively studied. Recent advances in genome-wide prediction and detection technologies have revealed the presence of these structures at numerous genomic loci and accumulated evidence supports their involvement in various biological processes, including transcription, within chromatin environments. Nevertheless, the biological functions and intracellular dynamics of G4s and Z-DNA remain incompletely understood, and continued development and refinement of biochemical methods and molecular tools will facilitate further investigation of their roles in cellular processes. In this review, we focus on G4 and Z-DNA, providing a comparative overview of their structural features and functional roles, while further discussing the mechanisms governing their formation within the genome, as well as chemical approaches for selective G4 recognition and modulation of Z-DNA formation.

title: Target-selective MG53-containing extracellular vesicles delivery in acute and chronic kidney injury
text: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a sudden loss of kidney function associated with high morbidity and mortality, and effective therapy remains an unmet need. We previously showed that MG53, a muscle-predominant protein, confers kidney protection against ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury and unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-mediated kidney fibrosis. Here, we show that limb remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) partially attenuates tubular apoptosis alongside a trend toward functional renal improvement against I/R-AKI, an event accompanied by a systemic surge of circulating MG53-containing extracellular vesicles (EVs). While the exact systemic trafficking kinetics and precise tissue origins of this native endogenous pool remain a proposed working hypothesis, a stark, exclusive 2.3-fold upregulation of MG53 cargo occurs exclusively within the injured renal microenvironment. To evaluate the translational utility of this axis, we characterized exogenous MG53-containing EVs derived from C2C12 myotubes (EV C2C12 ) or engineered NIH3T3 cells (EV MMT ). Upon intravenous administration, these vehicles exhibited rapid, injury-dependent accumulation within damaged proximal tubules. Utilizing a chronic injection regimen, sustained delivery of these payloads successfully mitigated baseline renal functional defects (Scr and UPCR) in mg53 -/- mice. Finally, in vitro assays demonstrate that MG53-containing EVs uptake is closely associated with intracellular AKT activation and enhances proximal tubule cell metabolic activity during hypoxia/reoxygenation stress. In summary, this work underscores the reparative capacity of endogenous MG53 accumulation while establishing that exogenous vesicular delivery serves as a viable translational strategy within an integrated muscle-kidney crosstalk axis.

title: Targeting Mitosis to Reprogram the Tumor Microenvironment: Combination Strategies for Cancer Immunotherapy
text: Dysregulated mitosis is a therapeutic vulnerability in cancer, but the consequences of mitotic targeting extend beyond tumor-cell death. Chromosome missegregation, micronucleus formation, and chromatin-bridge exposure can activate cytosolic DNA sensing and alter inflammatory signaling, immune recognition, and stromal interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME). These responses are not uniformly antitumor. Acute mitotic perturbation may enhance innate immune activation and tumor-cell susceptibility to immune elimination, whereas persistent chromosomal instability can promote inflammatory adaptation, myeloid immunosuppression, and immune escape. This distinction has important implications for combining antimitotic agents with immunotherapy. Here, we examine the molecular mechanisms linking mitotic disruption to TME remodeling, with particular emphasis on signaling through cyclic GMP–AMP synthase (cGAS) and stimulator of interferon genes (STING), immune checkpoint regulation, myeloid-cell responses, and stromal reorganization. We evaluate combination strategies involving immune checkpoint blockade, innate immune modulation, myeloid targeting, radiotherapy, and cell-death-enhancing interventions. Although preclinical studies provide mechanistic support for several approaches, clinical evidence remains uneven, and the immune consequences of individual antimitotic agents are difficult to predict across tumor types. We propose a testable framework integrating baseline chromosomal instability, p53 status, innate immune competence, and early treatment-induced biomarkers to guide therapeutic selection and scheduling. Translating this framework into clinical practice will require prospective validation, clearer separation of drug-specific effects from general mitotic stress responses, and evidence that immune remodeling improves patient outcomes.

title: Extracellular vesicles in viral myocarditis: Mechanisms, biomarkers and emerging therapeutic strategies
text: Viral myocarditis (VM) is an inflammatory heart disease most commonly triggered by viral infection and represents a major cause of acute cardiac dysfunction and chronic inflammatory cardiomyopathy. Although cardiomyocyte injury and immune activation are central to VM pathogenesis, the mechanisms by which viral infection coordinates intercellular communication to drive disease progression remain incompletely understood. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as key mediators of cell-to-cell signaling, capable of transporting viral components and host-derived factors that modulate immune responses and cardiac function. In this review, we integrate preclinical and clinical evidence to define the mechanistic roles of EVs in VM and evaluate their translational potential. We highlight circulating EVs as minimally invasive biomarkers for early diagnosis and disease monitoring. We further discuss emerging strategies to therapeutically target or engineer EVs to modulate both viral replication and maladaptive host responses.

title: Total synthesis of genomes
text: The total synthesis of genomes is a bottom-up bioengineering approach which empowers synthetic biologists to investigate complex biological hypotheses and reprogramme cells with novel functions. A successful genome synthesis requires (i) an informed design, (ii) a tractable approach to replace genomic with synthetic DNA, and (iii) a troubleshooting strategy for design flaws. While enabled by the advent of in vitro DNA synthesis and kilobase-scale in vivo DNA assembly approaches, this review highlights recent advances in megabase-scale assembly technologies as well as the nucleotide-resolution mapping of genotype-phenotype relationships. Collectively, these synthetic genomic techniques have enabled the completion of rewritten prokaryotic genomes and eukaryotic chromosomes. Furthermore, we discuss next-generation innovations in ML-driven genome design applied toward ongoing genome synthesis projects, which combined with expedited assembly techniques promise to increase the functional sequence space of redesigned organisms.

title: Pathophysiology-guided biomarkers and therapeutics for precision trauma medicine in polytrauma with musculoskeletal injuries
text: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. Conventional injury assessments, which rely heavily on anatomical scoring and nonspecific blood markers, fail to capture the dynamic molecular landscape underlying these conditions. To address this critical gap, we performed a comprehensive scoping review integrating evidence from basic science, translational studies, and clinical research published between January 2000 to June 2025, with particular emphasis on recent advances. The review highlights the discovery and validation of emerging blood-based and molecular biomarkers, including fatty acid-binding protein 3, syndecan-1, galectin-3, and trauma-associated microRNAs, as well as innovative diagnostic paradigms such as wearable biosensors, minimally invasive liquid biopsy platforms, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics. Unlike prior reviews, our analysis uniquely integrates findings across both military and civilian trauma contexts, providing actionable frameworks for clinical application. Building on these insights, we outline a practical roadmap: 1) deploy integrated multi-marker panels for early risk stratification, 2) expand inclusive trauma biobanking to capture diverse injury phenotypes, and 3) use adaptive, data-driven tools for real-time triage and personalized intervention. This approach links acute systemic responses to downstream recovery and rehabilitation, offering actionable guidance for both military and civilian trauma systems.

title: Solid-Earth geophysics and geodesy in Antarctica: achievements, current capabilities, and future directions
text: The Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS) plays a major role in the global climate, providing a natural laboratory to study the processes that interlink the cryosphere, solid Earth, atmosphere, and hydrosphere. Through its ongoing mass loss, the AIS currently contributes to global-mean sea-level rise at a rate of 0.4 mm a −1 . However, its impact on and feedback with climate and sea-level changes are still poorly understood. To generate reliable sea-level projections for the future, there is an urgent need to substantially improve our knowledge of the solid-Earth properties and subsequent response to ice-mass variations in space and time. This issue has been identified as a key question by the international community, strongly supported by the Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research (SCAR). We review how state-of-the-art Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) and seismic networks in Antarctica, in combination with further ground-based, airborne and satellite-based geophysical measurements, have been used to significantly advance our understanding of solid-Earth processes and their impact on the cryosphere. Future research activities should be coordinated to answer the most urgent science questions. For example, how can we consistently test and model, respectively, a realistic mantle rheology that includes lateral inhomogeneity and transient relaxation, together with AIS mass changes on all time scales since the Last Glacial Maximum, including Holocene retreat and readvance? What processes and boundary conditions should coupled ice-sheet/gravity-rotation-deformation models include in order to realistically reflect the complex interaction between the solid Earth, ice sheet and ocean? Based on the recent achievements and the most urgent science questions, a vision is articulated for science-driven, multidisciplinary geophysical observations and corresponding technological developments. Long-term observations and improved modelling must be combined to develop precise and reliable projections for Antarctica's future mass change and associated contribution to sea-level change at both regional and global scales.

title: Study of image classification models for the automatic identification of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma on Whole Slide Images
World-model-inspired latent action priors for home energy optimization
text: The integration of renewable energy sources into residential microgrids introduces operational challenges associated with intermittency, electricity-price volatility, and the progressive degradation of battery storage systems. Reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach for battery scheduling, yet many existing methods remain vulnerable to actions that fall outside the support of the training data and often generalize poorly across operating regimes. This work proposes an offline reinforcement learning framework that combines a conditional variational autoencoder with latent action priors in order to constrain policy optimization to a structured latent action space learned from expert demonstrations generated by entropy-regularized and deterministic actor-critic controllers. The proposed methodology consists of three stages: first, learning a latent representation of admissible battery actions from expert trajectories through a conditional variational autoencoder; second, extracting an offline policy within the learned latent manifold through implicit value-based policy improvement; and third, deploying an out-of-distribution detection mechanism that gradually blends the learned controller with a conservative fallback policy under distributional uncertainty. Experiments on the GEFCom2014 benchmark, the StoreNet House 4 scenario, and the CityLearn environment show that the proposed method achieves the highest daily net benefit among value-based and offline controllers, with improvements of up to 61.9% over deep Q-learning and 7.9% over standard model predictive control on GEFCom2014. In addition, the method converges substantially faster than competing baselines, requiring up to nine times less training time in CityLearn. At the same time, the results show that the approach does not uniformly dominate all references: in the policy-based comparison on CityLearn, deep deterministic policy gradients achieve a lower monetary cost, and in standard continuous-control benchmarks, proximal policy optimization and twin delayed deterministic policy gradients outperform the proposed method on specific metrics in selected environments. Ablation studies further show that expert-dataset diversity and rare-event coverage are essential for policy quality, while posterior-collapse diagnostics confirm that the learned latent representation remains informative throughout training. Overall, the proposed framework constitutes a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for offline energy management, particularly in settings where safe exploration, fast convergence, and degradation-aware control are more critical than unconstrained asymptotic performance.

title: Digital identity infrastructure and administrative exclusion in social protection delivery: An integrative review of evidence from developing
text: Digital identity systems are increasingly presented as administrative infrastructure that can improve the targeting, verification, and delivery of social protection in developing countries. However, the same systems may create new forms of exclusion when biometric authentication fails, registration documents are unavailable, connectivity is weak, or frontline staff apply eligibility rules inflexibly. This article examines how digital identity infrastructure affects administrative exclusion in social protection delivery. Using an integrative review design, it synthesizes peer-reviewed research and authoritative institutional evidence on digital identity, biometric verification, and social assistance in developing-country settings. The analysis is organized around four dimensions: enrolment and documentation, authentication and service access, data governance and accountability, and administrative capacity. The review finds that digital identity can reduce certain inclusion errors and improve payment traceability, but its benefits are conditional on inclusive registration, reliable fallback procedures, interoperable systems, data protection, and adequate frontline capacity. Without these conditions, digitalization may shift exclusion from paper-based eligibility barriers to technological and institutional barriers. The article contributes a policy-oriented framework for assessing whether digital identity reforms strengthen or undermine equitable social protection delivery.

title: The brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge for establishing correspondence between pre-operative and follow-up MRI scans of diffuse glioma patients
text: Abstract Registration of longitudinal brain MRI scans containing pathologies remains a challenging problem, due to substantial changes in tissue appearance. While medical image registration methods have advanced considerably, they often lack the required precision and robustness. To address this gap, we introduced the brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge, the first public benchmark specifically designed for deformable registration between pre-operative and follow-up scans of patients with adult-type diffuse gliomas. Conducted in conjunction with ISBI-2022 and MICCAI-2022, BraTS-Reg provides de-identified, multi-institutional, multi-parametric MRI data accompanied by expert-annotated landmark points across time. Training data with ground truth annotations were publicly released for algorithm development, while validation data without annotations enabled pre-testing. Submitted containerized algorithms were evaluated on hidden testing cases. Quantitative evaluation was based on median Euclidean error (MEE), Robustness, and the determinant of Jacobian of the displacement field. Top-ranked methods demonstrated comparable performance and shared key features, including pre-alignment of scans, deep neural networks, inverse consistency analysis, and per-case test-time optimization. The best method achieved MEE comparable to inter-rater variability for 63% of landmarks, underscoring the need for further improvements in accuracy and robustness relative to human experts. BraTS-Reg serves as a three-fold active resource for research on image registration, providing a publicly available dataset, a framework for a community benchmark, and online evaluation tools, accessible at https://bratsreg.github.io/ .

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
text: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: Observation of Environment and Reproductive-Endocrine Effects
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] Background: Endocrine disorders occur when the glands that make hormones do not work properly. Hormones levels that are too high or too low can cause problems such as late or early puberty, irregular periods, and infertility. Environmental factors - including pollution; chemical exposure at home and work; foods; medicines; and sleep habits - may cause problems with the endocrine and reproductive systems. Objective: To learn how environmental factors may affect the endocrine and reproductive systems. Reproductive Disorder Cohorts: Eligibility: Males or females, referring to sex assigned at birth, aged 8 years and older; they must have hypogonadism, infertility, or other reproductive disorders. Design: Adult participants will have 4 to 5 visits in 5 years. Children may have up to 12 visits; they may remain in the study up to the age of 23. Most visits will be less than 3 hours. Participants will be screened. They will have a physical exam. They will have blood and urine tests. They will complete questionnaires; they will answer questions about their diet, health, and other topics. Some may be referred for additional tests, such as imaging scans and semen analysis. Specific tests conducted during study visits will vary, depending on the participant s diagnosis. In addition to repeated blood and urine tests, these may include: Body composition measure: Participants will sit in a pod-shaped machine for about 6 minutes. The machines measures the air inside the capsule to record body fat and breathing volume. Resting energy expenditure test: Participants will lie down with a clear dome placed over their head. They will breathe quietly for 30 minutes. This test measures the number of calories their body burns at rest. Menopausal Women Cohort: Eligibility: Inclusion criteria: Females, ages 40-62, in late perimenopause (skipped at least 2 menstrual periods) or early post menopause (last menstrual period within 2 years), with a history of regular menstrual cycles during reproductive years. Exclusion Criteria: Previous surgery or procedure that induces amenorrhea or menopause, diagnosis of reproductive disorder, symptoms of irregular menstrual cycles, or medication or device use (eg, birth control pills) that would prevent the determination of menopausal status. Design: Women will have one study visit, and three at home specimen collections: Study visit, At home collections Day 7, Month 2 and Month 4. At the study visit, women will be screened, complete questionnaires, provide blood and urine for lab testing for hormones and chemical exposures, and a Body composition measure. Women will collect first morning void before their study visit, Month 2 and Month 4. A wristband (for chemical exposures) is worn from the study visit for 7 Days. Women will complete questionnaires during at home collections at Day 7, Month 2 and Month 4....

title: Machine-learning Algorithm for Prediction of CKD From Retinal Images
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This is a non-interventional study being conducted to validate the performance of a machine learning algorithm for prediction of eGFR from digital retinal images in a target population for future intended use as a populated-based screening tool. Secondary objectives will include prediction of blood pressure (\> or ≤ 140/90 mmHg) and presence or absence of T2DM as determined by glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c \>6.5%) or on the basis of clinical history. Once validated, the methodology will be deployed for health screening to improve access to healthcare.

title: AI-Integrated 3D-Printed Videolaryngoscope for Orotracheal Intubation in Critically Ill Patients
text: [Fase: NA; Estado: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Background: Orotracheal intubation is an essential procedure in critically ill patients requiring ventilatory support, and the use of videolaryngoscopy is recommended as the gold standard in clinical practice. In recent years, the development of videolaryngoscopes through additive manufacturing has demonstrated lower production costs, and their integration with artificial intelligence (AI) has shown promising results in improving procedural success and safety. Aim: To evaluate the clinical performance and usability of a videolaryngoscope developed through additive manufacturing and integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision, compared with a commercially available gold-standard videolaryngoscope. Methods: This is a multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority Phase I/II clinical trial with a single-blind design. A total of 120 critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units at four hospitals in southern Brazil will be enrolled. Participants will be individually randomized in a 1:1 allocation ratio to parallel groups. The interventions will be performed by at least 10 physicians. All physicians will receive standardized training on device use, and procedures will be monitored by trained research staff. Data will be recorded in electronic Excel spreadsheets, and statistical analyses will be conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics. All ethical principles will be strictly observed, including obtaining informed consent from participants or their legal representatives. A Data and Safety Monitoring Committee will be established to oversee the study. Conclusions: If the expected results are confirmed, patients, healthcare professionals, and healthcare institutions may benefit from the improved performance, safety, and usability of the experimental device, particularly in critical care settings and public health emergencies.

title: Investigating the Effect of Caffeine and Alcohol on Pupil Dynamics
text: [Fase: NA; Estado: RECRUITING] The goal of this study is to understand how caffeine and alcohol affect the ocular and physiological systems, especially how the pupil (the aperture in the colored part of the eye) responds to light. It will also test whether these changes can be used to detect recent caffeine or alcohol intake using a portable eye device. The main questions it aims to answer are: 1. How does caffeine change pupil responses, eye movements, and other ocular and physiological measurements? 2. How does alcohol change these same ocular and physiological responses? 3. Are the effects of caffeine and alcohol different from each other? 4. Can these changes be used to accurately identify whether someone has consumed caffeine or alcohol? Researchers will compare caffeine, alcohol, and a placebo (a look-alike drink with no active substance) to see how each affects the ocular and physiological outcomes. Participants will: 1. Attend three separate sessions where they will consume caffeine, alcohol, or a placebo (in random order) 2. Undergo pupillary response evaluation using a handheld device that measures responses to different colored light stimuli 3. Have their eye movements analyzed 4. Have retinal and choroidal thickness, blood perfusion, and ocular oxygen levels measured 5. Have basic body measurements recorded (such as pulse rate and blood pressure) 6. Complete tests at multiple time points over 2 hours after consumption The results of this study may help develop a quick and non-invasive way to detect recent caffeine or alcohol use for clinical and safety purposes.

title: A multipathogen view of Epstein-Barr virus pathogenesis and tumorigenesis.
text: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects more than 95% of the global population and contributes to multiple human cancers and autoimmune diseases. Co-infection with pathogens including Helicobacter pylori, human immunodeficiency virus, human papillomavirus, and Plasmodium falciparum can reshape host immunity and the EBV latency-lytic balance and, in some settings, promote reactivation. Collectively, these interactions may exacerbate chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and epigenetic dysregulation to accelerate disease progression and tumor formation. Existing clinical treatments control only the active pathogens but fail to target latent EBV. Emerging strategies such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) gene editing and EBV-targeted immunotherapy aim to eliminate latent viral reservoirs. This review outlines the synergistic mechanisms of EBV co-infection in oncogenesis, highlighting that further research on pathogen interactions is vital for developing better prevention and treatment options.

title: A Virus-like particle system based on parainfluenza virus PIV5-L for CRISPR-Cas9 and RNAi delivery.
text: Nucleic acid-targeting technologies based on CRISPR-Cas or small-hairpin RNA (shRNA) are essential for functional genomics and therapeutic development, yet a delivery platform that simultaneously ensures high efficiency, safety, modularity, and broad cell compatibility remains lacking. Here, we report L-VLP, a virus-like particle platform derived from a B-lymphoma-isolated strain of parainfluenza virus PIV5-L. This single-cycle, replication-deficient VLP functions as a dual-mode delivery system, capable of carrying either Cas9/sgRNA for CRISPR-mediated gene editing or shRNA for RNA interference, and achieves effective target gene knockdown or knockout in both breast cancer and B-lymphoma cells. Notably, the sgRNA or shRNA cassettes in L-VLP can be readily exchanged for any sequence of interest without altering the core vector architecture, providing a modular and versatile design. Functional assays confirm that L-VLP-mediated UBR5 silencing significantly inhibits tumor cell growth in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our work establishes L-VLP as a flexible and efficient platform for manipulating gene expression, with promising applications in both basic research and cancer target therapeutics.

title: CRISPR-Cas Systems in Protozoan Parasites: Genome Editing, Functional Genomics, Gene Regulation and Emerging Applications.
text: Protozoan parasites possess complex genomes, unusual DNA-repair mechanisms, multiple developmental stages, and, in several species, intracellular or vector-dependent life cycles that complicate functional genetic studies. CRISPR-Cas9 has become a central tool for functional genomics in these organisms, enabling targeted gene disruption, replacement, tagging, nucleotide modification and genome-wide functional screening. However, editing efficiency and outcomes vary substantially among parasite species and depend not only on Cas9-mediated double-strand break formation but also on target accessibility, guide design, delivery method, parasite stage, DNA-repair capacity, donor availability, selection and the biological cost of the induced lesion. This review focuses primarily on experimentally established Cas9-mediated genome editing in Plasmodium, Leishmania, Toxoplasma gondii, Trypanosoma, Babesia, Theileria and Cryptosporidium. We compare plasmid-based and transient expression, ribonucleoprotein (RNP) delivery, electroporation/nucleofection, stage-specific delivery, guide and donor design, selection strategies, editing outcomes, and molecular and functional validation. Particular emphasis is placed on homology-directed repair (HDR), canonical non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) and single-strand annealing (SSA), which determine whether editing results in indels, precise sequence replacement, tagging or larger genomic deletions. Species-specific differences are illustrated by efficient NHEJ-mediated disruption in Toxoplasma, donor-dependent repair in Plasmodium and Cryptosporidium, SSA-associated repair in Leishmania, efficient homologous recombination in trypanosomatids, precise editing in Babesia, and stage-specific delivery constraints in Theileria. The review further examines the progression from single-gene editing to marker-free manipulation, base editing, conditional approaches and genome-wide functional screens. Cas12a, CRISPRi/a, prime editing and related systems are discussed as emerging extensions. Overall, this repair- and delivery-centred framework explains why CRISPR editing differs among protozoan parasites and identifies the experimentally validated limitations that currently shape their genome-engineering potential.

title: An engineered probiotic with integrated biocomputation and multi-molecular recording for precision theranostics of colitis.
text: Engineered therapeutic microbes capable of sensing and responding to diseases offer transformative potential for precision medicine. However, their capacity to intelligently process the complex and dynamic biomarkers of multifaceted diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains limited. Here, we design a probiotic system that executes logic computations through four stage-specific inflammatory biomarkers, enabling precise diagnosis and closed-loop treatment of colitis in mice. Integration with a CRISPR-based molecular recorder allows dynamic tracking of biomarker levels and converts inflammatory signals into quantifiable, site-specific base-editing events, thereby achieving precise diagnosis and analysis of disease progression within a living mammalian gut. We additionally develop a multimodal machine-learning classifier that utilizes both bioluminescent reporter signals and sequencing data to accurately stage intestinal inflammation with an accuracy of 0.83 ± 0.05. Together, this work provides a robust platform for in situ biocomputation and marks a significant advance toward intelligent, precision theranostics for gastrointestinal disorders.

title: Characterization of the SsdA deaminase-family for improved cytosine base editors.
text: The choice of a suitable cytosine deaminase is a key decision when designing a base editor. Recently, bacterial toxins with cytosine deaminase activity have been established to build potent base editors for genome editing. Among those, SsdA gained considerable traction, being highly active and among the smallest established deaminases for cytosine base editors. The toxic nature of SsdA presents the major challenge, making wild type SsdA unsuitable for base editing. Although several modifications of SsdA are available, a comparison and deeper understanding of these modifications is still missing. Here, we investigate and compare the effects of several SsdA modifications. We enable a more educated choice for researchers by characterizing several improved SsdA variants for base editing. Amino acid substitutions at a key residue in SsdA suggest that steric alterations relieve its toxic effects. Indeed, the in vitro deaminase activity of SsdA was negatively linked to its in vivo performance. This indicates that base editing performance is highly compromised by toxic side effects, making less active deaminase variants the better genome editing tools. We further characterized a set of SsdA homologous proteins and showed that they were similarly toxic as SsdA. Two of them were confirmed to be cytosine deaminases and one of these allowed the construction of a new, highly functional base editing tool. This work deepens our understanding on DYW-family cytosine deaminases and broadens their use for genome editing.

title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression.
text: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

title: Deciphering the Mechanisms Underlying Therapeutic Resistance in Cancer through Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Technologies: Current Approaches and Future Perspectives.
text: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies are recent high-throughput sequencing advancements that enable transcriptome-wide profiling and characterization of cellular populations at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue spatial context. Their integration has been increasingly applied to cancer research, facilitating a deeper understanding of tumor biology and improving diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Growing evidence suggests that combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with ST offers a robust approach for exploring mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance. Together, these technologies support the prediction and monitoring of treatment responses and help identify novel therapeutic targets by revealing critical signaling pathways and immune cell populations associated with resistance. Artificial intelligence, including deep learning, computer vision, and generative models, further enhances the integration and analysis of data generated by scRNA-seq and ST, contributing to tumor resistance research. This review summarizes recent advances in the integrated application of scRNA-seq and ST to study tumor resistance and discusses the opportunities, challenges, and future directions of these technologies as a theoretical foundation for identifying therapeutic targets and developing treatment strategies.

title: Podocarpusflavone A sensitizes MASLD-related hepatocellular carcinoma to lenvatinib by targeting ABAT and ALDH2.
text: Despite the rising global incidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-related hepatocellular carcinoma (MASLD-HCC), immunotherapy offers limited survival benefits in this non-viral etiology, positioning lenvatinib as a critical treatment that necessitates novel strategies to enhance its efficacy. This study aimed to identify MASLD-HCC signature genes and to explore a novel agent to overcome lenvatinib resistance. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified signature genes, validated by immunohistochemistry, qPCR, Western blot, and spatial transcriptomics in human and murine specimens. Virtual screening identified a natural compound targeting hub genes. Direct binding was confirmed using molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and surface plasmon resonance. Therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms were comprehensively evaluated in vitro under lipotoxic stress conditions and in vivo using diet-induced orthotopic MASLD-HCC mouse models. A 170-gene signature was established, with ABAT and ALDH2 prioritized as hub genes. Podocarpusflavone A (PCFA) emerged as a dual-targeting agent that robustly reverses acquired lenvatinib resistance. Instead of increasing protein abundance, PCFA directly binds these targets, which is accompanied by markedly enhanced cellular ABAT and ALDH activities. This diminishes the protective GABA shield and disrupts the mitochondrial NAD⁺ balance, precipitating a lethal mitochondrial superoxide burst and inhibiting key oncogenic pathways. In vivo, the PCFA and lenvatinib combination profoundly suppressed orthotopic tumor progression and was associated with short-term improvements in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis-related histological findings, with no evident toxicity under the conditions tested. PCFA combined with lenvatinib represents a promising strategy for MASLD-HCC and provides mechanistic insights into its antitumor activity.

title: Cross-cohort analyses of OLFML2B cellular distribution and stromal associations in gastric adenocarcinoma.
text: OLFML2B has been associated with gastric cancer, but the cellular basis and clinical transportability of its tissue-level signal remain uncertain. Following a five-cohort screen and literature-informed prioritisation, we evaluated bulk, single-cell, spatial and proteomic datasets and an anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-treated cohort using question-specific preprocessing and an explicit evidence hierarchy. The Cancer Genome Atlas stomach adenocarcinoma cohort showed higher tumour expression, including 33 paired comparisons (median log2-scale difference 2.28; P = 1.951 × 10⁻⁵). Random-effects meta-analyses of Spearman rank correlations across five follow-up cohorts linked OLFML2B with fibroblast, extracellular-matrix and transforming-growth-factor-beta programmes (summary correlations 0.73, 0.69 and 0.56). Heterogeneity was substantial and all prediction intervals included zero. Among 413,873 reprocessed single cells, patient-level estimates were higher for fibroblast than epithelial detection in two primary comparisons, but did not establish higher fibroblast than myeloid detection; one epithelial contrast was sensitive to detection thresholds and ambient-RNA correction. Spatial associations in nine patients provided stromal context. Only one cohort supported the common-adjustment recurrence model. Secondary overall-survival meta-analysis of three commonly adjusted cohorts yielded a hazard ratio of 1.27 (95% confidence interval 1.01-1.59), with wider intervals after cohort omission. In 30 qualified proteomic pairs, the Wilcoxon analysis supported a positive location shift (Hodges-Lehmann estimate 0.380, 95% confidence interval 0.024-0.654; P = 0.0397), with plex sensitivity. Response associations in 45 anti-PD-1-treated patients remained imprecise. These findings support a stromal-associated expression context while leaving cellular function, residual confounding and clinical transportability unresolved. Cohort disagreement does not establish absence of biological or clinical effects.

title: Animal-derived anticoagulant peptides and small proteins from snake venom and tick saliva: Mechanisms, structural biochemistry, and translational barriers.
text: Animal-derived anticoagulant peptides and small proteins from snake venom and tick saliva are valuable but underexploited molecular prototypes for antithrombotic drug discovery. Snake venom evolved under predation pressure, whereas tick saliva has been refined through long-term blood feeding. Despite their distinct origins, both systems have generated compact cysteine-rich scaffolds that interfere potently with host hemostasis. This review compares representative anticoagulant peptides and small proteins from snake venoms and tick saliva, focusing on structural features, mechanisms, and translational potential. A curated dataset of 56 tick-derived and 61 snake-derived sequences was analyzed to identify shared structural constraints and divergent functional features. Mechanistically, these molecules target multiple coagulation nodes including the TF/FVIIa complex, contact pathway, FXa and thrombin activity, platelet aggregation, and fibrin formation. Beyond classical active-site blockade, we discuss allosteric inhibition via exosite occupancy exemplified by ixolaris and the active-site-inhibited derivative FFR-notecarin D, while noting that native notecarin D is a prothrombin activator and is not itself an anticoagulant. In silico docking of representative peptides, including TAP, ultravariegin, BF9-N17K-L19D, and ACH-11, was performed to generate structural hypotheses. Major translational barriers such as immunogenicity, rapid renal clearance, low oral bioavailability, and source scarcity are reinterpreted from a structural perspective. We conclude by outlining possible future directions, including AI-guided scaffold cyclization, exosite-selective mutagenesis, and responsive nanocarrier-peptide conjugates, which may contribute to the development of potentially safer FXI and FXII targeted antithrombotics if validated experimentally. Integrating structural biology, computational prediction, and mechanism-guided engineering will be essential to convert these natural prototypes into clinically relevant therapeutics.

title: From static structures to conformational ensembles: Artificial intelligence for protein sampling and dynamics.
text: After sparking a revolution in protein structure prediction, machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) are now reshaping the modeling of protein conformational ensembles and dynamics. A fast, scalable, and accurate representation of protein conformational ensembles could enable genome-scale studies of protein function, with broad applications in drug discovery and protein engineering. The challenges associated with this goal, however, are far greater than those involved in single structure prediction because of the broad timescales spanned by protein motion, the complex relationship between sequence and dynamics, and the scarcity of datasets with experimental measurements. Despite these difficulties, many promising solutions have emerged in recent years, ranging from accelerated molecular dynamics to direct sampling of the conformational distribution, as well as some hybrid methods. Here, we review recent AI-powered approaches to tackle protein dynamics and conformational sampling, and outline their current limitations.

title: Tumor digital twins uncover therapeutic strategies in triple-negative breast cancer.
text: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options and a high risk of relapse and mortality. Consequently, there is a critical need for personalized treatment strategies that reflect the unique biology, clonal architecture, and evolutionary dynamics of individual tumors. Here, we present a TNBC digital twin framework, built from prior knowledge and formulated as a mechanistic qualitative network in which nodes represent genes and proteins and edges denote the interactions between them. Parameterized with patient-specific molecular data, the model identifies potential resistance mechanisms and proposes tailored treatment plans to overcome them. We validate the model using clinical data from PARTNER, a large, randomized controlled trial evaluating platinum-based chemotherapy with or without PARP inhibitors. The model accurately predicts treatment responses and identifies mutational and transcriptional biomarkers associated with clinical outcome. Our approach offers an interpretable alternative to black-box predictive models, enabling transparent decision-making in precision oncology.

title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages through TLR4 N-glycosylation: A GnT-V mRNA delivery strategy to improve PD-1 inhibitor responsiveness.
text: PD-1 inhibitors have revolutionized cancer treatment, but their antitumor efficacy is limited by various constraints, including the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) driven by tumor-promoting tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). Reprogramming TAMs toward an antitumor state is a promising strategy to boost PD-1 inhibitor efficacy. However, the strategies for driving this switch remain poorly defined. Herein, we identified N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase-V (GnT-V) as a critical regulator of TAM reprogramming and PD-1 inhibitor responsiveness. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of PD-1 inhibitor-sensitive and resistant patients revealed that GnT-V expression was enriched in antitumor TAMs and positively correlated with the PD-1 inhibitor response. Validation data from spontaneous/xenograft tumors in mice and in vitro co-culture systems showed that GnT-V overexpression drives TAM repolarization toward an antitumor phenotype and enhances anti-PD-1 sensitivity. Mechanistically, GnT-V catalyzes β1,6-branched N-glycosylation of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) at Asn526 and Asn575, stabilizing TLR4 and sustaining NF-κB activation to drive antitumor TAM polarization and T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. To translate this mechanistic axis into a therapeutic strategy, we employed a clinically relevant mRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platform for in situ TAM reprogramming. The mRNA-LNP platform delivered GnT-V mRNA with high stability, achieved efficient GnT-V expression in a TAM-preferential manner, and showed no apparent systemic toxicity. Functionally, the platform-delivered GnT-V repolarized TAMs, reshaped the immunosuppressive TME, and synergized with anti-PD-1 to improve antitumor efficacy in vivo. Our findings establish the GnT-V/TLR4 N-glycosylation axis as a switch that governs TAM reprogramming and offer a promising biomaterial-based strategy that combines GnT-V mRNA delivery with anti-PD-1 therapy to overcome PD-1 inhibitor resistance.

title: Engineering Tunable Helper Lipid Architecture to Improve Messenger RNA Lipid Nanoparticle Performance.
text: Helper lipids are essential structural components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), yet systematic design principles linking helper lipid architecture to messenger RNA (mRNA) delivery performance remain poorly defined. Here we identify helper lipid architecture as a major, largely unexplored design lever for optimizing LNP performance. Using a modular library of more than 80 rationally designed helper lipids, we show that systematic variation in headgroup chemistry, linker topology, and tail cardinality reshapes both LNP biophysical behavior and biological performance. Martini molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with multimodal structural analyses reveal that high-performing scaffolds undergo a pH-dependent transition into fusogenic inverse hexagonal-like ordering, substantially lowering the energetic barrier for endosomal escape. These performance gains persist across the clinically relevant ALC-0315 and DLin-MC3-DMA platforms, establishing helper lipid architecture as a transferable design parameter across distinct ionizable lipid chemistries. Translating these design principles into function, optimized helper lipid formulations restore hepatic protein expression in a mouse model of ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency and increase antigen expression and immunogenicity in both preclinical models and in the in vitro human MIMIC platform. Together, these findings establish helper lipids as tunable molecular actuators of potency, tolerability, and stability, offering an engineering framework for next-generation mRNA vaccines and therapeutics.

title: Securing Cell-Free Expression: Safeguards for Distributed Biomanufacturing.
text: Cell-free expression (CFE) is an acellular biomanufacturing platform capable of producing diverse biomolecules, including proteins, enzymes, and mRNA, outside of living cells. Unlike traditional bioproduction, which requires sterile culture systems and large-scale bioreactors, CFE enables rapid, modular, and decentralized synthesis. CFE extracts can be freeze-dried, stored for extended periods, and reactivated on demand by simply adding a nucleic acid template. This makes it particularly suited for point-of-need applications such as diagnostics, vaccines, and potentially therapeutics in remote, resource-limited, or emergency settings. However, the same features introduce novel biosecurity concerns. Commercially available CFE kits already support the production of bacteriophages and virus-like particles with minimal specialized equipment. As benchtop DNA synthesis and CFE technologies become increasingly accessible, barriers of skill, facilities, and resources are significantly reduced, enabling malicious actors or small autonomous groups to generate harmful biological agents. To address these risks while enabling safe deployment, we recommend: (1) investing in yield optimization and the development of modular, good manufacturing practice-compatible CFE units for distributed manufacturing (performance and scalability); (2) engineering CFE systems with bioorthogonal or otherwise nontransferable components to reduce potential misuse (intrinsic safety feature); and (3) implementing risk-based restrictions for different CFE formulations, balancing innovation with security oversight (tiered access controls).
