By combining these measures, CFE can be responsibly integrated into global health security infrastructure, delivering its transformative benefits without compromising biosecurity.

title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity.
text: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

title: Multiplexed Fc array assays reveal the influence of TLR3 on the Th1-biased humoral response induced in mice following live-attenuated RVFV vaccination.
text: Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) can cause severe disease in humans and livestock. Several vaccine candidates are immunogenic and protective in pre-clinical animal models. Reported measurements of humoral immunity following vaccination typically assess antigen-specific activity, such as virus binding or neutralization, but do not consider the role of the Fc region. To address this knowledge gap, multiplexed Fc array assays were developed to characterize the Fc profile of antigen-specific antibodies following RVFV vaccination. The RVFV nucleocapsid protein (N) and glycoproteins (Gn/Gc) were conjugated to magnetic microspheres, and monoclonal antibodies were used to optimize assay conditions. Sera from vaccinated mice were incubated with the conjugated microspheres to capture antigen-specific antibodies, and then various detection reagents were used to measure the isotype of the antibodies and their ability to bind Fc receptors (FcRs) or complement (C1q). Two studies involving mice vaccinated with live-attenuated RVFV ΔNSsΔNSm or ΔNSs were used to demonstrate the utility of these assays. In WT C57BL/6 mice, both ΔNSsΔNSm and ΔNSs induced a high magnitude of IgG2c antibodies, indicative of a Th1-biased response; these antibodies also bound the four murine FcRs and C1q. However, following ΔNSs infection of a panel of innate immune knockout (KO) mice, several strains of KO mice, especially TLR3 KO, exhibited a reduced magnitude of IgG2c antibodies, demonstrating the impact of innate immunity on the Th1-biased response. Overall, the multiplexed Fc array assays performed as expected and can be applied to other RVFV vaccine platforms in the future to help inform rational vaccine design. There are currently no approved vaccines to prevent RVFV infection in humans. While some vaccine candidates exist, such as the live-attenuated ΔNSsΔNSm vaccine, most immunogenicity studies do not consider the contribution of the Fc region to antibody quality. In this study, multiplexed Fc array assays were developed to assess the Fc profile of antigen-specific antibodies following RVFV vaccination. These assays proved to be useful in identifying a Th1-biased response induced by RVFV ΔNSsΔNSm and ΔNSs and in identifying the contribution of innate immunity to this response. These assays can be applied to other RVFV vaccine platforms, such as mRNA and protein vaccines, to fully characterize the quality of an antibody response following vaccination.

title: mRNA-LNP delivery of a homo-tandem nanobody protects goslings from novel goose astrovirus infection.
text: Novel goose astrovirus (nGAstV) infection causes visceral gout and high mortality in goslings, but at present, there are no effective vaccines or antiviral agents. Here, we identified a neutralizing nanobody (Nb60) targeting the spike (P2) protein of nGAstV capable of inhibiting viral replication by blocking both viral attachment and entry. For effective in vivo delivery, we designed an mRNA-encoded homo-tandem nanobody (3×Nb60) flanked by an Anser interleukin-2 (IL-2) signal peptide and Anser untranslated regions that exhibited an approximately twofold improvement in neutralization potency compared to the mRNA-encoded Nb60 monomer. The mRNA encoding nanobody was encapsulated with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to prolong its half-life in serum by approximately 48 h. In a gosling infection model, the 3×Nb60 mRNA-LNP (2 mg/kg) produced 100% survival for both prophylaxis and therapy, significantly reduced viral shedding and viral loads in tissues, attenuated hepatic and renal pathology, and restored serum uric acid, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase levels to close to the baseline values. Epitope mapping revealed that Nb60 recognizes a critical conformational epitope on the P2 protein, with residues 529R and 553G being essential for binding. The findings establish an mRNA-encoded nanobody platform as a promising strategy for prophylaxis and therapy in the early stages of nGAstV infection.IMPORTANCENovel goose astrovirus (nGAstV) has caused widespread outbreaks of visceral gout in goslings across China since 2017, leading to substantial economic losses in the poultry industry. The disease predominantly affects goslings under 3 weeks of age, and the short disease course limits the utility of conventional vaccines. This study establishes an mRNA-encoded nanobody (Nb) platform in which avian-specific regulatory elements, including an Anser IL-2 signal peptide and an Anser globin untranslated region, enable efficient expression of a neutralizing Nb60 in avian cells. A homo-tandem design (3×Nb60) further prolongs the in vivo half-life, improves antiviral potency, and provides complete protection in goslings. By offering a species-matched delivery framework, this platform provides a rapid-response strategy for emerging avian viral diseases and may also shed light on the development of mRNA-encoded antibody therapeutics against human enteric viruses.

title: A multivalent mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine containing eight hemagglutinin antigens elicited broad neutralizing antibody responses and protected against influenza A virus challenge in swine.
text: The diversity within H1 and H3 subtype influenza A viruses (IAVs) in swine prevents effective vaccine control approaches with inactivated whole-virus vaccines. We addressed the challenge of controlling co-circulating hemagglutinin (HA) clades of swine IAV with the development of a multivalent messenger RNA (mRNA)-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine expressing eight HA proteins to maximize genetic coverage. We applied a computational approach to select eight HA genes that represented 95% of the observed IAVs detected in the United States between 2022 and 2025. Piglets were vaccinated and boosted intramuscularly with either individual HA mRNA-LNP or an 8-HA multivalent mRNA-LNP. Serum was collected to evaluate systemic antibody levels. Twenty-one days post-boost, pigs were challenged with a field-relevant H1 1A.3.3.3-c3 IAV strain. The 8-HA multivalent mRNA-LNP vaccine induced neutralizing antibodies against all eight antigens, and vaccinees were protected against lung lesions, with lesion scores similar to non-challenged animals. Homologous monovalent vaccination significantly reduced IAV detection in nasal secretions and in the lungs. Heterologous monovalent vaccination was not cross-protective but did not induce vaccine-associated enhanced respiratory disease. We provide evidence that monovalent and multivalent mRNA-LNP influenza vaccines elicited neutralizing antibody responses in pigs and protected against viral challenge. The versatility and capacity for rapidly updating the mRNA-LNP vaccine platform make it an appealing tool to improve animal health and minimize the circulation and diversity of IAV in swine.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A virus (IAV) is an important respiratory pathogen in swine, and zoonotic transmission of swine strains to humans remains a public health risk. Control strategies against IAV in swine herds rely heavily on biosecurity measures and vaccination. However, the antigenic diversity of IAV circulating in swine challenges current vaccination programs, and there is a need for broadly protective vaccines or platforms that can rapidly update components to reflect circulating diversity. mRNA-LNP vaccines have emerged as promising vaccine platforms, offering simultaneous delivery of multiple antigens, rapid development, scalable manufacturing, and potent immunogenicity. In this study, we assessed the immunogenicity and protective capacity of monovalent and multivalent mRNA-LNP vaccines encoding eight representative IAV hemagglutinin (HA) antigens. To our knowledge, this is the first study to objectively select multiple representative endemic swine IAV strains by quantifying genetic diversity within the phylogeny and to apply this selection to rationally design and evaluate a multivalent HA mRNA-based influenza vaccine in the swine model.

title: H5 influenza virus mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccination elicits adaptive immune responses in Holstein calves.
text: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 circulated widely in lactating dairy cows in the United States following the initial detection in 2024. Due to the critical need for intervention strategies for this outbreak, we evaluated antibody and cellular immune responses of a clade 2.3.4.4b H5 mRNA-LNP vaccine in calves. We found that the H5 mRNA-LNP vaccine induced a robust antibody and CD8+ T cell-mediated immune response and conferred protection against clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 infection.IMPORTANCEIt is important to develop vaccines that limit clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 infection in cattle. In this study, we found that a new H5 mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine is immunogenic when delivered intramuscularly to male Holstein calves.

title: In vitro wrapping of nonenveloped viral capsids with lipid bilayers.
text: In vitro reconstituted virus-like particles (VLPs)-particles with structure identical to those of virus particles except for containing noninfectious genetic information instead of a viral genome-are promising nanocarriers for delivery of therapeutic cargos. Among the simplest examples are the VLPs formed from the capsid protein (CP) of either Cowpea Chlorotic Mottle Virus (CCMV) or Brome Mosaic Virus (BMV), which form spontaneously from purified components upon mixing CCMV or BMV CP with single-stranded RNA under the right pH and ionic strength conditions. The structure of these VLPs is identical to that of the virus particles, consisting of 180 copies of the CP organized as 12 icosahedrally symmetric pentamers separated by 20 hexamers. In contrast, most viruses that infect mammalian cells are enveloped by a lipid bilayer filled with transmembrane virally encoded glycoproteins, and it has not yet proved possible to reconstitute these particles from their purified components. To take advantage of the robustness of unenveloped virus capsids and the biocompatibility of lipid-bilayer-wrapped particles, we demonstrate in vitro lipid-bilayer wrapping of intact plant viral (CCMV and BMV) capsids. Lipid compositions are chosen to match the opposite charge of the viral capsid, to promote stable membrane association. Our results provide an important first step toward the wrapping of in vitro reconstituted VLPs containing therapeutic mRNA. These enveloped virus-like particles combine the stability and scalability of plant virus capsids with the functional advantages of lipid envelopes, advancing their potential as platforms for RNA delivery, vaccine design, and therapeutic nanotechnology.

title: Public Health Informatics Practice in Governmental Health Departments in the United States: Scoping Review.
text: Public health informatics has been defined as "the systematic application of information and computer science and technology to public health practice, research, and learning" and is particularly critical to the design and implementation of systems and networks that support the activities of public health jurisdictions. Many literature or scoping reviews have focused on specific concepts within informatics but have left a gap in understanding the overall trends in published literature across the breadth of public health informatics practice. A broader assessment may better reflect the full scope of current practice and more comprehensively characterize the evolution of this field. This review was aimed at characterizing the current practice of public health informatics within the United States, specifically within governmental health departments. The PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines and recommendations were followed. Three databases were searched for various public health informatics terms: PubMed, the National Library of Medicine's biomedical literature database, which includes MEDLINE and other resources; ProQuest Public Health Database; and CINAHL. Two reviewers assessed the articles using a 2-tiered process first to determine eligibility based on the inclusion criteria and the second to identify the informatics implementation and jurisdiction. A total of 4581 publications were identified, of which 141 duplicate articles across the 3 data sources and 25 articles published prior to 2010 were removed. Based on initial screening of titles and metadata, 3249 articles were removed. The remaining 1166 articles underwent abstract and full-text review, resulting in 229 articles that met all eligibility criteria. Among the themes represented, 30.80% of articles involved surveillance systems or disease registries and 24.05% addressed aspects of health information exchange (HIE), including connecting to HIE entities, performing direct exchange between clinical systems, or developing system interoperability. State health departments accounted for 32.07% of the published articles, followed by federal or tribal implementations (30.38%). Implementations at local health departments were the least frequent (16.03%). A growing body of published literature and gray materials focuses on public health informatics. This scoping review buttresses other published scoping reviews by providing a cross-sectional view of applied public health informatics across public health authorities in the United States. This cross-sectional view offers a foundation for further characterizing informatics practice within these authorities. The broad distribution of publications across different public health jurisdictions provides support for the idea that most authorities are involved in informatics practice in one way or another.

title: Artificial intelligence-based finish-line detection and margin-related accuracy in fixed prosthodontic digital workflows: A systematic review and functional meta-synthesis.
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly incorporated into fixed prosthodontic digital workflows, but evidence regarding finish-line detection, margin handling, and margin-related crown accuracy remains heterogeneous. The purpose of this systematic review was to evaluate AI-based finish-line detection, margin-line extraction, and margin-related accuracy in tooth-supported fixed prosthodontic workflows using a functional meta-synthesis. The PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases were searched through May 2026. Studies evaluating AI, machine learning, or deep learning for finish-line detection, margin extraction, crown design, margin-aware crown generation, or margin-related accuracy were included. Findings were synthesized according to the functional role of AI, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using an adapted quality framework. A total of 17 studies were included. AI demonstrated measurable performance for margin detection and supported crown-design workflows, frequently reducing design time. Marginal and internal adaptation were generally clinically acceptable or comparable with conventional workflows, although superiority was inconsistent. Quantitative pooling was precluded by substantial methodological and outcome heterogeneity. AI showed technical feasibility for margin-sensitive fixed prosthodontic workflows, but current evidence remains heterogeneous, predominantly early-stage, and insufficient to establish consistent clinical superiority.

title: Mass spectrometry and machine learning for classification and molecular phenotyping of renal cell carcinoma and benign tumors.
text: Pathology classification of cancer tumor subtypes and benign tumors can be difficult due to cellular heterogeneity and similar morphological features. Renal Cell Cancer (RCC) poses a major challenge for uropathologists as advanced RCC is often incidentally diagnosed with complex histological characteristics. We hypothesised that molecular profiling of RCC and benign tumor specimen by mass spectrometry with machine learning methods enable accurate tumor classification and identification of candidate RCC biomarkers. MALDI-MSI and quantitative proteomics (LC-MS) provided peptide and protein profiles of RCC neoplasms and benign tumors presented in tissue microarray (TMA) format of 541 tissue cores from 126 patients. Machine learning models classified RCC subtypes: Clear cell RCC (ccRCC), Chromophobe RCC (chRCC), papillary RCC (pRCC), and oncocytoma (OC). Known and novel candidate protein biomarker panels for discrimination of RCC subtypes were identified. RCC peptide mapping, evaluated using patient-level cross-validation, reliably classified ccRCC and healthy tissue, but did not reliably discriminate the diagnostically challenging RCC subtypes chRCC vs OC. Quantitative proteomics identified over 5000 proteins and classified all four RCC subtypes with 95.5% patient-level accuracy, including robust discrimination of chRCC from oncocytoma. We report new candidate protein biomarkers for ccRCC and pRCC and distinguish histologically similar subtypes OC (benign) and chRCC (malignant), as demonstrated by mass spectrometry-based immunohistochemistry. Candidate prognostic biomarkers for ccRCC contribute to risk of relapse (CDK6, ATM) and risk of metastasis (DDB2, MK03). Digital histo-molecular differentiation of cancer tumor subtypes and benign tumors by mass spectrometry and macbine learning enables retrospective and prospective studies. Identified candidate protein biomarkers complement existing protocols in tumor pathology.

title: Predictors and biological correlates of anxiety response to virtual reality-based cognitive behavioural therapy after acute myocardial infarction: A secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial.
text: Anxiety after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) worsens prognosis. A randomized trial showed that 1-week immersive virtual reality-based cognitive behavioural therapy (VR-CBT) reduces anxiety in hospitalized patients with AMI; its primary results are published. This secondary analysis examined responder rates, depressive symptoms, biomarkers, cardiac safety, and response prediction. The completer set (62 VR-CBT, 74 control) was analyzed. Response was a Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA) reduction ≥50%. Biomarkers, impedance cardiography, and 12‑lead electrocardiography were assessed. Seven machine-learning models and a LASSO-based nomogram were compared (stratified 5-fold cross-validation ×3); a linear mixed model (LMM) assessed HAMA trajectories. Response rates at end of intervention were 59.7% vs 17.6% (P < 0.001). At 3 months the responder endpoint did not differ (35.6% vs 38.2%, P = 0.902), even after baseline adjustment (adjusted OR 0.61, P = 0.246); only the adjusted LMM suggested a marginal residual effect (B = -2.41, P = 0.048). Depressive symptoms improved more with VR-CBT (P < 0.001). IL-6 declined in both groups (borderline greater with VR-CBT, P = 0.051). No hemodynamic or arrhythmic safety signal emerged in the available data; QTc change favored VR-CBT (P = 0.016). The nomogram (treatment allocation, marital status, baseline HAMA) discriminated best (pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.762). Single-center, complete-case secondary analysis; baseline symptom imbalance; no external validation of prediction models. VR-CBT after AMI produced substantial short-term responder-level gains and no cardiac safety signal; whether the benefit persists after discharge remains uncertain. An interpretable nomogram may help clinicians estimate individual response likelihood with versus without VR-CBT.

title: Early Prehospital Prediction of Neurological Outcome After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Derivation and External Validation of the MIRA-29 Score.
text: Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA. MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC). Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99. MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

title: Survival Prediction Models for Metastatic Bone Disease: A Comprehensive Review of Development, External Validation, and Clinical Applicability.
text: Accurate survival estimation fundamentally guides treatment strategy for metastatic bone disease, balancing durable surgical reconstruction against palliative care. Over three decades, predictive tools have evolved from static classical scores into sophisticated nomograms and machine learning algorithms, integrating patient reserve, tumor biology, metastatic burden, and treatment context. In this comprehensive review, we systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science and identified 25 studies reporting the development or external validation of multivariable survival prediction models, encompassing classical scoring systems (Tokuhashi, Tomita, Bauer, Katagiri), nomograms (SORG), Bayesian networks (PATHFx), and machine learning algorithms (SORG-MLA, BMETS). While this methodological evolution improved individualized prognostication in derivation cohorts, external validation studies reveal a critical disconnect: algorithmic complexity does not guarantee clinical transportability. Our synthesis identifies several recurrent sources of this transportability failure, primarily temporal calibration drift from evolving systemic therapies, anatomic site mismatches between spinal and appendicular disease, and selection biases inherent to surgical versus radiotherapeutic cohorts. Consequently, a substantial gap persists between methodological sophistication and actual bedside applicability, and routine clinical deployment of these tools remains premature until these foundational deficits are systematically addressed. Bridging this gap requires shifting from universal prediction tools toward context-specific, prospectively validated models with routine temporal recalibration.

title: Oncology LLM evaluation: From benchmark performance to clinical readiness.
text: Large language models (LLMs) perform increasingly well on medical benchmarks, yet benchmark success does not necessarily establish clinical readiness in oncology. Building on recent critiques of medical LLM evaluation, this Perspective identifies four benchmark-practice mismatches: complete-information benchmarks versus active information gathering, single reference answers versus preference-sensitive decisions, cross-sectional snapshots versus longitudinal disease trajectories, and standalone model performance versus model-in-system readiness. To address these gaps, we propose a four-stage evaluation paradigm progressing from a structured knowledge and reasoning baseline to interactive and dialogue-based evaluation, longitudinal trajectory assessment, and model-in-system evaluation. Grounded in the longitudinal, multimodal, and multidisciplinary nature of oncology care, the framework emphasizes the need to calibrate evaluation to intended use and clinical risk and to sustain assessment through continuous monitoring across the model life cycle. Together, these principles offer an operational and oncology-specific pathway for building progressively stronger evidence of clinical readiness.

title: Advancing research approaches in nurse education: Embracing complexity and innovation.
text: Nurse education is embedded in complex settings, from classrooms and simulation laboratories to clinical learning environments, in which individual and organisational factors interact and shape educational, clinical, organisational and professional outcomes. This complexity challenges the research methods used to study nurse education. From a quantitative perspective, nurse education research has traditionally relied on descriptive and correlational designs, with limited adoption of experimental designs and advanced quantitative methodologies. On the qualitative side, researchers can gain an in-depth understanding of the experiences of students, clinical mentors, and academic educators. However, qualitative research often presents flaws in methodological rigour and congruence. Therefore, rigorous, theory-driven and data-informed approaches are needed. Advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning offer new possibilities and pose new challenges for both quantitative and qualitative methodological approaches. Using Complex Adaptive Systems theory as a conceptual framework, this paper outlines emerging quantitative and qualitative approaches to uncover new insights in nurse and healthcare education research. Embracing such approaches can provide practical, evidence-informed perspectives to guide educators, educational institutions and healthcare organisations.

title: Structural MRI Morphometry Across the Alzheimer's Disease Spectrum: Classification and Generalization.
text: Structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides quantitative measures of brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), but reliable classification also depends on the evaluation protocol and performance across cohorts. This study assessed a morphometry-based approach for distinguishing cognitively normal (CN) participants, those with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and those with AD. The primary cohort included 815 participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), with one screening MRI per participant and predefined training, validation, and test sets. MRI records were linked to FreeSurfer measurements using exact participant and image identifiers. A multinomial L2-regularized logistic regression classifier used 42 predefined structural features and five-fold cross-validation grouped by acquisition site. In the held-out three-class test (n = 121), balanced accuracy was 0.6119 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.5291-0.6873) and the macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) was 0.7525. Recall was 0.8529 for CN, 0.2931 for MCI, and 0.6897 for AD. Additional development analyses examined demographic and clinical variables separately from the primary MRI-only result. For the binary transfer experiment, a separate ADNI-trained CN-versus-AD model using 32 shared morphometric features achieved balanced accuracy of 0.8458 and ROC-AUC of 0.9016 in site-grouped out-of-fold evaluation. The fixed model was then tested without target-cohort tuning on 181 older participants from the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS-1), grouped by Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR = 0 versus CDR > 0). External balanced accuracy was 0.6492 (95% CI: 0.5799-0.7158) and ROC-AUC was 0.7502. Because ADNI diagnoses and OASIS-1 CDR groups are not identical clinical endpoints, the external experiment was interpreted separately from the primary three-class analysis. The results demonstrate the value of reporting class-specific performance and independent-cohort evaluation when assessing structural MRI morphometry.

title: Bridging the Gender Gap in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Machine Learning Approach to Screening Women for Moderate-to-Severe Disease.
text: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) can lead to severe complications if left untreated. Several challenges hinder OSA identification in females, resulting in underdiagnosis and undertreatment in this population. This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) approach specifically tailored to screen women for moderate-to-severe OSA. A retrospective study was conducted using clinical records of 1,210 women who underwent polysomnography at our institution. Collected data included demographics, body metrics, nocturnal oxygen saturation levels, medical conditions, medications, laboratory measurements, and polysomnography results. Four ML algorithms were employed to classify participants into moderate-to-severe and none-to-mild OSA groups. Due to the high missingness of laboratory values in the whole cohort, two sets of models were developed: one utilizing all subjects but excluding lab tests, and another restricted to a subgroup of 383 participants that additionally incorporated hemoglobin and lipid profile alongside the other features. Without laboratory measurements, the best-performing model was adaptive boosting, which achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and accuracy of 0.811 and 76.03%, respectively. When lab tests were included, gradient boosting machine outperformed its competitors, with the above metrics reaching 0.872 and 84.42%, respectively. The promising performance of our approach underlines the potential of artificial intelligence in refining screening strategies for OSA in women. Nadir oxygen saturation during sleep emerged as a particularly strong predictor, reinforcing the central role of nocturnal hypoxemia in OSA risk stratification. Future research should focus on incorporating broader clinical inputs and using larger, diverse datasets to develop a highly accurate, robust model that meets clinical standards and is suitable for real-world implementation. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) can lead to severe complications if left untreated, yet it is often underdiagnosed in women due to several diagnostic challenges. This study sought to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) approach specifically tailored to screen for moderate-to-severe OSA in females, facilitating timely identification and treatment. Our strategy demonstrated a promising performance, underlining the potential of AI to improve OSA screening in women. Nadir oxygen saturation during sleep emerged as a key predictor, highlighting the importance of nocturnal hypoxemia in OSA risk stratification. As one of the first studies to develop AI models exclusively for females, our work emphasizes the importance of sex-specific approaches in enhancing OSA screening accuracy.

title: The 32nd Annual Prostate Cancer Foundation Scientific Retreat Report.
text: The 32nd Annual Prostate Cancer Foundation (PCF) Scientific Retreat took place in Carlsbad, CA on October 23-25, 2025. The Annual PCF Scientific Retreat is a global forum for presenting the newest basic, translational, and clinical discoveries in prostate cancer, alongside work from related fields. Presentations highlight discoveries with strong potential to advance prostate cancer understanding, change clinical practice, and improve patient outcomes. The 2025 PCF Retreat featured research and special lectures from many disciplines, including: (i) next-generation theranostics; (ii) emerging immunotherapy approaches in prostate cancer; (iii) understanding and drugging the epigenome; (iv) clinical trial updates; (v) artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning; (vi) circulating biomarkers; (vii) harnessing the host microbiome in cancer; (viii) exercise interventions for patients with prostate cancer; (ix) CYP17A1-independent androgen biosynthesis as a mechanism of persistent androgen production; (x) Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for trial design and response assessment; (xi) tissue-guided optimization of combination therapy; (xii) PCF Women in Science Lifetime Achievement Award lecture; and (xiii) bridging biomedical research and drug development. The 2025 PCF Scientific Retreat illustrated how advances across diverse fields, including theranostics, immunotherapy, epigenetics, AI, and liquid biopsy, are converging to reshape how prostate cancer is understood, monitored, and treated. Recurring themes included tumor heterogeneity and lineage plasticity as determinants of treatment response, the need for predictive biomarkers to guide increasingly intensive and combination therapies, and the movement of effective therapies into earlier disease settings. This report reflects the state of the science as of October 2025.

title: Machine Learning-based Cluster Analysis Identifies Three Clinically Relevant Phenotypes of Patients With Degenerative Lumbar Scoliosis With Distinct Clinical Profiles and Postoperative Outcomes.
text: A retrospective observational study. This study aimed to apply machine learning-based clustering to identify distinct phenotypes of DLS patients with diverse clinical profiles and recovery ﻿﻿trajectories. Patients with degenerative lumbar scoliosis (DLS) exhibit substantial heterogeneity in pathology, baseline impairments, frailty, and surgical expectations. However, existing classification systems primarily rely on radiographic parameters and fail to integrate multidimensional patient characteristics, limiting their ability to capture patient heterogeneity and guide individualized surgical strategies. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was performed to determine possible patient phenotypes based on a set of screened preoperative demographic, clinical, and radiographic variables. Goodness-of-fit indices were used to determine the optimal cluster number. Baseline and outcome differences among phenotypes were evaluated using analysis of variance and subsequent post hoc Tukey's test. A phenotype classification tool was then established and deployed as a web-based application for clinical use. A total of 257 DLS patients were included. Three distinct phenotypes were identified: (1) mild type (n=98, 38.1%), characterized by younger age, minimal deformity, and the most favorable recovery with the lowest dissatisfaction; (2) frailty-dominant type (n=95, 37.0%), defined by advanced age, higher frailty burden, slower recovery, and persistent postoperative pain; and (3) deformity-dominant type (n=64, 24.9%), marked by severe coronal and sagittal malalignment, greater surgical complexity, and the highest rate of postoperative residual coronal malalignment. Across all phenotypes, combined lateral-posterior approaches reduced blood loss and instrumented levels compared with posterior-only approaches. Notably, in frailty-dominant patients, combined approaches further improved early ambulation (46.9% vs. 17.5%, P=0.002) and reduced dissatisfaction (21.9% vs. 44.4%, P=0.031). The phenotype classification tool demonstrated good agreement with the LPA-derived phenotype assignments (F1-score: 0.866). Machine learning-based clustering identified three distinct phenotypes of DLS patients. This classification captures the multidimensional heterogeneity of patients with DLS and highlights the importance of phenotype-specific surgical strategies. The accompanying web-based classification tool offers a practical means to integrate these findings into routine clinical practice. III.

title: Application of Machine Learning Algorithms to Health Systems Planning and Public Policy Using Real-World Data: Scoping Review.
text: The rapid advancement of information technology and machine learning (ML) has garnered significant interest from health care managers and policymakers. However, incorporating reliable and transparent predictions into health systems remains challenging, necessitating an investigation into gaps in digital health interventions within real-world settings characterized by resource constraints and reliability issues. This study aimed to map and synthesize the available evidence on the application of ML algorithms to real-world data in health systems and identify their operational targets and clinical implications for health planning and public policy formulation. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines, we searched the PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and LILACS databases for empirical studies published between 2016 and 2025 that evaluated the application of ML to health management, surgical queues, and public policy using real-world data. The study protocol was retrospectively registered with the OSF. Of the studies identified through the database searches (2016-2025), only 6 empirical studies met all inclusion criteria, revealing that the real-world deployment of ML in health management and public policy remains at an early stage. The included models addressed micro-operational tasks, such as surgical blood transfusion forecasting, early warning system mortality prediction, postsurgical discharge planning, laboratory error detection, patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) prediction, and emergency care classification. Although high discriminatory performance was reported (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.76-0.99), the studies were limited by single-center retrospective designs, a lack of independent external validation, and inadequate reporting of model calibration. Current evidence on ML for macrolevel health planning and public policy formulation is limited and micro-operationally focused. Translating these algorithms into public health governance (eg, waiting list regulation in universal health systems such as the Sistema Único de Saúde [SUS]) requires moving beyond "black-box" predictions toward explainable AI (XAI), natural language processing (NLP) to analyze unstructured data, transparent model calibration, and rigorous evaluations of health equity.

title: Identification of Proteomic Subtypes with Differential Responses to Immune Checkpoint Inhibition in Cutaneous Melanoma.
text: Predictive biomarkers for combined PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade in metastatic melanoma remain limited. We analyzed pretreatment proteogenomic data to define response and resistance biology. We profiled 208 pretreatment FFPE specimens from patients with metastatic cutaneous melanoma treated across 12 institutions, including 164 receiving dual PD-1+CTLA-4 blockade (Discovery, n=97; Validation 1, n=67) and 44 receiving PD-1 monotherapy. Tumors underwent TMT-based proteomics, RNA sequencing, and targeted/low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Pathway clustering, survival modeling, deconvolution, and machine-learning classification defined and validated subtype signatures. Proteomic pathway clustering identified three reproducible ICI subtypes: immune-enriched ICI-sensitive, ribosome-high, and EMT-like/stromal-enriched. Subtypes stratified progression-free survival after dual ICI in the Discovery (P=0.01) and Validation 1 cohorts (P=0.02). The ICI-sensitive subtype had the highest responder fraction (74% and 73%), compared with ribosome-high (67% and 60%) and EMT-like tumors (44% and 43%) in the Discovery and Validation 1 cohorts, respectively. Subtype-outcome associations were consistent with previous immunotherapy datasets, with pooled hazard ratios ≈0.5-0.8 for immune-enriched tumors. Subtypes plus clinical variables predicted 3-year progression/death better than clinical variables alone in Validation 1 (AUC 0.80 vs 0.64). A 127-protein classifier recapitulated subtype membership in Validation 1 (AUC 0.89-0.97) and predicted 3-year progression/death with AUC 0.79. Subtypes reflected distinct immune, translational, and stromal/ECM programs and nominated POLR3A-associated biology as a candidate resistance axis. Proteomic pathway states define reproducible, biologically interpretable melanoma subtypes associated with differential benefit from dual PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade. A clinically tractable 127-protein classifier provides a foundation for prospective biomarker-driven combination immunotherapy trials.

title: Nanozyme-Catalyzed Lateral Flow Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of RNA and Protein Biomarkers.
text: Molecular diagnostics have advanced rapidly over the past decade, driven by the demand for accessible and scalable testing solutions. However, current assays often focus on single biomolecule types, limiting their ability to capture the multifactorial nature of disease. Integrating distinct molecular readouts─such as transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers─could provide richer diagnostic information and improve clinical decision-making. Here, we present MOSAIC (Multiplexed Orthogonal Sensing Assay Integrated with CRISPRZyme), a unified lateral flow assay that enables simultaneous detection of RNA and protein biomarkers using a shared nanozyme-catalyzed readout. The assay combines CRISPR/Cas13a-mediated RNA detection and antibody-based protein detection, with assay components optimized through antibody conjugation tuning, blocking agent optimization, and probe loading calibration to achieve balanced and cross-talk-free performance. Using cardiovascular disease as a model, the platform successfully detects NTproBNP and LIPCAR long noncoding RNA simultaneously from the same sample. The assay was further optimized for spiked human plasma, incorporating tailored pretreatment and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to maintain RNA stability and performance in complex biofluids. Extending its versatility, the same assay design was adapted to detect SARS-CoV-2 biomarkers, the spike (S) protein and ORF1ab gene, in pooled human saliva. To enable standardized interpretation of multiplexed readouts, we additionally developed a machine-learning-assisted computational workflow that automates strip localization, signal extraction, and calibration curve construction. Together, these results demonstrate a modular, paper-based diagnostic platform that unites transcriptomic and proteomic analyses within one assay architecture, offering a practical step toward accessible and multiplexed molecular diagnostics across diverse disease contexts.

title: Stage-Wise Identification of Gait Biomarkers Across the Progression of Diabetes and Diabetic Neuropathy.
text: Purposeof the research: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy induces progressive gait deterioration, yet most Machine Learning (ML)-based gait studies rely on binary classification frameworks that fail to capture the stage-wise biomechanical changes occurring across the diabetes neuropathy continuum. To identify stage-consistent and stage-specific gait biomarkers across three clinical groups healthy controls (N), diabetes without neuropathy (D), and diabetes with peripheral neuropathy (DPN) using an interpretable machine learning framework.MethodsGait data were collected from 394 participants (N = 109, D = 163, DPN = 122) using the Zebris FDM platform. Spatiotemporal, plantar pressure, and symmetry parameters were extracted. Four pairwise classification tasks (N vs D, D vs DPN, N vs DPN, Healthy vs Diseased) were evaluated using Results: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Logistic Regression under stratified five-fold cross-validation. Cross-validated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature selection and a final XGBoost model were used for biomarker identification and interpretation. SVM achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across all tasks (N vs D: 0.80, D vs DPN: 0.75, N vs DPN: 0.91, Healthy vs Diseased: 0.85). SHAP analysis identified bilateral heel contact time and step length as stage-consistent core biomarkers, present across all four classification tasks. Stage-specific discriminators included forefoot load-timing disruption in early diabetes, midfoot unloading and lateral symmetry reversal at the neuropathic transition, and posterior Centre of Pressure (CoP) displacement in established neuropathy.ConclusionsDiabetic gait pathology progresses in a measurable, stage-ordered sequence from early forefoot load-timing disruption through midfoot redistribution and symmetry reversal at the neuropathic transition, to global spatiotemporal deterioration in established neuropathy. The stage-wise biomarker framework presented here provides an interpretable, clinically grounded basis for gait-based screening of diabetic neuropathic progression, warranting prospective validation.

title: Health Care Workload Impacts and Cost-Effectiveness of a Metabolomic Risk Score-based Health Check for Cardiometabolic Disease Prevention in Finland
text: BackgroundPredictive metabolomics enables efficient early cardiometabolic risk detection, supporting proactive prevention over traditional reactive healthcare approaches. We evaluated the impact of a novel metabolomic risk score (MRS)-based health check on healthcare workload and long-term cost-effectiveness compared with current practices in Finlands working-age population. MethodsA de novo individual-level microsimulation model was developed to estimate labour time and cost-effectiveness when identifying individuals at risk of cardiometabolic diseases (cardiovascular diseases; CVD or type 2 diabetes; T2D). The model used synthetic data on 256,372 Finnish individuals aged 50-54 years without prior CVD or T2D. From a societal perspective, three scenarios were assessed: 1) replacing the standard health checks with MRS-based health checks, 2) replacing standard health checks with MRS-based checks plus enhanced prevention, and 3) comparing enhanced standard checks with MRS-based checks plus enhanced prevention. Outcomes included time required to identify at-risk individuals, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio per QALY gained, and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves. ResultsMRS-based health checks substantially reduce workload, saving 193,140 hours for nurses and 2,843 hours for physicians over five years. The approach is likely cost-saving across all scenarios, with discounted long-term savings ranging from {euro}27 million to {euro}258 million. In scenarios 1-2, QALYs improve, with gains from 1,316 to 10,813. In scenario 3, no QALY gains are observed, and minor losses occur due to differences in baseline risk stratification. ConclusionsMRS-based health checks in primary and occupational care reduce workload and are likely a cost-saving strategy with potential health outcome benefits in identifying individuals at risk of cardiometabolic diseases. Plain language summaryHeart disease, stroke, and type 2 diabetes are common and costly health problems. Finding people at risk early can help prevent these diseases. This study looked at a new blood-test-based health check and compared it with current health checks in Finland. Researchers used a computer model based on over 250,000 people aged 50-54. They tested different ways of using the new test and compared time, costs, and health outcomes. The results suggested that the new test can save time for nurses and physicians and reduce healthcare costs. In most cases, it also improved health outcomes. This means that using this type of test could help healthcare services work more efficiently and support earlier prevention, which may benefit both individuals and society in the future. FundingThis work was supported by Nightingale Health Plc.

title: Primary Care Quality and Inappropriate Community Antibiotic Use: Evidence from Linked Provider and Household Data
text: Inappropriate antibiotic use presents a major global health challenge, particularly in resource-limited settings where access to quality care remains limited while access to antibiotics is relatively unrestricted. This study estimates the relationship between frontline primary care quality and community antibiotic use, drawing on detailed data from approximately 100 rural villages in China that link objective measures of village doctors clinical practice quality, assessed through unannounced standardized patient visits, to household-level antibiotic use data measured within the same communities. To mitigate potential endogeneity concerns, we employed an instrumental variable (IV) approach integrated within a double/debiased machine learning (DML) framework, using ensemble machine learning to combine information across multiple individually weak but jointly informative provider-level instruments. Higher clinical practice quality was associated with lower probabilities of inappropriate antibiotic receipt during healthcare encounters for cold or diarrhea symptoms (OLS: 6.2 percentage points; DML-IV: 9.6 percentage points) and households storing antibiotics at home for future use (OLS: 4.1 percentage points; DML-IV: 10.9 percentage points). These findings highlight the potential role of improving frontline primary care quality in community antibiotic stewardship. Methodologically, this study illustrates how causal machine learning can complement conventional econometric methods by addressing high-dimensional estimation challenges in global health economics research.

title: Oral rehydration salts and zinc for childhood diarrhoea in Bangladesh, 2019 and 2025: coverage, wealth inequality and reported source of care
text: BackgroundDiarrhoea remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five. WHO and UNICEF recommend oral rehydration salts (ORS) alongside 10 to 14 days of zinc supplementation. However, national progress in combined treatment coverage and its socioeconomic and care-related inequalities remains insufficiently understood in Bangladesh. We assessed combined coverage, wealth inequality and differences by reported source of care. MethodsIn this repeated cross-sectional study, we analysed children under five with caregiver-reported diarrhoea in the 2019 (n=1,589) and 2025 (n=1,634) Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS). We estimated combined coverage using design-based methods, wealth inequality using slope indices, and associations with source of care using pooled adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR). Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) estimates provided an external comparison. ResultsCombined ORS and zinc coverage increased from 35.0% (95% CI 32.3 to 37.7) in 2019 to 42.9% (40.1 to 45.8) in 2025. This was an increase of 7.9 points (4.0 to 11.8). In 2025, ORS and zinc coverage were 75.8% and 51.9%, respectively. The 2025 estimate was similar to DHS 2022 (difference -0.4 points, -7.0 to 6.3), whereas MICS 2019 was below DHS 2017-18. Unadjusted wealth inequality persisted in 2025 (slope index 13.0 percentage points, 3.4 to 22.6). Adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics attenuated the pooled slope index from 11.8 to 6.5 points (-1.7 to 14.6). Coverage was lower with pharmacy-only than public care (aPR 0.59, 0.53 to 0.66) and with no care reported (0.14, 0.11 to 0.18). Children with no care reported accounted for 43.7% of children without combined treatment in 2025. ConclusionsCombined coverage increased within MICS, but fewer than half of children received both, and zinc remained the larger gap. Wealth inequality was partly shared with education and region. Children with no care reported formed the largest group without both treatments and need reaching outside facilities.

title: Functional difficulty among children and adolescents aged 5-17 years in Ethiopia: Multilevel analysis of the nationally representative 2024-2025 DHS
text: BackgroundPopulation-based data on functional difficulty among school-age children in Ethiopia are scarce. The 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) included, for the first time, the UNICEF/Washington Group Child Functioning Module (CFM) for children aged 5-17 years. We estimated the prevalence and domain distribution of functional difficulty and associated factors in Ethiopia. MethodsWe analysed cross-sectional EDHS data from 11,122 children aged 5-17 years (weighted n = 10,726) and 4,739 mothers. Functional difficulty was defined as "a lot of difficulty" or "cannot do at all" in any of 11 domains, or daily anxiety or depression. We estimated design-based prevalence and fitted multilevel logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) for any, non-affective and affective difficulty. Interviewer effects were examined with random-intercept models and within-cluster comparisons. ResultsOverall, 9.5% (95% CI 8.1-11.1) of children had functional difficulty. Daily depression (6.8%) and anxiety (6.6%) dominated, and 70.3% of affected children had only affective difficulty. Difficulty in at least one non-affective domain affected 2.8% (2.2-3.7), with each domain at 0.5-1.4%. Prevalence ranged from 1.5% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 16.5% in Oromia Regional State. In adjusted models, children not attending school had higher odds of non-affective difficulty (AOR 2.82, 95% CI 2.01-3.96), and girls had lower odds (AOR 0.63, 0.48-0.84). Outcomes clustered strongly within families (sibling correlation 67.7%) and clusters (ICC 20.9%). Six of 163 interviewers (7.9% of the weighted sample) contributed 58.2% of weighted cases of daily anxiety or depression; in the same clusters they recorded daily symptoms for 56.4% of children, against 2.1% for other interviewers. Excluding 11 statistically outlying interviewers reduced the prevalence of any difficulty to 4.6% (3.6-5.8) and of daily anxiety or depression to 3.3%. The associations with school non-attendance and sex were unchanged. ConclusionsFunctional difficulties across the sensory, physical, cognitive, and affective domains, including anxiety or depression, affect about 2-3% of Ethiopian children aged 5-17 years and are strongly associated with being out of school. Appropriate interventions and resource allocation should be considered.

title: Assessing the Accuracy of the NeuroBooster Array for GBA1 Variant Detection
text: GBA1 variants are major Parkinsons disease risk factors, but their detection is challenging. We compared NeuroBooster Array (NBA) genotyping with reference sequencing in 3,744 individuals. NBA correctly identified 520/608 carriers (85.5%). Of 89 missed calls, 73 had no matching probe and 16 had missing calls. 25 participants had false positive calls. NBA should not be used alone for clinical decisions, but is very useful for large case control analysis.

title: Pooled Multiplex Amplicon Massive Parallel Sequencing for High-Throughput Confirmation of Whole-Genome Sequencing Potentially Pathogenic Variants in Patients with Parkinsonism
text: Whole-genome sequencing identifies large numbers of genetic variants, although only a subset requires independent confirmation for clinical interpretation. Sanger sequencing remains the standard confirmation method but is impractical for large-scale variant verification. We developed and evaluated a strategy for variant confirmation based on multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing of pooled DNA samples. Whole-genome sequencing data were obtained from 86 individuals, including patients with parkinsonism and controls. Variants were selected using phenotype-driven filtering, ClinVar classification, and pathogenicity assessment criteria. A total of 307 variants were targeted using a custom amplicon panel comprising 290 amplicons. DNA samples were normalized, pooled into 16 mixtures, and sequenced following automated library preparation. Variant presence and sequencing quality were assessed using standard bioinformatic tools. Of the 307 selected variants, 243 were successfully confirmed. Unconfirmed variants included sequencing artifacts (18), insufficiently covered targets (5), large insertions or deletions exceeding 12 base pairs (36), and variants located within homopolymeric regions (5). Results for selected variants were concordant with Sanger sequencing, and observed variant frequencies corresponded to expected frequencies in pooled samples. This approach provides a robust, rapid, and cost-effective method for high-throughput genetic variants confirming identified by whole-genome sequencing while requiring only limited DNA input. Despite complete concordance with Sanger sequencing, larger validation studies are needed before multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing can replace routine confirmatory testing. Key PointsO_LIDesign and application of a high-throughput verification strategy for WGS variants with minimal DNA input requirements C_LIO_LIReliable and independent confirmation of WGS findings C_LIO_LIUtilization of multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing (MPS) in sample mixtures C_LIO_LIDetection of point mutations, small indels and duplications. C_LI

title: Routine health information system data quality in a hill and mountain district of Nepal: a cross-sectional desk review of four years of DHIS2 data from Sankhuwasabha, 2021-2025
text: IntroductionNepals routine health information system runs on DHIS2, but no published data-quality assessment covers its mountainous districts. The method raises a second issue: the WHO Data Quality Review (DQR) tests internal consistency partly through related-indicator pairs, assuming each indicator is recorded independently. DHIS2 validation rules act on paired values at entry, so a rule-governed pair may agree for reasons unrelated to recording quality. MethodsIn this study, a WHO DQR Module 1 desk review was conducted on aggregated DHIS2 data from all 132 facilities in Sankhuwasabha district, analysed at district and local level (palika) resolution: seven datasets for completeness and timeliness, and 17 tracer indicators for internal consistency, for fiscal year 2081/82 (2024/25) against the three preceding years (2021/22 to 2023/24). Pairs were classified in advance as rule-governed or free, and three denominator-free ratios compared with Nepal Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) 2022 estimates for Koshi Province. ResultsCompleteness was at least 90.6% in every dataset and unit. Timeliness fell below 90% in 22 of 70 unit-dataset combinations, concentrated in four remote local levels. Of four rule-governed pairs only iron and deworming changed materially, 1.42 to 1.00; two never agreed, indicating rules that query rather than block entry. The free pairs diverged: Penta-1 to Penta-3 dropout fell from +3.6% to -5.4%, negative in 9 of 10 local levels, and BCG was below Penta-1 in 8 of 10. District totals were inverted at both steps (BCG 1,537, Penta-1 1,666, Penta-3 1,756), which redistribution cannot produce. ConclusionReporting is nearly complete, but the data carry a persistent immunization anomaly that completeness and timeliness miss, pointing to a systematic recording process. Because a rule-governed pair may agree by configuration, DHIS2 assessments should classify pairs against the active validation-rule set before interpretation.

title: Use of AI-Related CPT Codes by Patient, Geographic, and Payer Characteristics in the U.S., 2021-2026
text: ImportancePayment policy for clinical artificial intelligence (AI) is changing quickly, yet national data on which AI-enabled services are used, and for whom, are limited. ObjectiveTo describe national trends in the use of AI-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes and how use differs by patient, geographic, and payer characteristics. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsThis serial cross-sectional study used Epic Cosmos, a deidentified electronic health record dataset, to examine 11,605,867,309 encounters among 233,628,292 US patients from January 1, 2021, to April 14, 2026. Exposures: Calendar year, age, sex, race, ethnicity, rurality, area-level social vulnerability, census region, and primary payer. Main Outcomes and MeasuresEncounters with any of 65 CPT codes that require AI, identified by matching the CPT code set to US Food and Drug Administration-listed AI-enabled devices and classified as assistive, augmentative, or autonomous using the CPT Appendix S taxonomy. ResultsOf 11.6 billion encounters, 335,349 (2.9 per 100,000) included an AI-required CPT code. The odds of an encounter with an AI-required code were 9.88 (95% CI, 9.71-10.06) times higher in 2025 than in 2021. In unadjusted comparisons, use was higher among patients aged 65 to 85 years and among those with Medicare (OR, 5.11) or Medicare Advantage (OR, 5.12) vs commercial insurance. Use was lower among Black (OR, 0.72) and Hispanic or Latino (OR, 0.34) patients, Medicaid enrollees (OR, 0.65), residents of the most socially vulnerable areas (OR, 0.53), and residents of the most rural areas (OR, 0.86). Use of automated diabetic retinopathy screening increased after the service was added to a HEDIS quality measure. One newer code (quantitative brain MRI) appeared in rural areas within months of becoming effective, whereas older codes such as retinopathy screening took years. Conclusions and RelevanceIn this cross-sectional study, billed use of AI-enabled services remained rare but grew substantially and was concentrated among older and Medicare-insured patients, with lower use among Medicaid enrollees and residents of socially vulnerable areas. As the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services restructures payment for software and launches outcome-based models, tracking who receives AI-enabled care across payment pathways will be important for equitable access. KEY POINTSO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSHow has billed use of artificial intelligence (AI)-related CPT codes changed nationally since 2021, and how does use differ by patient, geographic, and payer characteristics? FindingsIn this cross-sectional study of 11.6 billion US encounters, 2.9 per 100,000 included an AI-required CPT code. Odds of use were nearly 10 times higher in 2025 than in 2021, higher among Medicare beneficiaries, and lower among Medicaid enrollees and residents of socially vulnerable areas. MeaningBilled AI use remains rare and uneven across payers and communities, so payment policy for AI may need to be paired with monitoring of who receives AI-enabled care.

title: Gamma delta T cells are expanded in the blood of chronic low back pain patients with lumbar Modic changes
text: ObjectivesModic changes (MC) are vertebral endplate and bone marrow lesions strongly associated with chronic low back pain. Type 1 MC (MC1, oedema-like) and type 2 or 3 MC (MC2or3, fat- and sclerosis-like) are commonly regarded as different stages of the same pathological process, yet their underlying biology remains poorly defined. In particular, it remains unclear whether MC are confined to the spine or accompanied by distinct systemic immune alterations. Here, we provide the first comprehensive characterisation of the circulating immune landscape in patients with lumbar MC. MethodsPeripheral blood mononuclear cells were analysed from 37 patients undergoing lumbar spinal surgery: 11 with no MC, 15 with MC1 and 11 with MC2or3. Samples were fluorescently barcoded, pooled, and stained with a 28-antibody phenotyping panel. Each pool was then split into 30 aliquots, and each of these was co-stained with a different PE-conjugated anti-integrin, -selectin, or -chemokine receptor antibody or isotype controls. Differences in abundance were tested with binomial mixed models adjusted for acquisition batch, age, and sex. Differentially abundant compartments were clustered by FlowSOM and the same binomial model was used to test differences in cluster abundance. Adhesion receptors were analysed as single chains. ResultsThe {gamma}{delta} T cell compartment was the only population significantly expanded in MC patients (median 0.58% of all recorded cells in nonMC donors versus 1.61% in pooled MC (OR = 2.38, q = 0.035)). Clustering {gamma}{delta} T cells into subsets showed compartment-wide expansion, primarily driven by V{delta}2+ T cells. The adhesion receptor screen revealed 6 and 2 integrin on basophils, endoglin on plasmacytoid dendritic cells, and {beta}7 integrin on IgA B cells as differentially expressed in MC, but none survived multiple-testing correction across the whole screen. ConclusionsLumbar MC are accompanied by expansion of circulating {gamma}{delta} T cells. This aligns with previously reported {gamma}{delta} T cell accumulation in MC1 lesions, underscoring the role of {gamma}{delta} T cells in MC pathophysiology.

title: Dysregulated B Cell Education Drives Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency in Down Syndrome
text: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) present with both increased rates of autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. To understand this paradox, we first examined lymph node (LN) architecture and immune cell composition in infants with and without DS, as well as peripheral blood B cells from unrelated adults with and without DS. Most strikingly, LNs from individuals with DS exhibited a marked paucity of germinal centers compared with typical lymph nodes. Stromal cells within DS LNs expressed significantly lower levels of the adhesion molecules ICAM1 and VCAM1, accompanied by significantly reduced CXCR5 expression within B cell follicles, suggesting impaired B cell migration and follicular organization. Although fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) were present at comparable frequencies in DS and control LNs, MARCO lymphatic endothelial cells (MARCO-LECs), another critical stromal cell population supporting LN architecture, were significantly reduced. In addition, follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), which are essential for antigen retention and B cell selection within germinal centers, were also substantially reduced. To determine the consequences of these abnormalities on humoral immunity, we performed paired single-cell RNA sequencing and V(D)J sequencing of peripheral blood B cells from adults with and without DS. DS memory and CD86+ switched memory B cell populations exhibited significantly elevated reactive oxygen species and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling gene signatures, coupled with reduced levels of somatic hypermutation in the memory population and increase usage of the autoreactivity-associated IGHV4-34 heavy-chain gene. Collectively, these findings suggest that early-life disruption of LN architecture, characterized by reduced expression of adhesion molecules, selective loss of MARCO-LECs, and depletion of FDCs, impairs germinal center function and B cell education. This defective microenvironment likely contributes to inadequate affinity maturation, as reflected by diminished somatic hypermutation and a more autoreactive B cell repertoire in adults with Down syndrome.

title: Comprehensive proteomics reveals stage-specific signatures in blood that precede diabetic kidney disease onset and progression
text: Diabetic kidney disease is the leading cause of kidney failure worldwide, yet the molecular events underlying disease initiation and progression remain unclear. We measured 5,420 circulating proteins in 830 adults with type 1 diabetes and examined their longitudinal associations with onset and progression of kidney disease over 10 years of follow-up. We identified 130 proteins associated with at least one outcome independent of established clinical risk factors, of which 59 replicated in an independent cohort. HAVCR1/KIM-1, GFRA1, CD14 and GDF15 predicted albuminuria onset up to a decade before detectable disease. Albuminuria progression pointed to the kidney-liver axis (ASGR1, RBP4), whereas rapid kidney function decline and incident kidney failure pointed to immune and tumor necrosis factor receptor signaling. Mendelian randomization prioritized UMOD, SORT1, CLSPN, MAST4 and EGF as potential targets. These findings reveal molecular perturbations preceding clinical manifestations of diabetic kidney disease and identify distinct pathways associated with disease progression.

title: Spatiotemporal mapping of ex vivo myometrial contractions in adenomyosis
text: ObjectiveUterine dyscontractility plays a major role in pain sensation, infertility, and adenomyosis pathogenesis. In vivo, contractility occurs in the inner myometrium and junctional zone, which is thickened in adenomyosis. We examined whether the junctional zone presents particular contractile features ex vivo by measuring contractility and oxytocin response in full-thickness serosa-to-endometrium myometrial slices retrieved from control and adenomyosis patients. DesignProspective ex vivo case-control study. SubjectsPremenopausal women following hysterectomy: adenomyosis (n = 16) and controls (n = 12). Contractility: 57 strips (11 vs 8 patients), immunofluorescence: 10 vs 9 patients. Main Outcome MeasuresWe resorted to spatiotemporal mapping, time-lapse video-based techniques used in the field of gastroenterology. We measured contraction frequency, amplitude, duration, velocity, site of origin, and propagation direction along the serosa-to-endometrium axis, before and after oxytocin. We measured oxytocin receptor density along the serosa-to-endometrium axis by immunofluorescence and machine learning-assisted segmentation. ResultsEx vivo contractile waves propagated throughout the outer and inner myometrium, with similar amplitude and frequency. Contraction frequency, amplitude, duration, and velocity did not differ between control and adenomyosis uteri. Oxytocin increased contraction frequency and velocity and systematically caused contractile waves to originate at the inner myometrium in both groups. In both groups, oxytocin receptor density was highest in the inner myometrium. Adenomyosis patients had a 1.8-fold higher oxytocin receptor density, but a smaller oxytocin-induced increase in contraction frequency. ConclusionWe provide the first ex vivo spatiotemporal time-lapse analysis of myometrial contractions. The whole myometrium contracts ex vivo, not just the inner part (junctional zone). This uniform myogenic motility is presumably inhibited neurally in vivo in the outer myometrium. Ex vivo adenomyosis basal contractility was similar to that of controls. Adenomyotic myometrium overexpressed oxytocin receptors compared to controls, but this did not translate into a stronger contractile response to oxytocin. In both groups, oxytocin caused contractile waves to originate at and propagate from the sub-endometrial myometrium, where receptor density is higher. This demonstrates that contractile wave direction can be controlled hormonally.

title: Real-World Outcomes of a Traffic-Light Approach to Lifestyle Modification in Chronic Disease: Evidence from an Integrative Health Clinic
text: BackgroundNon-communicable diseases driven by unhealthy lifestyles are a growing and largely avoidable burden among industrial workers. Patient-level evidence on the effectiveness of structured lifestyle programmes delivered alongside standard care -- such as a traffic-light dietary guideline, a Yoga protocol and a daily four-spice culinary infusion -- remains limited. The Integrative Health Clinic (IHC) at ESIC Medical College & Hospital, Faridabad, India, is a family-medicine-style outpatient clinic that follows the 21-item Health Building Lifestyle Guideline and delivers care through a 7-step COM-B-based protocol. We therefore estimated patient-reported relief and compliance with three lifestyle practices in patients attending the IHC. MethodsWe conducted a retrospective single-arm cohort of patients first seen between February 2025 and 30 September 2026, with follow-up through 4 November 2026. All patients received the three-component lifestyle intervention (advice on spice infusion, diet and Yoga) and were offered follow-up; the 1,466 patients with a usable telephone contact were called for feedback and reinforcement of practices. A physical visit with a coded diagnosis was treated as a valid record. Each patient called was coded once for relief and for spice, diet and Yoga compliance using the most recent definitive answer (YES/NO); calls without a definitive answer ("no response", "not interested") were skipped, and patients with no definitive answer on any call were classified as such. Disease burden, including the screening-detected diagnoses, was counted as patient-condition pairs and classed into 14 systems. ResultsThere were 4,047 valid visit records from 1,737 unique patients (904 female [52.0%]; mean age 40.3 {+/-} 14.6 years; 833 male [48.0%]; mean age 44.8 {+/-} 15.1 years). Of these, there were 1,035 single-visit [59.6%] and 702 revisit patients [40.4%], i.e. 2.33 visits per patient. The 1,466 analysed patients (763 female [52.1%] and 703 male [47.9%]) comprised 666 revisit and 800 single-visit patients. Their most frequent patient-condition pairs were hypertension (511), obesity (397) and arthritis (268); objective-evidence screening contributed 246 pairs in 233 patients (obesity 161, hypertension 39, anaemia 44, diabetes 2). Of the 1,466 (84.4% of 1,737) patients with a usable telephone contact who were called, 1,016 had a definitive relief answer: 850 (83.7%; 95% CI 81.3-85.8) reported relief and 166 reported no relief. The remaining 450 had no definitive answer. Among the 1,016 patients with a definitive answer, relief was 87.2% (395/453) in revisit versus 80.8% (455/563) in single-visit patients. Treating all 450 patients without a definitive relief answer as no relief, the conservative lower bound of patients reporting relief was 58.0% overall (850/1,466), 59.3% in revisit (395/666) and 56.9% in single-visit patients (455/800). Among the 1,016 patients with practice data, compliance with the spice infusion, diet and Yoga was 77.1%, 83.3% and 81.2%, respectively; counting all 450 non-responders as non-compliant gave conservative estimates of 53.4%, 57.7% and 56.3% for the three practices (n = 1,466). In the responding cohort, relief rose with the five-level compliance dose, from 5.2% (6/115) at dose 0 to 98.2% (326/332) at dose 4 (all three practices plus a repeat visit). ConclusionsIn this exploratory single-arm cohort, patient-reported relief was more frequent at higher levels of a composite measure that combined the three practices and repeat visits. Because there was no comparison group and all lifestyle components were delivered jointly alongside continuing pharmacotherapy, causality cannot be inferred. The findings support feasibility and justify prospective, controlled, disease-specific studies. The efficacy of the four-spice infusion remains under study and is not yet a proven treatment.

title: Functional connectivity of reward and cognitive control networks predicts body mass index but not binge eating disorder in women
text: BackgroundBinge eating disorder (BED) is associated with obesity as well as behavioral and neurobiological changes in the reward and cognitive control systems of the brain. To better dissociate neural mechanisms of pathological eating behavior, functional connectivity (FC) analyses have shown promise. However, there is currently no replicable signature of BED derived from fMRI. MethodsWe investigated FC in 61 women with varying symptoms of binge eating. The three groups included 21 women with BED, 20 women with subsyndromal BED (subBED), and 20 controls without binge eating (noBE) matched in body mass index (BMI) and age. To identify neural signatures of BED and BMI, we used seed-based FC "fingerprints" (nucleus accumbens, NAcc, for reward and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, dlPFC, for cognitive control) to predict group or BMI based on resting state and task-based (food bidding) FC. Furthermore, we explored spatial patterns of FC to quantify associations with BED and BMI. ResultsBoth seeds of the reward and cognitive control networks robustly predicted BMI (rs = .33 - .46). The dlPFC seed predicted BMI across conditions (resting state: p=.002; task: p=.012) while the NAcc seed only predicted BMI based on task-based FC (p=.007). In contrast, FC failed to classify binge eating groups better than chance. ConclusionsFC within reward and cognitive control networks primarily reflect obesity-related changes. Despite pronounced differences in eating behavior, BED could not be reliably dissociated from subBED or noBE using FC fingerprints. These results highlight challenges in identifying BED-specific functional markers.
