title: Persistent or recurrent depression in young adults: associations with systemic inflammation and early life adversity.
text: 1BackgroundThere is limited research on persistent or recurrent depression into young adulthood. We examined the prevalence of recurrent/persistent depression in young adults, and associations with childhood trauma/adversity and systemic inflammation, and if inflammatory markers mediated associations between childhood trauma and subsequent depression. MethodsALSPAC participants with ICD-10 depression assessments at ages 18, 24 and 30 were classified as never depressed, transiently depressed (one episode), or persistently/recurrently depressed ([≥]2 episodes). Trauma/adversity from birth to age 16/17 was characterised by type, timing and burden. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured at ages 9, 16, 18 and 24. Analyses used multinomial logistic regression, linear regression and causal mediation models. ResultsAmong 2,014 participants, 78.9% were never depressed, 15.0% had transient depression and 6.1% had persistent/recurrent depression. Trauma/adversity was more strongly associated with persistent/recurrent depression (RRR 3.17, 95% CI 1.98-5.06; FDR-P=6.2x10-) than transient depression, with a dose-response pattern and stronger associations for threat adversities. Middle-to-late childhood (11-17 yrs) emerged as a sensitive period for persistent/recurrent (RRR 2.85, 95% CI 1.47-5.52) and transient depression (RRR 1.85, 95% CI 1.25-2.73). Trauma/adversity was associated with modestly higher IL-6 at age 24 (all FDR-adjusted P<0.05); CRP associations did not survive multiple-testing correction. Neither marker mediated trauma/adversity associations with persistent/recurrent depression. ConclusionPersistent/recurrent depression affects approximately 1 in 20 young adults. Childhood trauma/adversity, particularly during middle-to-late childhood, was associated with persistent/recurrent depression, but measured inflammatory proteins did not mediate this association. Further work is needed to understand biological mechanisms underlying the embedding early life psychosocial stress.

title: Gender Differences in Socioeconomic Inequalities in Body Mass Index and Health-Related Mediators Among Young and Early Midlife Finns
text: IntroductionSocioeconomic differences in body mass index (BMI) are well established, but less is known about gender differences and their behavioral pathways. We examined gender differences in the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) and BMI, and whether dietary factors and physical activity mediated the associations. MethodsWe used survey data from the employees of the City of Helsinki aged 19-39 collected in 2017 (n = 4,400, 80% women). SEP was measured by highest educational attainment, and the examined mediators were consumption of fruit and vegetables, red and processed meat, sweets and confectionery and alcohol as well as leisure-time vigorous physical activity (VPA) and sedentary time. We conducted gender-specific multiple mediation analyses using structural equation modeling and additional analyses using multiple imputation by chained equations. ResultsWith increasing educational attainment, mean BMI decreased from 26.4 kg/m{superscript 2} to 24.0 kg/m{superscript 2} among women, and from 26.6 kg/m{superscript 2} to 25.2 kg/m{superscript 2} among men. Lower SEP was associated with lower consumption of fruit and vegetables, higher consumption of red and processed meat, and lower VPA in both genders. Women reported healthier diets but less VPA than men. The strongest SEP-BMI mediator among women was VPA (indirect effect: 0.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.26, 0.44), followed by fruit and vegetable consumption (0.15, 95% CI 0.08, 0.23) and red and processed meat consumption (0.06, 95% CI 0.02, 0.11). Among men, significant mediators were red and processed meat consumption (0.12, 95% CI 0.03, 0.23), sedentary time (0.11, 95% CI 0.01, 0.24) and VPA (0.10, 95% CI 0.02, 0.21). ConclusionsSocioeconomic inequalities in BMI appear stronger among women and are shaped through partly different mechanisms between genders. Improving VPA may be relevant among low- SEP women, whereas reducing sedentary time may be more relevant among low-SEP men. Reducing red and processed meat is beneficial for both genders.

title: Determinants of early child development among children aged 24-59 months in Ethiopia: 2024-25 Demographic and Health Survey
text: BackgroundThe 2024-25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) is the first national survey in Ethiopia to measure early childhood development using UNICEFs Early Childhood Development Index 2030 (ECDI2030). This provides a national estimate for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 4.2.1, the proportion of children aged 24-59 months who are developmentally on track. We estimated the prevalence of being developmentally on track and examined its child, maternal, household and community determinants in Ethiopia. MethodsThis cross-sectional study analysed 3,731 children aged 24-59 months (weighted n = 3,514) of 3,232 mothers in 771 clusters. Children were on track if they achieved the age-specific minimum number of the 20 ECDI2030 milestones. Prevalence was estimated with design-based methods. Four three-level mixed-effects logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) were fitted, and interviewer effects were assessed. ResultsOverall, 36.3% (95% CI 33.4-39.3) of children were developmentally on track. Prevalence ranged from 23.3% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 77.7% in Addis Ababa. In the null model, 21.5% of the variation lay between clusters (median odds ratio 3.24). In the final model, the odds of being on track were lower at 36-47 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 0.57, 95% CI 0.44-0.74) and 48-59 months (AOR 0.39, 0.30-0.51) than at 24-35 months. They were also lower after a preceding birth interval under 24 months (AOR 0.75, 0.57-0.99), after recent diarrhoea, fever or cough (AOR 0.59, 0.45-0.77), and where distance to a health facility was a big problem (AOR 0.61, 0.48-0.79). Odds were higher for girls (AOR 1.38, 1.12-1.70), with maternal education (more than secondary vs none: AOR 2.08, 1.19-3.63) and with weekly media exposure (AOR 2.15, 1.51-3.06). The covariates explained 55.9% of the between-cluster variance. ConclusionsNearly two in three Ethiopian children aged 24-59 months are not developmentally on track, and children fall further behind as they age. Interventions should target maternal education, access to information and health services, birth spacing and childhood illness, with priority for the lowest-performing regions and communities.

title: Early Prediction of Discharge Outcomes in Geriatric Rehabilitation: Development and Temporal Validation of a Multiclass Model
text: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a model that predicts on day 7 of subacute rehabilitation (timed to inform the first multidisciplinary team meeting) the probabilities of three mutually exclusive outcomes: minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration. DesignRetrospective cohort study with temporal validation. Multinomial regression and XGBoost models were trained on 80% of admissions during the years 2016-2024 of members of the largest national health maintenance organization (HMO), tested on the remaining 20% and members of other HMOs, and validated on year 2025 admissions. Models output patient-level outcome probabilities with the strongest feature contributors. SettingA public geriatric rehabilitation hospital. ParticipantsAll consecutive first admissions (N=10,920; median age 80 years; median length of stay 35 days). InterventionsNot applicable. Main Outcome MeasuresDischarge disposition: minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration (transfer to acute care without return, or in-hospital death). Predictors were demographic, functional, cognitive, clinical, and laboratory variables documented before day 7 with linkage to pre-admission community health records. Performance was assessed by multiclass area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score and positive predictive value (PPV). ResultsOverall, 34% of patients were discharged with minimal dependency, 44% with nursing-care dependency, and 22% deteriorated medically. Both models performed comparably. Multinomial regression achieved an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.83) compared with 0.72 (0.71-0.73) for FIM alone, and it was maintained on temporal validation (AUC 0.80, 0.78-0.82). At a [≥]60% probability threshold, the model flagged 32% of patients for nursing-care dependency and 5% for deterioration, with PPVs of 72% and 69%, respectively. ConclusionsDay-7 multiclass risk estimation from routinely collected data is feasible, interpretable and stable over time. Alerts could prompt earlier social-work involvement and closer monitoring of patients at risk of deterioration; prospective controlled evaluation is warranted.

title: Near point of care C-Reactive Protein and Serum Amyloid-A Test met WHO target product profile for TB screening
text: BackgroundTB eradication strategies in high burden countries need affordable, scalable, and accessible screening tools. This study investigated the diagnostic accuracy of C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA), and interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) as potential screening tools. MethodThis cross-sectional diagnostic study investigated stored archived serum samples from three groups of subjects; bacteriology confirmed symptomatic TB group (n=57), probable TB (n=56) and healthy controls (n=60). CRP and SAA concentrations were measured using near point-of-care fluorescence immunoassay (NPOCT-FIA), while IP-10 was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Diagnostic performance of individual and combined biomarkers was evaluated ResultsReceiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of serum amyloid A (SAA) and C-reactive protein (CRP) for identifying confirmed tuberculosis (TB). Compared with probable TB and healthy controls, SAA achieved an AUC of 0.961 (cut-off >31.0 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 88.6% specificity, while CRP achieved an AUC of 0.953 (cut-off 21.3 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 86.0% specificity. Interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.545). Combined CRP and SAA achieved 100.0% sensitivity and 83.3% specificity. ConclusionSAA and CRP met WHO target product profile criteria for TB triage screening.

title: Tau-vulnerable medial temporal lobe connectivity drives a functional-to-synaptic cascade in Alzheimer's disease
text: Distinct tau-vulnerable and relatively spared subregions exist within the medial temporal lobe (MTL). However, it remains unclear that how functional connectivity (FC), anchored to tau-vulnerable MTL subregions, is related to tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive decline across the Alzheimers disease (AD) continuum. We here probe into this with resting-state fMRI data from a discovery cohort (ADNI; N = 386; cognitively normal [CN], mild cognitive impairment [MCI], and AD; 144 with 2-year follow-up) and an independent validation cohort at local hospital (N = 100; CN, subjective cognitive decline [SCD], and MCI; 25 receiving high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [HF-rTMS]). We first separated the MTL into subregions with high and low neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) burden based on histological atlases, and calculated the seed-based whole-brain FC for each subregion. Second, group differences were assessed using ANCOVA, and associations with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta})/tau pathology, synaptic biomarkers, and cognitive performance were examined. Third, serial mediation, cross-lagged, and longitudinal regression analyses were performed to investigate the proposed pathological sequence, with additional evidence from HF-rTMS intervention and autopsy-confirmed Braak staging. Our results showed that, with the development of AD, FC reductions were focused on the high-NFT MTL network, particularly involving the inferior temporal gyrus and precuneus. Baseline tau burden in high-NFT MTL regions was able to predict subsequent FC alterations. Interestingly, FC between the high-NFT MTL and global brain showed region-specific associations with synaptic biomarkers, including negative associations in the cerebellum and positive associations in the precentral gyrus. We also observed a divergent association between the FC and cognition or pathology at different AD stages, shifting from positive in the early stages to negative in advanced AD. Serial mediation analyses supported a pathway linking tau burden to cognitive impairment through altered high-NFT MTL connectivity in the precuneus and occipital regions and subsequent synaptic dysfunction. Cross-lagged and longitudinal analyses further confirmed the proposed temporal sequence. Furthermore, HF-rTMS-related cognitive improvements were partially associated with enhanced synaptic plasticity through changes in precuneus-high-NFT MTL connectivity. Collectively, these findings support a spatiotemporal framework linking the dysfunction of tau-vulnerable MTL network to synaptic impairment and cognitive decline, highlighting high-NFT MTL-based FC as a potential imaging marker tracking AD progression.

title: The LAMp-LC Study: Unveiling the lung microbiome in Australians with early- and late-stage lung cancer using shotgun metagenomics
text: BackgroundLung cancer remains the leading cause of cancerl71related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. MethodsWe characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n=106, healthy n=10) using shotgun metagenomics and semil71quantitative culture to evaluate microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across earlyl71 and latel71stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culturel71based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking packl71years, sex, and tumour characteristics. ResultsCumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive Neisseria subflava, Gemella sanguinis, and Rothia mucilaginosa depletion, alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. {beta} diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst diversity was significantly reduced in early-stage vs. late-stage BWs. The earlyl71stage TME demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched (Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted (Streptococcus parasanguinis, Streptococcus cristatus, R. mucilaginosa) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral {beta}l71diversity restructuring. ConclusionsThe lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiomel71based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

title: Genome-Wide Study of Early Disability Severity in Multiple Sclerosis
text: Background and ObjectivesMultiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by demyelination and neuroaxonal injury. Genetics of MS susceptibility and long term disability is well characterized, but the genetic contribution to disability recorded earlier in the disease course is uncertain. We performed common-variant associations with the early period MS severity to identify potential causal loci, effector genes and associated pathways, and understand the relationships of early MS severity and other traits. MethodsThe primary outcome was the first age-related MS severity score (ARMSS), an age-adjusted severity measure, in 7,209 individuals of Swedish discovery cohorts and independent Italian and multi-national European replication cohorts. Replicated loci underwent conditional analysis, fine-mapping, time-to-event MS phenotype association analyses, and multi-omics-integrated gene prioritization. Using the genome-wide summary statistics, we also conducted heritability analyses, polygenic risk score association with MS susceptibility and late MS severity, gene-level analyses, cross-trait analyses, Mendelian randomization, and drug-repurposing screening. ResultsTwo suggestive loci were replicated: rs1234317 on chromosome 1 (effect allele T: beta = 0.100, SE = 0.0189, P = 1.08 x 10-7) and rs929769 on chromosome 5 (effect allele T: beta = -0.0956, SE = 0.0184, P = 1.95 x 10-7). Fine-mapping supported rs929769 strongly in chromosome 5, and rs1234317 and rs6657136 in chromosome 1 with lower confidence. The SNPs did not show a significant change in effect sizes when adjusted for heritable traits and exhibited attenuated associations with long-term MS disability progression. TNFSF4 was the top prioritized effector for rs1234317, TNFSF18 for rs6657136, and ADAMTS2 for rs929769. Early MS severity showed partial genetic overlap with MS susceptibility and late MS severity, but no significant correlation with a range of neurological, psychiatric, autoimmune, cognitive, and aging traits. Pathway analyses identified ion-channel regulation and folic acid metabolism. Mendelian randomization suggested nominal bidirectional causal associations with educational attainment. In silico drug screening nominated several candidate drugs. DiscussionThis study identifies candidate causal variants of early MS severity and their effector genes: TNFSF4, TNFSF18, and ADAMTS2. It provides insights into the genetic architecture and therapeutic measures for the early phase of MS severity.

title: Excess mortality after mental disorder diagnosis within and outside specialist psychiatric care: nationwide cohort study
text: BackgroundPeople with mental disorders have shortened life expectancy, but much evidence on excess mortality comes from specialist psychiatric populations. We examined variation across the broader diagnosed population by clinical context and time since diagnosis. MethodsWe followed 5,526,599 Finnish residents aged 5-95 years without recorded mental disorders at entry from 2011 to 2023 (63 million person-years). ICD-11-grouped diagnoses and mortality rate ratios (MRRs) were assessed by time since diagnosis, psychiatric care setting, substance use disorder (SUD) status, age, and cause of death. ResultsDuring follow-up, 1,463,064 individuals (26.5%) received a diagnosis; the overall adjusted MRR was 2.65 (95% CI 2.53-2.77). However, among diagnosed individuals aged 5-64 years, 46.1% belonged to a subgroup with rapidly declining excess mortality and little evidence of excess beyond two years. This subgroup had depressive, anxiety or fear-related, or stress-related disorders without diagnosed SUD or specialist psychiatric care during follow-up. At two years, MRRs ranged from 0.88 (95% CI 0.73-1.06) to 1.04 (0.88-1.22) in men and 0.92 (0.79-1.07) to 1.12 (0.96-1.31) in women. Excess mortality persisted in specialist care and was particularly high with SUD. It also persisted without SUD or specialist care in schizophrenia and other primary psychotic disorders and older adults with depression. ConclusionsExcess mortality after mental disorder diagnosis may be transient in large parts of the diagnosed population while remaining persistent in others with the same diagnosis. Recognizing these differences is important for interpreting mortality estimates and communicating prognosis across health care.

title: A dollar-aware food-environment index and a 27-year trajectory typology: a measurement foundation for diet and childhood-obesity research in Mississippi, 1997-2024
text: BackgroundThe retail food environment is a widely used exposure in behavioural-nutrition and obesity research. Grocery stores have declined across rural America while limited-assortment discount ("dollar") stores have proliferated, yet standard food-environment indices typically exclude dollar stores. We developed a dollar-aware index, assessed how counting dollar stores changes the measured exposure, and derived a trajectory typology. MethodsUsing annual establishment data from Data Axle for all 878 Mississippi census tracts (1997-2024), we classified food retailers with code-based rules and computed the modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI) in standard and dollar-aware forms. We fitted latent class tra-jectory models suited to the bounded index, tested their stability in seven sensitivity analyses, and related class membership to the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and urbanicity with multinomial regression. ResultsGrocery stores fell from 1,616 to 716 while dollar stores rose from 315 to 1,005, crossing in 2018. The indices ranked tracts almost identically (within-year Spearman [≥] 0.99), but where dollar stores and healthy outlets coexisted, counting dollar stores lowered the index by 4.5 points in 1997 and 9.1 in 2024, and tracts with only dollar-store retail, which the standard index cannot score, rose from 1 to 32. Six trajectory classes emerged: stable adequate (7.8% of tracts), steady decline (15.3%), early collapse (12.9%), late collapse (9.7%), persistently constrained (34.8%) and chronically low (19.6%); only 7.5% of children in classified tracts lived in stable-adequate tracts. Classes were stable across random starts and pandemic-year exclusion; collapse was robust, but its early-late timing split depended on tracts with few retailers. Chronically low and persistently-constrained tracts were predominantly urban (relative risk ratios 8.3 and 4.5), consistent with food swamps; persistently-constrained and steady-decline membership rose modestly with vulnerability (1.17 and 1.20 per 0.1 SVI), an association that was weaker with 2010 SVI; collapse classes had no cross-sectional social signature. ConclusionsCounting dollar stores changes the level of a widely used food-environment index, and whether a growing set of tracts can be scored, rather than how tracts rank. A 27-year typology separates urban food swamps from tracts whose food environments collapsed and provides a time-varying exposure for diet and childhood-obesity research. Contributions to the literatureO_LIStandard food-environment indices omit dollar stores; counting them barely changes how tracts rank, but it lowers index values where dollar stores and healthy outlets coexist and determines whether a growing set of tracts can be scored at all. C_LIO_LIWe provide a 27-year, tract-level trajectory typology of a dollar-aware index, tested in seven sensitivity analyses, that distinguishes urban food swamps from communities whose food environments collapsed. C_LIO_LITracts whose food environments collapsed are indistinguishable from others on present-day social characteristics, illustrating what cross-sectional exposure measures miss. C_LIO_LIWe document data issues that longitudinal food-environment studies using commercial data should check: vendor coverage expansions, store-size fields that shift with vendor coding, and code-based misclassification. C_LI

title: Serum Raman spectroscopy as a blood-based triage test for bladder cancer: a retrospective proof-of-concept study
text: BackgroundBladder cancer remains one of the most common urological malignancies. Current diagnostic pathways rely heavily on cystoscopy, an invasive investigation with significant cost and resource implications. A rapid blood-based assay capable of improving patient stratification before cystoscopy could reduce unnecessary invasive investigations while maintaining diagnostic sensitivity. MethodsArchived serum samples from patients with histologically confirmed bladder cancer and symptomatic control subjects were analysed using dried-serum Raman spectroscopy. Raman spectra were incorporated into supervised machine-learning classification models to generate predicted probabilities of bladder cancer. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. ResultsThe study included 49 patients with bladder cancer and 97 symptomatic controls. Predicted probabilities of bladder cancer were substantially higher in cancer patients than in controls. The Raman classifier demonstrated excellent diagnostic discrimination (AUC approximately 0.90). Incorporation of age into the classification model produced little additional improvement (AUC approximately 0.91). ConclusionsMachine learning-assisted analysis of dried-serum Raman spectra demonstrates promising diagnostic performance for bladder cancer. Prospective evaluation is warranted to determine its role as a minimally invasive triage test within contemporary bladder cancer diagnostic pathways.

title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
text: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
text: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built from training data only. A separate leave-one-anatomy-out experiment tests parameter-free index extension: verified cases of an unseen solid organ enter the knowledge base, and the refiner stays frozen. A light shape-aware projection head on a frozen multimodal encoder maps embedding similarity to the shape agreement of the masks, so the knowledge base returns cases that the refiner can use as a shape prior. We evaluate GRACE on 18 public datasets spanning CT, MRI and ultrasound, using nine refinement configurations and seven upstream segmentors that span weak, mid, and strong operating regimes. We report each change with the DSC of its input mask. On the weak tier, the input DSC is 0.386 and GRACE adds up to +0.35 DSC. On a strong segmentor, the input DSC is 0.932 and the mean change is small. Transfer to an imaging modality that is absent from training and from the index is partial and depends on the anatomy, and remains an open research direction. Our results suggest retrieval-conditioned refinement is a practical alternative to anatomy-specific correction models. Code: https://github.com/robustml-eurecom/grace

title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
text: AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge. BugGen 1.0 shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate context-aware RTL mutations. Still, it relies on the model for both choosing where to mutate and generating the edit, which increases inference costs and can lead to invalid choices. BugGen 2.0 changes this division of labor. Deterministic algorithms handle structural analysis, target selection, and validation, while the LLM focuses on localized semantic rewriting. Across four OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LLMs, BugGen 2.0 reaches every requested quota of compilable bug scenarios that cause at least two test failures, with 14-16 of 16 configured mutation types represented. In completed same-model comparisons, it reduces token use by 6.8x-15.4x relative to BugGen 1.0 and 1.5x-7.9x relative to Firefly. BugGen 2.0 also expands the dataset without simulating every new bug. After finding accepted scenarios with observable failures, it generates alternative mutations at the same locations, simulates only a subset, and estimates acceptance for the rest. This skips 63.6% of AES and 33.9% of FabScalar variant simulations. Full simulation finds that 77.7% of AES variants and 95.2% of FabScalar variants are accepted, with a 1.09% estimation error on the directly comparable FabScalar set. These results show that focusing LLMs on semantic rewriting lowers inference and simulation cost while improving consistency across models and designs.

title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
text: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic scene reconstruction. Existing 3DGS color transfer and interactive editing methods are guided by reference images and user-specified color adjustments. However, in many applications, users simply want aesthetically guided color enhancement that automatically makes the scene more visually appealing while maintaining consistent colors and tones across viewpoints. We present ReTouchGS, to our knowledge the first framework for reference-free aesthetic color enhancement of pretrained 3DGS models. It predicts a scene-level color lookup table (LUT) from the model and its associated camera parameters. ReTouchGS also supports reference-guided color transfer by fitting a scene-level LUT using one edited view of the same scene and its corresponding original render. A shared blend-aware color refinement network with only 44.7K parameters refines an analytic color update to realize either color mapping without rendering. It preserves geometry and delivers standard 3DGS assets in seconds. We also design the ReTouch3D benchmark to support the evaluation of aesthetic color enhancement and reference-guided color transfer across viewpoints. Experiments demonstrate high color accuracy and strong generalization to unseen scenes in both aesthetic color enhancement and reference-guided color transfer.

title: The Rhythm of Generated Video: Latent Chunking Leaves Periodic Traces in Compressed Bitstreams
text: Most AI-generated video detectors analyze decoded pixels and overlook how videos are produced. We show that causal video autoencoders leave an architecture-specific rhythm in compressed bitstreams: their temporal stride concentrates unpredictable content at latent-chunk boundaries, so rate-distortion optimized encoders allocate bits periodically. Without decoding pixels, we observe four-frame pulses in CogVideoX and Wan2.2 and eight-frame pulses in LTX-Video, which are absent from content-matched camera footage. Passing camera footage through a generator's autoencoder alone induces the pulse, supporting its proposed origin. A training-free peak-ratio statistic separates generated from camera video (AUC 0.84-0.94) and persists across tested quantization settings and H.264/H.265 encoding. Frame-size traces also identify four commercial generators, with 89.2%, 84.1%, and 83.0% accuracy under H.264, H.265, and AV1, beating the pixel-based UnivFD baseline (72.7-73.6%). Our results directly link generative architecture to measurable coding demand.

title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
text: Coding agents make videos by writing and refining programs in a build--inspect--edit loop. A finished film costs a median of $2.85 in model calls and 11 minutes, over a third of that time in builds that block the agent. We find that much of this time is avoidable, for two reasons. First, 37.5% of the frames of a session's later films were drawn before, many shifted in time or inside an edited scene. Second, half of the builds stop at a check, where the agent needs only the verdict, but which builds stop is unknown until the checks finish. We present CodeReel, a training-free execution layer behind agents' existing commands. Exact frame reuse keys each frame by its drawing commands, regardless of its position in time, and reuses each frame whose key recurs. Blocking-aware scheduling runs the checks first and starts the render alongside them, at idle priority, unless the session's recent builds make a pass unlikely. Scheduling spends CPU to answer sooner and reuse returns it; exact keys let later versions use frames rendered for a failed one as the agent thinks. We introduce EditLoop, a benchmark of replayable agent sessions whose films are checked against renders from scratch. On it, CodeReel cuts the agent's wait by 36.3% against Rebuild, a warm pipeline with parallel rendering, and by 57.9% against Sequential, today's step-by-step pipeline. On time-shifting edits its reuse renders 43.9%, close to the 43.0% whose pixels are new, while Manim-style caching renders 99.8%. With real agents, the median wait per build is 0.62x Rebuild's in Claude Code, on topics never used in development, and 0.67x in Codex CLI. The gain holds for five models and two frameworks.

title: Beyond Attribute-Centric Fairness: Modelling and Mitigating Unified Bias Representation in Omni-modal Large Language Models
text: Omni-modal large language models (OLLMs) provide joint multimodal understanding and generation capabilities, making them well-suited to complex environments and promising backbones for next-generation AI. Despite these advances, the harmful stereotypes encoded in such models manifest in increasingly diverse forms, leading to broader and more severe societal consequences. Existing debiasing methods typically impose separate fairness objectives for each sensitive attribute and modality to minimise demographic-dependent variations. However, in omni-modal settings, this attribute-centric paradigm struggles to jointly address diverse social biases with distinct fairness objectives and to generalise beyond predefined attributes. To this end, we propose OmniDebias, one of the first methods for promoting fairness in OLLMs, which employs a bias-centric formulation to extract and mitigate a shared bias representation across attributes and modalities while preserving attribute-related knowledge. Specifically, we exploit activation inconsistencies of a given attribute (e.g., gender) across semantic contexts (e.g., occupations) to disentangle bias from legitimate knowledge. We further consolidate multiple extracted biases into a shared representation, formulating a unified objective that captures the underlying structure across social biases and generalises to unseen attributes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that eliminating unified bias with both post-hoc editing and fine-tuning can consistently improve fairness across diverse attributes and modalities in OLLMs while maintaining favourable utility.

title: LOCUS: Causal Support Windows for Attribute Control in Autoregressive Image Generation
text: Unified autoregressive (AR) image generators struggle to satisfy multiple attribute constraints in a single prompt. Although these attributes are decodable from image-token latents, editing those latents at test time remains difficult. Adding a fixed attribute direction to the prefix can reinforce a requested attribute but rarely overrides a conflicting one, such as turning a car red when the prompt specifies blue. We investigate how the effect of an intervention depends on where it acts in the image-token sequence. We introduce the causal support profile, which measures, for each attribute, how often patching image-token states within a given window flips the rendered attribute. Structural attributes (count and position) are most responsive in early, narrow windows, while appearance attributes (color, size, and material) respond over later, broader windows. A budget-matched comparison of early and middle windows shows that the effect of window location depends on the target attribute, and two-dimensional support maps show that the responsive regions track spatial content. Based on these profiles, we propose LOCUS (Latent Optimization in Causal Support windows), which diagnoses which attribute failed and routes test-time latent optimization to its corresponding support window. With the generator, optimizer, reward, verifier, and token budget held fixed, support-routed windows outperform late windows by 23.6 percentage points in GenEval++ macro accuracy. With the generator frozen, LOCUS raises Janus-Pro's GenEval++ accuracy from 24.6% to 46.8% overall and from 19.5% to 40.5% on multi-attribute tags. On GenEval, LOCUS repairs 48.1% of failed generations in one rollout, compared with 37.4% for prefix optimization, and needs 14% fewer rounds on average to succeed.

title: TabDAG: Structured Evolutionary Search for Tabular Feature Engineering
text: Feature engineering can improve tabular prediction, but useful transformations are compositional, data-dependent, and subject to leakage constraints. We present TabDAG, a framework that combines evolutionary search with a graph representation of feature-engineering programs. Nodes implement row-wise or data-fitted transformations; edges encode dependencies among raw variables, intermediate values, and final features. The representation supports interactions, statistical encodings, clustering- and neighborhood-based features, and multi-stage compositions in a single executable program. Mutations are structured edits constrained by a parent-specific schema and checked before evaluation. In our experiments, no structurally invalid program reached evaluation, although proposals could be rejected and valid graphs could still fail at runtime. Across ten regression and classification datasets and three tabular model families, evolved features improve predictive performance over raw inputs. TabDAG and its combination with OpenFE achieve the two best mean ranks among the compared methods; pairwise rank differences between feature-engineering methods do not survive multiple-testing correction. The LLM-based searches use the same backbone and candidate-evaluation budget. A controlled ablation compares free-form Python, whole-graph JSON, and constrained graph edits with the search engine, budget, and backbone held fixed. Constrained edits yield fewer failed evaluations than either rewrite baseline. The resulting graphs expose the transformations and dependencies selected by search, enabling feature-level analysis of the observed gains.

title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing
text: Instruction-driven image editors produce convincing local edits in one pass, but inside an iterative refinement loop every accepted output becomes the next input, so unintended changes outside the requested region accumulate. We present ConserveEdit, an editor-agnostic controller that treats each refinement step as a transaction against a contract compiled once from the source image. The contract separates what may change (the authorized region of each target, with a bounded halo for shadows and reflections) from what must survive (protected content with explicit tolerances). Candidates from a frozen editor are composed through a source-anchored mask and committed only if target progress, drift on protected content, and image quality pass as separate tests; otherwise the step is rolled back and repaired. For any editor, this keeps every pixel outside the authorized region bit-exact and bounds drift independently of the number of iterations, whereas no fixed scalar trade-off reproduces the separate tests. On all 1053 MagicBrush test edits with a frozen Qwen-Image-Edit, masking is necessary but not sufficient. A direct call already alters the rest of the image (12.1 dB PSNR outside the mask); composed through the source-anchored mask, it stays bit-exact there and its DINO similarity to the ground truth rises from 0.67 to 0.85, matching ConserveEdit, so this gain comes from the mask. Next to automatic masks, however, masked direct editing changes a protected face or text on 48% of turns, and masked scalar selection avoids this mostly by abstaining (23% constrained success). Because its drift test names the violated entity, ConserveEdit shrinks the support instead (2% violations, 53% constrained success); in a simulator with known ground truth it raises constrained success from 55.0% to 61.8%. Automatic grounding remains the main bottleneck. Code and logs will be released.

title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
text: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals). For each family, we prove that an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to having an exact Gaussian fermionic TNS representation with a finite bond dimension determined by the Renyi-0 entropy. We also establish equivalent characterizations in terms of compactly supported Wannier-type orbitals and the momentum-space wavefunction, relating the spatial extent of these orbitals and the structure of the wavefunction to the required bond dimension.

title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
text: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings. Here, we develop an end-to-end computational pipeline connecting molecular structures to OTOC dynamics in protein systems. Our framework incorporates molecular motion through molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging appropriate for powder samples, and spin-network truncation, using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. We apply this framework to a dataset of over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 protein systems, spanning interspin distances of 5-17 A. We find that OTOC arrival times scale approximately linearly with interspin distance, revealing system-dependent operator-spreading velocities that enable correlations to propagate over extended distances within milliseconds. Our sensitivity analysis further shows that individual OTOCs predominantly constrain a single structural parameter, primarily associated with interspin distance. Together, these findings highlight the potential of OTOCs to probe spatially extended spin correlations on timescales compatible with solid-state NMR experiments.

title: Learning Grounded Reasoning from Human Gaze
text: Human visual reasoning is driven by systematic exploration and extraction of task-relevant visual evidence. Human gaze provides a window into this process, making gaze a useful source of guidance for visually-grounded reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs). However, human gaze also includes noise and redundancies that may transfer poorly to VLMs. In this work, we investigate how human gaze data can be effectively leveraged to improve visual reasoning in VLMs, while maintaining alignment with human behavior. We collect 7,109 human gaze trials from a diverse and challenging set of visual reasoning tasks, and train grounded reasoning models with different forms of gaze guidance. Across evaluations in chart understanding, visual search, and counting, we find that using human gaze as a prior for grounded reasoning consistently outperforms supervision using the full gaze sequence. Based on these findings, we introduce GGR (Gaze-Guided Reasoner), which achieves greater human alignment and more reliable visual grounding while matching or outperforming leading grounded-reasoning baselines in accuracy. Reinforcement learning further improves task accuracy, gaze alignment, and grounding quality despite using no gaze supervision. Behavioral analyses show that gaze supervised models exhibit more visual exploration before arriving at an answer. Our results suggest that the value of human gaze lies in guiding spatial exploration and shaping reasoning behavior without requiring complete imitation of human behavior.

title: A Universal Ratio Linking Cosmic Expansion and the Growth of Structure
text: We identify a universal relation between the onset of cosmic acceleration ($z_t$) and the turnover ($z_{\rm pk}$) of the linear growth observable $fσ_{8}$. In a spatially flat $Λ$CDM Universe, these two redshifts obey $R \equiv (1+z_t)/(1+z_{\rm pk}) = 1.1596$, independent of the present matter fraction and the overall expansion and growth normalisations. This provides a new consistency test for $Λ$CDM, linking both background and growth dynamics. We further establish the conditions under which this extends to broader classes of dark energy and modified gravity theories.

title: Any2Building: Unifying Point Clouds and Images for Building Reconstruction via Shared Spatial Queries
text: Abstracting structured buildings from limited observations is essential for 3D urban modeling and digital twins. Partial point clouds and overhead images of the same building provide incomplete 3D surface measurements and visual cues to its footprint, roof geometry, and rooftop structures, respectively. This motivates a unified framework that aligns geometric and visual cues in 3D and reconstructs buildings from either or both modalities. Building on this connection, we present Any2Building, a unified model for Level of Detail 2 (LoD2) building reconstruction from partial point clouds, overhead images, or both, with optional coarse geometric priors. At its core is an occupancy-grounded shared spatial queries representation that organizes available observations within a common 3D grid. Supervised by complete building surface voxels, these queries connect observational evidence to target geometry, enabling a shared generator to learn structural priors across tasks and providing spatial guidance for recovering missing structure. A trained voxel conditional surface-generation and low-poly remeshing pipeline then converts the predicted structure into compact LoD2 building models. To support this framework, we introduce BuildingWorld-Image, comprising approximately one million paired samples of partial point clouds, overhead images, and LoD2 building models across 18 cities. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that Any2Building outperforms existing methods in geometric reconstruction accuracy across unimodal and multimodal point-cloud completion, single-image building generation, and prior-assisted generation, while maintaining detailed and robust recovery when point cloud input modality is degraded.

title: Photon condensation driven by scalar spin chirality
text: Gauge invariance forbids equilibrium photon condensation for spatially uniform electric-dipole coupling, motivating alternative routes based on orbital magnetic response. We show that triangular molecular magnets coupled to a cavity support photon condensation driven by emergent scalar spin chirality. Starting from the half-filled Hubbard model in the Mott regime, we derive an effective Hamiltonian in which virtual ring exchange couples the cavity flux directly to scalar spin chirality. Mean-field theory, collective-fluctuation calculations, and finite-size exact diagonalization reveal a phase with spontaneous chirality ordering and a macroscopic cavity displacement, together with hybrid chirality-photon excitations. The condensation threshold can be tuned electrically through the molecular chirality splitting. Our results establish emergent orbital degrees of freedom in frustrated magnets as a route to equilibrium light-matter ordering beyond conventional dipolar cavity quantum electrodynamics.

title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
text: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll Δ_χ\ll Δ^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory. For the three-dimensional Ising model, Monte Carlo simulations yield a perimeter coefficient in good agreement with a Padé interpolation of our $\varepsilon$-expansion result.

title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs
text: Video question answering under tight frame budgets requires preserving localized motion and event order, yet current video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reduce comprehension to static multi-image reasoning by discarding unselected frames and encoding keyframes independently: (1) Spatially, whole-frame pooling dilutes small moving targets into static backgrounds; (2) Temporally, dropping intermediate frames or averaging tokens erases inter-frame motion, confusing direction, speed, and order. We propose VIVID (Visual Inter-frame Variations and Individual Dynamics), which moves beyond static snapshots like human vision: keyframes capture core states while inter-frame Patch Diffs preserve neighboring changes within $K_f$ keyframes. Autonomous Delta-Driven Keyframe Planning (ADKP) selects anchors from a $3\text{ fps}$ pool and feeds surrounding patch differences into Dual-Road Change Memory (DRCM), forming Dynamic Tokens at zero extra anchor tokens alongside a camera-stabilized Active Motion Region of Interest (ROI) and chronological Entity State Chains. Adding $0.22\%$ trainable parameters to a frozen $27\text{B}$ backbone, VIVID-Small ($50$ examples, $\sim 1.5$ GPU hours) beats all eleven baselines in overall accuracy across $8,083$ questions and trails only VIVID-Large ($3,600$ examples), which leads on MotionBench, Video-MME, and TempCompass.

title: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system with general bulk viscosity and Navier slip boundary conditions
text: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with Navier slip boundary conditions is established in a smooth bounded domain that may be multiply connected. Arbitrarily large initial data and vacuum are allowed, and the positive doping profile may have large spatial variations. The bulk viscosity satisfies a logarithmic derivative bound and a growth condition on its primitive, including every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with a logarithmic gain larger than one half. Time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponential convergence to the nonconstant hydrostatic state are obtained. For strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential convergence to the hydrostatic state in higher Sobolev norms are proved. An initial vacuum point persists and causes exponential growth of density gradients.

title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech
text: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them promising for speech-related applications. These include automatic lip reading, audiovisual speech analysis, and human-robot interaction, particularly in challenging environments characterized by low illumination or high dynamic range. Event-based lip reading, speaker recognition, and voice activity detection, however, mostly operate on a cropped region of interest (ROI), by hand or by the dataset, and no event-based method supplies that ROI as a spatial region; existing event-based face analysis gives the mouth as landmarks, which presents a mismatch between application and localization. The present work predicts a dense heatmap over the lip region from the full event "frame". Events are encoded as a polarity-separated voxel grid and processed at every location by a two-pathway continuous-time recurrent network (CT-RNN) with learned, log-space bounded time constants acting on the real elapsed time of each bin: a stateless fast pathway and a stateful slow pathway, utilised for refining and anchoring the prediction. The model reaches 69.5% on lips on four unseen speakers and switches target only 2.1 times per second, against 8.9 and 11.0 for convolutional baselines with more parameters. Adding a spatial encoder improves precision but fails on a new face scale. On a real event sensor, trained only on simulated events, the proposed model reaches 58.0% on lips against 43.2% for the CNN, with fewer than half its target switches.

title: Emergent Attraction and Competing Orders near the Van Hove Singularity in Rhombohedral $n$-layer Graphene
text: Unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral $n$-layer graphene exhibits a rich phase diagram with multiple distinct superconducting regions, whose microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we investigate the competition between charge-density-wave (CDW) and pair-density-wave (PDW) instabilities near the inner van Hove singularities (VHSs), using a patch renormalization-group approach with the realistic band structures incorporated. We identify two key findings. First, we find an effective attractive interaction emerging from purely repulsive interactions through RG flow in the presence of $C_3$ symmetry breaking. The resulting interaction structure, with two repulsive couplings and one attractive coupling, gives rise to competing CDW and PDW instabilities. Second, the competition is controlled by the detuning from the VHS. While CDW dominates near the VHS filling and at higher temperatures, PDW becomes the leading instability on either side of the VHS and at lower temperatures. This mechanism naturally produces two superconducting regions separated by a CDW-dominated regime, providing a possible qualitative explanation for the experimentally observed separation between SC1 and SC2.

title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
text: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone. Removal is exact within each layer; as with key-value eviction in attention, expired frames can retain residual influence through the cached inputs computed by earlier layers. We design a dedicated data structure and GPU kernels to achieve low caching and composition overhead. Across five open-source hybrid VLMs and four video reasoning benchmarks, Spool achieves the lowest p95 time-to-first-token in all 20 model-benchmark tests, reducing it by a geometric mean of $6.6\times$ over the faster of two recent vLLM baselines, while improving accuracy by 2.3 percentage points on average.

title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
text: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals). For each family, we prove that an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy is equivalent to having an exact Gaussian fermionic TNS representation with a finite bond dimension determined by the Renyi-0 entropy. We also establish equivalent characterizations in terms of compactly supported Wannier-type orbitals and the momentum-space wavefunction, relating the spatial extent of these orbitals and the structure of the wavefunction to the required bond dimension.

title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
text: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at https://github.com/xingyang-yu/StringQFT.

title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
text: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition. Following a quench to a free-fermion tight-binding chain, we uncover an unconventional dynamics in which the entanglement entropy decreases whereas the entanglement asymmetry increases, so that initially symmetric subsystems dynamically develop local symmetry breaking. This behavior is quantitatively captured by a quasiparticle picture describing the propagation of antipodal correlations. Our results reveal how symmetry-preserving dynamics can redistribute globally encoded symmetry-breaking coherence, making it locally accessible, and establish the initial entanglement structure as a key ingredient in determining the fate of local symmetries out of equilibrium.

title: Equilibrium Statistics and Stability in Random Two-Population and Three-Population Evolutionary Games
text: Multi-population matrix evolutionary games provide a framework for studying adaptation and strategic interactions among heterogeneous agents. When payoffs are uncertain, however, analysing a specified game does not reveal how frequently different evolutionary outcomes occur or how their probabilities depend on modelling assumptions. We study two- and three-population games with two strategies per population and both within- and between-population pairwise interactions, with payoffs fixed during each evolutionary trajectory. For two populations, we derive equilibrium-existence probabilities and analytical stability results for generic games and three structured classes: diversity, exclusive, and avoidance games. For generic two-population games, independent Gaussian sampling of payoff entries and of replicator coefficients produces different equilibrium statistics. Interaction structure further distinguishes coexistence from attraction: diversity and exclusive games share the same interior-existence probability, but only exclusive games admit asymptotically stable interior equilibria. Avoidance games admit transversely attracting equilibrium families without locally asymptotically stable individual points. For generic three-population games under independent payoff sampling, we obtain existence probabilities for all equilibrium types and joint existence-and-stability probabilities for boundary equilibria. Monte Carlo simulations support the analytical predictions and quantify multistability, while phase portraits illustrate initial-condition dependence. Under the same Gaussian payoff-sampling protocol, simulations show a lower frequency of fully mixed equilibria but a higher frequency of multistability for three populations than for two.

title: Sidorenko Inequalities in Oriented Graphs
text: We introduce relative Sidorenko and relative anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs, strengthening the corresponding well-studied notions for tournaments by allowing arbitrary host graphs. An orientation $\vec H$ of a graph $H$ is relatively Sidorenko if $\hom(\vec H,\vec G) \ge 2^{-e(H)}\hom(H,G)$ for every oriented graph $\vec G$ with underlying graph $G$, and relatively anti-Sidorenko if the reverse inequality holds. We provide a complete characterisation of the class of connected relatively Sidorenko graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs, and exhibit several families of relatively Sidorenko and relatively anti-Sidorenko oriented graphs. Despite the substantially stronger definitions, many known tournament Sidorenko and anti-Sidorenko examples satisfy the relative inequalities, suggesting a broader theory of these phenomena in arbitrary host graphs and motivating several new structural and classification problems.

title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
text: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.

title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
text: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings. Here, we develop an end-to-end computational pipeline connecting molecular structures to OTOC dynamics in protein systems. Our framework incorporates molecular motion through molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging appropriate for powder samples, and spin-network truncation, using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. We apply this framework to a dataset of over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 protein systems, spanning interspin distances of 5-17 A. We find that OTOC arrival times scale approximately linearly with interspin distance, revealing system-dependent operator-spreading velocities that enable correlations to propagate over extended distances within milliseconds. Our sensitivity analysis further shows that individual OTOCs predominantly constrain a single structural parameter, primarily associated with interspin distance. Together, these findings highlight the potential of OTOCs to probe spatially extended spin correlations on timescales compatible with solid-state NMR experiments.

title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
text: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video. We demonstrate how ID-MAE affords significant improvements in impairment inference results on both the DIVERT dataset and existing datasets, and enables strong results in additional tasks, such as trajectory and gaze prediction. For location-matched pairs, our model achieves a paired AUC of 0.706 for impairment detection on DIVERT, compared to 0.590 without reconstruction loss, improving over existing baselines. We probe the design space in terms of input modalities, masking scheme, positional encoding, attention mechanism, and decoding. We also investigate the interaction between various impairments in training and inference, demonstrating that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions. Code and data will be available upon acceptance.

title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
text: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC). Results show improved tracking over double-integrator MPC despite increased torque effort, while performance relative to DeePC depends on the reference trajectory.

text: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
text: Trajectory prediction models for automated driving are usually trained on data with a fixed sampling frequency, while positions received via vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication arrive at 1-10 Hz. We study whether a learned predictor that uses only the observation history keeps its advantage over constant velocity (CV) and constant acceleration (CA) models when the history frequency drops. On the Argoverse 2 motion forecasting dataset, the 5 s history of the focal agent was downsampled from 10 Hz to 5, 2, and 1 Hz, and the 6 s future was predicted without maps or neighboring agents. An LSTM-based recurrent neural network (RNN) trained for each frequency was compared with the same network trained at 10 Hz and applied to sparse histories after linear interpolation. Hypotheses and thresholds were fixed before training, the main RNNs were trained with ten seeds each, and results on 24,984 test scenarios have bootstrap confidence intervals over scenarios and seeds. The average displacement error of the frequency-specific RNN grew by 3.1% at 5 Hz, 10.1% at 2 Hz, and 20.3% at 1 Hz. Contrary to our hypothesis, its advantage over the better kinematic model did not vanish on straight motion and was 24-30% on both straight motion and turns at every frequency, while for pedestrians CV was more accurate. The 10 Hz model with interpolation was at most 1.3% less accurate than the frequency-specific model down to 2 Hz but 11.5% less accurate at 1 Hz. Each hypothesis was only partly supported.

title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
text: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed. We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations. At each step, WoRD runs one warm-started denoising chain per candidate goal, steers each chain toward the observed trajectory through a closed-form log-likelihood gradient, and reweights the resulting samples by Bayes' rule into a calibrated posterior over goals. We evaluate WoRD on simulated robot settings, pedestrian trajectories, and vehicle trajectories using four metrics targeting distinct failure modes. Across all three settings, the same inference procedure preserves calibrated multimodal beliefs through ambiguous prefixes where filter- and classifier-based observers collapse to a single mode or grow overconfident.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
text: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built from training data only. A separate leave-one-anatomy-out experiment tests parameter-free index extension: verified cases of an unseen solid organ enter the knowledge base, and the refiner stays frozen. A light shape-aware projection head on a frozen multimodal encoder maps embedding similarity to the shape agreement of the masks, so the knowledge base returns cases that the refiner can use as a shape prior. We evaluate GRACE on 18 public datasets spanning CT, MRI and ultrasound, using nine refinement configurations and seven upstream segmentors that span weak, mid, and strong operating regimes. We report each change with the DSC of its input mask. On the weak tier, the input DSC is 0.386 and GRACE adds up to +0.35 DSC. On a strong segmentor, the input DSC is 0.932 and the mean change is small. Transfer to an imaging modality that is absent from training and from the index is partial and depends on the anatomy, and remains an open research direction. Our results suggest retrieval-conditioned refinement is a practical alternative to anatomy-specific correction models. Code: https://github.com/robustml-eurecom/grace

title: Dynamics of a Single-Domain Dissipative Magnetic Gyroscope in Electric and Magnetic Fields
text: We formulate the coupled spin--rotation dynamics of a single-domain symmetric top ferromagnetic needle (a magnetic gyroscope) in static magnetic and electric fields. The conservative Hamiltonian contains the rotational kinetic energy, the magnetocrystalline and shape anisotropy, the Zeeman energy, the electrostatic energy of the dipole induced in the conducting needle, the linear magnetoelectric coupling, and the relativistic motional (spin-orbit) coupling. Gilbert damping is introduced, and in an electric field, Debye relaxation of the induced electric dipole of the conducting needle also results in dissipation. We give the equations of motion in the laboratory and body-fixed frames, with singularity-free quaternion kinematics. For a 120-nm-long single-domain cobalt needle in a 0.5~T field we find: (i) because the anisotropy field ($\approx 1.3$~T) exceeds the applied magnetic field, the spin reverses direction several times during the initial Gilbert-damping transient, and the parity of the number of reversals determines whether the easy axis ends up parallel or antiparallel to the spin; (ii) after the transient the needle librates about the field---precession accompanied by nutation at twice the precession frequency---with a period of about 20~ns, consistent with the libration period $2π(I_1/μB)^{1/2}$, while the Zeeman and rotational kinetic energies oscillate out of phase and the total energy is conserved; (iii) a static electric field $\mathbf E$ exerts on the conducting needle a shape-dependent polarization torque that tends to align the long axis of the needle with $\mathbf E$. The torques due to the magnetoelectric interaction and motional magnetic fields ($\lesssim1~μ$T) are negligible compared with the polarization torque. A conducting needle can therefore serve as a magnetometer only if $E\ll E_c$.

title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling
text: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed. The conditions under which the agents can combine their capabilities, however, are physical properties of the team and are known before any demonstration is collected. We encode the conditions as constraints on the team trajectories, and we enforce the constraints while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations of each agent alone. We prove that the proposed method can generate every team trajectory that satisfies the constraints, although the demonstrations contain no cooperation. Hence the constraints determine which team trajectories can be generated, and the demonstrations determine how likely each team trajectory is. Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show the effectiveness of the method, which generates cooperative team trajectories that satisfy the constraints and requires no retraining when agents join or leave the team. Finally, we implement the method on a multi-robot testbed.

title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
text: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging.
