title: AI-assisted liquid biopsy for early breast cancer detection: a laboratory translation framework for future multimodal integration.
text: Early breast cancer detection is imaging-dependent in clinical laboratory medicine, and there are important limitations for interval cancers and women with dense breasts. Liquid biopsy is being developed as an adjunct to imaging and tissue diagnosis. There are two classes of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) features and a separate class of extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated biomarkers, such as microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and proteins, to consider in the proposed framework. These literature reviews primarily focus on combinations of individual modalities, cfDNA-only combinations, cfDNA-protein panels, and multicancer models. There is a lack of prospective clinical validation of a machine learning model that integrates all three modalities for the early detection of breast cancer. We categorized performance evidence based on the purpose of the test for average-risk screening, dense breast triage, symptomatic assessment, high-risk surveillance, recurrence monitoring for breast cancer, and metastatic disease detection, and differentiated between direct breast cancer evidence and indirect methodological analogies. Translation involves modality-specific specimen processing, modality-specific analytical and clinical validation, locked/version-controlled pipelines, patient-, site-, and time-level data partitioning, leakage control, pre-specified thresholds and abstention rules, calibration assessment, external validation, subgroup analyses, reportable quality-control metrics, and defined revalidation triggers.

title: Sex-Specific Phenotypic Architecture in Cardiac Amyloidosis Identified by Explainable Machine Learning.
text: Females are under-represented in cardiac amyloidosis (CA), but whether this reflects sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity or differences in disease prevalence remains unclear. The objectives of the study was to characterize sex-associated differences in presentation and prognosis across CA subtypes using unsupervised clustering. We retrospectively analyzed 2,216 patients with confirmed CA enrolled between 2010 and 2022: light-chain amyloidosis (AL) (n = 583), variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) (n = 432), and wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRwt) (n = 1,201). Self-organizing maps with k-means partitioning were applied separately to each subtype, and conditional inference trees identified key phenotypic discriminators. Females represented 40.8%, 33.8%, and 15.9% of AL, ATTRv, and ATTRwt cohorts, respectively. Clustering identified 4 AL, 6 ATTRv, and 6 ATTRwt phenotypes. Across subtypes, female-predominant clusters generally showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, lower cardiac remodeling burden, and less pronounced biomarker elevation. Female-predominant AL clusters included preserved-function and multisystem profiles, whereas ATTRv clusters included neurologic-dominant and older cardiometabolic profiles. In ATTRwt, females were predominantly represented in a phenotype characterized by preserved systolic function and less structural remodeling. Conditional inference trees identified sex as the first discriminator in ATTRwt and a secondary discriminator in AL, whereas ATTRv clusters were primarily discriminated by cardiac variables and sex was not selected. Unsupervised clustering identified female-predominant phenotypes with less structural cardiac remodeling but distinct multisystem characteristics across CA subtypes. These findings support sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity in CA and generate hypotheses regarding female underrepresentation in contemporary CA cohorts.

title: Identifying sepsis treatment response subtypes and personalized bundles via causal machine learning.
text: To identify sepsis treatment response subtypes and derive personalized bundles using causal machine learning (CML). We conducted a retrospective multicenter study using the ICU-HAI registry from West China Hospital and the MIMIC-IV 3.0 database from the United States. Patients with sepsis in the ICU-HAI were assigned to development and internal validation cohorts. In the development cohort, CML algorithms were applied to estimate individual treatment effects (ITE)s of candidate interventions, and the optimal model was selected based on the adjusted Qini statistic. We then identified treatment response subtypes using latent profile analysis of ITEs and derived subtype-specific personalized bundles using LASSO regression. The stability of treatment response subtypes and the effectiveness of the personalized bundles were first evaluated in the internal validation cohort. A LightGBM-based model was developed for subtype prediction and deployed as an online tool which were then applied to the MIMIC cohort for external validation, and bundle effectiveness was further assessed for generalizability. Among 39,586 sepsis patients from ICU-HAI, three treatment response subtypes were identified. All subtypes shared hemodynamic support strategies. Subtype 1 (younger, lower severity) showed greater responsiveness to epinephrine and corticosteroids, whereas subtype 2 (older with renal impairment) and subtype 3 (cardiovascular comorbidities) were more associated with metabolic stabilization and fluid resuscitation, respectively. The subtype prediction model demonstrated high discriminative performance (AUROC 0.84-0.93). In the internal validation cohort, bundle adherence was associated with lower ICU mortality, with an OR (95% CI) of 0.34 (0.28, 0.41), with consistent findings in the external validation cohort (N = 33,253), with an OR (95% CI) of 0.25 (0.23, 0.28). The marginal structural model using 30-day mortality as the outcome yielded consistent associations. Leveraging electronic health record data to estimate ITEs identifies distinct treatment response subtypes in sepsis. Tailoring treatment bundles to these specific subtypes may offer advantages over uniform care strategies and holds promise for improving clinical outcomes. Ultimately, this approach outlines a scalable framework for precision sepsis care, though these findings warrant prospective validation.

title: Passive Monitoring for Detecting Hypomanic Symptoms in Bipolar Disorder Using Explainable Machine Learning: Longitudinal Observational Study.
text: When trying to intervene early to prevent manic episodes, clinicians are hindered by patients underreporting their symptoms as they are becoming hypomanic or manic (ie, emerging symptoms). Continuous passive monitoring using wearable technology offers a potential solution to address this problem by capturing behavioral signals that do not depend on self-awareness. However, its clinical usefulness requires validation before implementation. This study aimed to evaluate whether passively collected wearable data can detect hypomanic symptoms using an explainable machine learning framework. We applied explainable machine learning to densely sampled multimodal data from a 2-year observational study of digital monitoring in 178 patients with a diagnosis of bipolar disorder (mean follow-up 540 days; range 120-706 days). Data on activity and sleep were collected continuously using wearable technology. Self-reported data were collected daily on their mood, energy, and anxiety, and weekly using the Altman Self-Rating Mania Scale (ASRM). To identify robust digital markers of hypomanic symptoms, we analyzed 252 time- and frequency-domain features from 43 participants who experienced at least 1 ASRM-defined symptomatic interval. Passively collected data achieved high accuracy, comparable with daily self-reported data in detecting symptomatic intervals (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.91 vs 0.93, respectively). Combined daily passive wearable data features achieved higher sensitivity (92.0% vs 85.4%), balanced accuracy (0.90 vs 0.89), and stronger rule-out usefulness (negative predictive value 97.8% vs 96.1%) than self-report data, with daily sleep features alone driving most of this signal (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.91, sensitivity 91.8%). The high classification performance using wearable data was explained by reductions in spectral entropy and flux across domains, reflecting a decreased complexity and variability in mood, activity, and sleep patterns, consistent with a shift toward pathologically stable states. Passive monitoring using wearable technology can detect hypomanic symptoms with high accuracy, supporting its potential as a clinically meaningful tool for continuous, objective monitoring in patients who underreport hypomanic symptoms. These findings are associative and concurrent in nature; they do not establish predictive validity. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate predictive validity for early detection of ASRM-defined symptomatic intervals.

title: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Predicting Significant Fibrosis in Steatotic Liver Disease: Model Development Study.
text: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent, and noninvasive identification of patients with significant fibrosis remains a clinical challenge. We conducted an exploratory evaluation of explainable machine learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a US-based cohort of adults with SLD, with particular attention to sensitivity, false-negative risk, and the limitations of using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) alone to assess screening suitability. We evaluated explainable machine learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a US population-based dataset. A total of 43 routinely available clinical, demographic, anthropometric, laboratory, and lifestyle variables were included. After preprocessing and imputation, data were split into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. The synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) was used to address class imbalance in the training set. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), k-nearest neighbors, naive Bayes, an artificial neural network, and a stacked ensemble were trained and evaluated. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen κ, and the AUROC. Because the intended use case was screening or triage, sensitivity was given particular interpretive importance. In addition to overall discrimination, a primary analytical objective was to examine sensitivity trade-offs, false-negative classifications, and the implications of model performance for screening suitability. Global and local model interpretability were assessed using feature importance, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values, individual conditional expectation (ICE) plots, and individualized explanations. Among 7056 participants, 716 (10.1%) had significant fibrosis. XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination (AUROC 0.79), followed by random forest (AUROC 0.78) and logistic regression (AUROC 0.77); however, XGBoost had low sensitivity (0.17), indicating limited utility for screening at the evaluated threshold. Logistic regression and naive Bayes demonstrated the highest sensitivity (0.65 and 0.55, respectively), suggesting that models with slightly lower discrimination may be more appropriate for triage-oriented use. Across models, waist circumference, BMI, cardiovascular comorbidity, sex, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and liver enzymes were the most influential predictors. In this exploratory model development study, moderate discrimination did not necessarily translate into clinically meaningful screening performance. The model with the highest AUROC showed poor sensitivity, indicating a substantial risk of false-negative classifications and limiting its usefulness for screening in its current form. Because imputation was performed before the train-test split, the reported performance estimates may be optimistic and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of clinical readiness. Leakage-free preprocessing, threshold optimization, calibration assessment, decision curve analysis, external validation, and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical application.

title: Single-Time-Point Time-integrated Activity Estimation for Dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA Therapy: Evaluation of Analytical and Machine Learning Methods.
text: The routine clinical implementation of patient-specific dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy can be challenging due to the need for multiple-time-point posttherapy SPECT/CT imaging to estimate time-integrated activity (TIA). Single-time-point (STP) approaches offer a more practical alternative, although their accuracy has yet to be fully established. This study aimed to evaluate existing analytical STP methods and to assess the feasibility and performance of a machine learning (ML) framework. Thirty-four patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer undergoing 177Lu-PSMA-617 therapy were retrospectively analyzed. Reference TIAs were derived from multiple-time-point 177Lu SPECT/CT imaging at 3 or 4 time points (TPs) postinjection (TP1: 0.7-2.1 h, TP2: day 1-2, TP3: day 3-4, TP4: day 5-7) in cycle 1 for 147 tumors, 64 kidneys, and 65 parotid glands using monoexponential or biexponential fitting. Analytical STP methods, proposed by Hänscheid and Madsen, were evaluated across different TPs. For each organ, a ML model was developed using a residual learning approach, in which the log-transformed ratio between reference TIAs and analytical STP TIA estimates was modeled. Input features included combinations of STP SPECT-derived parameters, baseline 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET-derived biomarkers (for individual structures and whole-body tumor volume), and clinical variables. Model performance was evaluated by using multiple quantitative metrics within a 10-times repeated 5-fold nested cross-validation framework and compared with purely analytic STP approaches. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations. Analytical methods showed strong performance at optimal imaging TPs (TP2 for kidney/parotid, and TP3 for tumor), with the largest errors observed at early imaging (TP1). Overall, ML models provided modest improvement over analytical methods across structures at most TPs. The best performance was achieved using a ML model combining PET/SPECT imaging features with analytical TIA estimates. The mean percentage errors of the models, across TPs, ranged from -1.7 ± 17.9% (TP2) to 7.4 ± 65.3% (TP1) for kidneys, -0.4 ± 12.1% (TP2) to 4.5 ± 26.7% (TP4) for parotid glands, and 1.4 ± 14.8% (TP3) to -4.1 ± 100.5% (TP1) for tumors. Within the present cohort and modeling framework, the inclusion of clinical variables did not significantly improve model performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that the ML models applied a positive correction to the analytical TIA estimates at early imaging TPs and a negative correction at late TPs. Analytical STP methods yield accurate TIA estimates when applied at appropriate imaging TPs. ML models that integrate analytical estimates with imaging features provide modest improvements in accuracy with less sensitivity to TP selection. However, optimal timing remained structure-dependent, requiring a compromise when a single acquisition is used. These findings support the potential of ML-driven STP dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA-617 radiopharmaceutical therapy to enable more flexible and clinically feasible workflows, pending further validation with larger and more diverse data sets.

title: From keypoints to classifications: A SHAP-driven TabPFN framework for forward head posture screening.
text: Forward Head Posture (FHP) is a prevalent postural abnormality among adolescents, linked to musculoskeletal imbalances and long-term health risks. To investigate its prevalence and develop a research-stage screening framework, we conducted a large-scale population study involving 1,577 Chinese adolescents, recruited for the screening and assessment of FHP. Building on this cohort, we propose an end-to-end predictive framework that integrates human pose estimation with tabular machine learning. RTMPose was used to extract key anatomical landmarks from side-view images, followed by the computational derivation of seven predefined, anatomy-informed posture features. A TabPFN classifier trained on these features achieved an F1 score of 82.46% and an AUC of 0.837. Permutation-based SHAP analysis identified the horizontal angle between the right eye and shoulder as the strongest predictive contributor. A SHAP dependence plot also suggested a potential nonlinear dependence between features beyond that captured by pairwise correlation. These associations describe the behavior of the fitted model and do not establish causal biomechanical effects. These findings support the feasibility of a non-invasive and interpretable image-based framework for FHP screening. The framework remains a research-stage classifier, and prospective clinical validation and implementation evaluation are required before its use in school-based or public-health practice.

title: Analysis of outcome predictors in traumatic brain injury patients requiring intensive care management reveals an independent role of dynamic measures.
text: Research in traumatic brain injury (TBI) mediation and outcome have developed many methods of assessing patient state and response. While several outcome calculators for TBI have been suggested, these calculators do not include all collected variables in the management of these patients; with a paucity of studies on how these hundreds of variables contribute statistically to long-term outcome. Thus, this work endeavors to assess the statistical relationships between commonly collected variables at admission, and during the first 24 h of critical care, with overall patient outcome. From a retrospective dataset of 1,266 TBI patients requiring intensive care, unique patient variables (including demographic, injury pattern, pathophysiological, treatment and biochemical/imaging biomarkers) were explored. Intra-variable and variable reduction analysis were completed with importance assessed through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method. From all of this we developed predictive models to assess the 6-12-month Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) using general linear and XGBoost models. Of the 321 variables assessed, a final 36 variables were found to be the important and non-redundant, that included common variables (Glasgow coma scale (GCS), age, heart rate and blood pressure at scene of accident) and individualized measures (S100B level and long pressure reactivity). Survival based on these non-redundant variables resulted in an accuracy of 88.8% 0.723 AUC (0.65-0.795) vs the IMPACT LAB 80.9% 0.608 AUC (0.54-0.677). Notable combining the IMPACT LAB model with the non-redundant variables found an accuracy of 90.3% 0.765 AUC (0.693-0.838) and an improvement of the Nagelkerke R2 value from 0.317 to 0.499. These results found that overall general linear and XGBoost models behave similarly with an increase in non-IMPACT LAB variables performing better in XGBoost models. Broad categories of patient states like survival and favorable outcome can be determined by basic patient variables, however more dynamic measures of individualized response improve the predictive capacity for patient outcomes. Thus, to better understand patient state and more effectively monitor patient outcomes, dynamic and individualized patient physiology needs further evaluation.

title: AI-driven precision anti-infective therapy in critical care.
text: Severe infections, including sepsis and those caused by multidrug-resistant organisms, remain a persistent and significant global critical care challenge, leading to substantial morbidity, high mortality rates, and immense healthcare resource strain. Effective management is critically dependent on addressing the complex and time-sensitive needs for rapid diagnosis, timely antimicrobial therapy, accurate prediction of pathogenic microorganisms and antimicrobial resistance, and personalized therapeutic adjustment. Traditional methods, which often rely on non-specific scores and delayed results, are frequently insufficient for these dynamic, high-stakes clinical decisions. Artificial Intelligence have thus emerged as highly promising, transformative tools. We searched five databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of science, Cochrane library, and Scopus) from inception to October 2025 for studies involving AI methods applied to patients with severe infections. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, and case series. Data extraction focused on AI models, patient populations, outcomes, and management strategy application across five key clinical domains. A total of 78 studies met the inclusion criteria. AI models demonstrated significant utility in infection types and sepsis risk assessment, achieving high sensitivity and specificity in early detection. Substantial progress was also identified in the prediction of antimicrobial resistance and the implementation of optimal antimicrobial therapy and timing. Furthermore, AI enhanced the prediction of prognosis and mortality and provided tailored strategies for optimization for special populations. The continuous advancement and development of machine learning models have improved the accuracy of predictions. AI technologies show immense promise across the entire spectrum of severe infection management, from early risk assessment to precision antibiotic dosing and prognosis prediction. While the field is burgeoning with high-performing models, standardized clinical validation and rigorous implementation studies are essential to translate this technological potential into widespread clinical practice and improved patient outcomes.

title: Five-Year Functional Outcome Trajectories After Acute Ischemic Stroke and Their Associated Clinical, Biomarker, and Imaging Features: A Longitudinal Multicenter Study.
text: Functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary substantially, yet the heterogeneity of long-term trajectories and their associated baseline features remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to identify distinct 5-year functional outcome trajectories and characterize their associated clinical, biomarker, and imaging profiles. This longitudinal multicenter study included 9073 patients with AIS from the Third China National Stroke Registry (2015-2018). Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to repeated modified Rankin Scale assessments from discharge to 5 years. We then compared clinical, biomarker, and imaging features across the identified trajectory groups, and applied machine learning coupled with SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to identify and rank the key features associated with each trajectory group. Data were split by center to compare model performance and select the best-performing model for feature interpretation. Four trajectories were identified: Favorable Rapid Recovery (33.8%), Favorable Steady Improvement (44.8%), Adverse Fluctuating-Worsening (15.0%), and Adverse Progressive Deterioration-Death Group (6.3%). These trajectories differed in their clinical, biomarker, and imaging profiles. LightGBM achieved the best internal validation performance (AUC = 0.711) and was selected for subsequent SHAP interpretation. The key features associated with each trajectory group included younger age and lower National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) for Trajectory 1; lower coagulation markers and lacunar infarction for Trajectory 2; higher NIHSS, large vessel impairment, and low education for Trajectory 3; and advanced age, multimorbidity, and elevated inflammatory markers for Trajectory 4. Sensitivity analyses showed broadly similar feature patterns. Four heterogeneous 5-year functional outcome trajectories were identified after AIS, ranging from rapid and sustained recovery to progressive disability and mortality. These trajectories were characterized by distinct clinical, biomarker, and imaging profiles. Baseline features, including age, NIHSS, coagulation, inflammation, and vessel impairment, were key features associated with trajectory groups, with varying weights and directions. These findings provide a foundation for hypothesis generation in future research on risk stratification, personalized rehabilitation, and secondary prevention.

title: Association of questionnaire-defined probable obstructive sleep apnea with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in US adults: a NHANES study with machine learning analysis.
text: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome integrates cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, and metabolic dysfunction within a prevention-oriented framework, but the population-level association between obstructive sleep apnea and advanced CKM remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 8,523 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Survey-weighted logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between questionnaire-defined probable OSA (pOSA) and advanced CKM, with subgroup analyses and interaction tests performed across predefined population groups. Six machine learning models were also developed for exploratory classification of advanced CKM, and Shapley Additive Explanations were used to interpret the selected model. pOSA was more common among participants with advanced CKM than among those with non-advanced stages. In the core multivariable-adjusted survey-weighted model, pOSA was associated with higher odds of advanced CKM; however, after additional adjustment for body mass index categories, the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.92-1.49, p = 0.197). In the machine learning analysis, XGBoost had the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.876), whereas the random forest model showed favorable calibration with an area under the curve of 0.868 and was selected for interpretation. Age contributed most to the model output, followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate, smoking, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, glycated hemoglobin, and mean systolic blood pressure. These findings suggest a potential association between pOSA and advanced CKM syndrome among United States adults, while highlighting the importance of considering adiposity when interpreting this association. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)-related symptoms are common in adults and often occur together with metabolic, kidney, and cardiovascular problems. In this study, we analyzed the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data to examine whether questionnaire-defined probable OSA (pOSA) was associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. We found that adults with pOSA had higher odds of advanced CKM. However, the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant after additional adjustment for body mass index, highlighting the importance of considering adiposity when interpreting the observed association. In addition, we also used exploratory machine learning methods to classify adults with advanced CKM and to examine the relative contributions of routinely available variables. These findings suggest a potential association between pOSA and advanced CKM in adults, while highlighting the importance of adiposity in interpreting this relationship. Further clinical studies are warranted to confirm this observation.

title: Artificial Intelligence in the Advancement of Mechanical Circulatory Support and Cardiac Care: A Systematic Review of Its Role and Potential.
text: In recent years, there has been a notable surge in the ability of machines to perform complex and intelligent human-centered tasks, particularly within the domain of cardiovascular health. Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms reflect the considerable potential for such analyses to meaningfully extend into translational device development and clinical usage of medical devices, especially mechanical circulatory support (MCS) therapies. Here, we investigate and report the applications, limitations, and strategies in which AI is currently being employed in MCS and the potential opportunities of AI approaches to advance the field of MCS. To effectively assess the scope and impact of AI in MCS, we conducted a systematic literature review. A comprehensive search of 4 recognized research databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, Ovid MEDLINE, and ProQuest) was performed using this Boolean string: "(Artificial Intelligence) AND (AI) AND (Mechanical Circulatory Support) AND (MCS) NOT (Heart Transplant) NOT (Cardiogenic Shock) NOT (Critical Care)." This strategy was designed to identify the application of AI in MCS only. Database search results were then screened by titles and abstracts, followed by full-text eligibility assessment and duplicate removal. Following these screening and eligibility steps, 30 of the 328 identified articles remained for inclusion. Most relevant publications covered two main subjects: the prediction and management of postoperative outcomes, and the development of personalized device-patient matching and timing. Across the reviewed studies, AI/ML models demonstrated promising performance in study-specific predictions of complications, recovery-related outcomes, and survival and were investigated as tools to support clinical decision-making. Barriers to broad implementation of AI include the necessity for sizable, high-quality datasets to achieve algorithm training benchmarks, the lack of organized and complete databases, such as INTERMACS, and limited computational resources. Emerging frontiers of MCS recognize the potential for AI and ML techniques to refine image recognition capabilities, diagnostic assessment, device placement, and post-implantation monitoring approaches in the future. AI-driven approaches demonstrate a promising convergence of computational power and clinical expertise, with the potential to support more personalized, efficient, and informed management of MCS patients. However, the current evidence remains largely exploratory, and broad implementation will require robust clinical validation together with attention to data integrity, model accuracy, resource access, and clinical acceptance.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Lung Cancer Diagnosis using Rapid Isothermal Amplification of Serum microRNAs.
text: Early diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is essential for improving patient prognosis. However, existing serum biomarkers remain limited in sensitivity, stability, and clinical translation. Here, we developed an NSCLC liquid biopsy strategy integrating tissue-serum consensus miRNA screening, machine-learning-based classification, and tunable cascade isothermal amplification detection. Candidate miRNAs were identified from tissue and serum datasets, and a four-miRNA-based support vector machine (SVM) model was constructed for NSCLC classification. Furthermore, a cascade isothermal amplification circuit composed of linear and exponential amplification modules was designed for rapid, programmable, and quantitative miRNA detection. This circuit achieved target recognition, signal transduction, and cascade amplification under constant-temperature conditions within 20 min. Clinical validation showed good agreement between the cascade circuit and RT-qPCR results. The four-miRNA SVM model achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.935 and 0.905 using RT-qPCR and cascade circuit data, respectively. In addition, a two-miRNA comparator model further demonstrated the compatibility of this platform with alternative classification strategies. Overall, this study provides a rapid, tunable, and clinically translatable molecular diagnostic strategy for serum miRNA-based auxiliary diagnosis of NSCLC.

title: Predictive ability of hyperspectral signatures from single immobilized spermatozoa as a novel approach to non-invasive sperm selection during ICSI.
text: Can hyperspectral imaging of single immobilized spermatozoa prior to ICSI be used to characterize individual spermatozoa quality and develop predictive models for fertilization, blastulation, and blastocyst usability? Hyperspectral imaging characterization of individual immobilized spermatozoa was successfully implemented prior to ICSI and enabled the development of predictive models for key reproductive outcomes. Sperm selection during ICSI is mainly based on morphology and motility, which provide limited information about functional competence. Most techniques capable of assessing molecular sperm quality are destructive and cannot be applied to the injected spermatozoon. Hyperspectral imaging (HS) is a non-invasive technique capable of generating molecular spectral fingerprints of individual cells. This prospective two-phase study was conducted between March 2020 and August 2024 and included 93 couples undergoing ICSI cycles at a single IVF centre. Single immobilized spermatozoa were imaged prior to ICSI using a hyperspectral camera coupled to a micromanipulation microscope. Phase I evaluated the feasibility and short-term technical repeatability of hyperspectral acquisition, as well as preliminary classification consistency across repeated acquisitions. Phase II included a safety evaluation using a sibling donor-oocyte design and the development of predictive models using hyperspectral spectra and clinical data. Machine learning models based on XGBoost decision trees were trained to predict fertilization, blastulation, and usable blastocyst formation. Hyperspectral imaging was successfully implemented prior to ICSI. Phase I supported high short-term technical repeatability under stable acquisition conditions, with a global intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.999. Exploratory spectral classification across repeated technical acquisitions achieved a sensitivity of 93.84% and a specificity of 96.76%. In the safety evaluation, fertilization, blastulation, and usable blastocyst rates were comparable between HS-ICSI and standard ICSI groups. Predictive models based on hyperspectral spectra and clinical data were developed, with chained models integrating both data types showing the most favourable balance between predictive precision and uncertainty among the evaluated model configurations. Model performance may be influenced by limited training data and class imbalance; therefore, further validation in larger datasets is required. This approach may enable non-invasive functional characterization of individual spermatozoa and could support the future development of more informed sperm selection strategies during ICSI. This study demonstrates the feasibility of implementing hyperspectral imaging of single spermatozoa within the routine workflow of an IVF laboratory. This approach could enable non-invasive functional characterization, predict reproductive chances of individual spermatozoa, and support the future development of more informed sperm selection strategies during ICSI. This work was supported by the Centro para el Desarrollo Tecnológico Industrial (CDTI, Spain; Project ID: IDI-20210432). The authors declare no competing interests. N/A.

title: Common centromeric variation associates with molecular and complex traits in humans
text: Human centromeres harbor extensive structural variation that has remained largely inaccessible to human genetics because their repetitive -satellite arrays are absent from standard reference and imputation panels. Here we catalog 188,589 centromeric structural variants (SVs) from haplotype-resolved long-read assemblies of 196 Human Pangenome Reference Consortium individuals aligned to the telomere-to-telomere CHM13 reference. Resolving recurrent SVs into monophyletic components along centromeric haplotype phylogenies makes them imputable from pericentromeric SNPs ([Formula] vs. 0.065 unresolved). In 124 individuals with haplotype-resolved nanopore methylation, we identify 418 same-chromosome SV-CpG associations that form local hypomethylation-enriched domains in the centromeric region, most strongly for deletions. We also show that a truncated 113-bp monomer on chromosome 8 is associated with the position of the CENP-A-associated centromere dip region (CDR) in 151 individuals, independent of array length. Imputed into 630 individuals with expression and splicing data, centromeric SVs are associated with 141 genes, 14 of them new relative to the SNP-based cis-QTL analysis, including the H3K9 methyltrans-ferase SUV39H1. In 315,204 All of Us participants, we identify 170 associations between 61 SV predictors and 27 clinical phenotypes, including substance-related disorders and breast cancer. Our study brings a previously inaccessible class of variation into population-scale genetics and links centromeric SVs to centromere organization, gene expression, splicing and complex traits.

title: Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST): Comparing Self-Triage Systems and Multiple Generations of OpenAI Models Against Preliminary Expert Consensus
text: As digital self-triage becomes more widely used, quality assurance requires evaluation of both emergency recognition and overall agreement with clinical judgement, including how these outcomes differ across generations of large language models. The Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST) project intends to provide a framework to compare systems for digital self-triage against a medical gold standard in Germany. As a first step in developing and demonstrating the methodology, we compared study-specific implementations of SmED 5.4.11 accessed via API and Infermedica Engine API via Microsoft Azure Healthcare Agent Service with five structured OpenAI configurations spanning multiple model generations: gpt-4.1, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, and gpt-6-astra. The manufacturers of SmED and Infermedica offer MDR-certified Class IIb triage products, but these certified products were not directly evaluated. An LLM-based patient actor covered 480 physician-curated vignettes derived from German routine triage data. A pool of seven physicians provided preliminary reference classifications and consensus for 480 vignettes. Recommendations were mapped to three urgency categories-emergency, acute, and not urgent-and evaluated using winsorised weights derived from routine triage frequencies. Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% (95% CI 35.566.3%) for gpt-4.1 to 99.9% (99.7-100.0%) for gpt-6-astra. Weighted exact three-category agreement (accuracy) ranged from 54.4% to 68.8%; gpt-4.1 achieved the highest agreement despite the lowest emergency sensitivity. No system performed best across all urgency categories. The later-generation OpenAI configurations showed a more precautionary triage profile resembling SmED, with higher sensitivity for emergency cases; gpt-6-astra showed the strongest shift. This cross-sectional comparison across model generations suggests a shift towards more precautionary triage behaviour, without establishing a longitudinal improvement in accuracy. These findings highlight the limitations of overall agreement for evaluating self-triage and support category-specific assessment. Broader expert consensus and evaluation, as well as further steps to reduce dependence on SmED-derived source data, are needed and planned before drawing conclusions about clinical safety.

title: Defining and Characterizing Visits To Emergency Departments For Musculoskeletal Conditions: A Retrospective Analysis Using Two Publicly Available Databases
text: IntroductionThere are multiple ways to define and identify potentially avoidable emergency department (ED) visits, making it difficult to estimate their frequency accurately. In this study, we compared the proportions and characteristics of potentially avoidable ED visits identified using three commonly used algorithms. MethodsWe analysed the publicly available Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV Emergency Department dataset to estimate the proportions and characteristics of potentially avoidable ED visits identified using i) the eventual discharge diagnosis (Diagnosis), ii) the use of hospital resources (Resources), and iii) the triage acuity score assigned to the patient during emergency department triage (Triage Acuity). ResultsThe proportion of visits identified as potentially avoidable differed significantly between algorithms (7 - 36%), and few visits (<2%) were identified as potentially avoidable by all three algorithms. Presenting complaints, discharge diagnoses, and patient demographics were all similarly affected. We found that the proportions and characteristics of potentially avoidable ED visits were affected by the algorithm used to identify them. ConclusionMethods for identifying potentially avoidable ED visits are not interchangeable. Choosing the appropriate definition and classification method will require researchers to carefully consider the types of visits and the characteristics of patients they wish to identify.

title: Environmental toxic metal exposure and conditional mortality survival among US adults: a prospective cohort study
text: BackgroundHeavy metal exposure has been associated with mortality, but differences in early and median survival times remain unclear. We estimated associations of blood lead and mercury and urinary cadmium and arsenic at lower conditional survival-time quantiles. MethodsWe linked the 1999-2014 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey to mortality records through Dec 31, 2019, including 24,338 adults aged 40 years or older. Weighted censored quantile regression estimated associations at the 10th, 25th, and 50th percentiles, adjusting for age and other confounders across five imputations. Mercury and arsenic analyses used 2003-2014 cycles; urinary-metal cohorts required observed estimated glomerular filtration rate [≥]60 mL/min per 1.73 mZ. FindingsOf 24,338 participants, 6,992 died. Doubling urinary cadmium was associated with 1.71-1.92, 1.50-1.67, and 1.35-1.53 years shorter conditional survival at the 10th, 25th, and 50th percentiles (n=7,061). Corresponding blood lead estimates were 0.63-0.71, 0.55-0.65, and 0.61-0.63 years shorter (n=24,021). Some median estimates were not estimable. Cadmium associations persisted after lead adjustment; lead associations did not persist after cadmium adjustment. Arsenic had no statistically significant association with mortality in this study. Mercury was associated with longer survival despite adjustment for fish or omega-3 intake, possibly reflecting residual confounding. InterpretationLow-to-moderate cadmium exposure was associated with shorter survival, with the largest absolute loss among adults who die earliest. These findings support continued efforts to reduce cadmium exposure, with particular benefit for adults most vulnerable to premature death. FundingNone. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched PubMed from database inception to Nov 10, 2026, without language restrictions, using metal names and biomarker terms combined with "mortality", "survival", "quantile regression", "life expectancy", and related terms. We prioritised prospective studies in adult populations and systematic reviews, supplemented by targeted searches for analyses of survival time. Previous studies have associated lead and cadmium exposure with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Evidence for mercury has varied across populations and exposure levels, and findings for low-level arsenic exposure in US adults have been less conclusive. Most cohort studies reported relative hazards, although earlier research examined metal-associated differences in longevity and used machine learning to investigate variation in lead-associated survival. Evidence remained limited on how associations with metal biomarkers differ between early and median conditional survival times in general populations. Added value of this studyAmong 24,338 US adults aged 40 years or older in NHANES 1999-2014, with mortality follow-up through 2019, we estimated associations of four metal biomarkers with the 10th, 25th, and 50th conditional percentiles of survival time after examination. Censored quantile regression provided estimands in years of life. In the urinary cadmium cohort of 7,061 participants with an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 60 mL/min per 1.73 mZ, a doubling of cadmium was associated with 1.71-1.92 years shorter to 10% mortality, compared with 1.35-1.53 years at the median. The cadmium associations persisted in NHANES III, although the largest estimate in that cohort was at the median. Lead and survival time associations were attenuated after adjustment for cadmium. Arsenic estimates were not significant. We observed positive association between blood mercury and survival time, which might reflect some residual confounding that we couldnt control for. Implications of all the available evidenceThe evidence supports continued population-level efforts to reduce cadmium and lead exposure. With CQR, we were able to estimate the survival differences in years of life a

title: HOW SAFE IS EXERCISE? CROSS-SECTIONAL ASSOCIATIONS OF CURRENT PHYSICAL ACTIVITY WITH SELF-REPORTED FRACTURE HISTORY IN MID-LIFE
text: ObjectiveTo examine associations between the volume and intensity of leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) and fracture during mid-life, and whether adherence to World Health Organization (WHO) physical activity recommendations was associated with fracture. MethodsCross-sectional analysis of 322,749 UK Biobank participants aged 40-65 years using self-reported physical activity and fracture data. LTPA volume (LTPAv) was derived from walking, moderate and vigorous activity. Participants were categorised into LTPAv quintiles and by adherence to WHO physical activity recommendations. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations with self-reported fracture within the previous five years, with analyses stratified by sex and adjusted for sociodemographic and anthropometric factors. Walking, moderate and vigorous activity were mutually adjusted to examine associations by intensity. ResultsParticipants had a mean age of 47 years and 53% were female. Odds of fracture increased with higher LTPAv, although associations were non-linear and varied by age and sex. Associations were strongest in the highest quintile among men and women aged 40-49 years (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.64-1.99 and OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.28-1.58, respectively). Vigorous activity demonstrated the strongest independent association with fracture. Meeting, without exceeding, WHO physical activity recommendations was not associated with increased odds of fracture. ConclusionsHigher LTPA volumes were associated with greater odds of fracture, particularly vigorous activity, with associations strongest in younger adults and men. Activity consistent with WHO recommendations was not associated with greater odds of fracture, supporting continued promotion of physical activity during mid-life.

title: Peripheral Predictors of Speech in Noise Deficits in a Population Cohort
text: BackgroundAge-related hearing loss is the leading sensory deficit in older adults, yet audiometric thresholds at conventional frequencies often poorly predict speech understanding. Two competing hypotheses have emerged: extended high-frequency (eHF) hearing loss beyond 8 kHz may unmask variance in speech performance, while cochlear synaptopathy, inferred via auditory brainstem response (ABR) wave I amplitude reduction, may degrade temporal coding independent of audiometry. This study aims to identify the best predictors of speech in noise deficits in the general population. MethodsThis is a cross-sectional analysis of 526 ears from 263 tinnitus-free adults (178 [67.7%] women and 85 men based on self-reported gender) enrolled in the Swedish Tinnitus Outreach Project, a population-based cohort study. Participants underwent air-conduction audiometry from 0.5 to 16 kHz, loudness discomfort levels, distortion product otoacoustic emissions, click-evoked ABR, and standardized speech-in-noise and word recognition testing in a clinical setting. Their associations with age and speech outcomes were evaluated using multivariable regression models. ResultseHF pure-tone average was the most age-sensitive auditory metric, accounting for 64% of age-related variance, compared with 16% for PTA4 (the pure tone average of audiometric thresholds at 0.5, 1, 2, 4 kHz). eHF PTA thresholds (pure-tone average at 10-16 kHz) predicted speech-in-noise performance substantially better than PTA4, otoacoustic emissions, or ABR measures. ABR wave I amplitude did not significantly contribute to speech outcomes, even in high-reliability recordings (ICC = 0.96), whereas prolonged wave I latency was associated with poorer word recognition, particularly in older adults. In young adults, delayed wave I latency minimally affected word recognition, but in older adults an increase in latency from approximately 1.0 to 1.8 ms was associated with about a 27-percentage-point reduction in word recognition scores. ConclusionsThese findings identify eHF audiometry as a dominant clinical predictor of both cochlear aging and speech outcomes, and challenge the translational relevance of ABR-based synaptopathy markers in heterogeneous human populations, with implications for hearing assessment, clinical trials, and early intervention targeting in aging cohorts.

title: Integrating GWAS meta-analysis with human brain cell mapping implicates the amygdala and cortical inhibitory interneurons in tinnitus
text: PurposeTinnitus is a common and heterogeneous condition whose genetic architecture remains poorly defined and whose definition varies across studies. We asked which common genetic variants are associated with tinnitus, to what extent genetic associations are shared across heterogeneous tinnitus definitions, and in which brain cell populations tinnitus heritability is concentrated. MethodsGenome-wide association meta-analysis of 19 independent population-based cohorts from Europe and the United States (hereby named EARGEN), comprising 961,085 adults of European ancestry (75,584 tinnitus cases and 885,501 controls). Tinnitus was defined by self-report in 17 cohorts and by diagnostic codes in two. Single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) based heritability and genetic correlations were estimated by linkage disequilibrium score regression, genes were mapped by gene-based association together with positional and expression quantitative trait locus mapping. Heritability enrichment was tested by stratified linkage disequilibrium score regression across 31 brain cell superclusters derived from post-mortem human brain donors, and across the 461 cell clusters that compose them. Enrichment was tested for replication in the Million Veteran Program (MVP) under a self-report definition (114,325 cases, 201,343 controls) and a diagnostic-code definition (77,601 cases, 310,953 controls). ResultsFive independent loci reached genome-wide significance (p < 5 x 10-8) on chromosomes 2, 8, 12, 13 and 16, two of which (rs10877884 and rs2147632) have not been reported previously. SNP-based heritability was 0.0137 (SE = 0.0009) on the observed scale and 0.0535 (0.0036) on the liability scale. Genetic correlations were significant with hearing loss, anxiety disorder, major depressive disorder, chronic pain, and four further psychiatric, sleep and vestibular traits. Three superclusters showed a suggestive enrichment in the midbrain-derived inhibitory neurons, amygdala excitatory neurons, and medial ganglionic eminence interneurons at a false discovery rate (FRD) of 0.067, the two latter of which reached significance in the Million Veteran Program (MVP) under the diagnostic-code definition (0.030 and 0.006). At cluster resolution, the amygdala excitatory cluster was found significant (z = 4.82, false discovery rate = 3.3 x 10-4), whereas none of the ascending auditory relay cluster were found enriched (z [≤] 1.71, false discovery rate [≥] 0.21). ConclusionTinnitus-associated common variation concentrates in limbic and cortical neuronal populations rather than in the ascending auditory pathway. The predisposition to tinnitus therefore appears to be central and largely non-auditory in origin. The small number of genome-wide significant associations obtained despite a large sample emphasizes the need for more detailed and standardized phenotyping focusing on the tinnitus disorder.

title: Trends in Cardiovascular Risk Factors, Disease Management, and Predicted Cardiovascular Risk Among US Adults, 1999-2023
text: BackgroundCardiovascular risk factors have changed in the United States, but trends in prevalence, management, and predicted risk through the post-pandemic period remain incompletely characterized. MethodsWe analyzed 11 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) periods (1999-2000 through 2021-2023) among 60,199 nonpregnant adults aged [≥]20 years. Survey-weighted regression assessed age-standardized trends, subgroup differences, and measurement-change sensitivity. We assessed awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and diabetes. PREVENT equations estimated 10- and 30-year risks among adults without self-reported cardiovascular disease (CVD). ResultsObesity increased from 47.4% to 57.2% (odds ratio [OR] per decade, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.16-1.30), with class III obesity more than doubling (4.7% to 9.7%). Diabetes increased from 8.2% to 12.7% (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.19-1.34), while current smoking declined from 24.4% to 14.9% (OR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.71-0.81). Hypertension, dyslipidemia, chronic kidney disease, and prior CVD showed no significant linear trends, although mean systolic blood pressure (BP) (124.2 to 120.2 mm Hg) and total cholesterol (203.6 to 188.1 mg/dL) declined, alongside improvements in other lipids. Hypertension and dyslipidemia awareness and treatment increased, but BP control peaked at 32.5% in 2013-2014 before declining to 21.5%, while LDL cholesterol control rose from 17.0% to 34.2%. Diabetes awareness increased, but treatment trends were nonsignificant. Glycemic control peaked at 51.2% in 2003-2004 before declining to 41.9% (P for nonlinearity <0.001). Predicted 10-year total CVD risk declined from 5.66% to 5.28%; atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) risk declined by 0.16 percentage points per decade (95% CI, -0.22 to -0.09), while heart failure (HF) risk increased by 0.10 (95% CI, 0.03-0.17). Their 2021-2023 estimates were nearly identical (3.20% and 3.19%, respectively); 30-year risks showed similar divergence. ConclusionsImprovements in smoking, blood pressure, and lipids coexisted with rising obesity and diabetes, declining blood pressure control after earlier gains, and divergent predicted ASCVD and HF risks.

title: Elevated HbA1c is associated with advanced brain age in severe obesity
text: IntroductionBrain-predicted age, estimated from structural MRI data, is a machine-learning biomarker of biological brain aging. Greater brain age gap (BAG) indicates advanced brain aging and is associated with cognitive decline and mortality. Cardiometabolic risk factors, including elevated blood glucose, body mass index (BMI), blood pressure, and cholesterol, increase risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in aging. Their relationship with BAG in severe obesity remains poorly characterized despite increased prevalence of cardiometabolic risk factors among this population. MethodsT1-weighted MRI data from 97 adults (BMI 35-73) were used to calculate BAG using ENIGMA and Pyment brain age models. Associations between BAG and HbA1c, BMI, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia were examined using multiple linear regression and MM-estimation robust regression, adjusting for age, sex, and race. Post hoc analyses stratified models by clinical HbA1c cutoffs (normoglycemic, prediabetic, diabetic). ResultsHigher HbA1c was associated with greater BAGENIGMA (B = 1.58, p = .014) and BAGPyment (B = 0.93, p = .013) in linear regression models. In robust models, HbA1c remained significantly associated with BAGENIGMA (B = 1.70, p = .002) but not BAGPyment (B = 0.71, p = .13). BMI, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia were not associated with BAG in either linear or robust models. HbA1c was associated with greater BAGENIGMA (B = 2.15, p = .01) and BAGPyment (B =1.21, p = .04) in those at or above prediabetic levels and with BAGENIGMA (B = 2.49, p = .047) in those with diabetes. ConclusionsElevated HbA1c is associated with advanced brain aging in individuals with severe obesity. BAG was not associated with BMI, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, which may reflect the restricted BMI range inherent to the sample with severe obesity. title: "We don't complain; it's just part of being a woman": frequency, knowledge, and sociocultural beliefs about dysmenorrhoea in a South African university cohort
text: ObjectiveDysmenorrhoea is highly prevalent and affects participation and quality of life. However, little is known about dysmenorrhoea-related knowledge and sociocultural beliefs in South Africa. We investigated dysmenorrhoea frequency, knowledge differences between menstruating and non-menstruating individuals, and associated generational, cultural, and religious beliefs in a South African university cohort. MethodsWe analysed cross-sectional survey data from university staff and students. Participants completed demographic and dysmenorrhoea-related knowledge questions and an adapted Working Ability, Location, Intensity, Days of Pain, Dysmenorrhoea (WaLIDD) questionnaire. Free-text responses exploring generational, cultural, and religious beliefs were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. ResultsOf 863 participants, 578 were current or past menstruators. Dysmenorrhoea frequency was 75.4% (95%CI 71.7-78.9), with 53% reporting moderate and 31% severe dysmenorrhoea symptoms. Knowledge of dysmenorrhoea was higher among participants who had menstruated than those who had never menstruated (80.4% vs 55.3%, p<0.001). Most participants (85.1%) wanted more dysmenorrhoea education. Analysis of 246 free-text responses identified five themes: (1) menstrual pain is normalised, dismissed, and expected to endure, (2) reproductive meanings attached to menstrual pain, (3) moral, spiritual, and cultural interpretations of menstrual pain, (4) negotiating competing explanations for menstrual pain, and (5) managing and controlling menstrual pain symptoms. These themes reflected intersecting sociocultural and biomedical understandings of menstrual pain. ConclusionDysmenorrhoea was common and symptoms were frequently moderate or severe. Sociocultural beliefs shaped how menstrual pain was understood, communicated, legitimised, and managed. Findings highlight the need to integrate sociocultural perspectives into menstrual health education, support, and healthcare services.

title: Associations of drinking water per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances with cause-specific mortality in men with prostate cancer
text: BackgroundOver 3.5 million US men are living with prostate cancer (PCa). Certain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are carcinogenic and impair cardiometabolic health. Due to comorbidities and treatment, men with PCa may be uniquely susceptible to PFAS. ObjectivesTo develop and validate a model for drinking water perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), and perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), and study associations of each PFAS with all-cause, PCa, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in PCa survivors. MethodsWe conducted a cohort study of 51,289 men with PCa diagnosed from 2006 to 2017 and followed through 2024 from the New Jersey (NJ) cancer registry. PFAS monitoring data (n=26,161 results) were obtained from NJ government evaluations and Community Water Systems (CWS) compliance reports and were used to estimate PFAS concentrations using a two-phase XGBoost model with 67 predictors of PFAS contamination across 566 CWS. PFAS predictions between 2006-2024 were linked to participants address histories. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated from Cox models with sociodemographic, clinical and time-varying neighborhood covariates. ResultsThere were 19,749 deaths, including 3,778 PCa deaths, and 4,972 CVD deaths over 466,843 person-years. Higher PFOA exposure was associated with all-cause mortality in certain quintiles (aHRQ2vsQ1: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.07-1.12; aHRQ3vsQ1: 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11) and with CVD mortality (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.01-1.24). Higher PFNA exposure was suggestively associated with all-cause mortality (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.22, 95% CI: 0.98-1.50) and PCa mortality (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.42, 95% CI: 0.96-2.10). Associations were strengthened when applying five-year lags. For example, higher PFOA (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.06-1.25), PFOS (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.07-1.25) and PFNA (aHR[≥]3.8ng/Lvs <2ng/L: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.06-2.31) were associated with higher all-cause mortality. DiscussionExposure to CWS-level PFAS was associated with higher mortality in PCa survivors. Replication is needed to confirm findings.

title: Influenza Vaccination and Disease Severity Among Older Adults Hospitalized with Influenza in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study, 2016-2024
text: ObjectiveSeasonal influenza remains a major cause of severe morbidity and mortality among older adults, despite vaccine availability. We assessed whether influenza vaccination was associated with reduced disease severity among adults aged [≥]65 years hospitalized with influenza in France. Methods and AnalysisWe conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults aged [≥]65 years hospitalized with confirmed influenza (ICD-10 codes: J09 or J10) between October 2016 and December 2024 were included, excluding 2020-2021. Vaccination status was identified from reimbursed community pharmacy dispensing records. Entropy balancing was used to balance sociodemographic characteristics, chronic conditions pneumococcal vaccination, and COVID-19 vaccination. Weighted regression models estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), intensive care unit (ICU) admission, in-hospital death, and a composite severe outcome. Multistate survival models assessed transitions specific hazard ratios (HR) between hospitalization, ICU, discharge, and in-hospital death. ResultsAmong 132,443 influenza-associated hospitalizations, 72,852 (55%) occurred among vaccinated patients and 59,591 (45%) among unvaccinated patients. Vaccinated patients were older (mean age, 82.3 vs 79.3 years). IMV occurred in 2128 vaccinated (2.9%) and 2544 unvaccinated (4.3%) hospitalizations (aRR, 0.88; 95%CI: 0.83 to 0.93). In-hospital death occurred in 6300 (8.6%) and 4952 (8.3%), respectively (aRR, 0.90; 95%CI: 0.87 to 0.93). Vaccination was also associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (aRR, 0.96; 95%CI: 0.94 to 0.98), but not ICU admission (aRR, 0.99; 95%CI: 0.96 to 1.01). Among patients admitted to ICU, vaccination was associated with a lower hazard of death (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.85; 95%CI: 0.78 to 0.92) and a 2-day reduction in the median time to discharge. ConclusionIn this nationwide cohort study, influenza vaccination was associated with lower risks of IMV and in-hospital death among older adults hospitalized with influenza. These findings are consistent with possible attenuation of disease severity and support efforts to improve influenza vaccination among older adults.

title: Mapping disordered eating symptoms in the ABCD Study through the Eating Disorder Symptom Index
text: Eating disorders (EDs) are serious psychiatric conditions that typically onset during adolescence and are often marked by a chronic and severe illness course. Capturing ED symptoms as they emerge is critical for charting risk markers and associated outcomes to inform early intervention and treatment efforts. The Adolescent Brain Cognitive DevelopmentSM (ABCD(R)) Study is one such key study that could accelerate these efforts, but has been limited to date by a lack of clear, clinically informed definitions capturing youth at risk for ED-related concerns. The current manuscript aims to address this gap by defining ED symptom indices (EDSI) with a reproducible framework developed in collaboration with ED researchers and clinicians to identify youth with patterns of ED symptoms and behaviors that approximate subthreshold and diagnostic-like presentations. We describe item-level definitions and decision rules used to construct the EDSI, which include symptom indices of anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, and other specified feeding or eating disorders. We then compare youth meeting EDSI criteria with those identified by existing ED categorical definitions in ABCD Study data releases. By providing transparent definitions and analytical tools for identifying youth with potentially clinically meaningful ED behaviors, the EDSI framework aims to facilitate more reproducible and interpretable research related to EDs using the ABCD Study dataset, while also providing a structure to examine the emergence, persistence, and change of ED-like symptoms longitudinally across adolescence and into young adulthood in future research.

title: Determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents in Sekondi-Takoradi, Western Region of Ghana: A community-based cross-sectional study
text: Mpox re-emerged as a global public health concern in 2022, and the Western Region of Ghana became the epicentre of the countrys largest recorded outbreak in 2025. Ahead of a sub-national vaccination campaign launched in October 2025, no study had examined the determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the region using a theoretically grounded framework. This study determined the sociodemographic and Health Belief Model-based determinants of mpox vaccine acceptance among peri-urban residents of the Sekondi-Takoradi Metropolis, Western Region, Ghana. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 580 adults in six purposively selected peri-urban areas and their surrounding communities between July and August 2025, before the vaccination campaign began. Vaccine acceptance was measured as a three-category outcome (accept, hesitant, refuse) and analysed using chi-square tests and multinomial logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, Health Belief Model constructs, and peri-urban area. Overall, 75.7% of respondents were willing to accept the vaccine, 12.9% were hesitant and 11.4% would refuse. Perceived vaccine safety was the strongest determinant: respondents who considered the vaccine very safe had markedly lower adjusted odds of hesitancy (adjusted odds ratio 0.02, 95% confidence interval 0.00-0.12) and refusal (0.03, 0.01-0.13) than those who considered it unsafe. Uncertainty about vaccine effectiveness was associated with hesitancy (9.83, 1.95-49.50), and belief in its effectiveness with lower odds of refusal (0.22, 0.06-0.86). Higher educational attainment was associated with lower odds of hesitancy, being a student or employed with lower odds of refusal, and acceptance differed between peri-urban areas (55.1% to 95.6%). Knowledge of mpox transmission was associated with acceptance in bivariate analysis (p < 0.001) but not after adjustment. Risk communication that addresses vaccine safety and effectiveness, rather than generic disease-awareness messaging alone, is likely to be most effective in improving mpox vaccine acceptance in this population, with unemployed and less-educated residents warranting targeting. As a pre-campaign baseline collected during an active outbreak, these findings can inform the vaccination response in the Western Region and preparedness in comparable peri-urban West African settings.

title: Silent Drift and Site-level Variance in Clinical AI: Real-world performance and subgroup analysis for post-market monitoring of an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for high-risk use case of pulmonary embolism
text: BackgroundFDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for pulmonary embolism (PE) detection has been widely used; however, its performance has not been analyzed for subgroups, clinical sites, and temporal stability. MethodsThis retrospective, six-site health system study evaluated the Aidoc BriefCase PE triage model (K190072) across 14,736 CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) examinations between July 2023 and March 2026. Reference-standard PE characteristic labels were extracted from radiology reports using a zero-shot LLM pipeline validated against a radiologist-annotated 600 reports ({kappa} =0.98). Model performance was evaluated across demographics, embolus characteristics, and site. Temporal behavior was evaluated on operating point by logistic regression, with and without site adjustment, and by segmented regression. ResultsPE was present in 1,402/14,736 examinations (9.5%). Overall sensitivity was 64.1% (95% CI, 61.5-66.6%), specificity 98.8% (95% CI, 98.6-99.0%), compared with 93% sensitivity and 93.7% specificity in the FDA 510(k) summary. Sensitivity fell with peripherality (central 88.6%, lobar or segmental 63.1%, subsegmental 33.3%) and with chronicity (acute 65.5%, chronic 57.4%). Sensitivity differed significantly between the two highest-volume sites, 68.7% and 55.7% (P < .001), with CT scanner as the only variable different between the two sites. The false-positive rate fell 40% per year (P<.001) at a similar rate at two sites, while sensitivity fell 15% per year at site A (P<.036), from 72.5% to 65.0% between two halves of the study period. The manufacturer did not report model updates or threshold changes during the study period. ConclusionsDeployed sensitivity was substantially below the cleared benchmark and varied 13 points by site. The gradual shift in high specificity at the cost of low sensitivity, either from data drift or threshold change, either not monitored or not documented by the manufacturer, highlights the importance of independent continuous post-market monitoring.

title: Food-level dietary factors reveal cardiometabolic risk hidden by diet quality scores.
text: IntroductionDiet quality scores are well-established predictors of cardiometabolic health but compress an individuals food intake into a single dimension, potentially masking dietary variation relevant to disease risk. Whether this hidden variation carries prognostic information has not been tested at scale. MethodsWe applied non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to the reported intake of 148 individual foods and beverages from 87,162 UK Biobank participants. We tested the association of NMF-derived intake factors with incident coronary artery disease (CAD), type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) over a median 9.4 years of follow-up using Cox proportional hazards models. We evaluated the prognostic value of the factors beyond diet quality scores using stepwise Cox models and net reclassification improvement (NRI), and characterized their metabolic profiles through metabolome-wide association analyses (MWAS) of 249 circulating metabolites. ResultsNMF identified eight reproducible intake factors that were stable across geographically distinct samples. Four factors were significantly associated with incident cardiometabolic disease: a high sugar and processed foods factor was adversely associated with T2D (HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.11-1.27) and CKD (HR 1.15; 1.07-1.23), while a plant-based and fish factor was protective for CKD (HR 0.90; 0.84-0.96) and a cheese and whole grains factor was protective for CAD (HR 0.94; 0.90-0.98). The factors improved disease discrimination beyond both diet quality scores ({Delta}C up to +0.0049) and correctly reclassified 8-16% more individuals, whereas adding either score to models containing the factors produced negligible further improvement. The high sugar and processed foods factor was associated with depletion of omega-3 fatty acids and the plant-based and fish factor showed enrichment in polyunsaturated fatty acids. ConclusionsFood-level dietary intake profiling captures clinically relevant variation that established diet quality scores mask, offering a path toward more personalized dietary assessment for cardiometabolic disease prevention.

title: Transdiagnostic Psychiatric Polygenic Scores Reveal Pleiotropic Effects Across Medical and Laboratory Phenome
text: BackgroundCurrent psychiatric diagnoses lack biological grounding. Using transdiagnostic psychiatric dimensions derived through data-driven genetic studies with large-scale clinical health records of multiple physiological and clinical outcomes, we can gain new insights into biological similarity and differences between such dimensions, informing nosological discourse. MethodsHere, we examined data from 108,182 individuals of European-like ancestry and 13,229 African-like ancestry across two healthcare biobanks. Genetic liabilities of individuals were estimated as polygenic scores for five first-order psychopathology factors (compulsive, thought, neurodevelopmental, substance use, internalizing disorders) and one second-order factor (hierarchical/p-factor). Phenome-wide and laboratory-wide association scans encompassed 1,520 medical phenotypes and 123 laboratory metrics, meta-analyzed across sites. People with lived experience were involved in the design, preparation, interpretation and reporting of this work. OutcomesWe observed robust associations with up to 143 conditions (14 disease categories) for first- order factors and 221 conditions (15 categories) for the hierarchical factor (OR=0.75-1.94). Circulatory, digestive, and respiratory diseases were linked to neurodevelopmental, internalizing, and substance use liabilities. Metabolic conditions were negatively associated with thought and compulsive liabilities but positively associated with the remaining three factors. Laboratory results, particularly lipid and glucose metabolism markers, supported these differential findings. Immune markers also showed differential associations, with C- reactive protein and Complement C4 specifically linked to neurodevelopmental and thought factors, respectively. Similar trends emerged in the smaller African-like ancestry sample. InterpretationOverall, these findings support ongoing efforts to define biologically informed subtypes in psychiatry, such as immuno-metabolic profiles, which can facilitate patient stratification in clinical trials and support transdiagnostic precision psychiatry approaches. FundingThe work was supported by funding from the participating institutions. BFs and NRMs contributions were supported by the European Communitys Horizon 2020 Programme (H2020/2014-2020) under grant agreement No. 847879 (PRIME). NRM was also supported by the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research (NWO) Innovation Programme (Vidi grant No. 09150172410043). Research reported in this publication was also supported by the National Institute of Mental Health of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number R01MH124851. The content is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the funders. Research in Context Evidence before this studyWe searched PubMed from database inception to October 13, 2026, without date or language restrictions, using combinations of the terms "transdiagnostic", "cross-disorder", "genomic SEM", "polygenic score", "polygenic risk", "phenome-wide", "PheWAS", "laboratory", and "somatic". We considered original human genetic studies examining transdiagnostic psychiatric genetic liability and its associations with medical or laboratory phenotypes, excluding studies without relevant psychiatric genetic analyses. Previous studies demonstrated shared genetic liability across psychiatric disorders and phenome-wide associations of cross-disorder polygenic scores, although evidence was limited by ancestry representation, sample selection, and phenotypic ascertainment. Studies jointly examining multiple transdiagnostic psychiatric genetic dimensions across medical diagnoses and laboratory biomarkers remain limited.
