title: Effect of Y1Ste20 gene knockout on the mycelial morphology of Chaetomium globosum CGMCC 6882.
text: Chaetomium globosum CGMCC 6882 is an endophytic fungus isolated from Gynostemma pentaphyllum. However, its mycelia tend to intertwine and aggregate during submerged fermentation, eventually forming dense mycelial pellets. This phenomenon severely impedes diffusion and transfer of oxygen and nutrients from the fermentation broth to the interior of the mycelial pellets, thereby limiting the fermentation efficiency of C. globosum CGMCC 6882. To address this issue, a recombinant plasmid, pFC332-5 SrRNA-Ste20 gRNA, targeting the Y1Ste20 gene was constructed using CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing technology. Subsequently, a Y1Ste20 gene knockout mutant, designated C. globosum XY1104, was successfully obtained through protoplast transformation, regeneration, and screening and identification. Results from solid dishes and liquid culture media investigations showed that C. globosum XY1104 exhibited a significantly lower mycelial growth rate than the parental strain, C. globosum CGMCC 6882. Moreover, its mycelia were shorter and more slender, and exhibited a denser distribution, with the formation of mycelial pellets completely eliminated. These findings demonstrate that Y1Ste20 is a key functional gene involved in regulating mycelial growth and morphological development in C. globosum and that targeted modification of this gene can be used to achieve morphological modification of fungus. Overall, this study provides reference for morphological regulation of other filamentous fungi.

title: CRISPR/Cas9-based Targeting of MicroRNA and Protein-Coding Homologs (MIR160, MIR167, and CAMTA3) from B. juncea: Targetability assessment of sgRNAs and MIR160 functional studies in heterologous system of A. thaliana.
text: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing is a powerful tool for functional genomics in crops. However, targeting specific gene locus is challenging in polyploid B. juncea harbouring multiple gene homologs. Design of sgRNAs necessitates careful consideration for achieving target specificity while reducing off-targets. Herein, we present a systematic workflow that combines in-silico sgRNA prediction with in-vitro cleavage assays to pre-screen guide RNAs specific to B. juncea homologs. The guides targeting conserved regions of MIR160 were functionally validated in heterologous system of A. thaliana. Computationally predicted sgRNAs were in-vitro tested in non-coding MIR160 (14 copies), MIR167 (15 copies), and protein coding genes viz. CAMTA3 to demonstrate applicability in CRISPR/Cas9-based editing and transcriptional regulation experiments. Analysis of cleavage assays confirmed that both number and positional distribution of mismatches in the PAM proximal seed region affect Cas9 activity. In MIR160 and MIR167, several sgRNAs showed in-vitro cleavage activity across multiple homologs, suggesting suitability for multiplexed editing of homologous genes. Although, deactivated Cas9 is employed in CRISPR activation/ interference experiments, targetability of sgRNAs specific to CAMTA3 could be validated via in-vitro targetability assays containing active Cas9 instead of dCas9. Based on cleavage assays, polycistronic assembly of a minimum of 8, and, 5 sgRNAs is recommended for editing of 14 and 15 homologs of MIR160 and MIR167, respectively, in B. juncea. Varying the order of multiplexed sgRNAs is proposed as a strategy to achieve selective or redundant editing. Combinations of guides are proposed for achieving in-vivo excision of ~58 nt fragment from MIR160 precursor sequences. Targetability of 3 guides has been validated for both editing and transcriptional regulation of CAMTA3. In-vivo validation of sg160_1, designed to simultaneously target 13 MIR160 homologs in B. juncea, was confirmed by mutation spectrum analysis of CRISPR-edited A. thaliana. The Ath-MIR160b locus showed editing (T1 and T2 generations) corresponding to moderate to severe developmental defects. To conclude, we propose an integrated CRISPR/Cas9-based work-flow for selective as well as redundant editing of homologous gene copies in polyploid B. juncea, thereby facilitating deployment of CRISPR/Cas9 strategies for Brassica crop improvement.

title: Precision gene targeting: comparative roles of siRNA, miRNA, and CRISPR technologies in gene silencing and genome editing: a review.
text: Precision gene targeting has emerged as a powerful approach for selectively regulating gene expression and modifying disease-associated genetic pathways. Among the principal technologies, small interfering RNA (siRNA), microRNA (miRNA), CRISPR-Cas9, and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) provide distinct yet complementary strategies for gene regulation and genome manipulation. siRNAs mediate sequence-specific post-transcriptional gene silencing through degradation of complementary messenger RNA, enabling potent and generally transient suppression of target genes. In contrast, miRNAs are endogenous regulatory RNAs that modulate multiple transcripts through translational repression and mRNA destabilization, thereby influencing diverse cellular processes and regulatory networks. CRISPR-Cas9 expands the scope of precision gene targeting by enabling programmable modification of genomic DNA, whereas CRISPRi uses catalytically inactive Cas9 to achieve targeted transcriptional repression without introducing DNA double-strand breaks. This review provides a comparative and critical analysis of these technologies, emphasizing their molecular mechanisms, target recognition, specificity, delivery strategies, therapeutic applications, clinical development, advantages, limitations, and safety considerations. Collectively, these platforms have demonstrated therapeutic potential across a broad range of diseases, including cancer, genetic and metabolic disorders, cardiovascular and neurological diseases, infectious diseases, and ocular disorders. However, important barriers to clinical translation remain, including delivery limitations, molecular stability, target and off-target effects, immunogenicity, toxicity, genomic instability, and the need for precise and durable control of gene modulation. For CRISPR-based approaches, additional considerations include modality-specific genomic alterations, prolonged editor activity, and the ethical and regulatory implications of permanent genome modification. Continued advances in molecular engineering, delivery technologies, target-selection strategies, and platform optimization may improve the specificity, safety, durability, and therapeutic efficacy of these approaches and facilitate their responsible integration into precision medicine.

title: Multi-omics profiling identifies a CXCL9-PD-1+ CD8+ T cell axis for prediction of checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis.
text: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a life-threatening complication of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). We aimed to identify predictive biomarkers associated with symptomatic CIP (sCIP) and unravel the underlying pathogenesis. We integrated CyTOF, proteomics, single-cell RNA and V(D)J sequencing, single-cell secretomics, and spatial transcriptomics. These techniques were used to profile peripheral blood, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and lung tissue samples from two prospective multi-center cohorts of NSCLC patients receiving ICI combination treatments. Elevated serum CXCL9 levels combined with high frequencies of peripheral PD-1+ CD8+ T cells after induction ICI were associated with subsequent sCIP (AUC=0.954) and inferior overall survival (HR=7.19, p=0.004). Mechanistically, PD-1+ CD8+ T cells displayed a type 1 effector profile characterized by IFN-γ and MIP-1β secretion. CXCL9/CXCR3 signaling was associated with recruitment of these cells to inflamed lung tissue. The CXCL9-PD-1+ CD8+ T cell axis is associated with CIP pathogenesis. This mechanism supports a potential blood-based biomarker model for CIP risk stratification and identifies a promising preventive therapeutic target to optimize clinical management.

title: Integrating multi-omics data and experimental validation to elucidate the therapeutic mechanism of the Ephedra-Cinnamomi Ramulus pair in psoriasis.
text: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease driven by complex immune microenvironments, and the Ephedra-Cinnamomi Ramulus pair (EHCR) has shown therapeutic potential but its mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, by integrating network pharmacology, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and experimental validation, we show that, in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced mouse model, EHCR alleviates psoriasiform dermatitis during a seven-day IMQ/gavage regimen, with inflammatory fibroblasts nominated as a candidate cell population by target-score analysis. Mechanistically, EHCR suppresses the nuclear factor kappa B subunit 1 (NFKB1)/RELB, NF-κB subunit (RELB)/DExD-box helicase 21 (DDX21) signaling axis, wherein the canonical p50/p65 complex and RelB-containing non-canonical NF-κB complex may regulate DDX21 transcription, and this axis is hyperactivated in psoriatic fibroblasts. Two candidate bioactive constituents of EHCR, quercitrin and 3,3',4',5,7-pentahydroxyflavanone, showed measurable binding to p50 and RelB proteins in SPR assays and were associated with reduced NFKB1/RELB/DDX21 signaling in fibroblasts. Furthermore, EHCR attenuates GJA1-dependent, contact-dependent communication between fibroblasts and dendritic cells, with reduced gap junction protein alpha 1 (GJA1) expression and the abundance of dendritic cells adjacent to fibroblasts. Collectively, these findings suggest that EHCR attenuates IMQ-induced psoriasiform dermatitis during the seven-day IMQ/gavage regimen, in association with reduced NFKB1/RELB/DDX21 signaling in fibroblasts and attenuated GJA1-dependent, contact-dependent fibroblast-DC communication. The mechanism underlying these associations and their translational relevance remain to be established.

title: A public-data spatial transcriptomic framework for invasive lung adenocarcinoma tumor ecosystems and prognosis.
text: Public transcriptomic cohorts rarely contain audited spread through air spaces (STAS) labels or recurrence endpoints. We therefore evaluated a transparent invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tumor-ecosystem score as an exploratory cross-cohort framework rather than a clinical STAS predictor. We integrated GSE131907 single-cell RNA sequencing, E-MTAB-13530 spatial transcriptomics, an exploratory HRA001238/ST_LUAD processed subtype resource, and TCGA-LUAD bulk RNA sequencing. A fixed, equal-weight compact tumor-ecosystem score combined tumor epithelial, myofibroblast, invasive epithelial, CAF/ECM, and proliferation programs while subtracting alveolar differentiation. The formula was not optimized against survival, and no external preregistration or timestamped commit was available. Analyses benchmarked the score against ESTIMATE stromal and immune scores, an eight-collagen average, individual score components, and rank-based single-sample gene-set enrichment scoring (ssGSEA). Spatial sensitivity analyses accounted for repeated sections within patients, and TCGA models compared purity adjustment within an identical 155-patient subset. The GSE131907 reference contained 82,884 cells. The 40 E-MTAB-13530 sections came from eight patients and two donors. The mean-expression compact score differed by tissue class (Kruskal-Wallis H(2)=30.30, P = 2.63e-07); all eight patients had a higher patient-mean score in tumor than matched adjacent lung (paired Wilcoxon P = 0.0078), and the tumor coefficient remained positive with patient-clustered standard errors (6.27, 95% CI 4.22-8.31, P = 1.99e-09). Rank-based ssGSEA reproduced the spatial finding. The HRA001238/ST_LUAD proxy analysis was non-significant and provided no support for the primary framework. In TCGA-LUAD, the compact score was associated with overall survival after adjustment for age, stage, and sex (n = 492; HR per SD = 1.34, 95% CI 1.15-1.56; P = 1.58e-04). ESTIMATE StromalScore and the collagen average were not significant in corresponding models, and adding the compact score improved model fit. Within the identical 155-patient purity-complete subset, the score HR was 1.14 (95% CI 0.90-1.46; P = 0.282) without purity and 1.27 (95% CI 0.96-1.68; P = 0.098) with purity. The compact score is not reducible to a generic ESTIMATE stromal score, a simple collagen average, or one component, and its cross-method reproducibility supports a coordinated multi-program signal. Nevertheless, tumor-purity independence is not established, thematic circularity with stromal biology remains, and no analyzed cohort validates STAS prediction. The contribution is therefore an interpretable, benchmarked public-data framework with explicit compositional limits, not a clinical biomarker.

title: TISCH3: an expanded resource for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of the tumor microenvironment.
text: The Tumor Immune Single Cell Hub (TISCH) is a curated resource for exploring single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from the tumor microenvironment. Here, we present TISCH3, which expands the single-cell collection from 190 to 408 datasets and introduces 69 spatial transcriptomics datasets, bringing the total to 477 datasets. The 218 newly added scRNA-seq datasets span 48 cancer types, and the spatial collection spans 27 cancer types. Spatial samples are curated and processed individually, and single-cell references enable estimation of cell-type composition at each spot. The spatial workspace comprises six modules: Overview, GeneExp, spatially variable genes (SVGs), CellAssoc, Communication, and Downloads. These modules provide sample metadata and quality-control views, spatial gene expression maps, ranking of SVG, cell-type correlation and conditional intra-spot co-occurrence analyses, inferred cell-cell communication networks, and downloadable data and results. TISCH3 retains the single-cell analysis capabilities of TISCH2 and extends them to spatial exploration of the tumor microenvironment. The database is freely available without registration at https://tisch3.compbio.cn/.

title: Fibroblast-derived MDK promotes Lymph node metastasis in Luminal Breast Cancer through an SDC4-USP9X-RELB deubiquitination axis.
text: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is central to breast cancer staging and treatment decisions. Clinical observations indicate that luminal or hormone receptor-positive breast cancer may show a distinct clinical pattern of regional lymph node involvement, but the stromal and intracellular mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) data, a multicenter institutional cohort, public single-cell RNA sequencing data, spatial transcriptomics, and multiplex immunofluorescence. Fibroblast states and candidate cell-cell communication pathways were examined using CytoTRACE, pseudotime, and ligand-receptor analyses. Functional and mechanistic validation included co-culture and Transwell assays, a mouse footpad-popliteal lymph node metastasis model, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, protein stability assays, and ubiquitination assays. Group comparisons used parametric or nonparametric tests, as appropriate. The SEER and multicenter cohorts showed a higher proportion of lymph node involvement in HR-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer than in the HER2-positive and triple-negative groups. Single-cell analysis identified a TINAGL1 + CAF population enriched in lymph node metastases, and spatial analysis demonstrated its proximity to epithelial tumor cells. Ligand-receptor analysis and tissue imaging supported MDK-SDC4 as a candidate stromal-tumor communication axis. Fibroblast-derived MDK promoted tumor-cell migration and invasion, and these responses were attenuated by SDC4 knockdown. Mechanistically, SDC4 associated with RELB and regulated its ubiquitination and proteasomal stability. USP9X associated with SDC4 and RELB, and USP9X perturbation altered RELB ubiquitination and protein stability. In vivo, SDC4 knockdown and overexpression produced opposite changes in imaging signals and popliteal lymph node volume, while RELB or USP9X knockdown attenuated the phenotype associated with SDC4 overexpression. Histological and immunohistochemical examination provided additional tissue-level characterization of the lymph node lesions. Fibroblast-derived MDK promotes breast cancer cell migration and invasion through tumor-cell SDC4. In vitro and in vivo findings support an SDC4-USP9X-RELB regulatory axis involving RELB ubiquitination and stability, providing mechanistic insight into stromal-tumor communication in regional lymph node metastasis.

title: Discovery of chalcone-quinazolinone hybrids as BRAF kinase inhibitors with potential anticancer activity: Design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular modeling studies.
text: BRAF has emerged as an important target for inhibiting tumor cell proliferation. Accordingly, some chalcone-quinazolinone conjugates 4a-l were designed, synthesized and screened for their BRAF inhibitory activity. Compounds 4d, 4f, and 4l that revealed the most potent BRAFWT inhibition (IC50 = 0.572, 0.482, and 0.317 μM, respectively), in comparison to sorafenib (IC50 = 0.132 μM), were further tested for their efficacy on mutant BRAFV600E, where they showed promising inhibition (IC50 = 0.105, 0.067, and 0.275 μM, respectively), relative to vemurafenib (IC50 = 0.063 μM). The cytotoxic potential of 4d, 4f, and 4l demonstrated the selectivity of 4d and 4f towards HT-29 cancer cell line expressing BRAFV600E. Therefore, 4l was further evaluated for its inhibitory activity on EGFR, where it demonstrated potent inhibition with IC50 = 0.098 μM compared to gefitinib (IC50 = 0.037 μM). Moreover, 4f caused a cell cycle arrest at S and G2/M phases in HT-29 cells besides apoptotic induction. Potential biomarkers of apoptosis revealed the effectiveness of 4f in increasing Bax/Bcl-2 ratio by 19-fold, and upregulation of expression of Caspase-3 and Caspase-9 by 6- and 8-fold, respectively, relative to control HT-29 cancer cells. Molecular docking studies and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to correlate the biological activity of the newly synthesized compounds with their binding modes and investigate the dynamic stability of the 4f/BRAF complex.

title: Structurally diverse 7-phenylthieno[3,2-d]pyrimidines as multitarget antiproliferative agents across molecularly distinct breast cancer cell lines: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking.
text: Breast cancer heterogeneity and signaling crosstalk contribute to therapeutic resistance and support the development of small molecules active across molecularly distinct subtypes. Herein, new, structurally diverse 7-phenylthieno[3,2-d]pyrimidine derivatives were designed and synthesized, then evaluated alongside previously reported counterparts 12a and 12b against MCF-7, BT-474, HCC1937, and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines and non-tumorigenic MCF-10A mammary epithelial cells. Compounds 6, 11, 12a-c, and 17 emerged as the leading derivatives, displaying marked structure- and subtype-dependent activity. Among them, compound 17 showed the broadest antiproliferation profile, with IC₅₀ values of 1.69, 0.62, 3.25, and 7.12 μM against MCF-7, BT-474, HCC1937, and MDA-MB-231 cells, respectively. The previously reported counterpart 12a was the most potent EGFR inhibitor among the tested derivatives (IC₅₀ = 12.174 nM), followed by 17 (19.651 nM) and 6 (31.337 nM). However, all tested derivatives remained less potent than lapatinib (IC₅₀ = 8.046 nM). Compounds 12b and 12c displayed complementary hormone-pathway-oriented profiles involving ARO inhibition, ERα binding, and differential ERα agonistic/antagonistic modulation. Compound 17 showed the second-highest EGFR inhibitory activity and strongest ERα-binding affinity. Western blotting assay of 12c-treated MCF-7 and 17-treated MDA-MB-231 cells showed reduced p-AKT signals, differential p-ERK1/2 responses, and increased cleaved caspase-9 signals. Cell-cycle analysis revealed G₀/G₁ arrest by 12b and 12c in hormone-responsive cells and S-phase accumulation by 6 and 12a in triple-negative cells. Leading compounds increased caspase-9 levels and induced predominantly apoptotic cell death, as demonstrated by Annexin V-FITC/PI staining. Molecular docking provided qualitative binding models within the EGFR, ARO, and ERα binding sites. Collectively, the newly synthesized compound 17 represents the principal broad-spectrum and selectively cytotoxic lead, while compounds 6 and 12a-c provide complementary subtype-oriented profiles for further optimization.

title: Design, synthesis and bioevaluation of pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridines as potent and selective aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) inhibitors.
text: Due to the association of excessive aldosterone with multiple severe cardiovascular, renal and endocrine diseases, aldosterone synthase (CYP11B2) as the pivotal enzyme in aldosterone biosynthesis has been manifested to be an outstanding therapeutic target. Although baxdrostat (IC50 = 35 nM; selectivity factor, SF = 102) was approved recently for treating resistant hypertension, further inhibitors with innovative scaffolds were still urgently needed attaining superior inhibitory potency and selectivity to deal with patient stratification, potential resistance, and long-term safety surveillance on cardiovascular outcomes and glucocorticoid status. Replicating the optimal binding mode of natural substrate deoxycorticosterone and baxdrostat (linear configurations), aryl sulfonamido pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridines were designed, however, with a curve molecular shape to circumvent potential steric clashes with the β-sheets. Compounds with p-F (8j) and p-CN (8 m) substituents on the distal phenyl sulfonamido moiety turned out to be approximately four-fold more potent numerically compared to baxdrostat with IC50s of 9 and 12 nM, respectively. Both compounds were around two-fold more selective numerically compared to baxdrostat with SFs of 199 and 157, respectively. They showed substantially weaker inhibition of a panel of steroidogenic and hepatic CYP enzymes than of CYP11B2 and did not disrupt the growth of HepG2 and V79 cells. Compound 8j showed good pharmacokinetic properties with a half-life of 3 h and an oral bioavailability of 39%. Compound 8j reduced plasma aldosterone concentrations in rats by twenty-fold to 12 ng/L, whereas induced no statistically significant difference on cortisol levels. Compound 8j was therefore deemed promising for further development.

title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of quinazoline-based covalent PI3Kδ inhibitors targeting Lys779 residue.
text: Phosphoinositide 3-kinase δ (PI3Kδ) is a clinically validated therapeutic target for hematological malignancies, while selective covalent inhibition provides an attractive strategy for achieving sustained PI3Kδ suppression. Herein, a series of quinazoline-based covalent PI3Kδ inhibitors bearing lysine-reactive warheads were designed and synthesized to target Lys779 residue in the pocket of PI3Kδ. Compound C1 bearing a 2,4-difluorophenolic ester warhead, exhibited the most potent PI3Kδ inhibition with an IC50 value of 0.05 nM and > 150-fold selectivity over other class I PI3K isoforms in vitro. C1 exerted robust antiproliferative activity against SU-DHL-6 cells (GI50 = 0.025 μM), and mechanistic investigation revealed that C1 significantly induced apoptosis in a concentration-dependent manner. Washout assay demonstrated that C1 retained the sustained antiproliferative activity against SU-DHL-6 cells after drug removal. Docking simulation suggested a plausible covalent binding occurred and a stable covalent bond formed between the warhead 2,4-difluorophenolic ester of C1 with Lys779 through ester aminolysis in the pocket of PI3Kδ. This research highlights the scope of lysine-targeting covalent design and lays a solid foundation for the development of novel potent irreversible PI3Kδ inhibitors.

title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
text: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysozyme, and secretory immunoglobulin A]. Each of these 51 microbiome models were integrated with a time-point specific male whole-body metabolic model personalized based on LS's weight, blood glucose, and cholesterol. A healthy average (HeAve) community model from 34 individuals provided a reference. Our models predicted methane overproduction from high Methanobrevibacter smithii levels, coinciding with peak CRP and calprotectin. We found that Escherichia coli plays a central role in shaping the predicted metabolome and may promote inflammation through trimethylamine N-oxide and formaldehyde production, out-competing Desulfovibrio piger and Akkermansia muciniphila via active methyl and sulfur cycles. At a later time point, LS experienced a major shift in gut Proteobacteria ecology: E. coli, over-abundant at 675 × HeAve, dropped nearly 80-fold in one month, while Morganella morganii rose by nearly eight times, which coincided with a spike in LS's lactoferrin and lysozyme, a rise in species including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a change in predicted metabolic profile, and increased alpha diversity. We also noted a correlation between postulated inflammation periods and predicted lithocholic acid levels. This work extends two previous studies of 7 and 27 of these time points. Our analysis demonstrates the value of pairing multi-omics time-series data with systems biology approaches in an n-of-1 design, resolving how microbiome composition dynamics shape host-microbiome metabolism and inflammation.

title: Navigating the Drought Tolerance-Yield Trade-Off in Triticeae Cereals: From Molecular Networks to Climate-Resilient Breeding.
text: Drought driven by climate change severely threatens food security, particularly for wheat and barley grown in water-limited regions. A major breeding challenge is the trade-off between drought tolerance and yield. This review synthesises current knowledge of drought adaptation mechanisms in Triticeae crops, focusing on the transcriptional cascades, ABA-centric hormonal signalling and posttranslational modifications (kinases, phosphatases and ubiquitination) that confer resilience while often constraining carbon allocation to developing grains. Recent genomic advances, including genome-wide association study (GWAS), multi-omics integration and single-cell RNA-transcriptomics, have uncovered a wealth of drought-associated loci, although their translational potential is limited by data heterogeneity, environmental dependency and a persistent gap between laboratory validation and field performance. Emerging breeding approaches, such as speed breeding, wild-allele introgression, multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenotyping are accelerating the development of climate-smart cultivars. Tissue-specific and inducible expression systems show early promise in uncoupling stress protection from growth penalties. Looking ahead, we propose that overcoming the yield-tolerance trade-off will require integrating synthetic biology, explainable AI, systematic exploration of novel variation and field phenomics coupled with digital twin modelling. Collectively, this review provides a strategic framework for engineering next-generation, climate-smart Triticeae cereals capable of maintaining productivity under intensifying drought conditions.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
text: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: mRNA-LNP vaccine encoding for Fc-scaffold antigen drives FcγR-independent immunity.
text: While clinical translation of messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technologies has redefined vaccinology, the development of potent platforms against complex bacterial pathogens is often limited by the transient expression kinetics and rapid clearance of encoded antigens. One well established approach to enhance immunogenicity is the fusion of an Fc fragment to an antigen. However, the mechanism of Fc-mediated potentiation within mRNA-LNP systems is, yet, undefined, specifically regarding the necessity of receptor-mediated interactions. Here, we demonstrate that an mRNA-LNP vaccine, encoding an Fc-fragment fused to the Yersinia pestis F1 antigen, drives robust, protective immunity against the lethal bubonic plague by functioning as a pharmacokinetic stabilizer. Through systematic architectural design, variation of Fc isotypes, species-matched scaffolding, and glycosylation profiling, we reveal that Fc-integration extends systemic antigen bioavailability by over 300-fold, providing a sustained kinetic window for immune priming. Remarkably, immunogenicity is preserved in Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-deficient mice, as well as with a reduced FcγR-binding Fc variant, suggesting that protective immunity is independent of classical FcγR engagement in this model. These findings decouple Fc-mediated enhancement from receptor-mediated interactions, identifying structural stabilization and prolonged persistence as the primary drivers of efficacy in mRNA-LNP vaccines. Altogether, our results provide a mechanistic framework for the design of high-potency mRNA vaccines through engineered protein stability.

This review provides a comparative and critical analysis of these technologies, emphasizing their molecular mechanisms, target recognition, specificity, delivery strategies, therapeutic applications, clinical development, advantages, limitations, and safety considerations. Collectively, these platforms have demonstrated therapeutic potential across a broad range of diseases, including cancer, genetic and metabolic disorders, cardiovascular and neurological diseases, infectious diseases, and ocular disorders. However, important barriers to clinical translation remain, including delivery limitations, molecular stability, target and off-target effects, immunogenicity, toxicity, genomic instability, and the need for precise and durable control of gene modulation. For CRISPR-based approaches, additional considerations include modality-specific genomic alterations, prolonged editor activity, and the ethical and regulatory implications of permanent genome modification. Continued advances in molecular engineering, delivery technologies, target-selection strategies, and platform optimization may improve the specificity, safety, durability, and therapeutic efficacy of these approaches and facilitate their responsible integration into precision medicine.

title: eQt Protein Nanocage-Delivered IL-21 mRNA Systemically Reprograms Host Immune Cells Toward Stemness and Maturation to Achieve Anti-Tumor Immunity.
text: Effective cancer immunotherapy requires reprogramming host immunity toward stem-like states. However, clinical use of IL-21 is limited by short half-life and toxicity. Here, we develop a bio-inspired protein nanocage platform (eQt) that encapsulates IL-21 mRNA via high-affinity λN-boxB interactions during bacterial biosynthesis, enabling one-step manufacturing and pH-responsive endosomal release. eQt-IL-21 drives dendritic cell maturation, characterized by marked upregulation of CD80 and CD86, and transcriptome-wide enrichment of MHC-I antigen processing and presentation pathways (H2-K1, H2-D1, B2m, Tap2), establishing a highly stimulatory environment for T cell priming. Transcriptomic profiling of draining lymph nodes reveals that eQt-IL-21 preferentially diverts CD8+ T-cell differentiation away from terminal exhaustion toward a TCF-1+/CCR7+ stem-like progenitor identity, with concordant upregulation of Tcf7, Sell (encoding CD62L), and LEF-1, sustaining a self-renewing memory reservoir and long-lived central memory T cells (Tcm). In preclinical E.G7-OVA models, this immunological reprogramming translates into potent prophylactic efficacy and durable therapeutic remission of established tumors, without detectable systemic toxicity. This work establishes IL-21 mRNA-mediated immune-cell reprogramming as a mechanistic cornerstone of durable anti-tumor immunity, and positions the eQt nanocage as a versatile, scalable platform for precision cancer immunotherapy.

title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons.
text: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

title: The International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC): sustaining open sequence data at global scale.
text: The International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC; http://www.insdc.org/) provides global infrastructure for the collection, preservation, and dissemination of nucleotide sequence data through its three member organizations. As the collaboration approaches four decades of three-way data exchange, continued growth in both the volume and geographic distribution of data is creating new challenges. Cumulative volume now stands at over 75 PB, having doubled approximately every 2.5 years over the past decade. Data reuse is extensively demonstrated by the 39 055 publications citing INSDC records in the 12 months to August 2026. The INSDC has established a new governance structure and a formal pathway for membership, supported by minimal technical specifications that enable independently developed systems to interoperate. Prospect members are now progressing through this pathway. The collaboration is also responding to an evolving policy landscape, which needs to be balanced with its founding commitment to free and unrestricted access. Looking ahead, the INSDC is exploring more scalable approaches to data storage and federation, strengthening approaches to attribution and reuse, and considering applications of artificial intelligence for metadata enrichment and submission support. Altogether, these developments aim to sustain an open, global, and interoperable nucleotide sequence archive.

title: Linking Research Outputs to Support Transparency and Reproducibility in Preclinical Traumatic Brain Injury Studies: A Live Implementation Experience.
text: The PRE-Clinical Interagency reSearch resourcE-Traumatic Brain Injury (PRECISE-TBI) is a community-based consortium developing standards, resources, and tools to support preclinical traumatic brain injury (TBI) research. PRECISE-TBI aims to address barriers that contribute to the translational gap by improving transparency, interoperability, and accessibility of preclinical TBI data and methods. The PRECISE-TBI Education Focus Area develops and curates resources relevant to blast-related research, working with the broader community to address issues pertinent to both military and civilian populations. Using two complementary implementation examples, we illustrate the practical application of current PRECISE-TBI resources in preclinical TBI research, including the coordinated use of the Model Catalog and the Open Data Commons for TBI (ODC-TBI) repository. Together, these components form an integrated, FAIR-aligned publication and data sharing framework tailored to preclinical TBI research. We further describe a linked research output publication workflow, whereas traditional research articles are complemented by executable protocols hosted on protocols.io and curated, machine-readable datasets published as independent digital objects. This linked collection of research outputs has been referred to as the "Paper of the Future" in related PRECISE-TBI publications. These resources adhere to Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable principles through the use of persistent identifiers, rich metadata, and mapping to the community-defined Common Data Elements. This use case illustrates how PRECISE-TBI-aligned practices can facilitate compliance with the NIH Data Management and Sharing policy and provide a structured approach to documenting experimental design, provenance, and data limitations in preclinical TBI research. While this study does not evaluate downstream outcomes, the framework is intended to enable future assessment of data reuse, harmonization, and reproducibility by making research outputs transparent, citable, and evaluable through persistent cross-linking of publications, protocols, and datasets.

title: AI-Based Pain Assessment Trends: Bibliometric Analysis and a Four-Phase Framework for Clinical Translation.
text: The purpose of this study was to map the development and thematic structure of Scopus-indexed research on artificial intelligence (AI)-based pain assessment published between 2015 and 2025 and to develop a conceptual model supporting its clinical translation. A quantitative bibliometric and scientometric analysis was conducted and combined with author-developed conceptual framework development. English-language articles and conference papers published between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from Scopus using search terms related to AI, machine learning, deep learning, digital sensing, and pain assessment. Following automated filtering, duplicate removal, and title-abstract screening for eligibility, 720 of the 2,550 initially retrieved records were retained for analysis. Keyword normalization was subsequently performed as an analytical preprocessing step to standardize terminology before bibliometric and thematic analyses. Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer were used to analyze publication performance, annual trends, geographical distribution, keyword frequencies, co-occurrence relationships, and thematic clusters. The 720 included publications appeared across 408 sources and demonstrated an annual growth rate of 12.85%. The mean document age was 3.35 years, and the mean citation count was 12.39 citations per document. Publication output increased from 14 to 21 publications per year during 2015-2017 to 132 publications in 2024 and 137 in 2025. Five thematic clusters were identified: patient-centered biopsychosocial context; multimodal AI and physiological signal processing; perioperative outcomes and pharmacological prediction; multidimensional pain phenotyping and predictive modeling; and standardized assessment and psychometric validation. Research activity in AI-based pain assessment increased substantially during the study period and encompassed interconnected computational, physiological, clinical, behavioral, and methodological themes. However, important gaps remain in external clinical validation, dataset standardization, population diversity, explainability, and real-world implementation. A four-phase conceptual model is proposed, covering data-infrastructure development, algorithm design, clinical and ethical validation, and sustained implementation. The proposed model may help clinicians, researchers, healthcare organizations, and technology developers evaluate and plan the responsible integration of AI-supported pain-assessment systems. Clinical implementation should maintain professional oversight and prioritize patient-centered outcomes, transparent model behavior, diverse population validation, data protection, and compatibility with existing clinical workflows. The bibliometric findings describe the research landscape and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of clinical effectiveness.

title: A Clinically Weighted Transformer-Based Deep Learning Model for Automated FLIP Panometry v2.0 Interpretation.
text: Functional lumen imaging probe (FLIP) Panometry evaluates esophageal motility by measuring contractile responses and esophagogastric junction opening, but interpretation requires expertise and varies between readers. We aimed to develop a transformer-based deep learning model for automated FLIP Panometry v2.0 interpretation, incorporating a clinically weighted cost matrix that penalizes clinically consequential errors. 984 adults who underwent FLIP Panometry and high-resolution manometry (HRM) were included. Expert FLIP Panometry v2.0 interpretation, assigned blinded to HRM, served as the reference standard for training and evaluation. HRM (Chicago Classification v4.0) characterized the cohort and corroborated expert FLIP labels. Inconclusive or discordant HRM studies were excluded. A transformer model with a weighted cost matrix was evaluated on a held-out test set using the six-category FLIP Panometry v2.0 scheme and grouped binary ("normal" vs "not normal") and three-class ("normal," "abnormal," "obstructive") schemes. The model reproduced expert six-category classification in 83.5% of test studies (95% CI 76.4-88.7%). Binary accuracy was 94% (89-97%), with 97% sensitivity (91-99%) and 89% specificity (76-95%). Three-class accuracy was 89% (83-93%); sensitivity and specificity for obstructive patterns were 93% (82-97%) and 96% (90-99%). No normal studies were classified as obstructive, or vice versa. Versus an unweighted baseline model, cost-sensitive training was associated with 15% lower aggregate misclassification cost (95% CI -16% to 39%). A transformer-based model reproduced expert FLIP Panometry v2.0 interpretation with high agreement in a selected single-center cohort. Accuracy was numerically higher than prior convolutional models trained on different data. These findings support a potential role for AI-assisted FLIP interpretation, but external validation is required before clinical use.

title: Artificial intelligence tools for generating multimodal intensive care unit journey and discharge summaries: a scoping review.
text: To map and synthesise existing evidence on computational summarisation technologies, including machine learning-based and natural language processing-based approaches, designed to generate multimodal (textual, visual, and audio) patient summaries of adult intensive care unit (ICU) stays. This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance. Studies involving adults in any ICU setting and using artificial intelligence-enabled approaches to generate patient summaries were eligible. Searches were conducted across five major databases and grey literature sources. Two reviewers independently screened records. Data were extracted using a structured charting tool and independently verified by a second reviewer. Findings were synthesised using descriptive statistics and narrative synthesis. Eleven studies met inclusion criteria. Eight generated textual summaries, three produced visual outputs, and one developed an audio interface. Ten tools were clinician-facing; only one study generated summaries for families. Approaches included large language models, rule-based natural language generation, information extraction, trajectory modelling, and speech-based systems. No study implemented a fully multimodal summarisation system. All evaluations were conducted using retrospective data, simulations, or prototypes, with no prospective testing in live clinical workflows. Five themes emerged: predominance of text-based summarisation, early feasibility of large language models with reliability limitations, predominance of clinician-facing applications, heterogeneous evaluation practices, and limited evidence of clinical implementation. Current ICU summarisation research demonstrates technical proof-of-concept feasibility but limited clinical readiness. Progress will require rigorous evaluation, stabilisation safeguards, and multimodal, patient- and family-centred designs capable of operating within regulatory and safety-critical clinical environments.

title: Fully Automated, Explainable AI Analysis of Coronary CTA Improves Prediction of Major Cardiovascular Events.
text: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is central to noninvasive diagnosis and risk assessment, yet current workflows are labor-intensive and depend on semiquantitative scoring systems that do not fully leverage prognostic information in CCTA. The objectives of the study were to develop and validate a fully automated, explainable artificial intelligence (AI) system (AI-automated coronary analysis [ACA]) for comprehensive CCTA analysis to predict major adverse cardiovascular events and compare its performance with conventional risk markers. AI-ACA automatically extracts a suite of CCTA-derived biomarkers, including stenosis severity, plaque burden, and composition; AI-derived CAD - reporting and data system (CAD-RADS) (AI-CADRADS); coronary tortuosity; and subtended myocardial mass, to generate interpretable risk estimates. In a retrospective cohort (n = 1,702), we compared AI-ACA with Agatston score, standard demographic risk markers, and AI-CADRADS. Model explainability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations. AI-ACA demonstrated higher predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81) than Agatston score (AUC: 0.76) and demographic markers (AUC: 0.67), and similar performance to AI-CADRADS (AUC: 0.81). AI-ACA showed better prognostic discrimination than Agatston score, reflected by a higher Harrell C-index (0.791 vs 0.742) and greater separation in event-free survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank 31.79 vs 13.71). Shapley Additive Explanations analysis identified total plaque volume and burden, maximum stenosis severity, and AI-CADRADS as the strongest contributors to risk estimation. A fully automated and explainable AI platform for CCTA enables comprehensive quantitative characterization of CAD without manual intervention. Although prognostic performance was comparable to AI-CADRADS and modestly higher than Agatston score, the platform provides transparent biomarker-based risk assessment and scalable analysis that may facilitate broader clinical implementation of quantitative CCTA.

title: Comprehensive Clinical Decision-Support Framework for Obesity Prevention Using Large-Scale Health Checkup Data: Development and Evaluation Study.
text: Obesity prevention requires identifying nonobese adults at risk of developing obesity. Routine health checkups collect anthropometric, laboratory, medical history, and lifestyle information, but screening primarily describes current anthropometric status and does not directly provide individualized estimates of future risk for preventive counseling. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a comprehensive clinical decision-support framework for obesity prevention using large-scale health checkup data. This retrospective cohort study used repeated examination data from the Kangbuk Samsung Health Study. Adults with BMI less than 25 kg/m², at least 3 health checkup visits, a 2-year obesity-free washout period, and postindex follow-up were included. Incident obesity was defined as the first follow-up BMI of 25 kg/m² or higher. The framework integrated a single-visit prediction tier (which we termed lite), a survival component for time-to-transition context, a repeated-measurement updating tier (which we termed plus), and an explainability layer. The primary lite-tier and survival analyses used training-set-only imputation. A previously exported lite-tier Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) component was externally evaluated in 328,268 National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) participants. Among 231,683 initially nonobese participants, 38,094 developed incident obesity. In the aligned 5-year visit-1 test cohort, 4088 of 21,783 (18.8%) participants developed obesity. The lite-tier ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.918, an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.693, a Brier score of 0.087, and an expected calibration error of 0.005. AUPRC was approximately 3.7 times the no-information reference. AUROCs were 0.913 for BMI-only and 0.914 for BMI+age+sex. Observed 5-year incidence ranged from 0.1% (6/4357) to 64.7% (2821/4357) across accelerated failure time (AFT) risk quintiles. The plus tier achieved a landmark-row AUROC of 0.899 with less favorable calibration. The previously exported lite-tier XGBoost component achieved an external AUROC of 0.857, AUPRC of 0.575, and Brier score of 0.132. Large-scale health checkup data supported an integrated framework for single-visit triage, temporal risk context, risk-domain explanation, and exploratory repeated-measurement updating, providing a basis for prevention-oriented risk communication and follow-up prioritization. The overall gain in discrimination beyond BMI was modest, and the effects on clinical decisions and obesity prevention require prospective evaluation.

title: Factors Influencing Older Adults' Sustained Engagement in Digital Psychological Interventions in Resource-Limited Settings: Qualitative Study Guided by the Social Ecological Model.
text: Digital behavioral activation therapy (DBAT) is effective in reducing late-life depression (LLD). However, older adults in resource-limited settings often show low adherence and retention. This pattern is largely driven by the digital divide. Digital inclusion offers a pathway to address this gap by recognizing older adults as active participants rather than passive recipients. Despite this potential, limited research has examined low engagement from the perspective of older adults' lived experiences. This gap restricts understanding of the complex factors that shape engagement in digital psychological interventions. This study aimed to systematically explore, through the lens of digital inclusion and guided by the social ecological model, the multilevel factors influencing older adults' sustained engagement in digital psychological interventions within resource-limited settings, specifically focusing on the lived experiences of retained users who completed the full program. A descriptive phenomenological design was used. Semistructured interviews were conducted with older adults in Western Hunan, China. Data were transcribed using machine-assisted methods and verified manually. Data were analyzed using the Colaizzi phenomenological method combined with thematic and framework analysis guided by the social ecological model. Two researchers independently coded the data and refined themes through discussion. Nineteen older adults with LLD from resource-limited settings were included. Engagement in DBAT was shaped by factors across multiple levels. At the individual level, factors included health needs, learning motivation, physiological and cognitive limitations, and low digital literacy. At the interpersonal level, factors included intergenerational support, emotional burden, established social networks, and digital exclusion. At the society level, available devices and networks sometimes hindered engagement due to poor age-friendly design and unstable connectivity. Personal aspirations for digital participation often conflicted with social resistance. At the policy level, financial burden, standardized policy approaches, and unmet individual needs limited engagement. These factors interacted to influence engagement behavior. This study identifies multilevel factors shaping older adults' sustained engagement in digital psychological interventions within resource-limited settings, reflecting the experiences of retained users. The findings advocate for integrated, context-sensitive strategies grounded in a digital inclusion framework. Crucially, nurses play a key role in promoting technology access, improving digital literacy, supporting social participation, and advocating for equitable services. These efforts can enhance accessibility and adherence, ultimately fostering more equitable and sustainable digital mental health care for vulnerable aging populations. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2400091193; https://tinyurl.com/y5e6wt7p.

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression.
text: This review examines the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) models for the detection and prediction of glaucomatous progression. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed to analyze longitudinal data from optic disc photographs, optical coherence tomography images, and visual field tests to identify worsening glaucoma. Recent AI research has also expanded beyond simply detecting progression to predicting future disease trajectories. These approaches may provide more efficient assessment than clinician review alone. AI models can rapidly analyze large volumes of clinical data to support individualized glaucoma management; these models can guide treatment intensity and follow-up intervals by detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression. However, significant hurdles to clinical adoption remain, including the "black box" nature of AI, absence of a universally accepted reference standard for progression, variable data quality, and limited generalizability across populations and clinical settings. AI is poised to function as a clinical decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinicians. Prospective studies are needed to determine the impact of AI in improving patient outcomes, clinical efficiency, and healthcare costs.

title: Comparative performance of DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3 on China's National Medical Licensing Examination questions (2004-2022).
text: DeepSeek, a cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) platform developed in China, has attracted growing interest for potential applications in clinical medicine and medical education. DeepSeek-V3 (MoE architecture) and DeepSeek-R1 (reinforcement learning-optimized for reasoning) are its flagship models, but the performance difference between DeepSeek‑R1 and DeepSeek‑V3 remains inconclusive. The objective of this study was to compare the performance of DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3 on the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination (NMLE). This study employed DeepSeek-R1-0528 (released on May 28, 2025) and DeepSeek-V3-0324 (released on March 24, 2025) to perform the NMLE testing, and the subject area for the examination was Clinical Medicine. We collected the questions from NMLE 2004 through NMLE 2022, comprising 600 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) per annual examination, for a total of 11,400 MCQs. The NMLE tests were carried out using the free web-based version of DeepSeek, with DeepSeek-R1-0528 and DeepSeek-V3-0324 evaluated on separate computer systems. Model performance was assessed based on accuracy rates. The annual average accuracy rates for DeepSeek-R1-0528 and DeepSeek-V3-0324 were 91.2% (95% CI: 89.6% - 92.8%) and 91.1% (95% CI: 89.6% - 92.6%), respectively, with no significant difference observed between them (P = 0.591, Cohen's d = 0.086). The regression analysis showed that DeepSeek-R1-0528 showed no significant changes in accuracy rates from NMLE 2004 to NMLE 2013, while DeepSeek-V3-0324 showed a significant declining trend. Moreover, from NMLE 2014 to NMLE 2022, both models demonstrated significant declining trends in the accuracy rates. DeepSeek-R1-0528 and DeepSeek-V3-0324 answered 999 and 1,014 MCQs incorrectly, respectively, with 715 MCQs answered incorrectly by both models. DeepSeek-R1-0528 and DeepSeek-V3-0324 demonstrated near-identical and excellent performance on the Chinese NMLE.

title: Enhancing auto-segmentation accuracy and robustness through multiple deep learning systems.
text: Deep learning auto-segmentation (DLAS) can improve the efficiency and consistency of clinical contouring; however, no single DLAS system performs optimally across all cases, organs, and image slices, and each system may produce occasional poor-quality or outlier contours. Because multiple DLAS systems are available in some institutions, this proof-of-concept study evaluated a multi-system fusion framework designed to leverage their complementary strengths and generate more accurate and robust auto-contours, with potential extension to consensus generation from multiple manual contours. Using 35 abdominal CT datasets from three institutions, contours of the stomach, duodenum, liver, and right kidney were generated by three commercial DLAS systems and one non-commercial research DLAS model. Two fusion approaches were evaluated: conventional Simultaneous Truth and Performance Level Estimation (STAPLE), which combined all available DLAS contours, and a selecting-and-combining DLAS (scDLAS) approach. For scDLAS, previously developed contour quality classification (CQC) models used supervised machine learning and seven quantitative metrics to classify each contour slice as acceptable, requiring minor edits, or requiring major edits. Only contours in the highest available quality category were retained for STAPLE fusion. scDLAS configurations incorporating different numbers of DLAS systems were evaluated against the reference contours using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and changes in the distribution of contour-quality categories. No individual DLAS system consistently achieved the best performance across all four organs. STAPLE generally matched or outperformed the individual systems while maintaining comparable or lower interpatient variability. For the stomach, duodenum, liver, and right kidney, respectively, STAPLE achieved mean ± SD DSC values of 0.88 ± 0.10, 0.70 ± 0.13, 0.95 ± 0.02, and 0.92 ± 0.04, with corresponding HD95 values of 10.8 ± 12.6, 18.0 ± 12.3, 5.5 ± 2.2, and 6.8 ± 9.6 mm. The best-performing scDLAS configuration increased the mean DSC to 0.90 ± 0.09, 0.74 ± 0.14, 0.96 ± 0.02, and 0.94 ± 0.03, respectively. The highest duodenal DSC was achieved by 3scDLAS, whereas 4scDLAS achieved or tied the highest DSC for the other organs. The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of leveraging complementary outputs from multiple DLAS systems to improve the accuracy and robustness of auto-segmented contours. These findings support further evaluation of multi-system fusion as a strategy for generating more reliable initial contours for subsequent clinical review and editing.

title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories.
text: To develop and validate InterGenEHR+, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular data and longitudinal EHR trajectories for critically ill patients requiring mechanical ventilation and venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), enabling scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models in high-risk cohorts. InterGenEHR+ uses an optional large language model (LLM) parser for text-driven input. For single-time-point generation, we integrate variational autoencoders (VAEs) and diffusion models conditioned on observed variables. Multiple diffusion architectures support conditional longitudinal generation. The framework is evaluated on a multi-institutional VV-ECMO cohort of 874 patients using distributional fidelity metrics, imputation accuracy, adherence to clinical constraints, downstream mortality prediction tasks, and clinician evaluation. Gemma 3 4B with few-shot prompting achieves the best performance in parsing clinician prompts while maintaining a low spurious slot rate. The experimental results demonstrate strengths across IGE variants: IGE-TabDDPM and IGE-PMVAE show strong performance in single-time-point generation, whereas IGE-CSDI, IGE-FGTI, and IGE-MTSCI achieve the best performance on different longitudinal fidelity metrics. In downstream evaluations across five random seeds and three classifiers, models trained on synthetic cohorts retain predictive utility for mortality prediction on real test data. Clinician ratings further indicate that the generated trajectories are clinically plausible and consistent with the requested scenarios. InterGenEHR+ enables clinician-specified conditional generation of clinically coherent EHR trajectories with strong statistical fidelity and downstream predictive utility in the evaluated VV-ECMO cohort and could be extended to other clinical settings. This framework supports the development and evaluation of machine learning systems in data-sparse critical care settings and advances clinically grounded synthetic data generation for biomedical research.1.

title: miR-34a-5p, miR-340-3p, CCL22, and CXCL16 in Parkinson's disease: peripheral expression patterns and transcriptomic insights.
text: Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with peripheral immune alterations, in which chemokines and potentially regulatory microRNAs (miRNAs) may contribute to peripheral inflammatory alterations. This study, therefore, investigated the expression of miR-34a-5p/CCL22 and miR-340-3p/CXCL16 Axes in peripheral blood and explored their relationships with transcriptomic and immune-cell patterns in PD. The candidate miRNAs miR-34a-5p and miR-340-3p were selected based on target prediction, with previous experimental evidence additionally supporting the miR-34a-5p/CCL22 interaction, and their corresponding chemokine targets, CCL22 and CXCL16, were evaluated using RT-qPCR in peripheral blood from 34 patients with PD and 34 healthy controls (HCs). Anindependent transcriptomic cohort (GSE99039; 205 patients with idiopathic PD and 233 controls) was analyzed using machine-learning approaches, differential expression, functional enrichment, and CIBERSORTx-based immune-cell estimation. miR-34a-5p expression was significantly higher in patients with PD than in controls (β = 0.62, 95% CrI 0.13-1.11, P = 0.011), whereas CXCL16, CCL22, and miR-340-3p did not differ significantly between groups. In patients with PD, CXCL16 was inversely correlated with miR-34a-5p and miR-340-3p. Our findings also revealed a significant positive correlation between miR-34a-5p and miR-340-3p in both the PD and HC groups. In GSE99039, CXCL16 was consistently prioritized among 60 chemokine-related genes and showed a positive association with estimated neutrophil abundance and inverse associations with several T-cell populations. CCL22 showed weaker and more heterogeneous associations with immune-cell populations. Although CXCL16 and CCL22 were not differentially expressed between PD and controls, CXCL16 showed consistent associations with peripheral immune-cell composition in an independent transcriptomic cohort. Together with the increased expression of miR-34a-5p and its association with CXCL16, these findings support further investigation of chemokine-miRNA relationships in the peripheral immune alterations associated with PD.

title: Automated whole-dentition CBCT phenotyping enables explainable sex classification and age estimation through distinct dental features.
text: Tooth size and morphology are established primarily during development, whereas secondary dentin deposition and pulp-space remodeling continue throughout adulthood, providing biologically distinct information for sex and age estimation. This study investigated whether automated whole-dentition cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) analysis could capture these two signals. The initial cohort comprised 327 adult CBCT scans, of which 275 passed automated segmentation-completeness screening and entered the final analysis (141 female and 134 male participants; age range, 21-61 years). ToothSeg was used for automatic tooth segmentation and numbering. After excluding variables potentially reflecting image acquisition rather than dental biology, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were developed separately for sex classification and age regression. Performance was assessed using five-fold out-of-fold predictions, and feature importance was interpreted using SHAP. The sex model achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.807 and an AUC of 0.872, while the age model achieved a mean absolute error of 5.29 years and an R² of 0.645. Lower-right canine volume was the most important individual feature for sex classification and was greater in males (Cohen's d = 1.20). Mean incisor relative low-gray voxel fraction was the most important age feature and was inversely correlated with chronological age (Spearman ρ = -0.706). As an exploratory study, automated whole-dentition CBCT phenotyping showed internally predictive, biologically interpretable patterns for adult sex and age estimation. However, given the modest sample size and proxy low-gray metric, multicenter external and anatomical validation are required.

title: Molecular Programming of Steric Tags for Controlled Nanopore Translocation toward Precision Clinical Diagnostic Assistance.
text: The precise resolution of single-molecule events is often limited by the stochastic thermal motion of analytes, which traverse nanoscale sensing zones too rapidly for conventional detection bandwidths. This remains a fundamental challenge in nanopore chemistry, particularly for small and flexible peptides. Here, we report a chemically intuitive molecular programming strategy─steric blockage-enabled slow translocation (SLOW-Trans)─that overcomes this physical limitation through the rational design of sterically demanding probe molecules. By site-specifically conjugating rigid aromatic steric tags with precisely defined dimensions to peptide substrates, we actively reshape the translocation energy landscape within the ∼1.2 nm constriction of the M2MspA nanopore. Systematic variation of tag size and rigidity enables deterministic control over peptide residence time, transforming transient stochastic events into stable and highly discriminable current signatures. Using this strategy, we achieve a six-order-of-magnitude dynamic range (0.001-1000 ng/mL) for matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-1, -2, and -9). In a cohort of 231 clinical urine samples, the nanopore-derived MMP activity profiles showed excellent agreement with ELISA-derived measurements and, when integrated with a machine-learning classifier, enabled classification of urothelial carcinoma with 96.2% accuracy. As a proof-of-concept extension, the modular probe design was further adapted for PSA/KLK3 activity analysis in clinical serum samples, supporting the feasibility of extending the approach to an additional protease target. This work establishes a general chemical framework for programming molecular behavior in confined nanoscale environments, bridging molecular design principles with functional nanopore sensing.

title: Mechanistic Insight Into ROS-Mediated Antibacterial Signaling Enables Hierarchical Hollow Polyhedral Nanozymes for Autonomous Bioelectronic Sensing and Synergetic Theranostics.
text: Postoperative bacterial infections remain a major clinical challenge, necessitating rapid and precise diagnosis alongside effective therapeutic intervention. Herein, we report a mechanism-driven platform integrating hierarchical hollow CuSe polyhedral nanozymes for autonomous bioelectronic sensing and synergistic antibacterial therapy. Guided by first-principles calculations, the engineered CuSe nanozymes facilitate interfacial electron transfer and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Integrated into an enzymatic biofuel cell (EBFC), the platform enables self-powered electrochemical and thermal dual-mode detection of Salmonella Typhimurium, achieving limits of detection (LOD) of 1.12 and 0.81 CFU mL-1, respectively, over a linear range of 10-107 CFU mL-1. Furthermore, CuSe exhibits a photothermal conversion efficiency of 45.53%, enabling enhanced ROS-mediated antibacterial activity under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, with almost no visible bacterial colonies observed after 25 min of treatment. Transcriptomic analysis identified 88 differentially expressed genes, revealing alterations in metal ion homeostasis, oxidative stress responses, and bacterial metabolic pathways. Additionally, machine learning-assisted integration of electrochemical and thermal signals improves quantitative prediction performance compared with single-mode analysis. This study establishes an integrated strategy combining self-powered pathogen detection, synergistic antibacterial activity, and intelligent data analysis for potential point-of-care testing (POCT).

title: A Framework For Reconstruction And Analysis Of Extended Pedigrees From Large-Scale Genealogy And Archive Records
text: Genetic analyses in pedigrees remain a powerful approach to identify rare disease-causing variants. Reconstructing large enough pedigrees to yield sufficient power, however, still faces challenges. Clinical family histories are often incomplete, especially in late-onset diseases caused by genetic variants with incomplete penetrance. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is such a disease with a disproportionately large contribution from rare variants with high but variable penetrance. Here, we present an open-source pipeline to reconstruct extended pedigrees from large-scale archive data dating back to [~]1800, which we applied to a cohort of Dutch ALS patients carrying the C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansion (HRE). Among 238 C9orf72 HRE carriers, 91 (38%) were members of an extended pedigree. Of these, 48 (53%) were clinically classified as sporadic ALS. In total, we identified 39 extended pedigrees including affected relatives up to the eighth degree of relatedness. Our approach increased the number of identified relationships by 2.5-fold compared with clinically obtained family histories, that typically missed relationships beyond the third degree. Genome-wide IBD analysis in pedigrees with [≥]7 meioses fine-mapped the C9orf72 HRE to shared IBD segments spanning 10.2 - 127.0 centimorgans in 97% of pedigrees. This combined genealogical-genetic approach for large-scale reconstruction of extended pedigrees supports the reclassification of apparently sporadic cases, facilitates the discovery of new disease-causing variants in ALS, and is applicable to any disease with comparable genetic architecture.

title: Risk-Based Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Staging Identifies a Population With Mortality Comparable to Established Cardiovascular Disease: Disability-Adjusted Life Years Across AHA Stages, 2005 to 2023
text: BackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome was defined in 2023 as a five-stage continuum, with stage 3 assigned on predicted rather than established cardiovascular disease. Whether that stage identifies a population whose mortality resembles clinical disease, and how health loss is distributed across stages, is unknown. MethodsWe pooled nine National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (2005-2023) and assigned CKM stages 0-4 from measured risk factors, kidney function, urine albumin, self-reported cardiovascular disease, and 10-year PREVENT risk. Years lived with disability used Global Burden of Disease weights; years of life lost combined national death counts, linked mortality files, and period life tables. ResultsIn 2021-2023, 13.8%, 21.3%, 49.1%, 6.5%, and 9.3% of adults were in stages 0 to 4, respectively. Crude mortality was 6,709 per 100,000 person-years in stage 3, comparable to 6,375 in stage 4. Adjusted hazard ratios rose from 1.39 in stage 2 to 3.22 in stage 4, with no excess in stage 1 (0.99). CKM accounted for 20.0 million DALYs annually, with 76% of attributable years of life lost in stages 3-4. Lipid-lowering therapy was absent in 53.7% of stage 3 and 33.6% of stage 4 adults, a gap unchanged over 16 years. Stage 0 prevalence fell 2.3% per year and stage 1 rose 3.1% per year between 2006 and 2016. ConclusionsRisk-based stage 3 carries short-term mortality indistinguishable from established cardiovascular disease, yet the population continues to shift into stage 1, where mortality is normal, and stage 3 receives less intensive lipid-lowering treatment than stage 4. Risk-based stage 3 carries mortality statistically indistinguishable from stage 4 (6,709 versus 6,375 per 100,000 person-years), supporting the prognostic content of the staging framework.
