title: Diversifying deaths: the shifting spectrum of childhood respiratory infectious mortality, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
text: BackgroundChildhood respiratory infectious deaths are partitioned across four Global Burden of Disease cause modules--26 etiological attributions within lower respiratory infections, tuberculosis, COVID-19, and whooping cough--never jointly reported. Whether the structure of this combined mortality spectrum has changed over time, and with what implications for intervention design, has not been quantified. We assembled and analyzed the integrated spectrum for children and adolescents aged 0- 19 years, 1990-2023. MethodsWe integrated Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (release v8352) estimates into a 29-node spectrum--26 lower respiratory infection etiologies plus tuberculosis, COVID-19, and pertussis-- globally and across seven super-regions, with uncertainty propagated by summing bounds. We computed Shannon diversity, Herfindahl concentration, and effective cause counts; phenotyped pandemic-window collapse and rebound per cause; linked pathogen shares to WHO/UNICEF vaccine coverage; and mapped geographic concentration in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Segmented (joinpoint) log-linear models with breakpoints selected by the Bayesian information criterion were fitted to annual totals, Shannon diversity and leading pathogen shares. ResultsIn 2023 the 29 causes jointly accounted for 965,330 deaths (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 680,096-1,342,437). Shannon diversity rose from 2.336 to 2.711 (+16.1%) between 1990 and 2023; the effective number of causes nearly doubled (5.57 to 9.94), inversely coupled to total deaths (Spearman {rho} = -0.997). Whooping cough ranked second (112,954 deaths; 95% UI 64,576-185,708; 11.7%) and showed the spectrums only rebound above 100% (-57.4% collapse, +111.0% rebound). Tuberculosis ranked third (87,764; 57,779-124,912; 9.1%) with the highest concentration in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia (87.1%). COVID-19 entered at rank five (52,899; 47,275-59,183; 5.5%). Nineteen of 29 causes exceeded the poverty-lock threshold (>80.59% of deaths in sub-Saharan Africa plus South Asia). Joinpoint analysis placed breakpoints in total deaths at 2011, 2018 and 2021--the decline slowed from -3.4% to -2.3% per year after 2011, steepened to -7.1% per year in 2018-2021 and rebounded +4.5% per year in 2021-2023--while diversification accelerated to +1.18% per year in 2013-2020; all six leading pathogen shares carried a pandemic-window breakpoint at 2019 and 2021 (S. pneumoniae at 2018 and 2021). ConclusionsChildhood respiratory infectious mortality has become more diverse and more concentrated in poverty as it has declined. Single-pathogen interventions now address a shrinking share; the spectrums structure argues for platform interventions--oxygen, antimicrobial access, referral--tailored jointly by age and geography, implying that pathogen-specific strategies alone cannot finish the remaining mortality agenda.

title: Transdiagnostic gray matter volume reductions implicating social dysfunction in depression, schizophrenia, and alcohol use disorder: A neuroimaging meta-analysis
text: Anhedonia, social withdrawal and executive deficits represent transdiagnostic symptoms in depression, schizophrenia and addiction, yet transdiagnostic brain volumetric alterations and their contribution to these symptom domains have not been systematically characterized. Here, we capitalized on a pre-registered (https://osf.io/s57uq) coordinate-based meta-analysis across 147 VBM studies (n=13,041) to determine common and disorder-specific gray matter deficits in patients with schizophrenia (90 studies), major depression disorder (44 studies) and alcohol use disorder (13 studies). Original case-control articles comparing patients with healthy controls, published in English and reporting whole-brain results were included. We found shared GMV alterations in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, ventral anterior cingulate cortex, insula, superior temporal gyrus. On the network level, we found robust functional interactions of the identified shared regions with the cortical midline structures as well as social and theory of mind-related behavioral functions. Subsequent characterization analyses highlighted the involvement of dopaminergic and serotonergic neurotransmitters as well as associated genetic annotations. Overall, the present meta-analysis found common as well as separate GMV abnormalities in schizophrenia, major depressive disorder and alcohol use disorder suggesting a common neurostructural substrate and treatment target for social withdrawal and anhedonia across these disorders.

title: Automated Patient Identity Verification Framework for Multimodal Medical Imaging Using Deep Metric Learning and Domain Adaptation
text: PurposePatient identity management is fundamental in healthcare information systems, as identification inconsistencies can compromise patient safety, data integrity, and clinical workflow efficiency. Reliable linkage of medical images acquired across different imaging modalities remains challenging because of variations in image appearance, acquisition geometry, and imaging characteristics. In this study, we developed an automated patient identity verification framework for multimodal medical imaging using deep metric learning and data-augmented domain adaptation (DADA). MethodsThe proposed framework learned modality-invariant patient representations from labeled source-domain data while leveraging unlabeled target-domain data to mitigate cross-modality distribution shifts. Although patient identity annotations were available within the research dataset for evaluation purposes, target-domain labels were intentionally excluded from the DADA optimization process. Chest radiographs and computed tomography (CT) scout images obtained under routine clinical conditions were retrospectively collected and used for evaluation. Verification performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with the area under the ROC curve (AUC) used as the primary performance metric. ResultsThe proposed framework achieved consistently high verification performance across all evaluation conditions, with AUC values ranging from 0.9989 to 0.9999. Similarity-score distributions demonstrated distinct separation between same-patient and different-patient image pairs despite substantial differences between imaging modalities. ConclusionThese findings indicate that patient-specific anatomical representations can be preserved across heterogeneous imaging domains through metric learning and domain adaptation. The proposed framework may serve as a practical infrastructure component for patient identity management, multimodal data integration, quality assurance, and patient safety applications within healthcare information systems.

title: Fighting Addictions, improving Lives through COmprehensive drug rehabilitation with music (FALCO): Protocol for an international randomised controlled trial
text: BackgroundSubstance use disorders (SUD) are associated with a high global burden of disease, with 5.4% of all disability-adjusted life years lost due to alcohol and illicit drugs. Highly prevalent multimorbidity includes polysubstance use, mental health conditions, and other non-communicable and infectious diseases. Where traditional treatments are insufficient alone, music therapy (MT) is highly engaging and improves motivation and reduces craving; however, its long-term effects are unknown. The present study aims to examine long-term effects of active music groups (AMG) and music listening groups (MLG) versus treatment as usual (TAU) on addiction severity, recovery, and other outcomes in people with SUD. Immediate and short-term effects, as well as mechanisms of these interventions, will also be examined. MethodsIn individuals with SUD across a wide range of age, gender, socioeconomic, and cultural backgrounds, a parallel 3-arm assessor- and statistician-blinded pragmatic multinational randomised controlled trial (RCT) will determine long-term effects of AMG and MLG versus TAU on addiction severity, recovery, and other outcomes. Patients in participating rehabilitation centres in Europe and the Middle East will be randomised 1:1:1 to AMG plus TAU, MLG plus TAU, or TAU alone in a superiority framework. AMG or MLG will be offered for 1 year from randomisation. The primary outcome will be the composite score of drug/alcohol use of the EuropASI 1 year from randomisation. Embedded studies within a trial (SWATs) will examine (i.) immediate effects of AMG or MLG combined with individual components of TAU combined to determine the best combinations of interventions and (ii.) mechanisms using cognitive testing and brain imaging. With 600 participants randomised, the trial will have 80% power on the primary outcome. Patient representatives, health technology assessment (HTA) bodies, and interventionists have been involved from conception and will ensure feasibility and applicability of the intervention across Europe. The trial is currently recruiting; the first participant was randomised on 26 November 2025. DiscussionThis document describes the FALCO RCT, the main part of the FALCO project, which aims to reduce disease burden through innovative, effective, and affordable treatment, and will strengthen research and innovation expertise. Recommendations from FALCO will inform intervention delivery across Europe and beyond, leading to increased safety, effectiveness, and cost-effectiveness, and improved quality of life for individuals with SUD. Stakeholders will be involved in communicating findings across all European countries and regions and ensuring that findings are effectively implemented. Trial registrationClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07028983, registered 11 June 2025. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07028983

title: Human Plasma Proteomics Links Modifiable Lifestyle Exposome to Disease Risk
text: Lifestyle exposures influence disease risk, yet the molecular signatures linking modifiable behaviors to human biology remain incompletely characterized. Here we show that the plasma proteome carries a measurable record of modifiable lifestyle exposures. We developed the Human Exposomic Architecture of the Proteome (HEAP), a framework linking lifestyle exposures, plasma proteins, and disease risk at population scale. Applying HEAP to more than 50,000 UK Biobank participants, 2,686 plasma proteins, and 169 lifestyle exposures, we identified exposure-associated protein signatures that organized along shared health-behavior patterns and connected lifestyle variation to disease-relevant biology. Integrating disease associations, mediation analyses, Mendelian randomization, and colocalization showed that only a minority of exposure-responsive proteins were consistent with causal intermediates, whereas many appeared to function as biological reporters of exposure burden, disease liability, and early disease processes. Comparisons with exercise-training and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist studies linked observational lifestyle signatures to intervention-induced proteomic changes, suggesting that part of the exposomic signal reflects biology modifiable by intervention. Furthermore, proteome-based exposure scores captured exposure-associated biology, tracked behavioral change over time, and predicted disease risk. Overall, HEAP provides a resource for advancing disease prevention and precision medicine by linking modifiable lifestyle exposures to disease-relevant protein signatures.

title: A Synbiotic Infant Formula Promotes Balanced Immune-Microbiome Interactions in Term Infants: A Randomized Controlled Trial
text: Formula-fed infants have altered gut microbiota and immune development relative to breastfed infants. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) and microbes able to ferment these, like Bifidobacterium infantis, promote healthy immune-microbiome interactions in breastfed infants. In this randomized trial, 240 healthy term infants in the Philippines received a synbiotic formula (SynF; seven HMOs, bovine milk oligosaccharides, and B. infantis LMG11588) or control formula (CtrlF) for 6 months. SynF supported growth non-inferior to CtrlF and near universal B. infantis colonization (vs <10% in CtrlF). Markers of intestinal inflammation were lower in children fed SynF while secretory IgA was higher. SynF fed infants showed lower markers of systemic inflammation in plasma, slower immune cell maturation, and fewer upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) during their first 6 months of life. These findings suggest that synbiotic formula can dampen inflammatory responses to colonizing microbes and mild infections in fully formula-fed, term infants. Trial registration: NCT06073652.

title: Real-World Twelve-Month Weight Loss Outcomes in a Comprehensive Obesity Care Program Utilizing Individualized Nutrition Therapy and Incretin-Based Obesity Medications
text: Background/ObjectivesIncretin-based obesity medications (IOMs) produce substantial weight loss, but the added benefit of structured nutritional therapy remains unclear. We compared 12-month weight loss between individualized carbohydrate-reduced nutritional therapy plus IOMs (VINT+IOM) and IOM-based care without structured nutritional therapy (IOM only). MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study of 4,269 adults in a telemedicine obesity care program (VINT+IOM, n = 1,658; IOM only, n = 2,611), both pathways included clinician-guided medication management and behavioral coaching. The primary analysis included GLP-1-naive participants on a single ingredient (semaglutide or tirzepa ide). Adjusted weight change was estimated using longitudinal linear mixed-effects models. ResultsRetention through 12 months was 77% (VINT+IOM) vs. 72% (IOM only). In GLP-1-naive semaglutide users, adjusted 12-month weight loss was greater with VINT+IOM than IOM only (13.9 vs. 10.9 kg; difference 3.0 kg, 95% CI 0.6-5.4; P = 0.012); observed loss was 13.3% vs. 11.1%. In tirzepatide users, adjusted loss was 20.8 vs. 15.6 kg (difference 5.2 kg, 95% CI 1.8-8.7; P = 0.003); observed loss was 19.7% vs. 15.6%. Responder rates favored VINT+IOM. In the overall cohort, adjusted loss was 13.3 vs. 9.8 kg (P < 0.001), and the advantage persisted among participants with prior GLP-1 exposure. Weight loss continued between 6 and 12 months, and approximately 80% of participants in both pathways had IOM proportion of days covered [≥]80%. Self-reported side effects were similar (63.6% vs 64.6%). ConclusionsAdding individualized carbohydrate-reduced nutritional therapy to IOM-based care was associated with greater 12-month weight loss than IOM-based care without structured nutritional therapy. These real-world findings support further evaluation of individualized nutrition as an adjunct to incretin-based pharmacotherapy.

title: Clinical outcomes of bio-interventional cyclodialysis with one or multiple allogeneic reinforcements: a multicenter real-world evidence study
text: Introduction: Bio-reinforced cyclodialysis uses a biocompatible acellular scleral allograft spacer to maintain a surgically created cleft and enhance uveoscleral outflow. The titratable effect of 1 vs 2 spacers on intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering has not previously been evaluated. Methods: Analysis of 260 eyes (187 patients) in the prospective, multicenter CREST study (NCT05506423) undergoing combined phacoemulsification and bio-reinforced cyclodialysis with one spacer (N = 146) or two (N = 114). The primary endpoint was IOP change from baseline to month 12. Analyses comprised unadjusted comparison, baseline-adjusted regression, 1:1 propensity-score matching, doubly robust overlap weighting, and models accounting for enrolling site and fellow eyes. IOP after a secondary IOP-lowering procedure was censored. IOP reported as mean (95% CI) and medications as mean ({+/-}SD). Results: At baseline, IOP was 17.8 (4.2) versus 18.5 (5.7) mmHg and medications 1.3 (1.1) versus 1.5 (1.4), with one versus two spacers, respectively. Enrolling site was most imbalanced: one center contributed 38.6% of two-spacer eyes but 7.5% of one-spacer eyes. The unadjusted difference in IOP reduction was 2.5 mmHg (1.2-3.8; p<0.001) and persisted after propensity-score matching (2.4 mmHg; 0.9-3.8; p=0.001) and overlap weighting (2.0 mmHg; 1.2-2.8; p<0.001). After accounting for site, it attenuated to 0.9 mmHg (-0.1 to 1.8; p=0.080), and to 0.4 mmHg (-0.6 to 1.5; p=0.424) using both strategies. Medication reduction (-0.7 versus -0.6; p=0.643), freedom from secondary incisional surgery (98.6% versus 99.1%), and site-adjusted adverse-event rates did not differ. Conclusion: Two-spacer treatment was associated with numerically greater 12-month IOP reduction in unadjusted and patient-level adjusted analyses, but this association was substantially attenuated after accounting for enrolling site. These short-term real-world data are compatible with, but do not establish, an independent incremental effect of a second spacer. Further study is warranted. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT05506423. Plain Language SummaryGlaucoma damages the nerve at the back of the eye, usually because pressure inside the eye is too high. One way to lower that pressure is an operation that opens a small channel so fluid can drain out of the eye more easily. A thin piece of donated, treated tissue from the white of the eye is placed there to hold it open. Surgeons can place one of these spacers or two. Nobody knew whether two lowers the pressure more than one. We studied 260 eyes treated at nine centers, all of which also had cataract surgery at the same time. Of these, 146 received one spacer and 114 received two. We compared how far the pressure inside the eye fell over the following year. Eyes that received two spacers had a larger fall in pressure, about 2.5 millimeters of mercury more than eyes that received one. That is the unit used to measure eye pressure. However, the surgeons who chose two spacers worked mainly at a few particular centers, and those centers differed from the others in many ways. When we compared eyes treated at the same center, the difference between one spacer and two almost disappeared. These findings suggest that two spacers may be associated with greater pressure lowering, but this study cannot determine whether the second spacer itself caused the additional effect. A randomized study, in which patients are assigned to receive one or two spacers, would be needed to answer that question more definitively. title: The phenomic landscape of rare gain- and loss-of-function variation
text: Current large-scale phenome-wide association studies do not distinguish between genetic variants with distinct functional consequences, despite evidence that gain-of-function (GoF) and loss-of-function (LoF) variants can produce different phenotypes. Consequently, the phenotypic consequences of variants stratified by predicted GoF and LoF effects have not been systematically characterized at scale. Here, we systematically analyzed rare predicted GoF and LoF variants in 18,214 genes across 1,244 binary and 202 quantitative traits using whole-exome sequencing and electronic health records from the Mount Sinai Million Health Discoveries Program, a phenotypically rich hospital-based biobank comprised of 50,067 participants, primarily representing African, Admixed American and European ancestries. We identified numerous established and previously unreported ancestry-specific and shared gene- and variant-level associations, many of which were supported by complementary evidence from both diagnostic phenotypes and clinical measurements. Proteomic evaluation of the previously unreported association between VNN1 LoF variants and body mass index in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis revealed reduced circulating vanin-1 levels with LoF variants, which in turn were associated with body composition and additional cardiometabolic phenotypes. Functional stratification of predicted GoF and LoF variants revealed gene-trait associations that were attenuated when these variants were combined, demonstrating that traditional aggregation of variants with different functional effects can obscure association signals. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating predicted functional consequences into association analyses and establish a comprehensive resource linking exome-wide predicted GoF and LoF variants to the human phenome across ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry analyses.

title: Genomic diversity of respiratory pathogens in clinical versus community surveillance: a comparative analysis of SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza viruses in Washington State
text: BackgroundGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses typically relies on sequences from individuals seeking health care, and whether these sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community is not well-characterized. We aimed to compare the diversity, proportion, and dynamics of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 between clinical and community samples. MethodsIn this retrospective comparative genomic analysis, we used whole-genome sequences from community-based surveillance studies in the Seattle area, and clinical sequences from the Washington State Department of Health. We compared clade proportions and dynamics, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values between clinical and community samples. FindingsWe analyzed 538 RSV sequences collected between 2019 and 2021 (278 community, 260 clinical), 1506 influenza sequences (260 community, 1246 clinical) between 2019 and 2020, and 8660 SARS-CoV-2 sequences (5923 community, 2737 clinical) from 2020 to 2022. Clade proportions did not differ between clinical and community samples for RSV or influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2: clades 21J (Delta) and 21K (Omicron BA.1) were more frequent in community samples and clade 22B (Omicron BA.5) in clinical samples. SARS-CoV-2 clinical sequence clusters were more diverse than community clusters, whereas RSV and influenza showed no significant difference. Several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples for SARS-CoV-2. Ct values were lower in clinical samples for multiple SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza clades. InterpretationSeasonal respiratory viruses had similar dynamics and diversity in clinical and community samples, whereas pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differed between settings. Genomic surveillance programs should combine clinical and community sampling, particularly during pandemics in order to better capture viral diversity. FundingThis analysis was funded by the Washington State Department of Health Northwest Pathogen Genomics Center of Excellence (WA DOH contract number HED29377-1, federal grant number NU50CK000630 to University of Washington). The underlying studies were funded by Gates Ventures. RESEARCH IN CONTEXTO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses expanded substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic and has since been extended to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza, but most sequences come from people who sought medical care. We searched PubMed for studies published in English up to September 2026 using combinations of terms "genomic surveillance", "community surveillance", "respiratory syncytial virus", "influenza", "SARS-CoV-2", "whole genome sequencing", and included studies that sequenced respiratory viruses from defined clinical or community populations. Previous work has sampled hospitalized patients, sequenced random positive specimens, or sequenced wastewater, and has shown that such data can track variant emergence, clade replacement, and nosocomial transmission. However, few studies compared clinical and community sampling for the same virus in the same population and period, so it remains unclear whether clinically derived sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community. title: Design and Validation of a Compact Sensor for Peripheral Pulse Waveform Capture
text: Peripheral pulse waveforms captured across different sites of the vascular tree provide valuable insights into cardiovascular health. This study presents a low-cost compact sensor designed to minimize intrusion at the measurement site while capturing the pulse waveform. The sensor performance was characterized and evaluated through both in-vitro benchtop experiments and a pilot in-vivo clinical study against invasive arterial pressure waveforms. The proposed sensor was able to capture pulse waveform morphology with reliable beat to beat tracking. Although offsets were present in the calculated features, fundamental temporal trends and cardiac cycle profiles were preserved. Thus, this work lays the foundation for a scalable hardware platform capable of multi-site pulse monitoring, enabling its integration with emerging computational frameworks for cardiovascular risk screening.

title: Incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms: A nationwide population based longitudinal study
text: BackgroundUnderstanding the epidemiology of unruptured intracranial aneurysm (UIAs) is crucial for risk stratification, clinical decision making, and public health planning. The aim of this study was to perform a nationwide population-based analysis to examine the incidence of unruptured intracranial aneurysms in Sweden. MethodsData were obtained from the Swedish National Patient Register for all persons, aged 18 years and older, diagnosed with an intracranial aneurysm (ICD-10: I67.1) between the years 2000 and 2020. Crude incidence was calculated for the total population and age- and gender-stratified groups. Age standardized incidence was assessed using the European standard population. The incidence of intracranial aneurysms diagnosed with concurrent subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) was also examined. ResultsDuring the study period, 8681 patients were diagnosed with UIA. The median age of diagnosis was 63 years and 65.1% were women. The age-standardized incidence increased approximately 74% % between 2000 and its peak: from 4.6 (95% CI: 4,26-4.95) per 100,000 in the year 2000 to 7.99 (95% CI: 6.7-7.54) per 100,000 in the year 2019. {square} The increase in incidence of UIAs was most pronounced among women and those aged above 60. During the study period, the number of cases with SAH decreased slightly. ConclusionsThe increasing incidence of UIAs in Sweden might be due improved clinical detection rates, demographic changes, and changes in the prevalence of risk factors. These findings highlight the importance of enhanced surveillance, effective risk stratification, and targeted public health strategies to address the growing burden of UIAs.

title: Epidemiology of zero-dose among children aged 12-35 months in Ethiopia: Burden, correlates and spatial patterns; Evidence from a 2025 national survey
text: BackgroundChildren who have not received the first dose of a diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis-containing vaccine are classified as zero-dose. Understanding how many children remain without this dose beyond infancy, the correlates, and their geographic distribution can inform routine and catch-up vaccination services in Ethiopia. This study aimed to estimate the burden of zero-dose, identify its correlates, and map its spatial distribution among children aged 12-35 months in Ethiopia. MethodsWe analyzed data from 2,097 children aged 12-35 months in the Pathways for Ethiopia survey, a recent national population-based cross-sectional household survey conducted from August to November 2025. The burden estimates and regression analyses accounted for sampling weights, stratification, and clustering. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) were obtained through marginal standardization of survey-weighted logistic regression models. Spatial autocorrelation, hotspot, and spatial-scan analyses assessed geographic clustering. Ordinary kriging predicted prevalence at unsampled locations. ResultsThe weighted prevalence of zero-dose status was 20.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 15.9-26.3), with regional point estimates ranging from 0.8% in Addis Ababa to 35.9% in Somali. Its burden was 20.4% among children aged 12-23 months and 20.8% among those aged 24-35 months. Higher burden was associated with no antenatal care compared with four or more visits (aPR: 2.39; 95% CI: 1.61-3.53), unimproved compared with improved drinking-water sources (aPR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.18-1.97), and caregivers rating vaccination as less than very important compared with very important (aPR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.03-3.54). Zero-dose prevalence showed significant spatial clustering (Morans I = 0.229; p = 0.0001). Hotspots occurred among sampled communities in Somali, Oromia, Central Ethiopia, Afar, and South Ethiopia. Predicted prevalence was highest across parts of eastern and south-central Ethiopia. ConclusionApproximately one in five children aged 12-35 months had not received the first pentavalent dose. High zero-dose prevalence clustered among sampled communities in eastern and south-central Ethiopia. Moreover, antenatal care and drinking water source were independent factors. Immunization programs should prioritize these communities for identifying and vaccinating missed children, including those aged 24-35 months.

title: Socioeconomic position, socioenvironmental conditions, and subjective cognitive decline among midlife and older LGBTQIA+ adults in California
text: ObjectivesTo examine which measure of socioeconomic position and socioenvironmental conditions has the strongest relationship with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among midlife and older lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, and other sexual and gender minority (LGBTQIA+) adults. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 3869 LGBTQIA+ adults aged 50 years or older participating in a community-engaged survey in California. Using logistic regression, we examined overall associations between each indicator of socioeconomic position and socioenvironmental conditions and SCD. We used a dominance analysis to assess the relative importance of each indicator based on the proportion of variance in SCD it explained. ResultsOverall, 14.7% of the sample reported SCD. Midlife and older LGBTQIA+ adults in a lower socioeconomic position (i.e., lower education, unemployment, lower household income, fewer assets, financial insecurity, food insecurity, and unstable housing) had higher odds of SCD than those in a higher position, with significant odds ratios (OR) ranging from 1.28 to 2.55. In contrast, perceiving ones community as safe for LGBTQIA+ people was associated with lower odds of SCD (OR 0.47; 95% CI 0.38, 0.58). Dominance analysis indicated that household assets was the most important factor, explaining 4.4% of the variance in SCD (95% CI 3.5%, 5.4%), followed by household income (2.9%; 95% CI 2.2%, 3.8%) and perceived community safety (2.2%; 95% CI 1.4%, 3.1%). DiscussionSupporting the cognitive health of LGBTQIA+ people may require attention to both financial security across the life course and the broader social environments.

title: Pneumococcal nasopharyngeal carriage in children 2-60 months of age in Novi Sad (Serbia), October 2022-September 2026
text: BackgroundStreptococcus pneumoniae nasopharyngeal carriage in young children is an important source of transmission and may precede pneumococcal disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines can alter circulating serotypes. Continued surveillance is needed to monitor serotype replacement, vaccine serotype coverage, and antimicrobial resistance. MethodsA prospective surveillance study was conducted in outpatient pediatric practices from October 2022 to September 2026 among children aged 2-60 months in Novi Sad, Serbia. Healthy children attending preventive visits and children with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal specimens were collected and cultured for S. pneumoniae. Participant-level analyses used the first eligible specimen per child, while isolate-level analyses included all recovered isolates. Serotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed. Theoretical vaccine serotype coverage was estimated for licensed and selected investigational pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, with 23- valent polysaccharide vaccine evaluated separately. ResultsAmong 3,373 included children, 911 were pneumococcal carriers, giving an overall carriage prevalence of 27.0%. Carriage was higher among children with acute respiratory tract infection than among healthy children and was also associated with daycare attendance, chronic medical conditions, age, season, and surveillance year. In total, 1,312 pneumococcal isolates were recovered, of which 87.9% were typeable. The most frequent serotypes included 11A, 10A, 15A, 15B, 23A, 23B, 19A, and 6B. Theoretical serotype coverage was 8.2% for PCV10, 17.5% for PCV13, 20.0% for PCV15, and 47.3% for PCV20. More than half of typeable isolates were non-PCV20 serotypes. Resistance was most frequent to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline, while multidrug resistance was observed in 18.1% of isolates. Penicillin G non-susceptibility was uncommon. ConclusionPneumococcal carriage in children aged 2-60 months in Novi Sad was associated with age, clinical presentation, season, and surveillance year and involved diverse serotypes. Continued carriage surveillance, linked with invasive-disease and antibiotic-use data, would help determine whether the observed serotype and resistance patterns persist.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Advance Care Planning in Patients with Neurosurgical Conditions and Their Caregivers
text: IntroductionAdvance care planning (ACP) enables quality end-of-life (EOL) care that reflects patients values and preferences. However, ACP remains limited among individuals with neurosurgical conditions - such as stroke, glioma, or metastatic brain tumours - who often experience rapid decline and short prognoses. When ACP discussions occur only after cognitive deterioration or acute events, opportunities for meaningful conversations are lost. This study aims to assess the baseline knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of ACP among neurosurgical patients and their caregivers in Singapore. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional survey of 30 patients with symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (SICH) or brain tumours at the National University Hospital and their caregivers. Using validated ACP engagement questionnaires, we assessed participants KAP, and readiness on 5-point Likert scales (1 lowest - 5 best), alongside nine ACP knowledge statements. ResultsPatients demonstrated below-average ACP knowledge (mean = 4.1 / 9) and largely neutral attitudes (3.2 / 5) and perceptions (3.1 / 5). Misconceptions were common, including beliefs that ACP documents are legally binding, that preferred care cannot be delivered without ACP, and that ACP is solely a doctors responsibility. Consequently, both patients and caregivers showed low levels of ACP engagement. ConclusionThe findings highlight the need to introduce ACP education and conversations earlier in the care journey, especially for individuals at risk of cerebrovascular or cardiovascular events. Early engagement, particularly among those with hypertension or other risk factors, presents a crucial window for preparing patients and families for future care decisions. CLINICAL IMPACTO_ST_ABSWhat is NewC_ST_ABSO_LIThis study is the first to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of ACP among neurosurgical patients and their caregivers in Singapore. C_LIO_LIFindings revealed low levels of ACP engagement, below-average knowledge of and prevalent misconceptions regarding ACP among both patients and caregivers. C_LI Clinical ImplicationsO_LIThe findings highlight the need to introduce ACP education and conversations earlier in the care journey, especially for individuals at risk of cerebrovascular or cardiovascular events, such as those with hypertension or other risk factors. title: Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence During and After COVID-19 Social Distancing in Korea: A Nationwide 16-Year Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
text: BackgroundPediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a rare but devastating event. However, the extent to which large-scale public health interventions, such as COVID-19 social distancing policies, affected the incidence of pediatric OHCA remains unclear. MethodsWe conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis using data from the Korea Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Registry (2008-2023). The primary outcome was the monthly incidence of OHCA among individuals aged 0-18 years. The study period was divided into three phases: pre-intervention (January 2008-February 2020), social distancing (March 2020-April 2022), and post-lifting (May 2022-December 2023). We used segmented Poisson regression, adjusted for population size and seasonal variation, to estimate changes in monthly incidence at each policy change and reported the results as incidence rate ratios (IRRs). To determine whether these changes differed by age, we compared children with adults (19-64 years) and elderly individuals ([≥]65 years). ResultsOf the 456,839 registry entries, 10,965 were pediatric OHCAs, of which 6,891 underwent resuscitation in the emergency department. The crude incidence was 7.04, 7.14, and 8.35 per 100,000 person-years in the three phases, respectively. Before the pandemic, incidence rose slightly (annual IRR 1.006 [95% CI 1.001-1.012]; P = 0.032). At the implementation of social distancing, incidence fell immediately (IRR 0.926 [95% CI 0.865-0.991]; P = 0.027), without a significant change in slope (P = 0.081). After restrictions were lifted, incidence rose immediately (IRR 1.138 [95% CI 1.048-1.235]; P = 0.002) and then declined gradually (monthly IRR 0.993 [95% CI 0.988-0.999]; P = 0.023). These changes were confined to children aged 1-11 years (implementation IRR 0.812 [95% CI 0.666-0.991]; post-lifting IRR 1.562 [95% CI 1.278-1.909]). The pattern of change differed significantly by age group (P < 0.001), mainly because incidence rose in children, but not in adults or elderly individuals, after restrictions were lifted. ConclusionsNationwide social distancing was associated with a transient decrease in pediatric OHCA incidence, which was concentrated among children aged 1-11 years and was followed by a rebound above the expected level after restrictions were lifted. Surveillance of pediatric OHCA should account for abrupt changes in childrens daily environments, including the closure and reopening of schools and childcare facilities.

title: Antimicrobial stewardship strategies to optimise antibiotic prescribing in primary care: physicians awareness, beliefs, and strategy use
text: BackgroundNational efforts to promote antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) and prevent antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in primary care need strengthening. Research supports clinician-targeted AMS strategies to optimise antibiotic prescribing, but implementing them in clinical settings is challenging. AimAssessment of primary care physicians awareness of, use of, and beliefs about evidence-based AMS strategies, and perceived barriers and facilitators to implementing them in a country with high antibiotic consumption rates (Poland). MethodsA pre-registered observational survey study. Eligible physicians worked in primary care in Poland for 6+ months and were recruited via professional networks and social media. Data were collected through a pre-piloted online questionnaire and analysed descriptively. Results270 physicians (68.2% Specialists/Residents in Family Medicine) participated. Respondents were aware of the threat of AMR (88%), the importance of AMS (93%) and their role in AMS (89%). They most recognised, utilised, perceived as effective, and recommended rapid diagnostic tests, clinical guidelines, and scales/criteria. Respondents reported high familiarity but lower engagement with communication strategies, national actions, education/training, and campaigns. Delayed prescriptions were the least used and recommended. Main barriers were time constraints and insufficient awareness of which strategies to implement. Recommended strategies included tests, guidelines, scales/criteria, AMS action plans for general practices, patient communication resources, and promoting awareness of AMS and its role in high-quality care. ConclusionAwareness and use of evidence-based AMS strategies among physicians working in Polish primary care clinics appear high. Improvements may require reaching disengaged physicians, increasing uptake of underutilised strategies, and strengthening the impact of already used strategies.

title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
text: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental disorders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classification accuracy. The highest performing algorithm was able to classify the seizures with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of >0.9 for both the 0 vs. T and the T vs. A categories corresponding to excellent discrimination. In contrast, the accuracy of predicting seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. The addition of clinical variables to the models, such as demographics, anesthesia and anticonvulsant exposure, did not improve model performance. These results provide proof-of-concept of machine learning classification of seizure adequacy in ECT based on raw EEG data. The findings could pave the way for the development of more objective and personalized decision-support tools in ECT.

title: Middle Temporal Gyrus Neurite Microstructure and Scam Susceptibility in Older Adults Without Dementia
text: BackgroundFinancial exploitation is a prevalent public health concern among older adults, and emerging evidence links vulnerability to gray matter macrostructure and white matter microstructure, including within brain regions and networks implicated in early Alzheimers disease. Although diffusion tensor imaging is sensitive to age-related variation in brain microstructure, its scalar metrics cannot distinguish among the tissue properties contributing to observed differences. Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) models distinct tissue compartments, yielding estimates of neurite density, dendritic complexity, and extracellular free water. MethodsThis study examined associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics using ultra-high-field 7-Tesla imaging in 116 older adults without dementia. Neurite density index (NDI), orientation dispersion index (ODI), and free-water fraction were quantified within seven a priori regions of interest linked to early Alzheimers disease. Multivariate regressions evaluated associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics, adjusting for age, sex, education, and global cognition, with multiple comparison correction within each metric. For significant regions, post-hoc hierarchical regression models tested whether NODDI metrics explained variance beyond regional cortical thickness, total gray matter, and total intracranial volume. ResultsGreater scam susceptibility was associated with higher NDI ({beta}=0.30, pFDR=.025) and lower ODI ({beta}=-0.28, pFDR=.044) in the middle temporal gyrus (MTG). No other regions survived correction. Additionally, MTG NDI and ODI explained variance beyond macrostructure measures. ConclusionsThese findings identify NODDI metrics as novel microstructural correlates of scam susceptibility beyond macrostructure, supporting investigation of their relevance to financial vulnerability in older age.

title: Physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with limb loss 2-years after the 2023 Kahramanmaras-Türkiye earthquakes
text: IntroductionThe 2023 Kahramanmaras-Turkiye earthquakes resulted in many paediatric amputations. While prosthetic provision following disasters has been described, little is known about longer-term physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with earthquake-related limb loss. AimEvaluate health-related quality of life, prosthesis experience, pain, and function approximately two years post-amputation. MethodRetrospective analysis was conducted of children with earthquake-related limb loss who attend the XXX Center. Socio-demographic and amputation-related data, psychological status, outcome scores for pain, the Paediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) and the Trinity Amputation and Prosthesis Experience Scales (TAPES) were included. ResultsFifty-six children (50% female; 13.7{+/-}5.0 years old) were included. Children had unilateral upper limb loss (n=15), unilateral lower limb loss (n=31), bilateral lower limb loss (n=7), or combined upper and lower limb loss (n=3). Data were obtained 2.3{+/-}0.4 years following amputation. Median child-reported PedsQL scores were 72.3/100.0, with high social functioning (85.0/100.0) but lower emotional functioning (60.0/100.0). No differences in PedsQL outcomes were found between limb loss groups. Children rated their physical and emotional quality of life higher than carers rated them. TAPES median scores were 50.0/75.0 for psychosocial adjustment, 16.0/36.0 for activity restriction, and 34.5/45.0 for prosthetic satisfaction. Children with unilateral lower limb loss demonstrated superior adjustment and prosthetic satisfaction than children with unilateral upper limb or bilateral lower limb loss (p<0.05). ConclusionsChildren demonstrated favourable physical, social, and school-related quality of life 2.3 years after the earthquakes. However, emotional wellbeing remained affected, highlighting the importance of long-term mental health support alongside prosthetic and rehabilitation services.

title: Unraveling the Lifespan Trajectory of White Matter Hypointensity on T1-weighted MR Images and Clinical Application in Various Brain Disorders
text: White matter hypointensity on T1-weighted MRI (T1-WMHypo), a putative marker of white matter pathophysiological changes, has been less systematically investigated than the widely studied T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (T2-FLAIR) hyperintensity lesions. Here, we built the lifespan normative reference and assessed the clinical significance of T1-WMHypo across various brain disorders using a large multicenter dataset. We first established lifespan normative reference for T1-WMHypo volume by 34,148 healthy individuals (aged 4-85 years). Then, in 7,587 patients across 21 neurological and psychiatric disorders, normative reference-derived deviations revealed disease-specific patterns, with marked deviations in neurological diseases. Deviations of T1-WMHypo volume contributed to differential diagnosis, larger deviations correlated with brain atrophy, cognitive impairment, and poorer outcomes in various brain disorders. Elevated burden of T1-WMHypo volume predicted poor medication response in Parkinsons disease and accelerated disability progression in multiple sclerosis. These associations persisted after adjusting for conventional T2-FLAIR hyperintensity lesions. T1-WMHypo deviations provide an individualized marker of white matter pathophysiological changes, offering novel insights for precision medicine across development, aging and brain disorders.

title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
text: ImportanceLeg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. ObjectiveTo develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsWe retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score [≥]1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s){square}Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts median GDRS scores. ResultsWhen estimating experts leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 {+/-} 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 {+/-} 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and RelevanceWe have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials. Key pointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSCan a deep learning model use clinically-acquired videos to accurately estimate experts leg dystonia severity assessments in children with cerebral palsy? FindingsAn automated deep learning model (DxToniaNet) trained and tested on clinically-acquired smartphone videos of 298 children with cerebral palsy estimates leg dystonia severity with 90-94% accuracy compared to experts assessments. MeaningDxToniaNet is an objective and free tool to estimate leg dystonia severity and may thus help facilitate standardized tracking of longitudinal treatment responses and clinical trial outcomes.

title: How inherited variation shapes human disease trajectories
text: Although inherited variation is fixed at birth, its effects on health change with age and differ between common and rare variants. Here, we introduce Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that combines the age-dependent effects of polygenic and monogenic variation on health records, separating how much disease each individual accumulates overall from diseases to which they are prone. Mendelnoulli further allows polygenic and monogenic components to exert different influences on latent disease trajectories. We apply the model to 348 diseases, 36 polygenic scores, and 34 monogenic conditions across three biobanks and provide an atlas of the age-dependent effects of inherited variation on common human diseases. We show that polygenic effects change significantly with age, with Mendelnoulli improving held-out one-year discrimination for all 28 diseases tested compared with a model whose polygenic effects are constant over age (median AUC 0.95 vs 0.92). For individuals with no prior diagnoses, Mendelnoulli identified 8.6 more of every 100 new cases than that model, when each flagged the 5% at highest risk. For genes with an established disease, Mendelnoulli selected that disease for 27 of 30 genes and ranked it first for 17 (7 expected by chance), and recovered known differences in timing, such as earlier breast cancer effects for BRCA1 than BRCA2 (peak 48 vs 66 years). Mendelnoulli provides a unified model of common and rare genetic influences on disease trajectories across the life course.

title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
text: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions. At the category level, most risks are considered inconsistently by different systems, e.g., GPT allows 70.4\% editing attempts of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8\%. Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity, likely benefiting from mature NSFW identification works. Our findings highlight the need for safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.

title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
text: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks on Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS and Entity-30. We report more than 2,600 such edit processes, whereby each edit is scored on held-out images for success, side effects and accuracy loss. We compare standard training with label smoothing, gradient-based editable training, and our Edit-Ready Training (ERT), a novel method that rehearses the direct, closed-form weight edits LLMs perform. We show that preparing networks for editing raises the success of LLM edits substantially where standard networks are hard to edit. ERT further achieves the highest mean score for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 across all evaluated baselines. We will release our LLM testing framework alongside all tasks, editing trajectories and scores. Project page: https://viscom.uni-ulm.de/wsp

title: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits
text: Large language models increasingly rely on extended reasoning traces, yet the training signals used to shape this behavior remain coarse. Supervised fine-tuning on full trajectories forces the model to imitate an entire demonstration, overconstraining its output distribution, while trajectory-level reinforcement learning provides only weak credit assignment, rewarding or penalizing whole completions without identifying where they succeed or fail. We propose edit-based training, a general framework for learning from a model's own trajectories via localized textual corrections. Given a sampled completion, an editor identifies the first point of failure under a specified criterion and proposes a minimal replacement span. The model is then supervised only on these edited spans. By design, this concentrates supervision where the model's reasoning first breaks down and aims to preserve its existing reasoning patterns elsewhere. The method applies both offline and online, with the latter continually adapting supervision to the model's evolving failure modes. We instantiate this approach on reasoning instruction following with Qwen3-32B on the ReasonIF benchmark. Compared to full-trajectory imitation and trajectory-level reinforcement learning baselines, edit-based training substantially improves compliance with the reasoning instruction while largely preserving the model's skills on untargeted tasks. These results suggest that localized correction is an effective complement to these approaches for shaping how LLMs reason.

title: Beyond Covers and Titles: Evidence-First Ranking for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
text: Short-video platforms rank new uploads before anyone has watched them, using content towers that read a video's cover, title and frames. Existing attacks on content-aware recommenders perturb pixels or features and ignore platform re-encoding, and existing defenses train against norm-bounded perturbations that neither match real edits nor preserve recommendation quality. We show with REAP, a realizable attack through {a simulated platform channel (H.264 transcoding, rescaling, cropping and JPEG)}, that packaging edits raise a cold video by 32.0 rank-percentile points in unrelated audiences. We then observe that cold-start ranking does not need the packaging at all: a tower that sees only the video body ranks cold items best. Building on this, we propose Evidence-First Ranking (EFR), which scores cold videos from their body, admits packaging only through a support-gated residual bounded by $γ$, and merges cold and warm rankings by rank percentile, yielding an exact certificate against any packaging edit. On MicroLens-100K, EFR cuts the attack gain by 81% and raises cold-start Recall@100 from 0.1133 to 0.170, while keeping the merged NDCG@10 within 4% of the undefended system.

title: Can World Models Predict Rice Growth? Toward Agricultural World Models
text: World models can imagine how a physical scene evolves over the next few seconds, but growers need to know how a crop will develop over weeks to months: will this rice plant have headed a month from now, and how will it look at harvest? We introduce agricultural world modeling, the task of predicting how the same plant will look at a requested horizon of days to months, from one photo of it, its cultivar, and its camera view. In preliminary analysis, even state-of-the-art image generators get this wrong: they often grow the plant too little or give it the color and form of the wrong growth stage. We argue that they do not work out the plant's developmental state, which the photo reveals only indirectly. We therefore propose AgroWM, which reasons about development before it draws growth. Its reasoning module, PhenoClock, works out the current growth stage, predicts the future one, and writes a Growth Script with numeric targets for height, plant area, and color; its generation module, the Rooted Renderer, then edits the photo to follow this script, adding new organs and colors to the photographed plant. Because pixel scores can prefer an unchanged copy of the photo, we instead check each forecast's traits and developmental timing against the plant's own later photos. On rice, 54.6% of the forecasts of AgroWM are matched to the target stage (Stage R@1), against 34.8% for GPT Image 2.5, 24.0% for Qwen Image 2.1, and 47.4% for the strongest domain-specific baseline, the same backbone fine-tuned without Growth Scripts; 9 to 20 weeks ahead, it still reaches 46.4%, against 35.7% for that baseline. On maize, a crop with a different body plan and stage scale, the same design again scores best on all four measures.

title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
text: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a pretrained vision language model can be directly extended into a unified model with extensive parameter sharing. Specifically, HiUni reuses the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both capabilities, while confining task-specific computation to the output side. Yet such a design introduces two key challenges. Generation in pixel space is difficult to optimize, and semantic abstraction in pretrained ViT discards fine spatial details required for synthesis. To address these challenges, HiUni introduces a \emph{Pixel Diffusion Head} tailored to direct pixel-space optimization and a lightweight \emph{HiGate} pathway that provides fine-grained spatial details near the output stage. Extensive experiments show that HiUni achieves a similar average understanding score to the pretrained VLM while attaining competitive performance on image generation and editing. Controlled comparisons and analyses further demonstrate that a single dense backbone can effectively support both capabilities without task-specific backbone computation, highlighting a simpler path toward unified multimodal modeling.

title: SheetAlign: Grounded Interaction and Stage-Isolated Learning for Spreadsheet Agents
text: Spreadsheets are widely used for data analysis and supporting decision-making. Automating spreadsheet analysis while protecting sensitive data and controlling deployment costs motivates locally deployed open-weight large language models (LLMs). Meanwhile, complex spreadsheet tasks require both task reasoning and workbook understanding, while predefined operation interfaces impose additional tool-selection and invocation demands. We introduce SheetAlign, a spreadsheet manipulation framework with stage-isolated policy learning, organized around where to operate, what to change, and how to implement transformations. Task-guided inspection and API grounding anchor code generation in workbook observations and available operations, while stage-isolated learning optimizes program generation and review using edit-progress rewards. At inference, execution consistency selects programs through agreement among workbook states. On SpreadsheetBench, our grounded task interface improves Qwen3-4B's accuracy from 13.5% to 29.2% on average without training. With learning and execution consistency, SheetAlign achieves 32.8% accuracy on average on SpreadsheetBench and 30.1% on Domain-Spreadsheet, outperforming comparable baselines. The code will be made publicly available upon publication.

title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
text: Simulation-driven design of real engineering components has to meet three conditions at once. It runs on few solves, since a nonlinear finite-element simulation of a 3D part takes hours; its design space has many values, the hundreds to thousands of values of the part's CAD model; and a better design often needs a redesign, coordinated changes of the part's proportions rather than local polishing of its surface. Automated optimisers meet at most two of these conditions. Classical optimisers, Bayesian or derivative-free, need a person to cut the design down to a few parameters, and on all the values they need far more solves; industrial shape optimisers move every surface node of the mesh in one solve per cycle, but only in small steps that polish rather than redesign. We ask whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can meet all three by joining what it knows with what the simulation shows. GPT-6 Astra edits a magnesium stent through a CAD geometry parametrisation of about 1,650 values, with a budget of 15 simulations; every proposal is built in CAD, meshed and simulated with large-deformation plasticity and contact, and the LLM reads the full results of every solve. Within that budget it lowered the objective, a high percentile of the strains in the stent's bends, by 32%; on the same budget, the industrial shape optimiser Tosca improved the original design by a tenth and then stopped improving. An earlier GPT-6 Astra design, 25% lower in the same objective, was checked in an independent, higher-fidelity model of the full deployment with crimping and damage: it was 14% less strained than the original after the full chain, and its most damaged spot began to fail later and carried 63% less damage at full expansion. LLMs can thus join their learned knowledge with simulation data to adjust more than a thousand design values and reach valid designs with real improvements.

title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On
text: Editing a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) capture of a person so that they wear a new garment requires every rendered view to agree on the same garment details. Existing 3D virtual try-on (VTON) pipelines, however, edit training views largely independently and fuse them with hand-designed heuristics such as manually chosen reference views and fixed attention-blending weights. The resulting inconsistencies are baked into the 3D representation and surface as texture drift, blurred prints, and implausible geometry in novel views. We present GS-VTON-MVT, a three-stage framework that combines implicit and explicit 3D reasoning for consistent 3DGS try-on. (i) A multi-view inpainting transformer jointly edits a set of training views with full cross-view self-attention, so that cross-view correspondence is learned rather than imposed. (ii) A geometry-guided multi-modal ControlNet conditions the diffusion editor on the garment image together with depth and surface normals rendered from the current 3DGS state, supplying explicit structure where visual evidence is weakest. (iii) A pose-adaptive persona-aware attention replaces the fixed blending weight between current-view and reference-view features with weights derived from camera-pose proximity. On the 3D-VTONBench benchmark, GS-VTON-MVT improves FID, KID, LPIPS-based cross-view consistency, and user preference over general-purpose 3D editors and prior 3D try-on methods.

title: MorphTwin: Enriching Deformable Material Responses from Videos for Morphable and Interactive Physical Twins
text: Reconstructing interactive physical twins from video requires accurately capturing how objects deform while maintaining efficient simulation. We observe that reproducing motion in a video does not guarantee correct responses to new forces when the physical representation restricts how an object can deform. In spring-based twins, coupling between volume and shape responses creates such a limitation. We present MorphTwin, which enriches local deformation modes to capture and independently control these responses while retaining standard spring forces and explicit simulation. To support interpretable material editing and transfer, we use offline calibration to map shared relative response changes to stiffness updates on each reconstructed graph. Under identical inverse settings on synthetic scenes, MorphTwin reduces the mean absolute error of Poisson's ratio by 75.8% and the mean relative error of Young's modulus by 22.1% compared to PhysTwin. We introduce an egocentric stereo and RGB-D benchmark covering interactions with objects of varying stiffness. Real-world experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and up to 14.4% lower future tracking error than PhysTwin at interactive speeds.

title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
text: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states. A central obstruction to proving such bounds is that conventional cluster expansions for the logarithm of reduced Gibbs states can fail to converge due to noncommutativity. Our main insight is to construct a classical representation of the Gibbs state using an overcomplete basis. Although such representations generally involve negative quasiprobability weights, we show that a decomposition based on projective 2-designs admits a convergent cluster expansion with strictly positive weights at sufficiently high temperatures, allowing us to circumvent the obstruction. The separability of high-temperature Gibbs states is a natural byproduct of this decomposition. Finally, in the context of mixed-state phases of matter, our results imply that high-temperature Gibbs states belong to the same mixed-state phase as the maximally mixed state.

title: BRUCE (Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator): spatiotemporal interpolation of air temperature from heterogeneous sensor networks for operational heat monitoring
text: Accurate characterization of intra-urban temperature variability is essential for heat-health surveillance, yet official monitoring networks are too sparse to resolve fine-scale gradients, particularly in Global South cities.
