title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
text: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, OracleImitator matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across the budget range, recovering 90% of the attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost. Because the teacher is an explicit algorithmic object rather than an implicit optimization target, we can also measure directly how much of its ranking is recoverable by a policy restricted to what is visible at deployment.

title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons
text: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
text: Abstract Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/ . They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
text: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
text: Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing
text: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3 + microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1 + dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like proteins, supporting a role for this lectin in immune receptor regulation. Complementary in vivo transcriptomic profiling showed that Gal3 deletion suppresses type I interferon and microglial neurodegenerative transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings position Gal3 at the interface between Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and plaque-associated microglial responses in AD.

title: Pennycress population genomics reveals a complex global expansion history and local climate-adaptation targets for neodomestication
text: Abstract Background Field pennycress ( Thlaspi arvense ) is an emerging winter oilseed crop whose life cycle fits between corn-soybean rotations, yielding animal feed and feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel. Results Here we analyze the largest pennycress panel assembled to date, 739 natural accessions spanning four continents, combining genome-wide diversity analysis with multi-year field evaluation. Our genomic data support that pennycress originated in Eurasia and likely underwent a complex history involving multiple introductions and admixture. Scans for selective sweeps among populations between Eurasian and North American identify phenology-related genes, including the MADS-Affecting Flowering ( MAF ) transcription factors and the seed-dormancy gene DELAY OF GERMINATION 1 ( DOG1 ), suggesting possible targets of phenological adaptation. By cross-species climate genome-wide association studies, we detect 10 syntenic peaks, suggesting partly conserved molecular machinery underlying climate adaptation in Arabidopsis and pennycress. Multi-year, multi-location field trials of over 400 accessions in Illinois identify a significant locus associated with green canopy cover, a trait important for biomass, containing a tandem array of Mitochondrial Transcription Termination Factor ( mTERF5 ) genes. Finally, the field trials reveal significant genotype-by-environment interaction, underscoring the need for regional breeding programs. Conclusions Together, these results document worldwide patterns of genetic variation and candidate climate-adaptive genes that can accelerate the neodomestication of pennycress for cultivation in the midwestern United States.

title: A KNOX–BELL–Lignin Module Regulates Leaf Rolling and Drought Tolerance in Rice
text: Leaf rolling is a critical agronomic trait in rice that directly shapes canopy architecture and photosynthetic efficiency, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. Here, we identify RLC3 (OsBLH4), a BELL-type homeodomain transcription factor, as a key regulator of leaf rolling and drought tolerance. Genetic validation using rlc3-1, rlc3-2, and CRISPR/Cas9-generated rlc3-ko lines, supported by allelism tests, confirms the critical regulatory role of RLC3 in leaf rolling. Paraffin section analysis revealed that RLC3 loss-of-function mutations reduced bulliform cells (BCs) dimensions. Biochemical assays, ultrastructural observations and vascular permeability measurements further showed that these mutations disrupt lignin biosynthesis and secondary cell wall (SCW) formation, leading to aberrant midrib vascular patterning. This structural defect accelerates leaf water loss, which in turn ‌reduces BC turgor pressure, ultimately resulting in leaf rolling and reduced drought tolerance. Mechanistically, RLC3 directly binds to and activates the promoters of core lignin biosynthetic genes (OsCCR4, OsCAld5H1, OsPAL5, and OsCOMT5). Furthermore, RLC3 forms heterodimers with KNOX transcription factors OSH1/45/71, which differentially bind to and co-activate a subset of these targets: OSH1/71 specifically co-activate OsCCR4 and OsCAld5H1, whereas OSH45 additionally co-activates OsPAL5. Loss-of-function mutations in these KNOX genes result in leaf morphology alterations, with reduced lignin content and SCW thickness, ‌ which are partially consistent with the defects observed in rlc3 mutants‌‌. Together, our results reveal a KNOX-BELL-lignin regulatory module that connects transcriptional activation to SCW fortification and water loss regulation, enabling molecular design of drought-tolerant rice with balanced water retention and ideal plant architecture.

title: A universal platform for TCRα/β removal enables safer and more potent TCR therapies and autoimmune modeling
text: Adoptive T-cell therapies using tumour-specific T-cell receptors (TCRs) are limited by competition with endogenous receptors, impairing efficacy and posing risks of off-target autoreactivity. Here we present a CRISPR-based platform that selectively eliminates both endogenous TCR-α and -β chains without affecting transgenic TCRs, irrespective of codon optimization. This approach achieves >90% deletion efficiency in Jurkat and primary human T cells, enhancing expression and functional potency of transgenic receptors. Using an HLA-A*02:01-restricted DMF5 TCR, we show that dual TCR ablation boosts antigen-specific activation and cytotoxicity in vitro and enhances tumor clearance in vivo in human immune system (HIS) mice and prevents graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Targeted locus amplification showed that CRISPR-induced double-strand breaks did not alter lentiviral integration profiles, supporting genomic safety. Extending this approach to four insulin-reactive TCRs demonstrated that endogenous receptor removal increased transduction efficiency and functional activity, with one (1E6) showing selective activation and infiltration of islet grafts (SC-islets) in vivo. This study establishes a universal, safe, and scalable genome-editing platform for generating functionally precise human T cells. By integrating cancer immunotherapy and autoimmune disease modelling within a single framework, it provides a preclinical rationale for dual endogenous TCR removal to improve specificity, safety, and therapeutic efficacy in TCR-based cell therapies.

title: A chicken interferon-stimulated gene screen reveals limited genes restricting influenza virus replication
text: Avian influenza A virus (IAV) is a major global health threat. Not only does it cause significant economic losses to the agricultural industry, but it also presents a risk of spillover into the human population. However, several obstacles must be overcome for a successful cross-species transmission event to occur. One of these obstacles is the innate immunity of the host. While the innate immune response to IAV in humans has been well-studied, the innate immune response to IAV in birds is not as well understood. Here, we explore the interferon-induced immune response by identifying interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in chicken, quail, and duck cells, and find that they are largely species-specific. Using this data, we performed a CRISPR knockout ISG screen against two strains of IAV, the mouse-adapted PR8, and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10. We find that for PR8, IFITM3 is the dominant restrictor of viral replication with several additional hits with modest effects, consistent with previous work in mammals. For avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit; however, there were two additional hits absent for PR8, the HSP70 co-chaperone protein BAG5 and the deubiquitinase OTUD4. Overall, these findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and establish a screening system that can be used to identify ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species.IMPORTANCEWild birds, especially waterfowl and shorebirds, are the primary natural reservoir for influenza A viruses. These birds can transmit IAV to domestic poultry, where the spillover risk to humans increases. Chickens are the most common species of domestic poultry worldwide and frequently infected with avian influenza viruses. Despite this, relatively little is known about how their immune system responds to influenza infection. This lack of knowledge creates a barrier to finding ways of preventing or mitigating IAV infection in chicken flocks. In this study, we characterized the interferon-induced immune response to IAV in chickens and found that only a small subset of ISGs were responsible for restricting IAV in chicken cells.

title: Galectin-3 links microglial neuroinflammation to Aβ aggregation and lysosomal processing
text: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the molecular mechanisms linking microglial dysfunction to amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify galectin-3 (Gal3) as a regulator of plaque-associated microglial responses, linking Aβ aggregation, lysosomal function, and neuritic pathology. Using postmortem brain tissue from AD patients, we found that Gal3 + microglia preferentially associate with cored plaques and correlate with increased LAMP1 + dystrophic neurites. Gal3 was also detected in microglial lysosomal compartments, extramicroglial dystrophic structures, and in association with extracellular amyloid fibrils, suggesting roles in both intracellular and extracellular Aβ processing. In APP mice, Gal3 deficiency reduced plaque burden and neuritic dystrophy, increased plaque compaction, and enhanced TREM2 coverage around amyloid plaques. Mechanistically, in vitro microglial experiments showed that Gal3 modulates Aβ uptake and lysosomal processing, whereas lysosomal dysfunction promoted the accumulation of fibrillar Aβ from initially monomeric species, particularly in Gal3-deficient cells. Cell-free assays demonstrated that Gal3 preferentially binds fibrillar Aβ, inhibits secondary nucleation, and alters fibril morphology, while Gal3-modified fibrillar Aβ reduces N2a neuronal cell number. Finally, in silico structural analyses identified candidate Gal3 interactors enriched in leucine-rich-repeat and immunoglobulin-like proteins, supporting a role for this lectin in immune receptor regulation. Complementary in vivo transcriptomic profiling showed that Gal3 deletion suppresses type I interferon and microglial neurodegenerative transcriptional signatures. Together, these findings position Gal3 at the interface between Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and plaque-associated microglial responses in AD.

title: Editorial: Community series in trends in neuroimmunology: cross-talk between brain-resident and peripheral immune cells in both health and disease, volume III
text: Brain-resident and peripheral immune cells respond to endogenous and external challenges and interact with other body systems to maintain a balanced internal environment, ensuring the physiological function of organs and tissues. This third volume of the Community Series in Trends in Neuroimmunology (1-4), explores the existence of different networks involving the immune system, such as the neuroimmune cardiovascular circuit, the brain-glycinergic signaling-blood axis, and the glia-neutrophil axis, focusing on their roles in maintaining body homeostasis and the relevance of their impairment in the pathogenesis of different disorders. Fifteen peer-reviewed manuscripts, including ten reviews, four original articles, and one Hypothesis and Theory, encompass this special volume. Ninety-four authors from research laboratories located in eight countries: China, Germany, Greece, India, Mexico, Spain, Sweden, and the United States, took part in this initiative. The articles delve into the interdependence between the immune system and brain health, exploring how immune cells regulate physiological functions such as adult neurogenesis and behavior, as well as neurodegenerative disorders and pathological conditions ranging from infections to autoimmune diseases. Among these works, the "Senescent Niche Hypothesis" stands out, by its proposal that the pathological accumulation of senescent microglia constitutes an epileptogenic focus for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Another article highlights the role of Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) as a novel modulator of immune cells in chronic inflammatory disorders. Other studies examine the role of brain and peripheral immunity and inflammation in specific conditions, such as coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMVD), perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), traumatic brain injury (TBI), and bacterial infections of the central nervous system (CNS). This compilation also explores diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic immune-based approaches, such as using glycine receptors (GlyRs) as novel peripheral indicators of neuroinflammation, peripheral T cell subsets to predict the severity of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a scoring system based on patient, clinical and laboratory data to differentiate viral encephalitis (VE) from autoimmune encephalitis (AE), or using CAR Tcell therapy to address autoimmune neurological diseases. Additionally, three articles cover new technologies and tools, ranging from single-cell omics approaches in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and organoid-microglia systems for studying neurological and retinal diseases to the use of Drosophila melanogaster to dissect the role of innate immunity in the causality of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). Ultimately, this Research Topic addresses the complex nature of neuroimmune interactions and how imbalances among their components can trigger or otherwise contribute to disease development. Moreover, the articles in this edition seek to transcend reductionist approaches by proposing the neuroimmune axis as an essential therapeutic target for preserving neuronal integrity and treating neurological conditions.Among the featured contributions, Sepúlveda-Cuéllar et al. provide an insightful review of the role of immune cells, via cytokine and chemokine signaling, in regulating neurogenesis in adult rodents and its resulting impact on memory and social behavior. Unlike most reviews, which focus on pathological contexts, this work highlights evidence from non-pathological conditions. The authors summarized recent in vitro and in vivo studies examining the influence of these mediators on neurogenesis in the subgranular zone of the hippocampus, the subventricular zone, and the olfactory bulb (5-7), as well as the associated cognitive and social behaviors. Microglia, which are resident brain immune cells, have been shown to modulate neurogenesis through trophic factors and cytokines. Additionally, peripheral brain immune cells

title: Glioblastoma–Neuroblastoma Cocultured Multicellular Spheroid Model for Evaluating Temozolomide Response
text: Glioblastoma is the most lethal primary brain tumor, and its resistance to therapy is increasingly understood to arise not from tumor cells alone but also from their integration into the surrounding neural circuitry. However, no existing preclinical spheroid model isolates the direct effect of neuronal-lineage cells on glioblastoma's drug response within a rapid, scalable 3D system. We developed a heterotypic 3D coculture spheroid combining glioblastoma (U87-MG) with a neuronal-lineage surrogate population (SH-SY5Y) via the agarose liquid overlay method to directly understand this gap. Subsequently, growth, morphology, hypoxia, and temozolomide (TMZ) response over 14 days against glioblastoma only and neuroblastoma only spheroids were characterized. The coculture adopted a glioblastoma like compact, chemoresistant architecture yet, contrary to what this architecture alone would predict, it showed measurable chemosensitivity at every TMZ concentration tested, including 10 µM, a dose at which neither monoculture responded at all. This indicates that the neuronal-lineage surrogate population alters the overall TMZ response of the coculture spheroids. Drug-response data from glioblastoma only models may therefore not reflect true tumor behavior in the presence of neuronal-lineage cells, supporting the inclusion of neuronal-lineage surrogate components in preclinical glioblastoma drug screening.

title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
text: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
text: Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Echidna: a Bayesian framework for integrative inference of copy number alterations impacting phenotypic plasticity
text: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms.

title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference
text: When meeting new individuals or known individuals in new circumstances, we intuitively map out their relationships-not merely through direct experience, but by inferring new connections on the basis of prior relational knowledge. How such relational knowledge is represented and used in the brain remains a long-standing question in cognitive neuroscience. Here, using a behavioural task and computational modelling, we show that participants (N = 36) leveraged existing knowledge of relational structures to infer new relationships, facilitating adaptation in changing environments. Whole-brain neuroimaging identified consistent representations of relational structure in the hippocampus. To investigate the causal link between hippocampal representations and inference, we used neural network simulations to predict the behavioural effects of disrupting such representations. Consistent with this prediction, transcranial ultrasound stimulation of the human hippocampus (N = 20), transiently modulating its activity, disrupted structure-based inference (P < 0.001, Cohen's d = -0.89, 95% confidence interval -1.41 to -0.36), providing empirical evidence for a causal role of hippocampus in relational-structure learning and structure-based inference.

title: A multi-omic, spatial, and whole-slide image dataset of lung neuroendocrine tumours
text: Lung neuroendocrine tumours (lung NETs) are rare neoplasms comprising approximately 2% of lung cancers. Recent studies have identified distinct molecular groups based on transcriptome and methylome data, but genomic and morphological features remain underexplored due to limited whole-genome and imaging data. We have generated a multi-omic dataset of lung NETs (201 participants, for a total of n = 294 tumours), including RNA sequencing, EPIC 850 K methylation arrays, and whole-genome sequencing. This multi-omic dataset also include multi-regional whole-genome sequencing for 41 participants, allowing for the quantification of intra-tumoural heterogeneity. We additionally generated spatial proteomics (67 participants), spatial transcriptomics (4 participants) and whole-slide histopathology images for 198 cases. This dataset enables a comprehensive characterization of lung NET molecular groups and the identification of group-specific morphological features using deep learning algorithms. All quality control analyses, processed data, and scripts are provided to ensure reproducibility. This dataset is available as a basis for further molecular and morphological analysis of lung NETs, and for future research on multi-scale integration.

title: Neuroimmune transcriptional signatures across repeat expansion ataxias in the human brain
text: Hereditary ataxias are neurodegenerative disorders characterised by progressive cerebellar dysfunction, most commonly caused by pathogenic repeat expansions of short tandem DNA repeats. Despite shared genetic mechanisms, the downstream molecular processes leading to neurodegeneration remain incompletely understood. RNA dysregulation has been proposed as a key contributor, but transcriptome-wide changes in human brain tissue across multiple ataxia subtypes have been poorly characterised. This study aims to identify shared and disease-specific transcriptional signatures across repeat expansion ataxias. We used bulk and single nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNAseq) to analyse post-mortem brain tissue from individuals with repeat expansion ataxias in order to gain further mechanistic insight into disease biology. We analysed paired cerebellar and frontal cortex RNA-sequencing data from post-mortem brain tissue obtained from 23 donors with ataxia and 22 age- and sex-matched controls across two brain banks (including spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA)1, SCA2, SCA6, Friedreich's ataxia (FRDA), and cases with unknown molecular diagnoses). Bulk and snRNAseq analyses were used to examine transcript usage, differential gene expression, and cell-type-specific transcriptional changes and biological pathways across disease groups. These analyses revealed extensive transcriptional alterations in ataxia cases, affecting not only the cerebellum but also the frontal cortex. Across genetic subtypes, immune and inflammatory pathways were consistently activated and were associated with transcriptional changes in non-neuronal cell populations, alongside downregulation of neuronal and synaptic processes in the cerebellum. These findings were supported by snRNAseq, which demonstrated that immune-related transcriptional changes were most prominent in non-neuronal cell populations, including microglia and astrocytes. This process was accompanied by neuronal loss and relative expansion of glial populations in the cerebellum. Shared transcriptional signatures were evident across both molecularly diagnosed and undiagnosed cases. Hereditary ataxias are associated with common activation of immune and inflammatory pathways across brain regions and genetic subtypes, with prominent involvement of non-neuronal cell types. These findings highlight immune signalling as a shared feature of disease biology and suggest that inflammatory pathways may represent potential targets for therapeutic intervention. This study provides a comprehensive transcriptomic framework for understanding mechanisms underlying repeat expansion ataxias in the human brain.

title: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
text: Abstract Background An important application of single-cell genomics experiments is to identify genes specific to biological categories or experimental conditions. We develop ember (Entropy Metrics for Biological ExploRation), an entropy-based framework that uses Shannon’s chain rule across nested biological partitions. Four axioms characterize its Ψ score within a class of normalized entropy-decomposition scores. Results Applying ember to eight tissues from eight founder mouse strains, we find that gene specificity is often unintuitive: canonical markers can be supplanted, housekeeping genes are context-dependent, and mouse strain can drive unexpected cell type switching. Unsupervised learning on entropy metrics uncovers shared genes specialized to male gonads and kidney, as well as genes specific to non-consecutive developmental stages in the kidney. To facilitate further exploration of gene specificity in mice, we have also developed a comprehensive specificity database, along with a web interface, API and MCP server. Extending ember to a human PBMC dataset collected from 255 diverse individuals, we find that variation in PBMCs is largely localized to classical monocytes. We also find genes with unique specificity by sex, age and ancestral background. Conclusions Together, these applications establish ember as a powerful tool and provide a roadmap for elucidating the impact of human genetic variation using the murine model.

title: Endosomal mRNA transport coordinates local mitochondrial bioenergetics during polar fungal growth
text: Mitochondrial function relies on the precise spatial coordination of protein synthesis and import. Most mitochondrial proteins are nuclear-encoded and must be supplied across varying intracellular distances. In highly polarized cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, active long-distance mRNA transport is thought to sustain distal mitochondrial function, but its mechanistic coupling to protein import and organelle physiology is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that endosomal transport of mRNAs encoding mitochondrial proteins orchestrates local bioenergetics in infectious hyphae of Ustilago maydis . Using the subunit Atp3 of electron transport chain Complex V as a model, we uncover that the endosomal mRNA transporter Rrm4 is required for efficient mitochondrial protein import, particularly at growth poles. Loss of Rrm4 leads to defects in mitochondrial import, resulting in altered physiology. We propose that endosome-coupled mRNA transport constitutes a fundamental layer of subcellular mitochondrial homeostasis, with implications extending from fungal pathogenicity to neuronal disease.

title: Co-option of lysosomal machinery for sponge biosilicification
text: Biomineralization has evolved repeatedly across animals, resulting in novel strategies for buoyancy, locomotion and defense. Sponges are the only metazoans that build silica-based skeletons, and the mechanisms underlying their biosilicification are relatively understudied compared with other major silicifiers. Here, we show that in freshwater sponges, cells specialized for biosilicification, termed sclerocytes, highly express lysosomal-associated genes, including subunits of the V-H+-ATPase (VHA) proton pump, oculocutaneous albinism type 2 (OCA2) anion channels, cathepsins, silicateins, TMEM55A/B, TMEM192, TMEM199, and other genes involved in lysosomal function. We demonstrate that VHA protein localizes to the sclerocyte and propose that VHA-dependent silica deposition vesicle acidification is likely essential for silica spicule formation. This function mirrors the role of VHA in diatom biosilicification and in biocalcification across a broad sweep of taxa. We also found that genes homologous to the gene encoding plant silicon efflux transporter Lsi2 are highly upregulated in sclerocytes, and confirmed their localization using hybridization chain reaction fluorescence in situ hybridization. These results corroborate phylogenetic and transcriptomic evidence that Lsi2 homologs are involved in sponge silicic acid transport. Data mining of previous studies revealed that many lysosomal-associated genes have been correlated with biomineralization across eukaryotes, including coccolithophores, bryozoans, crustaceans, mollusks and mammals. As detoxification was a likely driver for the evolution of biomineralization, we propose that lysosomal machinery aided in detoxification by allowing sponges to sequester Si in acidified compartments to prevent its catastrophic intracellular precipitation. This lysosomal toolkit was likely independently co-opted for the formation of biomineralized structures in multiple species.

title: Integrating multi-omics data and machine learning in single-step GBLUP reaction norm models to improve prediction across untested environments in lodgepole pine
text: The effectiveness of genomic prediction in forest trees is often constrained by genotype-by-environment (GE) interactions, particularly when predicting performance in environments not represented in the training population. We evaluated the integration of genomic, enviromic (climatic and soil), and metabolomic (targeted monoterpene) information within multi-environment single-step genomic best linear unbiased prediction (ssGBLUP) reaction norm models to improve prediction in unobserved environments. Models incorporated environmental covariates (W) and genotype-specific responses using linear and nonlinear kernels, including Gaussian and Arc-Cosine formulations. The study examined 12 traits measured on 11,124 trees across four lodgepole pine progeny trials, with 1,490 trees genotyped with 25,099 SNPs. Predictive performance was assessed using leave-one-environment-out cross-validation. Additive genetic correlations among environments revealed substantial GE for early-growth traits and drought-related decline, with correlations frequently below 0.65. Inclusion of environmental covariates reduced variance attributed to site effects, indicating that these descriptors captured environmental heterogeneity. Incorporating GE and genotype-by-environmental covariate (GW) interactions improved model performance, increasing explained phenotypic variance by up to 29.58% and reducing residual variance by up to 3.13% relative to baseline models. Across traits, GE explained more phenotypic variation than GW, contributing on average 2.31% and 0.60%, respectively. Predictive ability was high across models (0.688-0.701), with gains of up to 7.85% when nonlinear kernels were combined with metabolomic covariates, particularly for traits exhibiting stronger GE. Monoterpene profiles yielded predictive performance comparable to climate and soil descriptors, highlighting the potential of integrating genomic, enviromic, and metabolomic information to improve prediction across environments and support climate-resilient forest tree breeding and deployment.

title: A temporal atlas of TDP-43 interactions reveals persistent network remodelling beyond stress granule clearance
text: Cytoplasmic aggregation of the nuclear protein TDP-43 is associated with several neurodegenerative disorders and may be promoted by cellular stress. However, the dynamics of TDP-43 protein−protein interactions during stress and recovery remain poorly understood. Here, we combined APEX2 proximity labelling with quantitative mass spectrometry to generate a temporal atlas of wild-type TDP-43 and pathology-mimicking TDP-43dNLS and TDP-43CTF variants. Interactomes were profiled across steady state, oxidative stress, and recovery. We reveal extensive state- and variant-dependent remodelling of TDP-43 interaction networks, uncovering distinct temporal interaction patterns throughout the stress response and recovery. Notably, distinct TDP-43 interaction signatures persisted after stress granule clearance, suggesting a molecular memory of stress. Together, our study establishes a comprehensive temporal resource for investigating TDP-43 interaction dynamics and provides a framework for understanding how stress-induced network alterations may contribute to TDP-43 proteinopathies.

title: Agentic reinforcement learning empowers next-generation chemical language models for molecular design and synthesis
text: Abstract Language models are revolutionizing the biochemistry domain, assisting scientists in drug design and chemical synthesis with high efficiency. Yet current approaches struggle between small language models prone to hallucination and limited knowledge retention, and large cloud-based language models plagued by privacy risks and high inference costs. To bridge this gap, we introduce ChemCRAFT, a novel framework leveraging agentic reinforcement learning to decouple chemical reasoning from knowledge storage. Instead of forcing the model to memorize vast chemical data, our approach empowers the language model to interact with a sandbox for precise information retrieval. This externalization of knowledge allows a locally deployable small model to achieve superior performance while being highly token-efficient compared to traditional multi-agent systems. To enable small language models for agent-calling ability, we build an agentic trajectory construction pipeline and a comprehensive chemical-agent sandbox. Based on sandbox interactions, we constructed ChemToolDataset, the first large-scale chemical tool trajectory dataset. Simultaneously, we propose SMILES-GRPO to build a dense chemical reward function, promoting the model's ability to call chemical agents. Evaluations across diverse aspects of drug design show that ChemCRAFT outperforms current cloud-based LLMs in molecular structure analysis, molecular optimization, and synthesis pathway prediction, demonstrating that scientific reasoning is not solely an emergent ability of model scale, but a learnable policy of tool orchestration. Furthermore, assessments in real-world drug optimization scenarios, including fentanyl analog optimization and pro-inflammatory GSTO1 inhibitors optimization, reveal that ChemCRAFT generates optimization trajectories mirroring human experts, confirming its reliability as a scientific assistant. This work establishes a cost-effective and privacy-preserving paradigm for AI-aided chemistry, opening new avenues for accelerating molecular discovery with locally deployable agents.

title: Unifying biomedical knowledge in a modern multimodal graph
text: Abstract Biomedical knowledge graphs (KGs) are widely used in the life sciences, yet many are derived from unstructured documents and therefore lack schema-level constraints, whereas graphs assembled from structured resources are difficult to harmonize into a unified representation. We present O ptimus KG, a multimodal biomedical labeled property graph (LPG) built from structured and semi-structured resources to preserve factual, type-specific metadata across molecular, anatomical, clinical, and environmental domains. O ptimus KG contains 190,939 nodes across 10 entity types, 21,818,752 edges across 27 edge types, and 67,070,490 property instances encoding 109,665,797 values across 145 distinct property keys, derived from 18 ontologies and controlled vocabularies. The graph enforces a top-level schema for nodes and edges and retains granular, type-specific properties, cross-references, and provenance. We assessed the validity of O ptimus KG by evaluating whether graph relationships are supported by evidence from the scientific literature using a multimodal agent, PaperQA3. PaperQA3 identified supporting evidence for 70.0% of sampled edges, whereas 83.4% of sampled false edges received no supporting evidence. Edges without literature support were concentrated in associations derived from experimental and functional genomics resources, suggesting that O ptimus KG captures biomedical knowledge that may precede synthesis in the scientific literature. O ptimus KG is distributed as Apache Parquet files, providing a standardized resource for graph-based machine learning, knowledge-grounded retrieval with large language models, and biomedical discovery use cases such as hypothesis generation.

title: The complex landscape of multidrug resistance (MDR) in Zymoseptoria tritici: MFS1 promoter plasticity and beyond
text: Multidrug resistance (MDR) in fungal pathogens poses a growing threat to fungicide efficacy and sustainable agriculture. In the wheat pathogen Zymoseptoria tritici, MDR is primarily linked to overexpression of the MFS1 transporter gene, driven by transposable element (TE) insertions in its promoter or their remnants. Here, we provide an extensive analysis of MFS1 promoter polymorphism and its phenotypic impact on MDR across 374 field isolates collected in Europe between 2020 and 2021. We identified six novel structural variants derived from diverse TE types, confirming that the MFS1 promoter undergoes recurrent and independent insertion events. While previously characterized inserts consistently confer resistance, other variants show limited or variable phenotypic effects. Genetic crosses and quantitative phenotyping further revealed that MDR behaves as a quantitative trait and genome-wide association study confirmed MFS1 as the major resistance locus but also identified additional candidate genes involved in xenobiotic detoxification and membrane transport, supporting a polygenic basis for MDR. Our findings underpin the interplay between TE-driven structural variation and background polygenic architecture in shaping resistance phenotypes. In parallel, this study highlights the need to improve MDR monitoring beyond single-locus genotyping and to re-evaluate current resistance management strategies that may inadvertently select for broad-spectrum resistance.

title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
text: Abstract Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

title: Generative pseudo-force fields for molecular generation
text: Abstract Generating stable molecular conformations typically forces a tradeoff between the physical realism of energy-based relaxation and the sampling efficiency of data-driven generative models. While machine learning force fields (MLFFs) can sample stable conformations by relaxing molecular geometries according to physical forces, they require costly ab-initio training data. Conversely, diffusion models (DMs) learn from equilibrium data alone but are dependent on noise schedules and time-step conditioning. In this work, we propose generative pseudo-force fields (GPFFs) to bridge these paradigms by training an MLFF on a quadratic pseudo-potential energy surface relative to reference equilibrium structures. Because no ab-initio calculations are required for the perturbed geometries, non-equilibrium training data can be generated on the fly by perturbing the equilibria with Gaussian noise. We show that GPFFs constitute a time-step-agnostic variant of variance-exploding DMs: the score comes from the predicted pseudo-forces but because force magnitudes implicitly encode the noise level, no time-step conditioning is needed. Our GPFF can hence be used as a drop-in replacement in standard diffusion sampling (ancestral, Heun) but also facilitates more efficient, adaptive variants and an MLFF inspired direct denoising scheme. Our proposed sampling algorithms support arbitrary structural priors and geometric constraints. On QM9, GPFF reaches 99 % validity with stochastic direct denoising at 256 neural function evaluations (NFE), and about 90 % at just 16 NFE with direct denoising, outperforming a matched diffusion baseline that shares its backbone, training recipe, and noise schedule across all samplers. Combined with custom priors, we showcase the fast and accurate generation process of our method in a molecular editor for a drug design setting.

title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
text: Abstract Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis, and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological, and human health studies. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models─including both endogenous and synthetic molecules─to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% of target molecular volumes and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems, the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility of the OLIVES and Go̅Martini models makes them best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. Finally, models were validated in interaction with membranes by comparison to reference atomistic data. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

title: Ontology pre-training improves machine learning-based predictions for metabolites
text: Deep learning has recently led to multiple breakthroughs in longstanding biological problems. Recent advances have shown that integration of expert knowledge can improve deep learning model predictive performance in complex domains such as biology. Bio-ontologies offer a rich source of curated biological knowledge that can be harnessed to this end. Here, we describe an intuitive and generalisable approach to embed the knowledge contained in a classification hierarchy derived from a bio-ontology into a deep learning model as an intermediate training step between general-purpose pre-training and task-specific fine-tuning: a process that we call'ontology pre-training'. We show that this approach leads to an improvement in predictive performance and a reduction in training time for a broad range of prediction tasks related to metabolite functions, activities and properties in living systems, using a range of datasets derived from MoleculeNet. We see the biggest improvement for regression tasks, e.g., prediction of lipophilicity and aqueous solubility of molecules, and a robust improvement for most classification tasks. Our approach can be adapted for a wide range of knowledge sources, models and prediction tasks.

title: Inulin-bentonite hybrid microparticles enhance orlistat efficacy while mitigating gut microbiota disruption in a high-fat diet rat model
text: Orlistat is an established pharmacotherapy for metabolic syndrome (MetS); however, its clinical utility is constrained by gastrointestinal adverse effects and gut microbiota disruption. This study evaluates hybrid inulin (INU)-bentonite (BEN) microparticles (InuClay) as a microbiota-protective adjunct to orlistat therapy. In vitro lipolysis under biorelevant fasted-state conditions demonstrated that InuClay significantly reduced free fatty acid liberation relative to untreated controls and INU alone ( p < 0.01). In a 21-day high-fat diet rat model of MetS, InuClay and orlistat monotherapies reduced cumulative weight gain by 4.5% and 5.7%, respectively. Co-administration achieved a 7.7% reduction that was significantly greater than either monotherapy alone. Combination therapy also produced the greatest reduction in fasting blood glucose (27%) exceeding both InuClay monotherapy (12%) and orlistat monotherapy (16%). At the microbiota level InuClay co-administration prevented orlistat-induced Proteobacteria expansion (2.5-fold reduction versus orlistat alone) while selectively enriching butyrate-producing taxa including Lachnospiraceae (1.42-fold) and Blautia (11.8-fold) without significantly altering alpha diversity. Circulating markers of cellular injury were substantially lower with combination therapy, with lactate dehydrogenase decreased by 63% and aspartate aminotransferase by 23% versus controls. These reductions were absent with orlistat monotherapy. Collectively these findings establish InuClay as a dual-action adjunct that enhances orlistat efficacy while attenuating dysbiotic shifts and systemic markers of tissue stress. As a 21-day proof-of-concept study, this work is intended to establish the feasibility of InuClay hybrids as adjunct therapy for improving the metabolic outcomes of orlistat administration. These preliminary findings support InuClay as a promising strategy for improving translational outcomes in lipase inhibitor-based MetS management.

title: Inhibitors of Gut Bacterial l -Dopa Decarboxylation with Reduced Susceptibility to Host Metabolism
text: Microorganisms in the human gut influence the efficacy and metabolism of host-targeted small molecule therapeutics, including the frontline Parkinson's disease drug levodopa (l-dopa). Previous work has identified a mechanism-based inhibitor of gut bacterial decarboxylases that degrade l-dopa, α-fluoromethyltyrosine (AFMT). However, early experiments with AFMT in rodent models suggested undesirable in vivo metabolism by host tyrosine hydroxylase, producing α-fluoromethyldopa, a metabolite likely to worsen Parkinson's phenotypes and prevent application as an l-dopa cotreatment. Here, we demonstrate oxidation of AFMT to α-fluoromethyldopa in vitro by recombinant human tyrosine hydroxylase. We then develop AFMT analogues that retain activity against bacterial decarboxylases but have reduced susceptibility to host hydroxylation. Suitable arenes for inhibitor design were identified using assays with commercially available noncanonical amino acids, which revealed aryl difluorination as a promising modification. Difluoroaryl AFMT derivatives are less prone to degradation by tyrosine hydroxylase in vitro yet still inhibit l-dopa metabolism by bacterial decarboxylases. This work exemplifies how substrate reactivity can streamline design of mechanism-based enzyme inhibitors, as well as how constraints posed by the host can be incorporated during development of microbiome-targeted therapeutics. The compounds reported here are promising starting points for future studies in animal models and further exploration of gut bacterial effects on l-dopa treatment efficacy.

title: Tailored isolation and metabolomic profiling of extracellular vesicles in Manila clam (Ruditapes philippinarum) hemolymph and insights into water-derived vesicles
text: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are evolutionarily conserved mediators of intercellular communication released by cells into biological fluids and the environment. Despite their increasing relevance in biomedical and veterinary research, knowledge of EVs in marine bivalves remains limited. This study first aimed to optimize protocols for EV isolation from the hemolymph of Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) using density gradient ultracentrifugation (dgUC) or size exclusion chromatography (SEC). EV-enriched fractions were identified and characterized for nanoparticle size distribution by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), for protein concentration and imaged by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and cryo-EM. Small EVs (<200 nm) were successfully purified with both methods. While dgUC provided higher-purity preparations, SEC provided higher particle-yields and compatibility with metabolomic analyses. Metabolomics performed on SEC fractions and hemolymph revealed a distinct metabolic signature of EV-enriched fractions, characterized by metabolites associated with nucleotide metabolism, glycolysis, redox regulation, and energy metabolism. Secondly, in a separate pilot study, we investigated the presence of EVs in water conditioned by Manila clams. EVs were concentrated by tangential flow filtration and ultrafiltration and characterized by NTA, atomic force microscopy, TEM and by CONAN assay to assess their purity. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of EV-recovery from conditioned water but also the need for methodological refinement and appropriate controls to improve EV purity and distinguish EVs released from clams or from other organisms. Overall, these preliminary results establish a foundation for future investigations into the role of EVs in bivalve biology and their application as minimally invasive biomarkers for aquaculture and environmental monitoring.

title: Editorial: Community series in trends in neuroimmunology: cross-talk between brain-resident and peripheral immune cells in both health and disease, volume III
text: Brain-resident and peripheral immune cells respond to endogenous and external challenges and interact with other body systems to maintain a balanced internal environment, ensuring the physiological function of organs and tissues. This third volume of the Community Series in Trends in Neuroimmunology (1-4), explores the existence of different networks involving the immune system, such as the neuroimmune cardiovascular circuit, the brain-glycinergic signaling-blood axis, and the glia-neutrophil axis, focusing on their roles in maintaining body homeostasis and the relevance of their impairment in the pathogenesis of different disorders. Fifteen peer-reviewed manuscripts, including ten reviews, four original articles, and one Hypothesis and Theory, encompass this special volume. Ninety-four authors from research laboratories located in eight countries: China, Germany, Greece, India, Mexico, Spain, Sweden, and the United States, took part in this initiative. The articles delve into the interdependence between the immune system and brain health, exploring how immune cells regulate physiological functions such as adult neurogenesis and behavior, as well as neurodegenerative disorders and pathological conditions ranging from infections to autoimmune diseases. Among these works, the "Senescent Niche Hypothesis" stands out, by its proposal that the pathological accumulation of senescent microglia constitutes an epileptogenic focus for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Another article highlights the role of Nerve Growth Factor (NGF) as a novel modulator of immune cells in chronic inflammatory disorders. Other studies examine the role of brain and peripheral immunity and inflammation in specific conditions, such as coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMVD), perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), traumatic brain injury (TBI), and bacterial infections of the central nervous system (CNS). This compilation also explores diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic immune-based approaches, such as using glycine receptors (GlyRs) as novel peripheral indicators of neuroinflammation, peripheral T cell subsets to predict the severity of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a scoring system based on patient, clinical and laboratory data to differentiate viral encephalitis (VE) from autoimmune encephalitis (AE), or using CAR Tcell therapy to address autoimmune neurological diseases. Additionally, three articles cover new technologies and tools, ranging from single-cell omics approaches in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and organoid-microglia systems for studying neurological and retinal diseases to the use of Drosophila melanogaster to dissect the role of innate immunity in the causality of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). Ultimately, this Research Topic addresses the complex nature of neuroimmune interactions and how imbalances among their components can trigger or otherwise contribute to disease development. Moreover, the articles in this edition seek to transcend reductionist approaches by proposing the neuroimmune axis as an essential therapeutic target for preserving neuronal integrity and treating neurological conditions.Among the featured contributions, Sepúlveda-Cuéllar et al. provide an insightful review of the role of immune cells, via cytokine and chemokine signaling, in regulating neurogenesis in adult rodents and its resulting impact on memory and social behavior. Unlike most reviews, which focus on pathological contexts, this work highlights evidence from non-pathological conditions. The authors summarized recent in vitro and in vivo studies examining the influence of these mediators on neurogenesis in the subgranular zone of the hippocampus, the subventricular zone, and the olfactory bulb (5-7), as well as the associated cognitive and social behaviors. Microglia, which are resident brain immune cells, have been shown to modulate neurogenesis through trophic factors and cytokines. Additionally, peripheral brain immune cells

title: FPGA-Based Neural Network Accelerators for Space Missions: A Survey
text: Space missions are growing ever more ambitious, placing greater demands on onboard computing. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have garnered interest due to their reconfigurability and cost-effectiveness. At the same time, neural network (NN)-based methods are proving invaluable for critical spacecraft tasks such as autonomous operations, remote sensing, selective downlink, and data compression. This survey reviews and classifies the state-of-the-art in FPGA-based NN accelerators for space missions. We examine current trends, highlight key challenges, and suggest directions for future research. This work highlights key aspects for integrating high-performance NN acceleration into next-generation spacecraft computing systems.

title: A comprehensive review of fish feeding behavior analysis in aquaculture: tasks, techniques, and applications
Accelerating Iterative Data-Driven Hotspot Protein Engineering Using Annealed Oligos and Cell-Free Expression
text: Abstract Protein engineering increasingly leverages data-driven strategies to navigate complex fitness landscapes, but conventional high-throughput screening workflows mainly capture sequence-function data for only high-performing variants, producing limited datasets for learning. Recent approaches retaining full sequence-function information frequently rely on laborious cell-based cloning and expression or broad sequencing, which slows iterative design. This problem has been partly addressed through the rapid cell-free assembly and expression of predefined variants from gene fragments. However, gene fragments present limitations for hotspot engineering, where their size can prevent closely spaced mutations from being independently swapped, and the limited quantities typically supplied do not readily support multiple screening rounds. We extend this approach to hotspot engineering using short (∼20−40 bp) annealed oligo fragments to rapidly screen predefined variants in <9 h while preserving complete sequence-function data. Bulk-prepared oligos provide sufficient material for repeated screening rounds without cloning or amplification. Their small size also facilitates the independent swapping of hotspot mutations. This workflow is validated by screening 3 to 10 fragment assemblies for two proteins. Its utility for high-iteration protein engineering is demonstrated with an additive model-guided screening campaign, which identified variants with >100% increase in fitness.

title: Lane departure accident prevention in foggy conditions: A Prior-Guided Dynamic Feature Fusion Transformer framework for real-time lane detection
Markov Decision Process-based Real-time Navigation for Autonomous Aerial Vehicles Using Video
text: Abstract Autonomous aerial vehicle navigation is critical for applications ranging from search and rescue operations to warehouse automation, requiring real-time decision-making under severe computational and power constraints. While traditional geometric approaches using 3D point clouds provide accurate navigation, they impose prohibitive computational overhead for resource-constrained drones, and existing computer vision algorithms for semantic navigation create a fundamental performance bottleneck where static parameter configurations fail to adapt to varying environmental conditions. This paper addresses this gap through a novel Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework that dynamically optimizes object detection parameters based on input characteristics, intelligently selecting algorithm configurations from both feature-based (HoG/Edgeboxes with SVMs) and neural network (CNN) detection pipelines while utilizing classifier confidence scores as quality indicators. Comprehensive evaluation across KUL traffic sign datasets, custom BU-RU drone-collected footage, and hardware-in-the-loop AirSim simulations demonstrates significant performance improvements: 20-70% execution time reduction while maintaining 98-100% detection accuracy compared to static approaches, real-time 30fps processing at 480 $$\times $$ × 270 resolution, and up to 18 $$\times $$ × improvement in frame processing rates during closed-loop navigation tasks. These computational efficiency gains translate to substantial energy savings, achieving 6.9W power reduction on NVIDIA Jetson TX2 hardware through proportional decreases in processing time and computational load.

title: Learning Realistic Athletic Sprinting Without Demonstrations
text: We present a muscle-driven simulation system for generating biomechanically accurate motion for high-speed athletic locomotion tasks that does not require motion demonstrations. Our approach integrates state-of-the-art biomechanical athlete models into a new, high-performance GPU simulator capable of running at 1000 × real-time. High-throughput simulation enables large-batch reinforcement learning to train control policies that operate directly in the model’s high-dimensional muscle excitation space, and are guided only by task-specific episode termination conditions and a reward that encourages maximizing speed while reducing forces needed to respect joint limits. These policies train within a few hours on a single GPU and generate “near visually realistic” motions for complete athletic activities such as a full 100-meter sprint or performing popular athletic locomotion drills like side-shuffling, backpedaling, and carioca. The generated sprinting motions also exhibit strong agreement with experimental data captured from sprinters.

title: Distance Does Not Matter: The Role of Physical Robot Presence in Social HRI with Older Adults
text: Abstract As the global older population increases, more older adults need assistance in their daily lives. There is an increasing interest in using social robots to assist with everyday activities to promote overall wellbeing and health. However, whether and how social robot physical presence can influence human-robot interactions (HRI) with older adults has not yet been explored. In this paper, we present the first long-term HRI study conducted in a long-term care home that investigates the interaction behaviors of older adults during dance sessions facilitated by physically present and remotely present social human-like robots. Our results show that the older adults had similarly high levels of engagement and enjoyment during the interactions regardless of if the social robot was physically or remotely present. Although higher participation rates were observed in the in-person HRI, participation rates in the remote HRI were consistent to those in other non-robot facilitated physical activity interventions for older adults. Overall, this paper explores the role of robot presence and its impact on HRI, while providing insight into the potential use of remote HRI for providing social assistance to older adults.

title: POSNNET: Positioning Neural Network Estimation Tool
text: Many applications rely on IMU and GNSS data for localization, typically fused using algorithms such as the Kalman filter or its variants. Although this approach provides accurate localization without requiring additional infrastructure, its performance degrades in GNSS-denied environments. Deep learning methods have been proposed to address this issue in real time; however, because they do not leverage future data, they yield suboptimal reconstructions in applications that do not require real-time processing. To overcome this limitation, we introduce POSNNET, a post-processing framework designed to reconstruct position and velocity during prolonged periods of weak or absent GNSS signals. POSNNET is intended for localization scenarios in which real-time processing is not required, including sports performance analysis, infrastructure-free road mapping, and wildlife tracking, although its applicability across these domains requires further validation. The framework estimates velocity using state-of-the-art neural networks that leverage both past and future IMU and GNSS data. Position is subsequently recovered through weighted bidirectional integration. To improve reconstruction accuracy and consistency, the outputs of multiple neural networks are combined. POSNNET was validated offline against causal real-time baselines using simulated GNSS outages in a 100-h outdoor equestrian dataset characterized by higher speeds and more complex dynamics than typical pedestrian motion, with the sensor-fusion output serving as the reference trajectory. It achieved average trajectory errors, relative to this reference, of 4.07 m for simulated GNSS outages lasting from 30 s to 2 min and 7.06 m for outages lasting from 2 to 5 min, corresponding to an 93.4% (for outages lasting 30 s to 2 min) and 95.6% (for outages lasting 2 to 5 min) improvement in accuracy over the strongest evaluated real-time state-of-the-art method.

title: Body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated walking cost in cerebral palsy
text: Abstract Background Children with cerebral palsy (CP) exhibit substantially elevated energetic costs of walking, yet the biomechanical origins of this excessive cost remain unclear, limiting the effectiveness of current interventions. Methods We tested whether reducing the mechanical demands of body-weight support or mediolateral stabilization produced different energetic responses between children with CP and typically developing (TD) peers. Using a custom mechatronic system, we independently applied controlled vertical body-weight support (1–60% body weight) and mediolateral stabilization stiffness (50–1500 N/m) while children with CP and TD peers walked on a treadmill at a fixed nondimensional speed. We quantified steady-state energetic cost using indirect calorimetry and used linear regression models to determine energetic responses to each intervention. Results Providing body-weight support significantly reduced net energetic cost in both groups, with a 3.5-fold greater effect in the CP group ( n = 23) compared to TD peers ( n = 10). Across the 1–60% support range, energetic cost decreased by 41% in CP to a level not significantly different than TD participants. Higher baseline energetic cost and greater knee flexion stabilization produced negligible energetic effects in both CP (n=14) and TD groups, with negligible differences in energetic response between groups. Conclusions Energetic cost associated with body-weight support is the dominant contributor to elevated energetic cost of walking in children with CP, whereas mediolateral stabilization contributes minimally under the conditions tested. These findings identify gravitational support as a key biomechanical target for energy-focused rehabilitation and assistive technology interventions.

title: Coherence transfer in quantum networks
text: Detecting coherence transfer in complex quantum networks is challenging under uncharacterized experimental conditions and with limited access to the system. Here, we use the coexistence of static and dynamic coherence to derive a nonlinear criterion for coherence transfer. The criterion applies even when the verification capabilities of checkpoint nodes are uncharacterized. It requires only minimal one-network output analysis, up to the number of output state dimensions. Each output requires only two-setting measurements of state populations, regardless of the network size. The criterion is general for both spatial and temporal networks, including those with multiple coherence sources, and applies to quantum transport in solid-state nanostructures. Experimentally, using entanglement swapping, we transfer polarization-entangled pairs in four- and six-photon entanglement networks. The criterion provides experimental evidence of coherence transfer in multiphoton entanglement networks. Our findings provide a practical tool for investigating the presence, role, or function of coherence transfer in quantum networks.

title: A comprehensive review of fish feeding behavior analysis in aquaculture: tasks, techniques, and applications
Physiology-Informed Digital Twin-AI Framework Guides Interpretation of Heterogeneous Pacing Therapy Response in HFpEF
text: Abstract Background Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) exhibits marked heterogeneity in response to pacing. Because diastolic relaxation is energy dependent and impaired myocardial energetics are common in HFpEF, we hypothesized that favorable response to accelerated atrial pacing would be defined not only by hemodynamic unloading but also by preserved or improved cardiac efficiency (CE). Methods Patient-specific digital twins of 146 HFpEF patients were used to train a variational autoencoder that generated a virtual population (n ≈ 25,000), in which simulations quantified pacing-induced changes in left atrial pressure (LAP), systolic blood pressure (SBP), cardiac output (CO), and CE, defining four response phenotypes. Classifiers predicting these phenotypes from baseline clinical variables were trained in the virtual cohort and applied to myPACE, where treatment × predicted-response interactions with trial outcomes were evaluated in exploratory analyses. Results Across the virtual population, most patients exhibited reduced LAP (95.6%) and increased CO (93.8%), whereas only 36.1% improved CE. In myPACE, the predicted SBP-reduction phenotype showed a significant treatment × predicted-response interaction for NT-proBNP (p = 0.015). In the pacing arm, the predicted SBP-reduction and CE-improving phenotypes were associated with greater quality-of-life improvement, without a significant treatment interaction. Conclusions A physiology-informed digital twin-AI framework identified a predicted SBP-reduction phenotype associated with differential NT-proBNP response to accelerated pacing in HFpEF. Simulated CE provides a candidate mechanistic explanation for this signal. When routine clinical data are insufficient to identify digital twins, AI trained on twin simulations offers a potentially generalizable route for bringing mechanistic models to such data.

title: A bio-digital circular framework for sustainable duck feed production using agro-industrial side-streams and aquatic biomass
text: Abstract The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIREEM framework, a bio-digital circular approach for the valorization of Snack Food Industry By-products (SFIB) and aquatic biomass ( Azolla pinnata and Spirulina platensis ) in poultry feed production. The framework integrates IoT-assisted process monitoring, computational feed optimization, machine-learning prediction, and circular resource-utilization principles. An IoT-assisted pelleting system incorporating a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and real-time sensors was used to monitor and control processing conditions, while a Python-based Least-Cost Ration (LCR) model optimized feed formulations under predefined nutritional and economic constraints. Under the simulated conditions, the optimized formulation reduced the estimated feed production cost from approximately 22,000 to 12,450 EGP ton⁻¹ (43.4%) and reduced logistics-related CO₂ emissions by 93.8% within the defined assessment boundary. Machine-learning models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with Gradient Boosting providing the best prediction of body weight and Extra-Trees providing the best prediction of feed conversion ratio among the evaluated models.
