Feature-importance analysis indicated that age and metabolizable energy were major predictors of growth-related performance, whereas Azolla inclusion showed a greater contribution to feed conversion ratio than to body weight prediction. In addition, 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation indicated that the economic performance of the optimized system remained feasible across the majority of the simulated uncertainty scenarios, with SFIB cost and transportation expenditure identified as important cost drivers. Overall, the results support the potential of SHIREEM as an integrated computational framework for circular feed-resource utilization and localized production. However, the findings represent a computational proof-of-concept and require experimental and commercial-scale validation before biological, environmental, and economic performance can be generalized to practical poultry production systems. To support regional adoption, agricultural policymakers could consider developing appropriate quality-certification frameworks for bio-based feed resources and supportive policy mechanisms that facilitate the responsible upcycling of locally available agro-industrial residues into animal feed.

title: Literature review of wildlife disease surveillance capacity in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations region: status, gaps, and recommendations for national and regional strengthening
text: Southeast Asia is a globally recognized hotspot for emerging infectious diseases, yet wildlife disease surveillance (WDS) across the region remains fragmented, under-resourced, and poorly characterized. This review used domains adapted from a Needs Assessment Tool (NAT) for national wildlife health programs as an organizing framework to synthesize evidence from peer-reviewed literature, World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) country profiles and surveillance surveys, and regional network reports to analyze WDS capacity in the ASEAN region. Findings show predominant reliance on passive, outbreak-driven surveillance; fragmented legal and governance mandates; limited wildlife-specific laboratory capacity; non-interoperable digital data systems; and dependence on externally funded, time-limited projects for sustained surveillance activity, alongside promising innovations, including digital field data tools, ranger- and community-based networks, and multisectoral One Health platforms, in several countries. The review highlighted wide heterogeneity within the region, from highly institutionalized systems to near-absent or limited documented infrastructure. Regional mechanisms, including the ASEAN One Health Network, the South-East Asia Wildlife Health Network, and WildHealthNet, provide a foundation for coordination, but gaps in systematic surveillance, data sharing, and sustained financing remain. The review concludes with a set of specific recommendations for national and regional strengthening, tied directly to existing frameworks, tools, and platforms already operating in the region.

title: Data-Intensive and Ai-Mediated Anticipatory Governance: A Functional Typology of Institutional Capacity, Decision-Making, and Governance of Expertise
text: Abstract Anticipatory Governance (AG) has emerged as a strategic approach for addressing uncertainty, systemic risk, and complexity in contemporary socio-technical systems. Governments and universities increasingly rely on Big Data, Data Science, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support future-oriented public decision-making, yet the institutional and societal implications of these technologies remain conceptually fragmented. This article addresses this gap through a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) that examines how data-intensive and AI-enabled capabilities become embedded across foresight, knowledge creation, policy design, and policy assessment. Rather than treating the generic technical differences among Big Data, Data Science, and AI as the principal contribution, the study develops a functional typology that distinguishes infrastructural observation and evidentiary integration, analytical modeling and interpretation, and AI-enabled decision mediation. The review analyzes how these functions respond to uncertainty, non-linearity, interdependence, and feedback; reshape informational, analytical, and decisional capacity; and redistribute epistemic and decisional authority. The findings indicate a cumulative but non-deterministic movement from expanded observability, to analytical structuring, to increasingly mediated action. We conceptualize this movement as decisional embedding: the degree to which technological systems enter the institutional production of alternatives, prioritization, recommendation, adjustment, or execution. The contribution lies in showing that technological integration in anticipatory governance is not merely an increase in computational capability, but a reconfiguration of knowledge, judgment, responsibility, and authority. The article concludes with implications for accountable, contestable, and human-governed hybrid decision architectures.

title: Sensor-wide association studies: a methodological architecture for developing and evaluating functional human traits
text: Background Wearable and other digital sensors enable longitudinal observation of physiology and behaviour. However, reproducible associations and predictive performance do not establish which physiological construct a sensor-derived representation measures. An explicit framework is needed to distinguish statistical representation, construct interpretation and mechanistic explanation. Objective This Hypothesis and Theory article proposes Functional Human Traits (FHTs) and Sensor-Wide Association Studies (SWAS) as a conceptual and methodological architecture for developing and evaluating individual-level representations of physiological response capacities. Conceptual framework An FHT is defined as a quantitative representation of a specified physiological response capacity, supported by temporal repeatability over a justified interval and independent biological evidence under stated conditions. SWAS links documented sensor features, exploratory analysis, candidate construction and independent evaluation. Outcome-guided screening estimates feature–outcome associations, whereas unsupervised analysis identifies statistical structure; neither directly identifies a physiological construct. Candidate construction requires an explicit measurement model, individual-level estimation with uncertainty and tests addressing competing interpretations. Evaluation distinguishes statistical replication, technical robustness, temporal repeatability and biological support. A hypothetical cardiovascular heat-response example illustrates candidate construction using a longitudinal model. Environmental sensing and semantic integration are optional supporting components where relevant to the research question. Implications SWAS integrates established association-study and sensor-based measurement principles around explicit FHT identification requirements. Biological support does not establish a causal mechanism or clinical usefulness; digital biomarker applications require separate validation for their intended use. The feasibility and added value of FHT/SWAS remain to be demonstrated empirically.

title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery
text: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

title: Individual differences in infants’ early home music environment are associated with later expressive vocabulary development outcomes
text: Informal music experiences and engagement (e.g., parent-child singing activities) are common in infancy and early childhood. However, the specific role of the early home music environment in fostering infants' development remains understudied. Recent theories and empirical evidence demonstrate shared biology between music and language processing, as well as overlapping acoustic characteristics of speech and song. Emerging yet limited work has established positive links between infants' early home music environments and their later receptive vocabulary development. Here, we assessed whether infants' home music environment is a significant unique predictor of infants' expressive vocabulary development, an established early marker of children's language outcomes. In this longitudinal study, 42 parents completed the Music@Home questionnaire to capture their 6-12 month old infants' home music environments. Parents subsequently completed the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventory when their infants were 18- and 24-months of age as a measure of their infants' expressive vocabulary development. Generalized linear mixed-effects modeling revealed that infants' general home music environment and the amount parents sing to their infants at 6-12 months significantly predicted their infants' 18- and 24-month expressive vocabulary outcomes, even when accounting for other parental factors (parents' musicality, education levels, parental verbal responsivity, and parents' affective attachment). The model including parent singing demonstrated better fit than the model including the general home music environment. These findings highlight the importance of rich home musical activities, especially parent singing, as a correlate and potential facilitator of early vocabulary development. Findings also motivate further research on how enriched home music environments may serve as a potential protective factor for children at risk for developmental speech/language disorders.

title: Hierarchical data-driven dynamical surrogate models of social decision-making
text: Social decision making is inherently complex, shaped by dynamic trust building, biases, and adaptive strategies. Yet in laboratory settings, its study is often constrained by small datasets that nonetheless encode rich and sophisticated cognitive processes. This scarcity has historically limited modeling approaches to hand-tailored frameworks that embed strong priors about the underlying mechanisms. Recent advances in data-driven modeling of latent dynamical processes provide an alternative, extracting generative models directly from behavioral data without restrictive assumptions. Building on these methods, we derive hierarchical digital surrogates from sparse, non-Gaussian investment sequences in repeated trust games. Our approach proceeds in three stages. First, we demonstrate that, despite the limited data, the inferred models can accurately predict future investments and outperform theory-driven reinforcement-learning and Bayesian cognitive models, establishing predictive validity and providing a solid baseline for subsequent mechanistic analyses. Second, we analyze the latent dynamics of these models and show that they capture mechanistic structure in how investments and choice uncertainty are organized in state space and how social versus non-social cues are represented, in a way that parallels patterns observed directly in the empirical behavior. Third, we exploit the generative nature of the hierarchical digital surrogates to run in-silico experiments beyond the original data, such as probing how specific cues steer participants into trusting or mistrusting states and simulating responses to novel, unobserved cue-outcome combinations and trustee strategies. Together, this work demonstrates how generative digital surrogates open a new path toward mechanistic, data-driven accounts of social interaction dynamics that both reproduce observed behavior and support hypothesis generation in virtual environments.

title: Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer
text: Routine laboratory panels drawn during cancer treatment constitute longitudinal physiological recordings of organ function, yet their temporal structure is discarded by single-timepoint prognostic tools. A transformer trained on 2,777,595 laboratory measurements from 3905 patients with multiple myeloma or ovarian cancer predicted which of 162 treatment-associated complications would be newly recorded within two years, spanning eight clinical categories, achieving 1.5- to 6.1-fold enrichment above prevalence. Across individual endpoints it exceeded non-sequential baselines, including engineered-trajectory models, by +0.024 to +0.070 in mean AUROC. Predictions generalised across both cancers, divergence concentrating in disease-specific complications, and biomarker masking recovered signatures consistent with established pathophysiology. External validation on MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass showed transferability, strongest for renal and metabolic endpoints, attenuated for infection endpoints. On CoMMpass it added prognostic value to ISS staging. Routine oncological laboratory data carry complication-specific physiological signal months before a complication is recorded, and require no testing beyond standard oncological care.

title: MolEvolvR: A web-app for characterizing proteins using molecular evolution and phylogeny
text: Studying proteins through the lens of evolution can reveal features such as conserved domains, lineage-specific variants, and co-occurring domain architectures in phylogenetic context across all superkingdoms. MolEvolvR enables researchers to conduct such evolution-focused studies to generate testable hypotheses about protein function and evolution. MolEvolvR is a novel web-app allowing researchers to visualize the molecular evolution of their proteins of interest in a phylogenetic context across the tree of life. It accepts multiple input formats - protein/domain sequences, homologous proteins, or domain scans - and, using a general-purpose computational workflow, returns detailed homolog data and dynamic graphical summaries (e.g., phylogenetic trees, multiple sequence alignments, domain architectures, domain proximity networks, phyletic spreads, co-occurrence patterns across lineages). MolEvolvR performs domain-centric searches to capture remote homologs that are missed by full-length searches, integrates domain architecture evolution with phyletic distribution analyses, and provides evolutionary context visualizations that reveal lineage-specific adaptations versus those that are broadly conserved. Thus, MolEvolvR is a powerful, easy-to-use web interface for computational protein characterization spanning all superkingdoms. The web-app can be accessed here: https://jravilab.org/molevolvr.

title: Regularized ensemble polygenic risk prediction with GWAS summary statistics
A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
text: Abstract Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/ . They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
text: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

title: A multi-omic, spatial, and whole-slide image dataset of lung neuroendocrine tumours
text: Lung neuroendocrine tumours (lung NETs) are rare neoplasms comprising approximately 2% of lung cancers. Recent studies have identified distinct molecular groups based on transcriptome and methylome data, but genomic and morphological features remain underexplored due to limited whole-genome and imaging data. We have generated a multi-omic dataset of lung NETs (201 participants, for a total of n = 294 tumours), including RNA sequencing, EPIC 850 K methylation arrays, and whole-genome sequencing. This multi-omic dataset also include multi-regional whole-genome sequencing for 41 participants, allowing for the quantification of intra-tumoural heterogeneity. We additionally generated spatial proteomics (67 participants), spatial transcriptomics (4 participants) and whole-slide histopathology images for 198 cases. This dataset enables a comprehensive characterization of lung NET molecular groups and the identification of group-specific morphological features using deep learning algorithms. All quality control analyses, processed data, and scripts are provided to ensure reproducibility. This dataset is available as a basis for further molecular and morphological analysis of lung NETs, and for future research on multi-scale integration.

title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
text: Abstract Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis, and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological, and human health studies. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models─including both endogenous and synthetic molecules─to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% of target molecular volumes and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems, the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility of the OLIVES and Go̅Martini models makes them best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. Finally, models were validated in interaction with membranes by comparison to reference atomistic data. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

title: Emergence of epistatic fitness landscapes from parallel adaptive walks in breeding network metapopulations
text: Abstract Global networks of crop breeding programs leverage diverse germplasm, but diversity increases the complexity of maintaining stability in their elite gene pools. To characterize genetic heterogeneity in breeding metapopulations and develop insights on how to manage it, we simulated the evolution of breeding populations in the context of fitness landscapes. We revealed the geometric decrease in the average effect size of alleles segregating as standing variation that become fixed along an adaptive walk. We also demonstrated how independent adaptive walks of subpopulations were influenced by genetic drift, leading to cryptic genetic heterogeneity among elite gene pools. This variation was released when elite lines derived from independent subpopulations were crossed, leading to segregation for 2 - 4x more major QTL in admixed families as in unadmixed families, and 2 - 4x more epistatic interactions. We developed an “isoeliteness” metric to infer genetic compatibility between breeding lines, which was strongly correlated with transgressive segregation for fitness in admixed families. The emergent property of fitness epistasis for additive traits under stabilizing selection is well-understood in evolutionary genetics, but under-appreciated in crop quantitative genetics. Our findings suggest that in breeding networks, germplasm exchange strategies should incorporate measures of isoeliteness between breeding lines to mitigate emergent fitness epistasis in oligogenic locally-adapted traits.

title: From APT to APBT: a taxonomy and large-scale metadata exposure audit of genomic surveillance infrastructure
text: Introduction Open genomic repositories are critical infrastructure for pathogen surveillance, variant tracking, outbreak reconstruction, and public health decision making, yet many were designed primarily for rapid scientific data sharing rather than adversarial verification. In cybersecurity, Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) describe long duration, strategically coordinated campaigns against digital systems. This paper extends that logic to genomic surveillance by introducing Advanced Persistent Biological Threats (APBTs): persistent cyber biological campaigns in which malicious actors target sequence data, metadata, reference datasets, and analytical models to degrade surveillance reliability over time. We present, to our knowledge, the first integrated multilayer taxonomy of APBTs, structured around a four phase lifecycle, and examine whether metadata conditions relevant to this threat model are present in an operational genomic repository ecosystem. Methods We audited 100,000 SARS-CoV-2 NCBI BioSample records using 23 checks across five metadata layers: temporal, geographic, host and specimen, provenance and administrative, and technical and analytical. Where selected provenance or technical information was unavailable in BioSample, linked BioProject, SRA, and Nucleotide/GenBank resources were examined before an exposure indicator was assigned. Results Every record triggered at least one APBT relevant metadata exposure indicator. The mean composite exposure score was 5.22 (SD = 2.37), and 51.5% of records were classified as High or Critical. Exposure affected 3.8% of records in the temporal layer, 0.5% in the geographic layer, 52.0% in host and specimen metadata, 74.2% in provenance and administrative metadata, and 100.0% in technical and analytical metadata. Cross repository retrieval recovered substantial information not visible in BioSample alone, particularly for BioProject association, sequence linkage, sequencing platform, and assembly method. Information on who collected the sample was absent from 51.3% of records, while BioProject association remained unavailable for 28.8% after linked NCBI resources were examined. Discussion The findings do not demonstrate deliberate metadata poisoning. However, the structural incompleteness of BioSample metadata creates vulnerabilities that an adversary can exploit to introduce poisoned, misleading, or weakly traceable metadata into genomic repositories. As a result, maliciously altered metadata can appear plausible, remain undetected, and influence downstream genomic analysis and surveillance.

title: Dynamic Graph and Multi-Stage Mamba Fusion for Multimodal Survival Prediction
text: Abstract Multimodal survival prediction using whole-slide images (WSIs) and genomic profiles is important for cancer prognosis; however, integrating gigapixel histopathology with high-dimensional molecular data remains challenging. Existing methods often rely on dense or fixed fusion strategies that may introduce redundant interactions and inadequately capture patient-specific pathology--molecular associations. We propose a sample-adaptive WSI-omics framework that constructs sparse pathway--patch interactions and combines graph-based refinement with selective state-space aggregation for patient-level survival prediction. The framework was evaluated on five TCGA cohorts using patient-level 5-fold cross-validation. Compared with SurvPath, the proposed method improved the average C-index from 0.609 to 0.638, corresponding to an absolute gain of 0.029. The improvement reached significance only in BLCA under the paired \((t)\)-test, indicating cohort-dependent statistical support. Matched profiling showed lower memory consumption than the Transformer replacement, while case-level visualizations provided model-derived pathway--patch associations. These results support sample-adaptive sparse interaction modeling for WSI-omics survival prediction. External validation, repeated-seed evaluation, and pathologist-guided interpretation remain necessary before clinical application.

title: Wolbachia dominance and host-form-consistent geographic structuring of the Culex pipiens complex microbiome across the Republic of Korea
text: Mosquito microbiomes are shaped by host genetic background and by the environment, but separating the two in wild populations is difficult, particularly when a single endosymbiont dominates the sequenced community. We present the first nationwide, complex-specific survey of the Culex pipiens complex microbiome in the Republic of Korea: 16S rRNA gene (V3–V4) amplicon sequencing of 29 pools of the two Korean host forms, Cx. pipiens pallens (cpp) and Cx. pipiens form molestus (cpm), collected between 1 and 15 August 2022 from 23 sites in 22 surveillance regions. Wolbachia accounted for 45.1% of the bacterial community on average (up to 94.7% in individual pools) and set the first axis of abundance-weighted ordinations. Beneath this dominance, mosquitoes from Jeju Island and from the mainland harbored distinct bacterial communities, differing in composition, phylogenetic diversity and evenness. This island–mainland contrast was detected by log-ratio (Aitchison) and presence/absence distances with or without Wolbachia in the data, became clearer in abundance-weighted distances once Wolbachia abundance was accounted for, was consistent across both host forms, and was robust to pool size, geographic coordinates and the removal of 114 genera of potential reagent or vertebrate origin. In contrast, the two host forms, despite marked differences in blood-host preference, autogeny and diapause, showed no detectable compositional difference in four of five distance metrics, with only a modest difference in which lineages were present. Wolbachia dominance depressed the apparent evenness of the remaining community without reducing its richness. Because host form and region were partly confounded and no negative controls were sequenced, the form comparison and the status of low-abundance taxa remain provisional, whereas the geographic contrast does not depend on either. These results show that the Cx. pipiens complex microbiome in Korea is structured more by geography than by host form, and that a dominant endosymbiont can obscure biogeographic structure in abundance-weighted analyses, which log-ratio, presence/absence and covariate-adjusted analyses recover. Sequence data are available under NCBI BioProject PRJNA1479552.

title: Comparative genomics of Xanthomonas euvesicatoria strains from pepper and rose in the Mekong Delta, Vietnam
text: Bacterial spot caused by Xanthomonas euvesicatoria is a serious threat to crop production. This study isolated and characterized two X. euvesicatoria strains, XP10 from pepper and XR13 from rose, collected in the Mekong Delta, Vietnam, using pathogenicity assays and whole-genome analysis to investigate their virulence potential, genetic diversity, secretion systems, and CAZyme repertoires. Both strains induced typical leaf spot symptoms and cross-infected pepper, tomato, and rose, indicating their ability to infect hosts across the Solanaceae and Rosaceae. In addition, in vitro biochemical assays detected no pectolytic activity in either strain. Amylolytic and proteolytic activities were detected only in XR13 and were absent in XP10, whereas lipolytic and cellulolytic activities were detected in both strains. Meanwhile, whole-genome sequencing, ANI values above 98%, and core-genome phylogenomic analysis confirmed the assignment of both strains to X. euvesicatoria . However, these analyses also revealed that XP10 and XR13 belong to distinct intraspecific lineages, with XP10 clustering with X. euvesicatoria pv. euvesicatoria , whereas XR13 represents a distinct X. euvesicatoria lineage with the closest affinity to X. euvesicatoria pv. rosa . Pangenome analysis identified a large conserved core of 3,791 gene families, while accessory gene fractions were enriched in functions related to secretion, cell-envelope biogenesis, defense, and regulation or stress response. Furthermore, genes associated with secretion and motility ranged from 175 in XP10 to 191 in XR13 and encompassed major secretion and motility systems. The presence of T4bP- and plasmid-encoded pT4SSi-associated genes, with an enhanced T1SS in XR13, suggests potential for adhesion and competitive fitness, whereas pT4SSt in XP10 may support horizontal gene transfer. Notably, CAZyme repertoires were similar in size but functionally divergent, and frameshift-driven pseudogenization of an alpha-amylase gene and a PF13688 metalloprotease gene in XP10 may account for its non-amylolytic, non-proteolytic phenotype. Overall, X. euvesicatoria strains from pepper and rose in Vietnam share a conserved virulence backbone yet display fine-scale functional diversification, highlighting the value of genome-informed, multi-host disease management in mixed-cropping systems.

title: Large haploblocks underlie rapid, repeatable adaptation during evolutionary rescue
text: Evolutionary rescue can prevent population extinction following abrupt environmental change, but the genetic architectures that enable rapid adaptation under simultaneous strong selection and severe demographic bottlenecks remain poorly resolved. In particular, rescue may rely on either dispersed adaptive variants or clusters of tightly linked alleles that can respond to selection despite strong drift. We investigated the genetic architecture of evolutionary rescue in Callosobruchus maculatus , the cowpea seed beetle, following a shift to lentil, a novel and stressful host. To do so, we combined experimental evolution, whole-genome sequencing, backcross introgression, early-generation genomic sampling, association mapping, and transcriptomics. Initial adaptation produced widespread genomic differentiation, but backcrossing localized evidence for adaptive variation primarily to large regions on chromosomes 1 and 9. These regions contained large haploblocks with patterns consistent with suppressed recombination, possibly due to structural variation. On chromosome 9, a rare haplotype increased from approximately 0.5% to 48% in a single generation in one genetic background, consistent with extremely strong selection ( s ≈ 0.9995). On chromosome 1, a 14 Mb haploblock contained nearly all genetic variation for two fitness-related traits and was associated with differential gene expression. Across genetic backgrounds, chromosome 1 was repeatedly implicated in adaptation, whereas lines from one source population additionally involved chromosome 9. Together, these results show that evolutionary rescue can rely on large, non-recombining haploblocks, providing a mechanism by which clustered genetic architectures can respond rapidly and repeatably despite severe population bottlenecks.

title: Machine learning for host-pathogen protein-protein interaction prediction: A tutorial paper
text: The study of Host-Pathogen Protein-Protein Interactions (HP-PPIs) is critical for understanding mechanisms of infectious disease and for the development of therapeutic interventions. Computational prediction of HP-PPIs has become essential due to the limitations of experimental approaches, which are labour-intensive and expensive. In this tutorial, we present a step-by-step machine learning pipeline for HP-PPI prediction implemented in Google Colab. The workflow consists of six stages implemented in six Google Colab notebooks: dataset preparation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, machine learning model training, hyperparameter tuning and validation and model deployment. Six widely used classifiers, including LightGBM, Multi-layer Perceptron, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were evaluated using balanced and imbalanced datasets from human-bacteria protein interactions. Amino acid composition was evaluated as a standalone feature descriptor, while pseudo amino acid and conjoint triad descriptors were concatenated into a second feature set. Among the classifiers, LightGBM achieved the highest mean cross-validation performance Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and was subsequently selected for evaluation on an independent test set. Leave-One-Pathogen-Out validation was additionally performed to assess the ability of the selected model to generalise to unseen bacterial pathogens. This tutorial provides a reproducible and adaptable framework for HP-PPI prediction that can be extended to other pathogen systems. It is beginner-friendly and provides a starting point for researchers with limited computational backgrounds exploring the research domain of infectious disease biology.

title: Joint single-cell capture of Cas9 edits and transcriptomes reveals on- and off-target effects on gene expression
text: A longstanding barrier in genome engineering with CRISPR-Cas9 has been the inability to measure editing outcomes and their functional effects at single-cell resolution. Here we present Superb-seq, which captures single-cell edits and transcriptome effects by integrating Cas9 editing, T7 in situ transcription and single-cell RNA sequencing. We performed Superb-seq on 35,000 cells from three cell lines. Using seven guide RNAs to target four chromatin remodeler genes in 10,000 K562 cells, Superb-seq detected 5,761 edited cells, all on-target sites and 36 off-target sites. Superb-seq improved estimation of downstream perturbation effects on gene expression compared to Perturb-seq. We compared Superb-seq to 4 bulk off-target detection methods and identified between 6 and 210 edit sites across 3 benchmarking guides. Nineteen off-target edits were associated with differential gene expression, nine of which were cell type-specific. In summary, Superb-seq illuminates the consequences of Cas9 genome editing by connecting single-cell edits with changes in gene expression.

title: Identification of translation events that drive nonsense-mediated mRNA decay reveals functional roles for alternative RNA isoforms
text: Abstract The nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) pathway targets mRNAs undergoing premature translation termination for degradation. Previously, RNA-seq of yeast lacking NMD revealed that most genes targeted by NMD lack obvious premature termination codons (PTCs). We develop a combined approach using RNA-seq and 40S ribosome profiling to identify cryptic premature termination events that could account for NMD on nearly all these transcripts, including many alternative RNA transcript isoforms associated with annotated genes. Many NMD-targeted transcripts appear to be involved in two-promoter gene regulatory systems and share properties with long un-decoded transcript isoforms (LUTIs). In particular, we show that the DAL5 LUTI regulates expression of the DAL5 protein-coding mRNA in response to changes to environmental nitrogen. Our work expands the functional roles for LUTIs and establishes the importance of NMD in their regulation.

title: Characterizing malaria parasite drug response using single-cell transcriptomics
text: Gene expression analysis in malaria parasites has been used to define transcriptional regulatory networks but has been used less frequently to characterize parasite response to drug treatment or to show how parasites may evade killing. Here, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to hundreds of thousands of individually infected asynchronous red blood cells to evaluate the parasite's response to treatment with three chemotypes that can be used for treatment (artemisinin) or prophylaxis and treatment (atovaquone and ganaplacide). We found that each treatment gave rise to different cell populations with different transcriptional profiles. Comparing single-cell transcription patterns in compound-treated cells to transcript patterns observed previously with synchronized cells showed an enrichment of cells expressing gametocyte-associated genes after artemisinin treatment but fewer life cycle perturbations after treatment with the two other compounds. In contrast, bulk analysis showed an enrichment of pyrimidine biosynthesis transcripts for atovaquone treatment. Our results show that scRNA-seq may be used to profile diverse drug responses across many life cycle stages and to potentially classify drug classes.IMPORTANCEDetermining the mechanism of action (MOA) of compounds with antimalarial activity remains a key activity in both drug development and drug resistance studies but remains challenging for some chemotypes. Here we highlight the potential of single-cell transcriptional sequencing to augment the process of MOA deconvolution. We develop a new analytical pipeline that involves comparing single-cell transcription patterns to existing profiles from synchronized parasites to comprehensively characterize life cycle stage enrichments that may be observed after chemical perturbations. We also show that transcriptional feedback regulation may be present for some drug classes.

title: PEGylated oligonucleotide hybridization improves intracellular stability of lipid nanoparticle-delivered mRNA
text: Hybridizing mRNA with PEG-conjugated RNA oligonucleotides improves intracellular stability of LNPs delivered mRNA. A small number of short PEG chains protects mRNA from degradation while preserving nanoparticle stability and cellular uptake.

title: Supramolecular dynamics as a design dimension beyond static properties in nanomedicine
text: Supramolecular nanomedicines exhibit dynamics ranging from molecular exchange and reorganization to structural persistence. Understanding and controlling these dynamics guides the design of nanomedicines with desired biological functions.

title: Indole–hydrazone hybrid derivatives as emerging therapeutics for enhanced skin cancer therapy: molecular design, biological evaluation and nanoliposomal delivery
text: To advance skin cancer therapeutics, a series of indole–hydrazone derivatives (5a–5l) was synthesized via the hydrazone condensation reaction and formulation development of 5l -based nanoliposomal gel (GEL4).

title: Orthogonal ensemble and single-particle characterisation of antisense oligonucleotide lipid nanoparticles
text: Antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) remain underexplored relative to siRNA and mRNA LNPs. Using an orthogonal workflow (DLS, NTA, AF4), we show that ionisable lipid identity and microfluidic flow rate govern key LNP attributes. Replacing SM-102 with MC3 increased size and reduced ASO recovery, while lower flow rates increased LNP size and improved recovery, highlighting formulation-property relationships for ASO LNP optimisation.

title: Investigation of anti-SARS-CoV-2 multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors in a range of preclinical therapeutic settings
text: The spread of respiratory viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, has presented significant challenges over the last 30 years, with few effective therapeutic options available to this day. Bicyclic peptides represent a unique, modular modality in the antiviral armamentarium against future pandemics. This study utilizes tool molecules to provide a deeper evaluation of multivalent bicyclic (Bicycle) molecule efficacy in several preclinical SARS-CoV-2 challenge settings. We explore both pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure therapeutic settings via subcutaneous and intranasal routes of administration. We contextualize this further in bespoke scenarios where the immune system is compromised, as well as viral transmission. Promisingly, in all studies, we observe efficacy, significantly reducing infectious viral burden at each study endpoint. These data further support the candidacy of Bicycle molecules as a differentiated antiviral therapeutic class in the context of pandemic preparedness. IMPORTANCE: The COVID-19 pandemic triggered a rapid wave of innovation, accelerating the delivery of new vaccine technology and antiviral treatments. In our first paper, we described the discovery and molecular optimization of Bicycle molecules as a novel drug class for the potential treatment of SARS-CoV-2. Here, we have performed deeper characterization of these tool molecules in established animal models to evaluate scenarios for deployment, simulating SARS-CoV-2 transmission, testing more convenient delivery routes, such as intranasal, as well as looking at immunocompromised animals. The Bicycle molecules demonstrated positive outcomes in each of these studies and suggest that Bicycle molecules, as convenient and effective antiviral treatments, could be an important addition to help future preparedness against new viral pandemics.

title: Bdnf mRNA‐LNP Drives Nasal Epithelial BDNF Production and Improves Cognition in Aged and Alzheimer's Disease Mouse Models
text: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have rapidly emerged as a transformative approach for treating a range of health challenges. Accelerated by the success of mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines during the COVID-19 pandemic, this platform holds promise beyond immunisation for the transient expression of therapeutic proteins in targeted tissues. Despite this promise, non-invasive delivery of mRNA-encoded cargo to the brain remains a challenge, as most peptide drugs do not pass the blood-brain barrier. Here, we present the development of an intranasal mRNA-LNP therapeutic that drives production of neurotrophic factors in the nasal epithelium and delivery of the encoded protein to the brain. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate that intranasal delivery of mRNA encoding the neurogenic factor BDNF (Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factor) enhances memory performance in both aged mice and a transgenic mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. This approach offers a promising platform for delivering therapeutic proteins to the brain and opens new avenues for treating age-related and neurodegenerative disorders.

title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
text: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

title: The Gut Microbiota/Gut Brain/BDNF Axis Mediates Ginsenoside Re’s Neuroprotection in Parkinson’s Disease
text: Ginseng, as a traditional medicinal and edible resource, has shown potential in the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases, particularly Parkinson’s disease (PD), through its active components, ginsenosides (GS) and ginsenoside Re (GsRe). This study aimed to systematically investigate the neuroprotective effects and molecular underpinnings of total ginsenosides (GS) and ginsenoside Re (GsRe) in a 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) induced PD mouse model, with a focus on gut-brain axis modulation. The results showed that GS and GsRe ameliorated motor deficits, reduced substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) dopaminergic neuron loss, restored intestinal barrier integrity, and reversed gut dysbiosis. Mechanistically, GsRe crossed the BBB (Blood brain Barrier), upregulated brainderived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and inhibited the TLR4 adaptor WDFY1, blocking excessive NFκB activation, M1 microglial polarization, and neuronal apoptosis. BDNF deficiency exacerbated TLR4 pathway hyperactivation, suggesting that BDNF modulates TLR4mediated neuroinflammation and contributes to the neuroprotective effects of GsRe. GS and GsRe target the gutbrain axis as an integrated hub: normalizing gut microecology to limit peripheral inflammatory signal translocation, while suppressing central neuroinflammation via the BDNF/TLR4 axis. These findings reveal a gut microbiota/gut brain axis whereby GsRe alleviates neuroinflammation by concurrently modulating gut microbiota composition and the BDNF/TLR4 pathway, providing a mechanistic basis for GS/GsRe based PD interventions.

title: Engineering signal transduction for closed-loop gene and cell therapies
text: Chronic diseases are still treated largely with interventions that are constitutive, intermittently administered and poorly aligned with real-time physiology. Synthetic biology is changing this paradigm by treating gene circuits as programmable genetic software that can be deployed across cellular therapeutic hardware spanning from prokaryotic to eukaryotic systems, including probiotic cells, designer cells, immune cells and stem‑cell‑derived platforms. In this framework, engineered systems can sense disease-associated signals, compute them through synthetic or repurposed transduction pathways and adjust therapeutic output to maintain physiological variables within a desired range. Closed-loop therapeutics therefore begin to merge diagnosis, treatment and prevention within the same living platform. Across metabolism, inflammation, infection, cardiovascular regulation and cancer, early mammalian systems show that endogenous sensing, intracellular computation and therapeutic actuation can be combined in clinically relevant architectures. The emerging concept of setpoint medicine captures the clinical ambition of these systems: not simply to deliver a dose, but to keep physiology within an interpretable and therapeutically desirable range. Realizing this vision will require durable and modular control circuits, hardware-aware delivery strategies, interpretable safety frameworks, controller-style performance metrics and increasingly AI-assisted design, calibration and oversight. If these challenges can be met, the future of therapy may be defined less by intermittent dosing than by the continuous control of physiology.

title: Exponent Polytopes for Abstracting Chemical Reaction Networks into Formal Specification Models for Compositional Design of Biomolecular Circuits
text: Model based design has shown promise for synthetic biological circuits. However, many approaches remain empirical and limited in scale. Here, we develop specification models from chemical reaction network (CRN) models. These specifications encode assumptions explicitly and guarantees that must be met under those assumptions. Specifically, we show how monomial dominance relations in open CRNs induce polyhedral regime assumptions in logarithmic coordinates. These assumptions give polyhedral assume guarantee contracts that encode system behavior. Further, we show how order of magnitude dominance assumptions can be written explicitly as contract assumptions and used to derive tighter guarantees. We demonstrate two biological circuit design applications: identifying the biological mechanisms that meet the required system-level specification, and screening promoter and ribosome binding site choices to determine expression gains that satisfy a specification through contract composition and refinement. Ultimately, these results provide a path from CRN descriptions of synthetic biological parts to specification-based compositional design.

title: CyanoSource: A Biofoundry-based plasmid vector and gene knockout collection for the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
text: Abstract Generating gene knockout mutants is critical for understanding the function of genes and developing strains for biotechnology applications. Standardised gene knockout libraries facilitate robust and replicable studies between laboratories and provide strains to laboratories lacking expertise in knockout generation. We have developed a Biofoundry-based pipeline to automate the construction of a gene knockout library of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, which we have called CyanoSource (https://cyanosource.ac.uk). The CyanoSource collection consists of barcoded MoClo-compatible plasmid vectors and single-gene deletion mutants generated by homologous recombination-mediated transformation. Where possible, the complete coding sequence of each gene has been replaced with a kanamycin resistance positive selection cassette and a sacB negative selection cassette. The vectors used for generating each deletion can be modified as required for site-specific re-engineering. Here we outline the software tools and the development of automated wet-lab techniques used to generate the CyanoSource library. Our optimised method for assembling sequence-checked vectors showed a successful assembly efficiency of up to 85%. We next developed a high-throughput (96-well plate) foundry-assisted method for Synechocystis transformation that resulted in a 79% success rate in obtaining transformants and demonstrated that manual transformations can be significantly downsized. To date, we have generated 1,488 plasmids and 585 partially segregated and segregated mutants. CyanoSource will provide an important new community resource for systematic analyses of unknown gene functions, gene regulatory networks, and a common standard for the analysis of Synechocystis mutants.

title: Reprogramming Protein Function by Expanding Chemical and Combinatorial Space: Integrating Chemical and Computational Strategies
text: Proteins are biological macromolecules that perform critical functions, including catalysis, molecular recognition, and cellular regulation. Natural evolution has generated remarkable protein diversity, leaving vast opportunities for engineered molecular innovation. Protein engineering has evolved from the rational design of proteins over the last few decades to approaches based on directed evolution and computational methods to enhance their properties. Protein engineering is shifting from optimization-based approaches to an integrated approach, which includes rational design, directed evolution, computational and generative modeling, synthetic chemistry, synthetic biology, and laboratory automation. These strategies widen the scope of experimentally accessible chemical and structural toolboxes in proteins without sacrificing the physicochemical constraints, cellular compatibility, evolutionary processes, and experimental validation. Meanwhile, synthetic chemistry is extending the natural abilities of proteins by incorporating noncanonical amino acids, novel cofactors, and modified metal centers and catalytic environments. These technologies enable the creation of artificial enzymes, programmed molecular binders, synthetic receptors, molecular machines, and biomaterials that have functions beyond those of their natural counterparts. This review introduces advances in the protein engineering field, from past methods of modifying proteins to present-day opportunities for generating proteins with artificial intelligence, and explains how the fields of computation, chemistry, and biology are driving the future of programmable proteins.

title: An integrated high-throughput strategy for discovering and validating productive genomic integration hotspots in CHO cells
text: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells have long served as the primary workhorse of the biopharmaceutical industry. Conventional cell line development relies on random integration methods, which require multiple rounds of selection pressure and clonal verification to isolate monoclonal cell lines with the highest productivity. However, this approach often results in significant clonal variation and poor expression stability, thereby necessitating labor-intensive screening. To address the limitations mentioned above, site-specific integration of a protein expression cassette into predefined chromosomal loci exhibiting high expression and stability has emerged as a promising strategy. In this study, we established a high-throughput method for the detection and analysis of insertion sites to identify genomic “hotspot” loci from a stable, high-expression cell library generated via lentiviral random integration. Among 5,474 candidate integration loci, 12 candidate hotspot loci, together with four previously reported loci, were selected for validation of monoclonal antibody expression using a CRISPR/Cas9-mediated site-specific integration system. In parallel, we developed an Auto-MCS platform for CHO cell line development that enables the simultaneous screening of hundreds of monoclonal cells, thereby facilitating the efficient generation and characterization of site-specifically integrated monoclonal cell lines. Comparative evaluation of clones carrying different integration loci in 24-deep-well plates identified four newly discovered hotspots with 1.55- to 3.22-fold higher relative specific productivity than the previously reported reference locus NW_003626341.1. Shake-flask evaluation was subsequently performed on three clones from each of these four newly identified hotspots, and the best-performing clone was selected for inoculation-density optimization and further fed-batch evaluation. Following optimization, this clone achieved a mean antibody titer of 1.172 ± 0.019 g/L in a 3-L bioreactor fed-batch culture. Collectively, these findings provide a set of productive genomic hotspots for site-specific integration and may facilitate the development of high-performance CHO cell lines for biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Coffee biotechnology from yeast-assisted fermentation to spent coffee grounds valorization
text: Coffee fermentation plays a central role in determining coffee quality through the generation of flavor-related metabolites, whereas spent coffee grounds (SCG), the major byproduct of coffee consumption, have emerged as promising renewable feedstocks for sustainable biorefineries. Although controlled coffee fermentation and SCG valorization have attracted increasing attention, these fields have largely evolved independently. This review presents an integrated perspective on coffee biomass utilization by connecting flavor-oriented yeast-assisted coffee fermentation with the post-consumption biological valorization of spent coffee grounds. Particular emphasis is placed on the biochemical mechanisms by which yeasts degrade coffee mucilage and convert mucilage-derived substrates into flavor-related compounds and how fermentation-induced changes may influence coffee aroma after roasting. This mechanistic understanding provides a scientific foundation for the rational development of starter cultures capable of generating targeted sensory profiles tailored to consumer preferences. In addition, recent advances in the microbial and enzymatic valorization of SCG are summarized, including pretreatment-based strategies and the direct biological conversion of untreated SCG. Although these processes occur at distinct stages, shared yeast metabolic pathways provide a biochemical foundation for developing complementary biotechnological applications. By extending coffee biotechnology across the production and consumption chain, this review highlights strategies for increasing coffee value while maximizing the utilization of coffee-derived biomass.

title: SEA-Lab: Experiment-grounded recursive self-improvement in an automated laboratory
text: AI scientists can generate hypotheses, plans, and protocols. Translating these outputs into reliable experiments requires adapting them to local equipment and resources using feedback from observed outcomes. A key challenge is to retain laboratory execution feedback as reusable knowledge for subsequent planning. We present SEA-Lab (Self-Evolving Autonomous Lab), which combines an environment-grounded Dry-Lab Harness that generates protocols and machine-readable procedures, a wet-lab execution harness that coordinates heterogeneous devices and records execution traces and experimental measurements, and a recursive self-improvement mechanism that uses physical feedback to revise reusable execution policies and experimental strategies. Across three rounds of review on 219 tasks, protocol-review pass rates reached 90.41%. On 66 automation-eligible tasks, mean virtual-validation pass rates increased from 16.7% to 87.7% after two revisions. On two liquid handlers, runtime fell by 45.8% for plate replication, 34.1% for well rearrangement, and up to 68.6% for sample normalization. We demonstrated the system in a phage-display experiment linking four automated experimental steps: molecular cloning, phage titration, sample normalization, and ELISA screening. Of 96 starting samples, 93 yielded a sequence-correct clone, and primary ELISA screening identified ten candidates. These results illustrate how laboratory feedback can guide planning around local resources, refine execution on different laboratory instruments, and inform method revision based on experimental results.

title: Engineering antimicrobial peptides through the design–build–test–learn framework
text: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance has intensified the need for alternative anti-infective strategies. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer diverse mechanisms of action, but their translation remains constrained by poor physiological stability, host toxicity, and manufacturing costs. This review examines AMP development within a design-build-test-learn (DBTL) framework that connects computational discovery, peptide production, experimental evaluation, and iterative optimization. Proteome mining and generative artificial intelligence expand the accessible sequence space, while solid-phase synthesis, engineered microbial hosts, and cell-free systems convert selected sequences into testable molecules. Chemical modification and formulation provide complementary routes to improve stability and delivery. Standardized screening and in vivo studies then establish the evidence needed to prioritize candidates and inform subsequent design and production decisions. Throughout this cycle, activity must be optimized together with toxicity, stability, manufacturability, and delivery rather than treated as the sole measure of success. This review discusses applications in medicine, agriculture, food preservation, and biotechnology, and identifies remaining limitations in data quality, assay comparability, scale-up, and translational support. The DBTL framework provides a basis for coordinating these activities, although its practical value depends on experimentally validated feedback and application-specific development criteria.

title: Advances in microfluidic platforms for phenotypic microbial analysis and digital-twin-oriented modeling: A comprehensive and critical review
text: Microfluidics has revolutionized experimental microbial analysis by enabling precise, high-throughput phenotypic measurements of growth, inhibition, and stress responses in microscale environments that replicate natural and industrial conditions. This article provides a comprehensive and critical review of recent advances in microfluidic platforms for phenotypic manifestations of microbial metabolic activity and digital twinning. It begins by situating microfluidics within classical microbial culture strategies and explaining how miniaturization enables precise environmental control with reduced resource use. The architecture and operation of microfluidic chips are examined: microcolonies-based, droplet-based, biofilm-oriented, and single-cell systems, together with flow control, nutrient delivery, and CFD-assisted design. Using extensive literature data, a cross-comparison with conventional culture highlights reproducibility and scaling challenges where applications for growth and toxicity screening are compared through three quantitative performance metrics: Fold Speed Increase (FSI), Fold Resource Saving (FRS), and Microfluidic Performance Gain (MPG), providing scenario-dependent estimates of screening-time and liquid-volume efficiency under explicitly stated comparison assumptions. The review critically analyzes microscopy-based detection methods, including optical, fluorescence, and time-lapse imaging, which underpin most microfluidic studies, outlining their analytical power and current limitations in quantitative, in situ metabolic sensing. Finally, perspectives are offered on coupling microfluidics with integrated sensing, AI, and mechanistic modeling to enable digital twins for predictive and sustainable microbial biotechnologies.

title: What Were You Thinking? An LLM-Driven Large-Scale Study of Refactoring Motivations in Open Source Projects
text: Context . Code refactoring improves software quality without changing external behavior. Despite its advantages, its benefits are hindered by the considerable cost of time, resources, and continuous effort it demands. Aim . Understanding why developers refactor, and which metrics capture these motivations, may support wider and more effective use of refactoring in practice. Method . We performed a large-scale empirical study to analyze developers’ refactoring activity, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify underlying motivations from version control data, comparing our findings with previous motivations reported in the literature. Results . LLMs matched human judgment in 80% of cases, but aligned with literature-based motivations in only 47%. They enriched 22% of motivations with more detailed rationale, often highlighting readability, clarity, and structural improvements. Most motivations were pragmatic, focused on simplification and maintainability. While metrics related to developer experience and code readability ranked highest, their correlation with motivation categories was weak. Conclusions . We conclude that LLMs effectively capture surface-level motivations but struggle with architectural reasoning. Their value lies in providing localized explanations, which, when combined with software metrics, can form hybrid approaches. Such integration offers a promising path toward prioritizing refactoring more systematically and balancing short-term improvements with long-term architectural goals.

title: UCLCHEM 4.0: An open source gas-grain astrochemistry simulation framework
text: Abstract Astrochemical modelling is a key tool for interpreting the formation and destruction of molecules in the interstellar medium, complementing the increasingly detailed observations from modern facilities. UCLCHEM is a gas-grain astrochemical modelling framework that computes the chemical evolution of a parcel of gas and dust under a time-dependent physical description. This description can be user-defined, for example when post-processing hydrodynamical simulations, or one of the included parametrizations of cloud collapse, protostellar cores and shocks, covering scenarios ranging from from extragalactic environments to protoplanetary disks. The chemistry is solved with a rate-equation formalism in three phases (gas, surface and bulk ice), which are coupled through freeze-out, thermal and non-thermal desorption, and a geometrical treatment of the growth and shrinkage of the ice surface and bulk. This release adds an object-oriented Python interface, a description of the upgrade from two to three phases, and expanded support for post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and user-defined parametrizations. We give an overview of the physics and chemistry included in UCLCHEM, the inner workings of the solver, and the programming interface.

title: Integrated QTL mapping and CRISPR screening in pooled iPSC-derived microglia reveals genetic drivers of neurodegenerative risk
text: Mounting evidence implicates microglia in neurodegeneration, but linking disease-associated genetic variants to target genes and cellular phenotypes is hindered by the inaccessibility of these cells. We differentiated 261 human induced pluripotent stem cell lines into microglia-like (iMGL) cells in pools with phenotypic (differentiation, phagocytosis and migration) and single-cell transcriptomic readouts. Burden analysis of deleterious variants detected 36 genes influencing microglial phenotypes. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis identified 7,121 eQTL-associated genes and 79 colocalizations across four neurodegenerative disease genome-wide association studies, half of which had limited prior evidence of causality. Integration of eQTL and phenotypic associations highlighted the role of disease-relevant variants, including LRRK2 and TREM2 acting through microglial phagocytosis. A coupled CRISPR screen identified a role for TREM2 in phagocytosis and highlighted the importance of cell type in the directionality of phenotypic effects. By contextualizing variant effects within iMGLs in different inflammatory states, we provide a comprehensive framework for interpreting the function of risk loci in neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Unpacking “Personal” Health Informatics for Proactive Collective Care
text: Care is primarily a collective phenomenon, with a practice that involves sharing health and wellbeing information within a trusted “care circle” of family members and companions for sensemaking, interpretation, decision-making, and follow-through. However, current digital health tools and information systems are designed for individuals and primarily intended for Personal Health Informatics (PHI). This mismatch between collective practice and individualistic design creates new challenges for the proactive use of such systems in care settings and limits adoption, sustained engagement, and meaningful use. To examine how people practice collective care and how (if) they perceive, adopt, and integrate PHI systems for proactive care, we conducted a sequential mixed-methods study. Through an initial survey (n=87) and semi-structured interviews (n=22), we found that their practices involve collectively understanding, analyzing, and sensemaking health information. However, we also found that their use of existing systems to support such practices is constrained by factors at personal, relational, technological, and structural levels that evolve over time. To address these constraints and explore redesigning PHI toward “Collective Health Informatics”, we conducted eight stakeholder interview sessions with 12 participants, a follow-up survey (n=114), and six co-design workshops with 12 participants to understand the dynamics required in collective settings while retaining agency. Using a design probe evaluation (n=38), we refine a design vision for coordinated, trustworthy action across such care relationships. Our findings motivate CC-Proact , an operational map that translates ecological influences into three design levers: Agency , Elicitation , and Engagement . Using this map, our work empirically examines collective care practices and offers six design recommendations to build responsible systems that proactively support collective care.

title: Foreign Loan Financing for Indonesia’s Defense Modernization: Fiscal and Strategic Risks, Procurement Governance, and Industrial Self-Reliance
text: Indonesia’s defense modernization requires substantial and sustained financing, yet fiscal constraints limit the government’s capacity to fund large-scale major weapons systems (MWS) procurement through annual budget allocations alone. This study examines the opportunities, risks, and policy implications of foreign loan financing for defense modernization and the strengthening of national defense-industrial self-reliance. Using a qualitative literature-review approach, the study applies content analysis to academic publications, regulations, policy documents, official institutional data, and selected international experiences. The findings show that foreign loans can improve financing certainty for long-term defense acquisitions and create opportunities to support technology transfer, offsets, domestic content requirements (TKDN), and the development of national industrial capabilities. However, these benefits are accompanied by significant risks, including debt-sustainability pressures, exchange-rate exposure, long-term fiscal commitments, supplier dependence, and potential technological reliance on foreign partners. The analysis further indicates that the effectiveness of foreign financing depends on procurement design, bargaining capacity, institutional coordination, contractual enforcement, and domestic absorptive capacity. Accordingly, this study proposes an integrated policy framework built on four interrelated pillars: fiscal sustainability, institutional strengthening, optimization of TKDN and offset mechanisms, and comprehensive debt-risk management. Foreign loans should therefore be treated not merely as financing instruments, but as strategic defense-economic policy tools capable of simultaneously supporting military modernization and strengthening Indonesia’s defense-industrial independence. The evidence base combines peer-reviewed scholarship with official Indonesian budget, planning, regulatory, and procurement documents available through September 2026.

title: Synthetic Data in MR Spectroscopy: Current Practices, Applications, and Considerations
text: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. This review provides a structured overview of current practices in synthetic MRS data generation, with emphasis on the physical, biochemical, and computational assumptions that underpin commonly used models. A decomposition of synthetic MRS data is presented in terms of core building blocks, including basis sets, signal formation models, and metabolite parameter distributions such as concentration and relaxation properties. This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics. Beyond single-voxel modeling, synthetic data generation across multiple MRS modalities is discussed, including functional MRS, diffusion-weighted MRS, and spectroscopic imaging, with emphasis on modality-specific challenges such as physiological variability, motion, and confounding signal contributions. The role of synthetic data in clinical and preclinical research, acquisition optimization, software validation, and emerging artificial intelligence applications is further examined, with particular attention to domain shift and representational realism. Current practices in validation, reporting standards, and data accessibility are also reviewed, and key gaps limiting reproducibility and interoperability across studies are identified. Overall, this work provides a unified conceptual framework for synthetic MRS data generation, clarifies underlying assumptions across modeling choices, and outlines open challenges toward improving realism, standardization, and utility in both methodological and translational applications. Conducted by the MRS Synthetic Data Working Group under the Code & Data Sharing Committee of the MRS Study Group of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine (ISMRM), this review encompasses the existing literature, supplemented by the collective experience and in-house methodologies of its contributors, providing a community perspective that extends beyond the published record.

title: Metadata-based assessment of SNOMED CT and LOINC adoption across 800 000 Swiss patients
text: Abstract Background Semantic interoperability is essential for enabling the secondary use of clinical data in research and healthcare. International standards such as SNOMED CT and LOINC are key enablers, yet empirical evidence on their real-world adoption remains limited. Objective This study presents a nationwide analysis of terminology usage based on metadata collected from hospitals contributing to the SPHN Federated Clinical Routine Dataset. The dataset includes information on approximately 800 000 patients, with a minimum data coverage spanning 2018 to 2025 across six Swiss University Hospitals. The goal is to quantify the adoption of semantic standards, identify strengths and gaps in their usage, and highlight areas requiring further harmonization to support data quality and interoperability. Methods We analyzed the use of SNOMED CT and LOINC international standard terminologies across participating hospitals by querying aggregated metadata from the SPHN Metadata Catalog via its SPARQL endpoint. Results A total of 6 557 distinct SNOMED CT codes and 3 693 distinct LOINC codes were identified, representing approximately 717 million data instances. SNOMED CT and LOINC accounted for 60% and 32% of coded data instances, respectively. The remaining code instances originated from other coding systems (e.g. ATC, ICD-10-GM, CHOP). Despite this adoption, substantial heterogeneity was observed across hospitals, with most codes being institution-specific. A greater diversity of distinct codes was observed in domains such as ‘Substance’ and ‘Organism’, whereas frequently instantiated concepts were concentrated in ‘Clinical Finding’, ‘Procedure’, and ‘Qualifier Value’ hierarchies. LOINC code usage was dominated by routine laboratory tests across all institutions but with little overlap in the coding practice between them. Conclusions While SNOMED CT and LOINC are widely used within the SPHN framework, significant variability in code usage and limited cross-institutional overlap highlight ongoing challenges for semantic harmonization. This study provides the first nationwide empirical baseline of terminology adoption in SPHN and demonstrates the value of metadata-driven approaches for monitoring interoperability readiness. The findings support targeted efforts to improve standardization and enhance the reuse of clinical data for research.

title: Clinician Acceptance of Large Language Model–Generated Discharge Summaries
text: Importance: Hospital discharge summaries are essential for continuity of care, but fragmented electronic health record (EHR) data can compromise their quality and safety. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for clinical documentation tasks despite limited evidence regarding their performance in health care settings compared with the current standard of care. Objective: To evaluate clinician acceptability of LLM-generated discharge summaries derived from EHRs compared with routine clinician-written summaries. Design, Setting, and Participants: In this retrospective comparative effectiveness study using a prespecified noninferiority framework, acceptability of LLM-generated discharge summaries was compared with clinician-authored discharge summaries. Admission records from 5 London hospitals for September 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, were evaluated against the full admission record by practicing physicians. Admissions were eligible only if the clinician-authored discharge summary contained identifiable clinical summary, plan and requested actions, and information given sections.
