title: No convergence in three decades: national trajectories of episode-fatality ratios for childhood lower respiratory infections in 204 countries, 1990-2023
text: BackgroundLower respiratory infections (LRI) remain the leading infectious cause of death in children, and survival once ill is a direct tracer of health-system quality. Whether countries are converging toward the best survival performance achieved within their own region has never been tested at national level. We measured each countrys distance to an empirical episode-fatality-ratio (EFR) frontier in 204 countries from 1990 to 2023. MethodsFor each country and year we computed EFR = LRI deaths/incident episodes using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimates for ages 0-19 years. Deaths span the full 1990-2023 series; episodes are observed for 1990, 2019 and 2023, with intermediate years linearly interpolated. The frontier was the 10th-percentile country EFR within each GBD super-region and year (sensitivity: 5th and 25th percentiles); the gap = EFR_country/EFR_frontier. We classified 33-year gap trajectories into catch-up phenotypes, ranked COVID-window (2019-2023) movers, cross-tabulated gap against avoidable deaths to build a priority list, and benchmarked upper respiratory infections (URI) at three time points as a near-zero-fatality contrast. FindingsThe median countrys gap was 1.86 in 1990, 1.80 in 2019 and 1.86 in 2023; the share of countries more than twice their regional frontier was 44.6% in 1990 and 46.6% in 2023. Of 137 eligible countries, 67 narrowed and 69 widened their gap, with one unchanged. Nineteen countries achieved sustained catch-up, concentrated in North Africa and the Middle East (7) and Latin America (5), with China closing from 2.43 to 0.50, below its regional frontier; 28 countries regressed, led by Central Asia (Uzbekistan x3.5) and including the United States (x2.0). Over the COVID-19 window the median gap peaked at 2.00 in 2021 (+10.8% versus 2019, from unrounded medians) before returning to 1.86. Combining gap with avoidable deaths identifies two distinct policy problems: high-burden, moderate-gap giants (Nigeria 67,490 avoidable deaths, gap 2.4; India 54,109, gap 1.6) and extreme-gap outliers (Uzbekistan, gap 28.6). The Sub-Saharan Africa frontier fell further behind the High-income frontier (ratio 4.2 in 1990, 9.5 in 2023); the median Sub-Saharan African country sits 11.0 times the global 10th-percentile frontier but only 1.78 times its own regional frontier, so within-region benchmarking understates the regions true distance. URI gaps likewise did not converge (median 4.15 to 4.60). Joinpoint regression formalized the pattern: the median gap showed no net narrowing over 33 years (average annual percent change +0.03% per year, 95% CI -0.05 to 0.12). InterpretationConvergence toward the survival frontier is not the default national trajectory: over three decades the typical country made no net progress toward the best decile of its own region, and pandemic-era divergence was only partly reversed. National gap trajectories separate system-wide quality shortfalls from extreme outliers warranting audit, and expose a measurement trap in which regions whose frontiers stagnate appear closer to best practice than they are.

title: Warming, thermal variability, and the 96% decline in childhood respiratory-infection mortality in China: a national time-series analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 and the C-LSAT high-resolution climate dataset
text: BackgroundChildhood respiratory mortality in China has fallen by over 90% in three decades alongside sustained national warming, yet national long-run evidence on temperature and child respiratory mortality is lacking. MethodsWe linked Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 mortality estimates (rates use a fixed 2022 population denominator, so rate trends equal death-count trends) for China -- lower respiratory infections (LRI), ages 0-19, and asthma, ages 0-24, 1990-2021 -- with C-LSAT 0.5{degrees} gridded temperature data (1990-2019), aggregated nationally and to five climate zones. Four annual indicators (mean temperature, diurnal temperature range, seasonal amplitude, interannual variability) entered regressions of log mortality rates with Newey-West standard errors. A bootstrapped (500 resamples) quadratic model probed the minimum mortality temperature (MMT), with PM2.5-adjusted analyses and future-exposure, permutation, and detrended falsification tests. Changes in Chinas national thermal regime for 2041-2060 were additionally projected under three CMIP6 SSP scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5; WorldClim v2.1 1970-2000 baseline, MRI-ESM2-0) using a matched-cell delta method. ResultsLRI deaths fell by 96.3% (330,194 in 1990 to 12,098 in 2021; 95% uncertainty interval 9,669-14,891) and asthma deaths by 94.9% (3,287 to 167), while mean temperature rose 0.364 {degrees}C per decade and diurnal temperature range narrowed 0.092 {degrees}C per decade. Baseline coefficients were large (mean temperature -1.696, SE 0.174; diurnal temperature range +2.408, SE 0.336; seasonal amplitude -0.162, SE 0.082; interannual variability +2.924, SE 1.514, per 1 {degrees}C in log rate), but the future-exposure test failed and detrending nullified every coefficient: the associations are trend-level, and short-cycle causal effects are not identifiable. Nor was the national MMT identifiable -- observed temperature support spans only 6.66-8.13 {degrees}C, and the nominal turning point of 35.84 {degrees}C is an extrapolation artifact (quadratic term p = 0.963). Within the observed range, warming and declining mortality moved in the same direction. A CMIP6 scenario projection (WorldClim v2.1, MRI-ESM2-0, matched-cell national means) indicates a further +2.19 to +3.02 {degrees}C of national warming by 2041-2060, with little change in diurnal temperature range or seasonal amplitude. ConclusionsThe 96% decline in childhood respiratory mortality cannot be attributed to warming. China sits on the low-temperature side of the optimum, and the marginal direction of future warming requires stronger designs to establish. The falsification framework offers a discipline for climate-health inference in China. Bias-corrected scenario projections place Chinas 2050s mean temperature (approximately 9.4-10.3 {degrees}C on the C-LSAT scale) still far below multi-country optima (14.7-19.8 {degrees}C), noting that an annual-mean construct is not fully comparable with daily-scale MMT estimates.

title: After the vaccine era: sequencing platform investments as the childhood pneumonia spectrum diversifies
text: BackgroundThe historic decline in childhood pneumonia mortality was driven substantially by single-pathogen vaccines against Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) and Streptococcus pneumoniae. Yet the pathogen spectrum underlying child pneumonia deaths is diversifying: the effective number of pathogens rose from 5.57 in 1990 to 9.94 in 2023, and the residual burden is shifting toward opportunistic and hospital-associated pathogens for which no licensed childhood vaccines exist. This paper asks how resources should be sequenced between single-pathogen interventions and platform investments as this transition proceeds. MethodsWe analyzed Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 deaths from 29 pathogens in ages 0-19 years by super-region, combined with WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for PCV3 and Hib3. We quantified the spectrum transition under two denominators (26- and 29-pathogen calibers), constructed a share-by-intervenability matrix assigning each pathogen to a dominant intervention channel (vaccine-reachable, mixed, platform-sensitive) under explicit classification rules, compared platform-sensitive deaths with a transparently computed scenario of residual vaccine-preventable deaths, and cross-classified pathogens by age tropism and poverty lock. We anchored platform interventions to verified published evidence. ResultsThe vaccine-preventable group share fell from 54.0% to 40.2% while the opportunistic/hospital group rose from 18.1% to 23.1% (29-pathogen caliber, 1990-2023). Super-region vaccine coverage showed no significant association with pathogen-share change (PCV3 Spearman {rho} = 0.108, p = 0.818; Hib3 {rho} = -0.036, p = 0.939), a null result we report as evidence that simple coverage-burden correlations do not hold at the regional level, not as evidence against vaccine value. In 2023, vaccine-reachable pathogens accounted for 441,410 deaths (45.7%, channel including COVID-19), mixed for 126,926 (13.1%), and platform-sensitive pathogens for 396,995 (41.1%). Platform-sensitive deaths were 2.9-5.1 times the scenario estimate of residual vaccine- preventable deaths (52,435-77,512). Nine of 14 classifiable pathogens fell into the poverty-locked, infant-tropic cell (480,922 deaths; Fisher OR = 9.0, p = 0.1758). ConclusionsThe marginal value of single-pathogen strategies declines as the spectrum diversifies and residual deaths concentrate in platform-sensitive, poverty-locked, infant-tropic pathogens. Vaccine scale-up remains a certain and sizeable opportunity; the next increment of marginal resources should increasingly fund platform capabilities (oxygen systems, antimicrobial access and stewardship, infection prevention and control, referral, and nutrition) delivered as a package to the populations where the residual burden is locked.

title: Multi-Ancestry Rare and Low-Frequency Variant Analysis Reveals Novel and Convergent Biological Pathways for Cannabis Use Disorder
text: Large disparities in Cannabis Use Disorder (CUD) prevalence exist across U.S ethnic groups, yet genetic research has disproportionately focused on individuals of European descent. This study investigated the genetic architecture of CUD severity across three populations--American Indians, Mexican Americans, and European Americans--focusing on rare and low-frequency variants (minor allele frequency < 5%). CUD severity was measured using a validated composite of 20 cannabis-related life events, enhancing phenotypic resolution and power. In American Indians, ten genome-wide significant common variants were identified. Analyses of rare and low-frequency functional variants revealed novel, convergent biological pathways across ancestries. Notably, the arylsulfatases activation pathway was significantly associated with CUD severity in Mexican Americans and supported in American Indians, implicating sulfated lipids such as sphingolipids in CUD neurobiology. Related, in European Americans, the heparan sulfate degradation pathway--central to synaptic remodeling and extracellular matrix regulation--showed significant negative association with CUD severity. The integrin beta-1 cell surface interaction pathway, critical for neuronal adhesion and signaling, was uniquely enriched in Mexican Americans. Immune-related pathways, including shared involvement of a p38-gamma/delta MAPK signaling cascade, were supported across multiple cohorts. These findings highlight both ancestry-specific and shared mechanisms contributing to CUD severity, emphasizing the biological complexity of addiction. Importantly, these pathways represent potential therapeutic targets, suggesting that modulation of sulfated lipid metabolism and extracellular matrix remodeling may offer novel strategies for intervention. By integrating multi-ethnic cohorts and rare variant analyses, this study identifies underappreciated genetic contributors to CUD and underscores the importance of population-informed addiction genetics research.

title: No Point Beating Around the Bedpan: Lessons from a Major Intra-Hospital NDM-Producing Escherichia coli Carriage Outbreak : a Mixed-Methods Study.
text: Antimicrobial resistance constitutes a major threat to global public health. Among emerging extensively drug-resistant bacteria (eXDR), carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) expose hospitals to outbreaks through rapid dissemination, and to therapeutic limitations. Through a mixed epidemiological-qualitative methods study, we report the most extensive CPE carriage outbreak known to date in France, which occurred at Hopital Europeen Marseille (HEM) between January and June 2025. By the end of November 2024, the admission of an index patient returning from Senegal carrying an NDM-producing Escherichia coli led to an extensive transmission, despite adherence to national "screen and isolate" guidelines. Nearly 7,500 rectal screening tests identified 481 CPE carriers (including 343 NDM, 129 OXA-48-like and 9 other CPE), and 14 vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium carriers. This major outbreak prompted an extraordinary response involving clinical, technical and administrative teams within the institution. It highlighted operational limitations in current screening, cohorting and biocleaning strategies in the context of a hospital-wide outbreak. We describe the outbreak trajectory, the control measures implemented and provide a structured synthesis of lessons learned across organisational, scientific and policy domains.

title: Sustained Viral Suppression and its association with Psychiatric Morbidity and Sleep Quality among Older Adults with Human Immunodeficiency Virus: Evidence from a Retrospective Cohort in Ibadan, Nigeria.
text: PurposeOlder adults with HIV are at risk of psychiatric disorders and poor sleep quality, but evidence from sub-Saharan Africa is limited, particularly regarding sustained viral suppression. This study examined the prevalence of psychiatric disorders and poor sleep quality symptoms and their association with sustained viral suppression among older adults with HIV in Nigeria. MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted among older adults receiving care at a tertiary HIV clinic in Ibadan, Nigeria. Viral load data from 2019-2023 were abstracted from medical records to determine sustained viral load suppression, while psychiatric morbidity and sleep quality were assessed cross-sectionally in 2023. Psychiatric morbidity, including major depressive disorder, anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder and mania, was assessed using the World Mental Health Composite International Diagnostic Interview (WMH-CIDI), while sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Mixed-effects logistic regression assessed changes in viral suppression over time and associations with psychiatric morbidity and sleep quality. ResultsAmong 400 participants, 63.5% were female and mean age was 58.2 years ({+/-} 6.5). The 12-month prevalence of major depressive disorder was 25.8% while 17.5% had anxiety disorder, 29.3% had poor sleep quality, 3.3%, bipolar disorder, and 1.0% mania. Viral suppression improved significantly over the retrospective period. Sustained viral suppression was significantly associated with higher odds of good sleep quality (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.07-2.66, p = 0.025), but not psychiatric morbidity. ConclusionPsychiatric disorders and poor sleep quality are common among older adults with HIV in Nigeria. Sustained viral suppression was associated with better sleep quality but not psychiatric morbidity highlighting the importance of integrating mental health and sleep assessment into comprehensive HIV care for older adults.

title: Deep Learning of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Ophthalmoscopy for Type 2 Diabetes Classification
text: PurposeTo evaluate whether fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy (FLIO) combined with deep learning can detect metabolic signatures for classification of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). DesignCross-sectional analysis of participants included in the AI-READI dataset (version 3) with FLIO imaging. Subjects1,783 participants from the AI-READI dataset (version 3) with HbA1c measurements and FLIO imaging scans: 425 normoglycemic, 569 prediabetic, and 789 diabetic. MethodsGlycemic groups were defined from self-reported diagnosis, glucose-lowering medication, and HbA1c. Center-of-mass mean lifetime ({tau}CMM) maps, corrected for background and system timing offset, were generated from the raw time-resolved FLIO scans. Group differences in central-window {tau}CMM were tested by one-way ANOVA and by age-adjusted analysis of covariance. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), ResNet-18, and XGBoost were trained on {tau}CMM maps for three-class (normal, prediabetic, diabetic) and two binary (normal vs. impaired; normal vs. diabetic) classification of T2DM and compared them with an age-only classifier and with models combining FLIO and age. Main Outcome MeasuresMacro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, F1 score, and positive predictive value (PPV). ResultsGroup-averaged {tau}CMM was longer in prediabetic and diabetic than in normoglycemic participants in both the SSC (p < 0.001) and the LSC (p < 0.001), but only the SSC difference remained significant after age adjustment (p = 0.017). For 3-class classification, the CNN using FLIO achieved the highest AUROC (0.60 {+/-} 0.04), compared with 0.51 {+/-} 0.03 for an age-only classifier. ResNet-18 and XGBoost showed similar performance. Binary classification of normal vs. diabetic participants yielded AUROC 0.67 {+/-} 0.04 (CNN), 0.64 {+/-} 0.04 (ResNet-18), and 0.62 {+/-} 0.04 (XGBoost). All three FLIO models exceeded the age-only classifier in all T2DM classification tasks, whereas adding age to the FLIO models did not improve model performance. ConclusionsFLIO-derived {tau}CMM maps capture retinal signals associated with diabetes status that exceed what age alone provides, but yield modest classification performance with current artificial intelligence models. These findings highlight both the potential and the challenges of using FLIO for early metabolic screening and monitoring, informing future development of clinically applicable imaging biomarkers.

title: Diet Soda Consumption is Associated with Shifts in Gut Microbiome Function of Overweight Young Women
text: BackgroundLow-calorie sweeteners (LCS) are consumed as sugar substitutes and may alter gut microbial composition. Their effects on microbial functional pathways and cardiometabolic physiology in humans remain poorly understood, particularly among individuals with overweight. MethodsWe conducted a secondary analysis of an 8-week, single-arm pre/post intervention involving eight overweight young adult women who consumed sucralose- and acesulfame-potassium-sweetened Diet Pepsi three times daily. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples was used to profile microbial functional pathways with HUMAnN2. Multivariable linear mixed models (MaAsLin2) assessed associations between pathways and metabolic biomarkers. We hierarchically clustered nominally significant pathways into six representative groups and calculated Spearman correlations with interleukin-6 (IL-6), leptin, and HOMA-IR. P values were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Biomarkers were measured using clinical chemistry and immunoassays. ResultsMaAsLin2 identified 33 microbial pathways nominally associated with the intervention (exploratory FDR [≤] 0.25); one pathway (PWY-5104) also met the conventional FDR [≤] 0.10 threshold. Eighteen pathways were upregulated and 15 downregulated, with log fold changes ranging from -2.47 to 3.18. The 33 pathways were grouped into six functional clusters. L-alanine biosynthesis (PWY0-1061) was positively correlated with circulating IL-6 ({rho} = 0.74; q < 0.01). Phosphopantothenate biosynthesis I (PANTO-PWY) was not significantly correlated with IL-6 ({rho} = -0.46; q = 0.22). ConclusionGut microbial functional analysis identified a positive association between L-alanine biosynthesis and circulating IL-6. This finding complements previously reported taxonomic shifts in this cohort and suggests a potential relationship between LCS consumption, microbial function, and host inflammatory signaling.

title: Plasma proteomics reveals signatures of cognitive aging and response to the FINGER multidomain lifestyle intervention
text: The FINGER trial demonstrated that a multidomain lifestyle intervention benefits cognition in older adults at-risk of dementia, yet the underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. We measured neurodegeneration-related proteins using the NULISAseq CNS disease panel in 1158 FINGER participants to investigate associations between circulating proteins, cognitive trajectories, and intervention response. Independent of the intervention, ten proteins spanning immune, neuronal, and metabolic processes were associated with poorer cognitive trajectories, with TREM2 among the strongest signals. The intervention led to changes in eight proteins, including CRH, IL-7 and MME. Eleven proteins modified the cognitive response to intervention, with KDR and CRH showing the strongest effect. Complementary Elastic Net analyses confirmed CRH, and further identified PTN and CCL2 as markers of intervention responsiveness. Additional proteins showed APOE {varepsilon}4- and sex-specific associations with the intervention response. Together, these findings identify proteomic signatures of cognitive response that could inform precision dementia prevention.

title: Determinants of prices of commercial electric breast pumps sold in Germany: a cross-sectional analysis
text: In Germany, statutory health insurance covers the rental or purchase of breast pumps when a medical indication is present for the mother or infant, and a physician has issued a prescription. However, parents must pay out of pocket for commercially available breast pumps for returning to work or personal circumstances. High indirect costs for continuation of breastfeeding and direct costs for breast pumps and related equipment may pose substantial barriers to breastfeeding families, an issue relevant for health equity. To our knowledge, no studies have assessed the direct financial costs associated with the purchase of commercially available breast pumps. In this cross-sectional study, we examined digital marketplaces in Germany for commercial electric breast pumps between March 2025 and May 2026, across major online platforms. Our objective was to explore pump features that predict price. We identified 282 commercial electric pump models from 108 brands. Basic information was unavailable for half of surveyed breast pump brands. The median price for surveyed commercial electric pumps was {euro}72.70 (IQR: {euro}82.70), with costs ranging widely from {euro}19.99 to {euro}659.57. Prices varied by marketplace, manufacturer location, accessories, pump system type, power source, battery capacity, flange sizes, availability of instruction manuals, and "single user" claims; predicting significantly higher costs. Half of pumps surveyed offered only one flange size, signaling additional expenses for mothers needing alternative sizes. These findings highlight important considerations for maternal health and consumer safety. Health technology assessments and a review of current health policy on reimbursement for commercial electric breast pumps is needed. C_LIO_LIThere is a sparsity of flange sizes sold outside of the mid-range (24 mm), signaling ancillary costs for flanges with appropriate fit C_LIO_LIHealth technology assessments for commercial electric breast pumps and a review of health policy related to breast pump reimbursement in Germany are warranted C_LI

title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
text: BackgroundLaboratory medicine underpins clinical decision-making across nearly every care setting. Clinical laboratory errors and delays can compromise diagnostic reliability and patient care. However, laboratory quality and operational data are commonly reviewed through separate manual workflows, limiting timely recognition of emerging problems across complementary data sources. MethodsWe developed and evaluated LabARIA (Laboratory Agentic Reasoning and Integrative Analytics), a multi-agent AI system for coordinated surveillance of specimen workflows, analytical quality control, and laboratory operations. We conducted a single-center retrospective system development and evaluation at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical Center using laboratory data collected from May 1 through June 18, 2026, including 177,480 specimen-panel records, 75,103 internal quality-control (IQC) measurements, 633 proficiency-testing challenges, and 422 recalibration or maintenance actions. Forecasting agents were evaluated using patient-result streams with controlled perturbations, and synthetic staffing and inventory data. We assessed specimen rejection, cancellation, and turnaround-time patterns; warning recall and lead time before documented laboratory actions; assay-specific patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) performance; and exploratory operational forecasting discrimination. FindingsLabARIA characterized specimen and workflow patterns across clinical units and time periods, including hemolysis-related potassium rejections in the intensive care unit during early morning hours (49 of 367 tests [13.3%]). For analytical quality monitoring, the IQC agent generated warnings before 407 of 422 recorded QC actions (recall, 0.964 [95% CI, 0.942-0.978]), with a median lead time of 5.40 days (95% CI, 3.75-6.07). PBRTQC agent selected different monitoring strategies across 35 analytes. In a separate analysis, adding PBRTQC increased action recall from 0.964 to 0.993 (95% CI, 0.979-0.998). A dashboard presented tiered alerts for human review, and an accompanying chatbot supported interactive exploration of the summaries. For the operational forecasting module, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 7-day inventory and staffing risk forecasting were 0.800 (95% CI, 0.696-0.881) and 0.877 (95% CI, 0.778-0.950), respectively. InterpretationLabARIA demonstrated the feasibility of coordinating laboratory quality surveillance across heterogeneous data sources, providing a foundation for intelligent clinical laboratories. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether this approach improves monitoring beyond conventional methods, supports laboratory decisions, and benefits patient care without excessive alert burden. FundingNo external funding. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched PubMed and arXiv for studies published between Jan 1, 2016, and Nov 1, 2026, without language restrictions, using ("clinical laboratory" OR "clinical laboratories" OR "laboratory medicine") AND ("artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning" OR "large language model" OR "large language models" OR "agentic AI" OR "multi-agent" OR "multiagent" OR "quality control" OR "laboratory operations"). We included studies addressing laboratory quality monitoring or operations and excluded those focused solely on disease diagnosis or treatment selection. Reliable clinical laboratory services are essential to patient care, yet quality and operational surveillance often relies on manual and retrospective review of data distributed across separate systems, placing substantial burdens on laboratory personnel and contributing to reactive responses to emerging problems. Although laboratory automation has advanced, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning applications in clinical laboratories have generally focused on narrowly defined tasks, such as identifying preanalytical errors, supporting test interpret

title: Effect of Data Preprocessing Decisions on Sepsis-3 Labels in MIMIC-III and eICU-CRD: A Sensitivity Analysis
text: ObjectivePublished Sepsis-3 detection rates range from 3.4 % to 65.2 % in MIMIC-III and from 9.8 % to 47.9 % in eICU-CRD. We tested whether data preprocessing decisions alone produce differences of this magnitude when data, cohort and sepsis definition are held fixed. Materials and MethodsUsing the MIMIC-III and eICU-CRD databases we developed and applied a configurable pipeline (medalabel) that stepwise maps the databases into the OMOP Common Data Model, standardizes and cleans the data, and preprocesses them to compute Sepsis-3 labels. Each setting of the preprocessing represents one decision of published Sepsis-3 implementations, and settings can be freely combined. On fixed cohorts of first ICU stays (13,388 in MIMIC-III, 94,782 in eICU-CRD), we changed one setting of a reference configuration at a time (51 variants in five preprocessing domains) and compared detection rates and septic stays (Jaccard index) with the reference. We approximately reconstructed six published pipelines and combined the settings with the largest effects in pairs to test whether their effects add up. The time a value is measured can differ from the time it is documented and thus available for automated analysis. Beyond the usual retrospective view based on measurement time, the pipeline optionally combines both time points to simulate a real-time system. ResultsThe reference configuration labelled 31.5 % of ICU stays in MIMIC-III and 8.2 % in eICU-CRD as septic. Changing a single setting resulted in sepsis detection rates of 15.3-58.6 % in MIMIC-III and 4.6- 17.2 % in eICU-CRD. The largest shifts from the reference, all in the same direction in both databases, came from the SOFA baseline, up to +27.1 percentage points (pp) in MIMIC-III and +9.0 pp in eICU-CRD, from disabling imputation (-16.3 and -2.5 pp), the temporal window (+12.6 and +5.3 pp) and aggregation (-10.1 and -0.8 pp); clinician-validated parameter sets had little effect (-4.8 and -1.1 pp). Even variants that changed the rate by less than 2 pp labelled partly different patients, with Jaccard indices as low as 0.67 in MIMIC-III and 0.56 in eICU-CRD (1 = identical septic stays). Reconstructions deviated from the published rates by 2-10 pp. Two settings applied together deviated from the sum of their single effects by 0.9-11.8 pp in MIMIC-III and by up to 4.9 pp in eICU-CRD. Simulating a real-time system lowered the MIMIC-III rate by 5.0 pp and delayed the label in 45 % of the stays that remained septic. DiscussionWith the infection criterion held fixed, preprocessing decisions alone can produce a considerable part of the variation between published sepsis detection rates. Similar rates can stem from different patients, which makes studies and prediction models difficult to compare, and retrospective labels rely on values that a real-time system would not yet have. ConclusionSepsis-3 labels from health records are only comparable if their data preprocessing is known. Configurable pipelines allow quantifying the effect of these decisions, computing alternative labels on the same data and, in future, validating them against clinician-adjudicated cases.

title: Resource Overlap and Reporting of Independence in Public Prostate Cancer Research
text: ImportancePublic prostate cancer data may appear under different repository identifiers or releases while representing overlapping patients, specimens, or sample records. The implications for reported analytic independence require assessment at both resource and publication levels. ObjectiveTo characterize supported nonindependence among selected public prostate cancer resources and assess reported overlap control in publications using related resources. DesignCross-sectional methodological audit. Resource records were reconciled through September 2, 2026; recovery of retained sources and adjudication continued through September 8, 2026. Language-model extraction and targeted original-source checks informed deterministic classification. The authors manually verified all positive findings, including supplementary materials, in September 2026. SettingPublic prostate cancer repositories and Europe PMC and PubMed retrieval, with a publication cutoff of August 15, 2026. ParticipantsA nonrepresentative frame of 189 repository study records and 108 publication/version records contributing 230 publication-resource-pair records. ExposuresAnalytic use of both endpoints of a confirmed resource relation in the same linked claim. Main Outcomes and MeasuresSupported identity levels and resolvable patient-identifier counts; reported overlap control when linked analyses required independent records. Unresolved evidence was retained separately. Published results were not reanalyzed. ResultsThe audit identified 101 supported resource pairs: 97 with direct patient, specimen, or sample-record identity, 1 with component containment, and 3 with study/source nonindependence. Among 108 publication/version records, 8 (6 journal articles and 2 preprint versions) used related resources in analyses requiring independence without reporting applicable overlap controls. Another 3 reported applicable controls, 16 retained reporting gaps, and 81 fell outside the qualifying use or relation criteria. One of the 8 had 45 shared sample identifiers in two validation sheets, corroborating sample-record reuse but not donor identity. No global independent-patient total or prevalence estimate was established. Conclusions and RelevanceResource nonindependence coexisted with absent claim-specific control reporting, with direct sample-record corroboration in one publication. The findings support provenance-aware use and explicit reporting, without establishing effects on published results.

title: Improvement in Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) diagnosis and management after automatic loading of CKD in the electronic health record problem list
text: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) is often underrecognized and undiagnosed. We evaluate the impact of an algorithm-based automatic loading process for CKD in the electronic health record (EHR) problem list at a large health system. MethodsStudy populations included patients receiving primary or nephrology care at Geisinger (intervention group) and 4 large health systems in the Optum Labs Data Warehouse (OLDW), a longitudinal, real-world data asset with de-identified administrative claims and electronic health record (EHR) data,(comparator group) from 2008-2023. Since 2013, an automated process has been regularly implemented at Geisinger, adding CKD to problem lists of patients meeting laboratory criteria for CKD (outpatient eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73m2 on 2 lab values for [≥] 3 months without intervening normal values). We conducted difference-in-differences (DiD) and difference-in-difference-in-differences (DiDiD) analyses comparing CKD diagnosis rates, CKD-related lab tests, use of renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system inhibitors (RAASi) and statins for those >50 years within 1 year of incident CKD (index date) at Geisinger vs. OLDW health systems before (2008-2012) and after (2013-2023) CKD auto-load implementation. Analyses relied on summary-level data and did not permit adjustment for individual-level characteristics. ResultsAmong patients with incident, undiagnosed CKD (n=21,995 in Geisinger; n=208,402 in OLDW), CKD diagnosis within 1 year of index date increased from 28.4% in 2008-2012 to 65.7% in 2013-2023 at Geisinger whereas CKD diagnosis decreased from 22.6% to 20.7% at OLDW (DiD estimate 39.1%; 95% CI: 38.1%, 40.1%; p<0.001). Among CKD-related labs, DID estimates favored Geisinger for follow-up eGFR, parathyroid hormone, and phosphorus testing (all p values <0.001). CKD auto-load was associated with increased use of RAASi and statins (p values <0.05). ConclusionsAn algorithm-based problem list auto-load process was associated with higher CKD diagnosis, some CKD-related labs, and use of recommended medications. This scalable strategy should be validated in other health systems.

title: When will it ever be enough? Black mothers and community advocates perspectives on why evidence of racism in English maternity care does not lead to action: a co-produced focus group study
text: BackgroundRacism shapes the maternity care and outcomes of Black, African, Caribbean and mixed-Black women in the UK. Services monitor inequities through outcomes and experience data, yet evidence of racism often results in inaction, and existing explanations rely mainly on staff perspectives. We drew on Black mothers and community advocates accounts to explain what stops monitoring of racism from leading to action, and how they propose evidence of racism should be recorded so that it does. MethodsThis co-produced qualitative study was underpinned by critical realism and Black feminist thought. Four focus groups were held in London from June to July 2026 with nine Black, African, Caribbean and mixed-Black mothers who used NHS maternity services and seven community advocates. Lived experience co-researchers co-led the study design, data collection and analysis. We used critical realist thematic analysis to propose mechanisms explaining participants accounts, each tested against rival explanations. ResultsWe propose three mechanisms: credibility discounting, evidence neutralisation and containment of change. Participants described Black womens accounts being discounted until someone else raised the same concern, consistent with testimonial injustice. Recorded evidence appeared to be neutralised through audit culture, as concerns were acknowledged or deflected without action. Change that would shift power or accountability appeared to be contained, consistent with institutional racism. Participants also described harm from staff who shared their racial identity, linked to internalised racism intersecting with language and migration, and to workplace cultures in which Black staff are also dismissed; we interpret this harm as a possible outcome of these mechanisms. Participants proposed that services account for their response to each concern, supported by community-generated evidence, independent observation, qualitative routes and ethnicity-disaggregated data. This would require protection for those who raise concerns and sustained funding and backing for action. ConclusionsOur findings suggest more evidence alone is unlikely to address racism in maternity services. An independently reviewed record of how services respond to each concern could show when they do not act. Change is more likely where services shift power and resources to community organisations working with Black families, while remaining accountable for acting on evidence of racism.

title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa in bronchiectasis: unmasking population diversity and antimicrobial resistance in the Australian context
text: BackgroundPseudomonas aeruginosa infections in bronchiectasis airways result in poorer lung function, advanced lung lobe involvement, worsened life quality, and higher hospitalisation rates. Despite high prevalence, little is known about P. aeruginosa population genomics, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) rates, persistence, and transmission dynamics in Australians with bronchiectasis. MethodsP. aeruginosa (n=137) isolated between 2009 and 2025 from 59 Australians with bronchiectasis underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing against 11 antipseudomonal drugs, whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and in silico AMR determinant identification. Data were integrated with 4,575 publicly available bronchiectasis-derived P. aeruginosa genomes to determine global phylogenomic and AMR determinant patterns. ResultsHigh AMR rates were identified in the Australian isolates, with 75.9% resistant to at least one antimicrobial, 19.7% multidrug-resistant, and 9.5% extremely drug-resistant. AMR rates were highest (64.2%) for ciprofloxacin and cefepime (44.5%), and lowest for piperacillin/tazobactam (8.8%) and colistin (0.7%). Phylogenomics uncovered several instances of within-host evolution, hypermutation, persistence, and multi-lineage infections. Of the fifty-seven identified multilocus sequence types (STs), seven (12.3%) were novel, five were high-risk international clones (ST274 [6.6%], ST395 [0.7%], ST244 [0.7%], ST277 [0.7%], ST298 [0.7%]) and three were common global clones (ST253 [5.1%], ST155 [3.6%], ST260 [0.7%]). No high-risk AMR-conferring mobile genetic elements were seen, although numerous chromosomal AMR determinants were identified. AMR determinant prevalence was consistent with the global dataset, with no evidence of geographic clustering. ConclusionsOur study provides critical insights into P. aeruginosa diversity in Australians with bronchiectasis. High AMR rates and chronic colonisation highlight the need to improve diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship measures, and infection control practices in this neglected clinical cohort.

title: Mental Stress-Induced Peripheral Microvascular Dysfunction and Cardiovascular Events after a Premature Myocardial Infarction: A Prospective Cohort Study
text: BackgroundImpaired macrovascular function during acute mental stress predicts adverse events in coronary artery disease, but microvascular stress responses are less understood. Because psychosocial stress and coronary microvascular dysfunction are more common in women, sex differences also warrant study. MethodsWe studied individuals aged 18-60 years within 8 months of a myocardial infarction (MI) who underwent a standardized mental stress challenge and were followed for cardiovascular events. We measured peripheral microvascular function with the reactive hyperemia index (RHI) before and after stress; abnormal RHI was defined as [≤]1.67. We also measured brachial flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and myocardial ischemia. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization; a secondary endpoint included recurrent events. Cox regression examined stress-induced RHI decline, adjusting for pre-stress RHI and demographic, clinical, and psychological factors. ResultsAmong 487 participants (mean age 51 years; 43% women), 89 first and 90 recurrent events occurred over a median 34 months. Women had lower RHI than men before and after stress, and a larger stress-induced decline. Each standard deviation stress-induced RHI decline was associated with 36% higher risk of first events (hazard ratio [HR], 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01, 1.82) and 44% higher risk of cumulative events (HR, 1.44, 95% CI, 1.04, 2.00), with no significant sex interaction. Abnormal post-stress RHI conferred adjusted HRs of 2.59 (95% CI, 1.13, 5.92) in women and 2.09 (95% CI, 1.11, 3.93) in men; abnormal pre-stress RHI was not predictive (HR, 1.12, 95% CI, 0.71, 1.76). IL-6 and FMD changes and stress-induced ischemia were related to RHI decline but did not explain its association with outcome. ConclusionsMicrovascular dysfunction with mental stress is more prevalent in women, and signals an elevated cardiovascular risk after MI in both women and men. What is already known on this topicMacrovascular dysfunction in response to acute mental stress has been related to increased risk of recurrent events in people with coronary artery disease. However, less is known about microvascular responses to stress. What this study addsA decline in microvascular function with mental stress is an independent predictor of subsequent cardiovascular events after a myocardial infarction (MI), and a stronger predictor than pre-stress microvascular function alone. Women have worse resting microvascular function and a more adverse microvascular response to stress. How this study might affect research, practice or policyMicrovascular dysfunction may represent an important pathway linking psychological stress to adverse cardiovascular outcomes in people with MI. The microvascular response to stress should be evaluated as a potentially modifiable marker of cardiovascular risk and intervention studies should determine whether targeting stress-related microvascular dysfunction can reduce cardiovascular risk in this population.

title: Weighting the weeks that matter: entropic tilting for epidemic forecast evaluation
text: The performance of infectious disease forecasting models is commonly calculated under the implicit assumption that forecast accuracy is equally important across time. This approach may obscure or under-weight differences in model performance during the epidemic periods that matter most for public-health decisions. Here, we introduce the weighted prequential score (WPS), a forecast evaluation framework that can emphasize epidemic periods of interest. The WPS is a weighted average of scores over time, where weights are constructed through entropic tilting which up-weights priority periods while keeping the WPS as close as possible to the arithmetic average. We demonstrate the WPS on forecasts of incident hospitalizations submitted to the CDC FluSight challenge, focusing on two priority periods: weeks of rapid growth in incidence and weeks near the seasonal peak. Across season-location-horizon pairs, doubling the weight assigned to priority periods changes the top-ranked model in 10%-26% of eligible settings, while the top-ranked model remains unchanged regardless of the amount of weight assigned in 37%-68% of settings. We demonstrate that for suitable weights, the models favored by the WPS yield an average gain in accuracy during priority periods that is at least as large as the average accuracy lost during the remaining weeks. Because weights can be defined using observed outcomes, the WPS is not a proper scoring rule. Hence, we recommend using the WPS as a retrospective evaluation diagnostic. The WPS can guide public-health practitioners in selecting models that perform well during periods most relevant to their decisions, while encouraging forecasting teams to improve accuracy during these critical weeks. Author summaryIn the context of public health decisions, the importance of accurate infectious disease forecasts may vary over the course of an epidemic. For example, accurate forecasts of incident hospitalizations around the seasonal peak may be particularly important for hospital staffing decisions. We introduce a forecast scoring rule that allows users to emphasize accuracy during the epidemic phases most relevant to their decisions. We demonstrate our approach on forecasts of influenza hospitalization incidence, focusing on periods of rapid growth and weeks surrounding the seasonal peak. We find our approach leads to model rankings that prioritize accuracy during these periods with minimal losses in performance across the entire epidemic.

title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
text: ImportanceEarlier age at menopause associates with increased later life dementia risk, but the biological links that underlie this relationship remain poorly understood in population-based samples. ObjectiveTo evaluate the relationship between history of menopausal timing and AD/ADRD-related blood-based biomarkers in postmenopausal women. DesignObservational study using the U.S. Health and Retirement Study. AD/ADRD-related biomarkers were measured from venous blood draws conducted in 2016 and released in 2025. We estimated linear and nonlinear associations between spontaneous menopause timing and biomarkers, accounting for sociodemographic and health covariates. We evaluated effect modification by APOE 4 carrier status. Secondary analyses evaluated associations with hysterectomy history. SettingPopulation-based. ParticipantsCommunity-dwelling post-menopausal women aged 65 years or older. ExposurePrimary: Self-reported spontaneous age of menopause among women with no history of hysterectomy. Secondary: Self-reported history of hysterectomy (oophorectomy history was not assessed). Main Outcomes and MeasuresNeurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) measured in plasma, and phosphorylated tau (p-tau181) and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15), measured in serum, by Simoa or ELLA. ResultsAmong 1449 women [≥] 65 years, 38.4% self-reported a hysterectomy. Among 893 postmenopausal women without a history of hysterectomy (mean [SD] age at biomarker collection, 75.2 [7.2] years; mean age at menopause, 50.2 [5.2] years), menopausal timing was nonlinearly associated with NfL. Between menopausal ages 45-50, menopause timing was associated with higher NfL (0.010 SD units/year, [95% CI: -0.007, 0.027]), while from menopausal ages 50-55, the association reversed (b= -0.031, [95% CI: -0.051, -0.011]). Associations with GFAP or pTau-181 were not significant, but were directionally similar to those observed for NfL. Later menopausal timing linearly associated with lower GDF-15 (b = -0.015, [95% CI: -0.027, -0.004]). Self-reported hysterectomy was associated with higher GDF-15 (b= 0.118, [95% CI: 0.015, 0.220]), but not other biomarkers. Associations did not significantly differ by APOE {varepsilon}4 status. Conclusions and RelevanceIn a nationally representative study, earlier age at menopause in midlife was associated with later life AD/ADRDs biomarkers reflecting neuroaxonal degeneration and inflammation, underscoring the importance of understanding reproductive aging in dementia risk. KEY POINTSO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSWhat is the association between menopausal timing and blood-based Alzheimers disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) biomarkers among postmenopausal women 65 years and older in the United States? FindingsMenopausal timing is associated with higher NfL in women who experienced menopause before age 50, but lower NfL in women with menopausal ages after 50. Earlier menopausal timing is linearly associated with higher GDF-15. Secondary analyses showed associations between hysterectomy history and higher GDF-15. MeaningYounger menopausal timing associates with higher AD/ADRD-related biomarkers measured decades later in a population-based cohort, underscoring a link between reproductive aging and future neurodegenerative risk.

title: Smoking trajectories and brain health in middle-aged adults: a 15-year longitudinal study
text: BackgroundSmoking is a prevalent and preventable risk factor for poor brain health. These habits often establish in early adulthood and have lasting consequences, yet most research focuses on later-life smoking, overlooking important prevention windows. We examined smoking trajectories from early adulthood in relation to midlife brain health. MethodsIn 1,900 adults (65.6% female, mean age 32.5 years) from the Dutch population-based Generation R Study (ORACLE subset), smoking was assessed five times over 15 years, from before pregnancy to midlife. K-means clustering identified smoking trajectories, alongside measures of current smoking, pack-years, and abstinence years. At mean age 47.7 years, MRI assessed gray and white matter volumes, white-matter hyperintensity volume, cerebrovascular markers, and vertex-wise cortical thickness and surface area. FindingsFive trajectories were identified: non-smoking (63%), quitting before pregnancy (12%), quitting during/after pregnancy (11%), relapsing (9%), and persistent smoking (4%). All compared with non-smoking, quitting before pregnancy was associated with 6.57 cm3 larger gray matter (95%CI[0.27,12.87],p=.041), 7.71 cm3 larger white matter (95%CI[0.77,14.65],p=.030), and larger cortical surface area in bilateral middle/inferior temporal regions. Quitting during/after pregnancy was associated with more lacunes (OR=2.39; 95%CI[1.23,4.68],p=.011), but similar brain volumes. Relapsing was associated with 0.15 standard deviations more white matter hyperintensity volume (95%CI[0.00,0.30],p=.045) and thinner regions in the right cortex. Persistent smoking had double white matter hyperintensities (0.31 standard deviations; 95%CI[0.10,0.50], p=.003) and widespread bilateral thinner cortices. Similarly, single-timepoint measures like current smoking (vs never smoking) were linked to 9.72 cm3 smaller gray matter volume (95%CI[-16.53,-2.19],p=.005), 0.17 standard deviations more hyperintensity volume (95%CI[0.03,0.32],p=.015), and widespread thinner cortices. Each additional pack-year was associated with 0.45 cm3 smaller gray matter volume (95%CI[-0.85,-0.06],p=.025); each additional abstinence year was associated with 0.01 standard deviations less hyperintensity volume (95%CI[-0.02,0.00],p=.022). InterpretationSmoking trajectories from early adulthood and midlife are associated with midlife brain health, supporting early and sustained smoking cessation. FundingHorizonEurope Research and Innovation Programme (HappyMums, grant agreement No 101057390); European Research Council (TEMPO, grant agreement No 101039672; ORACLE, grant agreement No 678543).

title: Distinct DNA-binding modes of Sp8 and Sp6 shape a hierarchical regulatory network in limb ectoderm
text: Sp8 and Sp6 are closely related transcription factors expressed in the limb ectoderm, where they control proximo-distal and dorso-ventral patterning, yet their direct targets and molecular mechanisms have remained unclear. Combining genome-wide chromatin occupancy with transcriptomic profiling in vivo, we identify shared and specific targets and reconstruct the Sp8/Sp6 gene regulatory network, establishing Sp8 as its dominant, hierarchical node. Mechanistically, the two factors diverge: Sp8 binds DNA directly at canonical GC-rich Sp motifs, regulating targets including Fgf8 and Sp6 itself, whereas Sp6 acts as a transcriptional cofactor. Via indirect binding to AT-rich motifs through Dlx, both cooperatively regulate limb-patterning pathways, including Wnt, FGF, TGF-β/BMP, and Notch. Biochemical assays confirm that both form homo- and heterodimers and interact with Dlx5 through their zinc-finger domains. Together, these findings reveal how Sp8 and Sp6 orchestrate AER formation and dorso-ventral patterning, providing a mechanistic framework for congenital limb malformations such as split-hand/foot malformation.

title: A defence-in-depth strategy for securing AI-driven biological sequence design
text: Generative artificial intelligence can design biological sequences, from proteins to whole genomes, opening opportunities for medicine and biotechnology, but the same capability can be misused. The Wübben Sandpit conference brought together experts in biology, AI, biosecurity, ethics, medicine and policy to ask how the field can capture the benefits while managing the risks. Here we set out a defence-in-depth strategy that builds safeguards into every stage, from the data used to train models, to the models themselves, to the synthesis of physical DNA. We argue that responsible governance is not a brake on progress but a precondition for it. Generative artificial intelligence can design biological sequences, from proteins to whole genomes, however this capability can be misused. Here the attendees of the Wübben Sandpit conference outline a defence-in-depth strategy that builds safeguards into every stage of sequence design.

title: An extracellular contractile injection system for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells
text: Protein delivery into plant cells remains a major barrier in plant biotechnology. The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system, a phage tail-like bacterial nanomachine that naturally delivers proteins into insect host cells. Here we retargeted PVCs to plants by engineering their tail fibres to recognize the plant cell surface receptor FLAGELLIN SENSITIVE 2 (FLS2). We designed and characterized a library of FLS2-targeting PVCs and evaluated their ability to deliver native and non-native cargoes, including a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and R2 retroelement genome editor. Engineered PVCs delivered Cre into wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells with efficiencies up to 16%. Delivery was FLS2 dependent and scaled with receptor abundance, reaching 75% of leaf cells in FLS2-overexpressing Arabidopsis . We further demonstrated the PVC-mediated delivery of R2 protein, resulting in the targeted insertion of a reporter gene into the plant genome and the expression of the integrated gene. This work establishes PVCs as a platform for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells, laying the foundation for targeted and precise plant genetic engineering.

title: MR1-dependent MAIT cell activation is regulated by autophagy-associated proteins
text: The antigen-presenting molecule, MR1, presents microbial metabolites to MAIT cells, a population of innate-like, antimicrobial T cells. It also presents an unidentified ligand to MR1-restricted T cells in the setting of cancer. The cellular cofactors that regulate MR1 antigen presentation have yet to be fully defined. We performed a mass spectrometry–based proteomics screen to identify MR1-interacting proteins and discovered the selective autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of SQSTM1/p62 increased MAIT cell activation in the presence of Escherichia coli but not the synthetic ligand 5-OP-RU, whereas depletion of Atg5 and Atg7, key autophagy proteins, increased MAIT activation irrespective of the ligand used. This regulation appears to occur at an early step in the MR1 trafficking pathway. These data implicate distinct roles for autophagy-associated proteins in the regulation of MR1 activity and highlight the contribution of the autophagy pathway to regulation of cellular antigen presentation.

title: Evolution of Chromosomal and Plasmid-Encoded β-Lactamases in Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter and Shared Features of VIM with NDM and IMP
Dynamic changes in mRNA isoform usage during human retinal organoid development
text: Alternative mRNA splicing is a key mechanism for generating isoform diversity in eukaryotic cells. However, the extent of the splicing changes that occur during complex regulatory processes like neurodevelopment are still incompletely characterized. We perform nanopore-based long-read RNA sequencing on differentiating human stem cell-derived retinal organoids to identify temporal patterns of isoform usage across developmental stages. We find that retinal organoids undergo dynamic shifts in isoform usage throughout differentiation, which are not necessarily accompanied with changes in overall gene expression, as is observed for many genes involved in the regulation of mRNA splicing itself. Further analysis of human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells uncovers neuron-specific splicing signatures. Additionally, allele-specific gene expression analysis reveals extensive allelic imbalance in induced pluripotent stem cell-derived organoid cultures. By combining direct long-read RNA sequencing with human stem cell retinal models we develop a comprehensive database of isoform-level changes in differentiating human retinal organoid cells during development. These results uncover dynamic shifts in transcript usage during retinal differentiation, adding to our knowledge base of post-transcriptional RNA processing in the developing central nervous system and human in vitro culture systems.

title: The histone demethylase KDM6B preserves adipogenic balance by restraining hypermetabolic LYVE1+ perivascular macrophages
text: White adipose tissue expandability protects against metabolic disease, yet the epigenetic programmes that maintain the macrophage states supporting this adaptation remain poorly defined. Here we show that the H3K27 demethylase KDM6B sustains LYVE1 + adipose tissue perivascular macrophages (PVMs) during diet-induced white adipose tissue expansion, thereby maintaining adipogenic balance. In humans, KDM6B expression in adipose tissue macrophages associates with insulin sensitivity, glycaemic control and reduced inflammation. In mice, myeloid Kdm6b deletion reprogrammes septal and capsular LYVE1 + macrophages towards a CLEC1A + hypermetabolic perivascular state, leading to defective adipogenesis, adipocyte hypertrophy, vascular rarefaction, inflammation and impaired glucose homeostasis. Mechanistically, KDM6B limits H3K27me3 deposition at the Bmp2 locus to maintain macrophage-derived BMP2 signalling to adipose progenitors. Myeloid Bmp2 deletion partially recapitulates Kdm6b -deficient adipose dysfunction, whereas recombinant BMP2 promotes homeostatic tissue remodelling. Collectively, KDM6B acts as an epigenetic switch controlling the metabolic fate of LYVE1 + PVMs, maintaining the balance between adipogenesis-supportive and metabolic PVM states that determine adipose tissue expandability and metabolic homeostasis.

title: NKTR-255, a polymer-conjugated IL-15, enhances CAR T cell therapy by engaging endogenous antitumor immunity
text: CAR-T cells have yet to show widespread efficacy in solid tumors due in part to poor persistence and dysfunction in the tumor microenvironment. Further, heterogenous expression of target antigens can lead to escape of antigen-null tumors that resist CAR-T killing. Strategies to cooperatively boost both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity may be critical for achieving durable efficacy in cancer patients. NKTR-255 is a polymer-conjugated IL-15 with extended half-life that can boost endogenous T and NK cells, as well as CD19 CAR-T cells in B cell malignancies. However, whether NKTR-255 is sufficient to overcome CAR-T dysfunction in the suppressive solid tumor microenvironment, and how NKTR-255 and CAR-Ts together re-shape endogenous antitumor immunity, is not known. Using mouse models of ROR1+ lung adenocarcinoma, we show that NKTR-255 significantly boosted accumulation and function of tumor-infiltrating CAR-T cells targeting ROR1. Compared with NKTR-255 or CAR-T treatment alone, combination of NKTR-255 and CAR-T therapy increased endogenous tumor-specific T cells that preserved a PD-1+Tcf1+ stem-like phenotype. Consequently, NKTR-255 and CAR-T combination therapy completely eliminated ROR1+ tumor cells and significantly improved survival, with enhanced tumor control dependent on both CAR-Ts and endogenous T cells, though all mice ultimately succumbed to progression of ROR1- tumor. Compared to IL-15-armored CAR-T cells, systemic NKTR-255 induced greater accumulation and reduced terminal differentiation of endogenous tumor-specific T cells, resulting in superior tumor control. Thus, combining NKTR-255 with CAR-T therapy is a promising strategy to enhance both CAR-T and endogenous antitumor immunity to promote coordinated control of aggressive tumors.

title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
text: As a primary port of pathogen entry, the intestinal mucosa has developed a sophisticated set of defences to ward off infections. Investigating the human-specific intestinal barrier responses to pathogens is limited by the lack of models integrating the necessary architectural complexity with an autologous immune compartment 1 . Here we developed engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon combining a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. These tissues recapitulate morphological and functional properties that are region specific and compare with those of the native organ. We use the model to characterize the human epithelial response to Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium at the single-cell level, uncovering the distinct gene regulatory networks that underpin luminal versus intracellular pathogen presence. Invaded epithelial cells initiate an IL-18 signalling axis that triggers cytotoxic T cell activation, resulting in epithelial shedding and barrier disruption. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial and immune compartments, providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

title: Diurnal rhythmicity in metabolism and salivary effector expression shapes aphid performance on host plants
text: Diurnal rhythms influence insect behavior, physiology, and metabolism, optimizing their performance by adapting to daily changes in the environment. While their impact on agricultural pests has been briefly explored, our understanding of how these rhythms drive adaptive responses in pest biology and influence host colonization remains elusive. Here, we show that a notorious global aphid pest, Rhopalosiphum padi , exhibits distinct diurnal patterns in feeding behavior, with elevated honeydew excretion at night and extended phloem salivation during early nighttime. Temporal aphid transcriptome profiling reveals four diurnally rhythmic clusters, two of which peak at night, exhibiting enrichment in carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism. Beyond the established role in manipulating host responses and allowing sustained feeding, our study reveals novel evidence of cyclical fluctuations in salivary effector expression in an insect species. Silencing key effector genes, peaking in expression during the increased nighttime salivation, results in a more pronounced reduction in aphid excretion activity on host plants during the night compared to the day, a phenomenon not observed on artificial diets. A better understanding of aphid diurnal rhythms and their roles in shaping aphid performance provides a promising avenue to refine and optimize pest management, granting a strategic advantage for minimizing crop damage.

title: How the layer-dependent ratio of excitatory to inhibitory cells shapes cortical coding in balanced networks
text: The cerebral cortex exhibits a sophisticated neural architecture across its six layers. Recently, it was found that these layers exhibit different ratios of excitatory to inhibitory (EI) neurons, ranging from 4 to 9. This ratio is a key factor for achieving the often reported balance of excitation and inhibition, a hallmark of cortical computation. Although previous studies have explored various biologically realistic aspects of classical balanced networks, such as the effects of more complex neuronal properties including spike frequency adaptation using adaptive exponential integrate-and-fire (AdEx) neuron models (1), the temporal evolution of randomly connected balanced networks through second-order mean-field approximations (2), predictions of nonlinear dynamics across diverse neuron models ranging from integrate-and-fire to Hodgkin–Huxley formulations, thus bridging population dynamics to neuronal electrophysiology (3), the impact of spatial heterogeneity in balanced networks (4–6), and variations in synaptic timescales (7), the specific effects of differences in excitatory-inhibitory (EI) ratios on layer-specific dynamics and computational properties have, to the best of our knowledge, not yet been addressed. We investigate this question using a sparsely connected network model of excitatory and inhibitory neurons. To keep the network in a physiological range of firing rates, we varied the inhibitory firing threshold or the synaptic strength between excitatory and inhibitory neurons. We find that decreasing the EI ratio allows the network to explore a higher-dimensional space and enhance its capacity to represent complex input. By comparing the empirical EI ratios of layer 2/3 and layer 4 in the rodent barrel cortex, we predict that layer 2/3 has a higher dimensionality and coding capacity than layer 4. Furthermore, our analysis of primary visual cortex data from the Allen Brain Institute corroborates these modeling results, also demonstrating increased dimensionality and coding capabilities of layer 2/3.

title: Allometric analysis reveals distinct anatomical patterning and genetic architecture across wheat nodal roots
text: Root anatomical traits influence resource acquisition, metabolic costs, hydraulic conductance, and stress adaptation in cereal crops. Although classified as a single root class, nodal roots may differ anatomically according to their position along the culm. As shown in maize, this variation is particularly notable in root cross-sectional area (RxA). However, it remains unclear whether these differences reflect developmental differentiation or simply variation associated with RxA. We quantified root anatomical traits across four main-culm nodes (basal to apical) in 190 hexaploid wheat genotypes grown under field and greenhouse conditions. To distinguish RxA-dependent from RxA-independent anatomical variation, we applied allometric size correction, adjusting traits to a reference RxA, and conducted parallel genome-wide association studies (GWAS) using raw and size-corrected traits. Raw measurements revealed increases in RxA and cortical area from basal to apical nodes, accompanied by decreases in metaxylem area. After correction to a common reference RxA within each environment, anatomical differences among nodal positions persisted, with roots emerging from more apical nodes exhibiting smaller stele and metaxylem areas. Differences in cortical area were primarily associated with greater cortical cell file layer number rather than increased mean cortical cell diameter. GWAS identified largely distinct genetic associations for raw and RxA-corrected anatomical traits, varying across nodal positions and environments. Together, these findings demonstrate that anatomical variation across the wheat nodal root system cannot be explained by RxA alone. Our results highlight nodal position and allometric scaling as important considerations for anatomical phenotyping and distinguishing genetic associations with overall root cross-sectional area from those with tissue organisation.

title: The RdRp Thumb-1 Pocket Is a Conserved Target for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development
text: RNA viruses cause human diseases ranging from mild colds to deadly pandemics. Direct-acting, broad-spectrum, non-nucleoside antivirals have been characterized as impossible to develop because allosteric binding sites are poorly conserved. The HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) Thumb-1 allosteric site and its interaction with the HCV NS5B Λ1-loop governs an essential conformational change required for polymerase initiation. The only approved NS5B Thumb-1 inhibitor, beclabuvir, has been shown to be inactive against a broad panel of non-HCV viruses, including poliovirus, rhinovirus, coronavirus, coxsackievirus, influenzavirus, and HIV. A conserved, homologous allosteric site on RdRp that spans multiple viral families has not been reported. Here, we report GALILEO’s discovery that the Thumb-1 pocket, its associated Λ1-loop and their interaction are conserved between RNA viral families for the first time. The discovery is structurally validated through comparative analysis of Protein Data Bank (PDB)-deposited viral polymerases utilizing a method that allows independent, public validation. We further demonstrate that beclabuvir’s dependence on its indole C6 carbonyl to interact with the HCV-specific residue R503 restricts its activity to HCV. The discovery is biochemically validated with MDL-001, which does not contain a C6 carbonyl substituent. MDL-001 directly blocks viral RNA synthesis in isolated HCV and SARS-CoV-2 replication complexes and selects for the canonical Thumb-1 resistance mutation P495S in HCV NS5B. The discovery is validated at the cellular level through demonstration of MDL-001’s broad-spectrum, in vitro inhibition of both HCV and SARS-CoV-2. Preclinical proof of concept and development of MDL-001 in HCV, HBV, HDV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV have been previously reported. These findings establish RdRp Thumb-1 as a conserved allosteric pocket and a druggable target for broad-spectrum direct-acting antiviral development.

title: Antifungal Activities of Thymol against Aspergillus versicolor on Wheat Grains in the Post-harvest Period: in Silico, in Vitro, and in Vivo Approaches
text: Aspergillus versicolor (A. versicolor) is a toxigenic fungus species that causes significant post-harvest food spoilage. It is present in several foods, including wheat. The pathogenicity of this species is mainly related to the production of mycotoxins, primarily sterigmatocystin, a carcinogenic toxin that threatens human and animal health. The aim of this work is to conduct in silico, in vitro, and in vivo studies to evaluate the antifungal activity of thymol, a major compound of thyme essential oil (EO), against A. versicolor. Molecular docking of thymol was performed against two fungal proteins, specifically cutinase and chitin synthase. Thymol shows strong interaction with these two target proteins, forming conventional hydrogen bonds. In order to determine the antifungal potential of thymol against A. versicolor in vitro, the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum fungicidal concentration (MFC) were evaluated in agar medium. The results obtained show a significant antifungal effect of thymol against A. versicolor, with a MIC value of around 0.5 mg/mL and an MFC value double that of the MIC. The MIC concentration causes total inhibition of mycelial growth, resulting in 95% destruction of A. versicolor spores after 24 hours of exposure. Regarding the treatment of grains with thymol, a concentration of 1 mg/mL corresponds to the MFC, causing total inhibition of A. versicolor fungal proliferation and ensuring protection during 8 weeks of storage. A 100% germination rate of wheat grains treated with the MIC concentration thus ensures the agricultural safety of thymol. The results suggest that the antifungal effect of thymol, combined with its safety for wheat, presents a promising alternative for the development of a fungicide for the post-harvest preservation of grains in general, and wheat in particular, against storage fungi. Keywords: Antifungal potential, postharvest fungi, natural compound, grain storage, molecular docking.
