title: New approach methodologies in nanomedicine: bridging the gap between in silico , in vitro , and in vivo systems
text: Rapid advances in biomedical research and nanomedicine have driven the development and implementation of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) for predictive evaluations of novel formulations.

title: Climate Resilience and Smart Community Governance Through Digital Transformation
text: This research has investigated the concept of digital transformation as a way to build climate resilience and smart community governance. In particular, this study sought to explore the ways in which digital technology, data-driven decision-making, intelligent infrastructures, and participatory governance can help communities prepare for, respond to, and recover from climate risks. In this regard, qualitative and conceptual research approach has been used in order to identify relevant concepts of climate resilience, smart community, digital governance, sustainability, and community participation. Technologies that may contribute to climate risk assessment, resource management, emergency response, and community planning such as artificial intelligence, IoT, big data analytics, cloud computing, digital platforms, and geographic information systems have been considered in the analysis. This research has developed a conceptual framework that incorporates climate risk assessment, digital data gathering, intelligent analysis, smart infrastructures, stakeholder participation, adaptive governance, and continuous monitoring into an organized resilience process. In addition, special attention was paid to transparency, inclusiveness, accessibility, data security, privacy, and human-centered decision-making in digital transformation. According to the research, digital transformation can serve as an integrative platform for addressing climate risks, coordination of institutions, evidence-based governance, and increasing community resilience. The framework highlighted that the use of technology should supplement but not substitute human thinking, institutional accountability, and community engagement. The research made a contribution to the formation of a conceptual basis for the combination of digital transformation and climate-resilient/smart community governance.

title: Exploring Trust Calibration in XAI - The Impact of Exposing Model Limitations to Lay Users
text: Trust calibration—aligning user trust judgment with model capability—is crucial for safe deployment of explainable AI (XAI), yet is often evaluated via global trust ratings detached from objective performance evidence. We present a preregistered, incentivized between-subject online study (N = 418 representative UK sample) on explainable skin-lesion classification that disentangles expectation-setting from experienced performance. Participants completed 15 case evaluations using a fixed XAI panel (malignancy score, reliability score, and saliency map). We systematically manipulated five experimental onboarding conditions varying example-based information and limitation disclosures with five stimulus packages naturally varying observed prediction quality. Calibration was operationalized as the deviation between trust-related judgments (TAIS and case-wise ratings) and objective performance benchmarks for the encountered cases, analysed with hierarchical mixed-effects models. Only limitation disclosure for case-wise measures reliably impacts trust calibration, and short-term experience did not yield progressive calibration. Further, the experienced package of stimuli explained substantially more variance than the experimental manipulation. However, participants were hard-pressed to differentiate between case-wise perceived trust, trustworthiness, and accuracy estimation. We discuss implications for designing limitation communication and for measuring and analysing calibration metrics in XAI evaluations. All study materials and data of this study are publicly available for replication and further academic use.

title: Enhancing Performance and User Engagement in Everyday Stress Monitoring: A Context-Aware Active Reinforcement Learning Approach
text: Accurate stress monitoring in everyday settings requires informative labels without excessive user burden. Ecological Momentary Assessments (EMAs) provide self-reported labels, but poorly timed or frequent prompts can reduce their utility. This article presents a context-aware active reinforcement learning algorithm for stress detection using photoplethysmography (PPG) from smartwatches and contextual data from smartphones. The algorithm uses the user’s current context and response history to decide when to trigger an EMA. We first evaluate context-aware label selection in an offline study and then deploy the approach for real-time EMA triggering in a separate online cohort. Under the reported evaluation, Random Forest F1 increased from 0.21 for the offline cohort to 0.32 for the online cohort; adding contextual features increased it to 0.36. Personalization increased AUC by up to 0.10 across Random Forest, XGBoost, and SVM classifiers. These results support context-aware EMA scheduling and personalized modeling for real-world stress monitoring, while differences between the study cohorts limit causal attribution of the observed performance gains.

title: Adult Glioma Segmentation in Sub-Saharan Africa Using Transfer Learning on Stratified Finetuning Data
Optimizing Brain Tumor Segmentation with MedNeXt: BraTS 2024 SSA and Pediatrics
Improved Multi-task Brain Tumour Segmentation with Synthetic Data Augmentation
Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Improved Convolutional Baseline for Brain Tumor Segmentation in Sub-saharan Africa Adult Glioma Dataset
Information Overload and Disutility in Generative AI Systems as Cognitive Extension: A Bounded Rationality Perspective
text: Generative AI systems promise cognitive extensions by enhancing information access and use. However, from the bounded rationality perspective, their utility is fundamentally constrained by inherent human cognitive limitations. This article argues that when the volume of AI-generated information exceeds users’ processing capacity governed by working memory constraints, attentional resources, and verification capabilities, it produces cognitive disutility rather than enhancement. We introduced a formal model to quantify this interaction, demonstrating that net cognitive benefits decline systematically as information overload increases beyond individual processing thresholds. The analysis reveals that successful cognitive extension depends not on maximizing informational output but on strategically aligning AI design with human cognitive ergonomics and individual differences in processing capacity. Ultimately, truly augmentative systems must minimize cognitive overhead to prevent overload, while preserving users' epistemic agency and decision-making autonomy.

title: Genome-resolved metagenomics reveals population-dependent gut microbiome responses to albendazole-ivermectin treatment
text: Soil-transmitted helminth control relies on mass anthelmintic treatment, yet helminth-anthelmintic-microbiome interactions and their role on treatment response remain poorly understood. We characterised the microbiome, resistome, and functional profiles of 858 paired stool metagenomes from 429 children treated with albendazole or a fixed-dose albendazole-ivermectin co-formulation in the ALIVE clinical trial in Ethiopia and Mozambique. Baseline microbiome composition differed more by country than infection status and was not associated with albendazole efficacy or adverse events. Co-formulation treatment, particularly three consecutive daily doses, was associated with depletion of Enterobacteriaceae, predominantly Escherichia coli, in Ethiopia, with reductions in E. coli-associated resistance genes and metabolic pathways. Genome-resolved analyses of over 22,000 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes confirmed this depletion across multiple E. coli strain-level populations, linking taxonomic, resistome, and functional signals to one ecological event. These findings reveal an off-target effect of combination anthelmintic treatment relevant to large-scale deworming programmes and expand genomic resources for African gut microbiota.

title: Bilayer Composition Controls Ferrocyanide Permeability in Soy Lecithin Vesicles
text: Soy lecithin vesicles are attractive nanocarriers owing to their biocompatibility, stability, and low cost. However, controlling the permeability of their bilayer remains a key challenge for their rational use in delivery systems. In this work, we demonstrate that the permeability of soy lecithin vesicles can be systematically tuned by modifying the bilayer composition through the incorporation of dioleoylphosphatidylcholine (DOPC), dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC), and cholesterol. The resulting vesicular systems were characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS), fluorescence spectroscopy using 6‐propionyl‐2‐dimethylaminonaphthalene (PRODAN) as a probe of the bilayer microenvironment, and electrochemical measurements of potassium ferrocyanide (K 4 [Fe(CN) 6 ]) release. Changes in lipid composition produced distinct PRODAN responses, consistent with differences in probe localization and bilayer organization, and markedly altered permeability toward encapsulated K 4 [Fe(CN) 6 ]. The studied formulations spanned a broad range of K 4 [Fe(CN) 6 ] release behaviors, from substantial retention to complete release at different rates. These results show that relatively small compositional changes provide a practical strategy for tuning the transport of this ionic probe across soy lecithin bilayers. Because permeability depends on the physicochemical nature of the encapsulated species, each prospective cargo must be evaluated in the selected formulation.

title: Training-data provenance, participant consent, licences and intended-use restrictions in brain foundation models on Hugging Face
text: Introduction: Brain foundation models pretrained on electroencephalographic, magnetoencephalographic and functional magnetic resonance recordings are distributed through public model repositories, yet the governance documentation that accompanies them has not been measured systematically. Methods: A cross-sectional audit coded four documentation dimensions (licence, training-data provenance, participant consent and intended-use restrictions) in 66 brain foundation models and their referenced training datasets retrieved programmatically from a public model repository, and tested four hypotheses with exact statistical tests plus two sensitivity analyses. Results: Licence documentation reached 89.4% (95% CI 79.7 to 94.8) and training-data provenance 81.8% (95% CI 70.9 to 89.3), whereas participant consent was documented in 0 of 66 models (95% CI 0 to 5.5) and intended-use restrictions in 10.6%. Documentation completeness increased with model popularity (rho 0.58, p < 0.001). None of the 25 distinct training-dataset identifiers named in model cards resolved to a repository dataset card. Conclusions: Brain foundation models are released with licences and provenance notes but almost uniformly without consent or use-restriction documentation, concentrating the governance gap on participant consent rather than on licensing.

title: Chemotherapy-Minimized Blank Microsphere Transarterial Embolization (BMS-TACE) Plus Low-Dose Lenvatinib, Iparomlimab and Tuvonralimab, and SBRT in Hepatocellular Carcinoma With Macrovascular Tumor Thrombus
text: [Fase: PHASE2; Estado: RECRUITING] Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with macrovascular tumor thrombus carries a poor prognosis, and systemic therapy alone provides limited benefit in this population. This single-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial evaluates the efficacy and safety of a regimen combining chemotherapy-minimized, blank microsphere-based transarterial chemoembolization (BMS-TACE), low-dose lenvatinib, the anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody iparomlimab and tuvonralimab, and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). In BMS-TACE, blank microspheres are the principal embolic agent and chemotherapy is used only as an adjunct at a fixed, minimal dose (doxorubicin 10 mg and lobaplatin 10 mg), in order to limit chemotherapy-related liver injury and systemic toxicity and to allow repeated embolization in patients with limited hepatic reserve. Forty-two participants with BCLC stage C HCC and tumor thrombus in the main portal vein or superior mesenteric vein (Vp3/Vp4), hepatic vein, or inferior vena cava, without extrahepatic metastases, will be enrolled. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review using mRECIST.

title: Integrative Multi-omics Analysis to Predict Monoclonal Gammopathies Clinical Evolution
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] This prospective, multicenter, observational study aims to identify molecular and immunological markers associated with disease progression in patients with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM). By integrating genomic, transcriptomic, immunophenotypic, and oral microbiome analyses, the study seeks to characterize the biological mechanisms underlying the transition to symptomatic multiple myeloma (MM). The study also includes in vitro modeling to investigate bone damage and immune dysfunction. Healthy volunteers (HV) undergoing joint replacement surgery for osteoarthritis will serve as controls. The ultimate goal is to improve early risk stratification and support future preventive strategies through a multi-omics approach. There is a pressing need for new strategies to identify high-risk individuals based on biological rather than purely clinical parameters. This study proposes an integrative, multi-omics approach to investigate the transition from MGUS/SMM to MM. By analyzing the immunome and oral microbiome alongside molecular profiling, the goal is to identify reliable biomarkers of progression. The resulting insights could be enable more accurate risk stratification and guide the design of future preventive clinical trials aimed at delaying or halting disease evolution.

title: The Efficacy of Psilocybin Therapy for Depression in Parkinson's Disease
text: [Fase: PHASE2; Estado: RECRUITING] The purpose of this study is to understand whether people with Parkinson's Disease and depression have improvement in their symptoms after psilocybin therapy.

title: Natural History and Genetics of Food Allergy and Related Conditions
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] Background: \- About 15 million Americans have a food allergy. Because there are no cures or effective prevention or treatment for food allergies, researchers want to learn more about them. Objective: \- To learn more about the causes and effects of food allergy and related conditions. Eligibility: * People ages 2 99 who have food allergy and/or a related genetic or other condition * Their relatives * Healthy relatives and volunteers Design: * Participants will have at least 3 visits over 1 2 years, and then once a year for up to 12 years. Each may last a day or longer. * Participants will be screened with medical history, physical exam, and questionnaires. * Participants may have the following: * Blood tests * Allergy skin prick tests: Drops of allergens are placed on the back or arm. The skin is scratched under each drop. * Leukapheresis: blood is taken from a needle in one arm, passed through a machine, and returned through a needle in the other arm. * X-rays * Esophageal string test: One end of a string is taped to the cheek and the other end is packed into a capsule. When the capsule is swallowed, the string unwinds; it is left in for at least 1 hour. * EGD and colonoscopy: Biopsies are taken from the gastrointestinal system. * Tiny biopsies of skin * Photographs of the body * Collection of cells through: * Swab of nose, inside of cheek, or skin * Gentle skin scrape * Tape stripping: piece of tape is put on the skin and pulled off.

title: MicroRNAs as Biomarkers in First Episode Schizophrenia
text: [Fase: NA; Estado: RECRUITING] This study investigates whether tiny molecules called microRNAs (miRNAs), found in special brain-derived "packages" (neural-derived extracellular vesicles, or NDEs) that travel from the brain into the blood, can serve as helpful indicators (biomarkers) for schizophrenia. Currently, doctors diagnose schizophrenia and monitor treatment primarily through clinical interviews, which can be slow and imprecise. This study will work with 80 individuals recently diagnosed with first-episode schizophrenia who are beginning treatment with either aripiprazole or risperidone, along with 80 healthy volunteers. Blood samples will be collected from all participants. For individuals with schizophrenia, blood will be drawn at the beginning of treatment and again after 12 weeks. By comparing patterns of brain-derived miRNAs in the blood of patients versus healthy volunteers, and by observing changes in these miRNAs during treatment, the researchers hope to discover whether these molecules can help diagnose schizophrenia more quickly and predict how well a treatment will work. If successful, this study will provide initial evidence that these miRNAs could become valuable new tools leading to earlier, more accurate diagnoses and more personalized treatment selection.

title: Electrophysiologic Sleep Phenotyping and Sleep-Dependent Neuro-maturation in Clinical and Healthy Pediatric Populations
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING] Background: During the first few decades of life, the brain changes dramatically in shape and function. Sleep lets researchers measure these changes. Researchers want to create a database of sleep and neurodevelopmental data in a group of infants and children to learn more. Objective: To address a knowledge and data gap in the field of sleep and neurodevelopment in infants and children. Eligibility: Children ages 6 months to 76 months who may or may not be at risk for neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Also, children ages 6 months to 8 years who have a referral for a sleep study. Design: Participants will have neurodevelopmental testing. They will have a medical, psychiatric, and family history. They will have a physical and neurological exam. They will be interviewed and complete surveys. They will give a cheek swab and/or blood sample. Some participants will have 1 study visit that lasts 2 days. Other participants will have up to 4 study visits. Each visit will last 2 days. Visits occur every 8 months to 1 year, for a total participation time of 2 years. Participants will have a 20-minute daytime electroencephalogram (EEG), if possible. This EEG session will be used to calibrate the machine for the overnight study. Participants will take part in an inpatient overnight sleep study. Electrodes will be placed on the participants. For young children, parents will help place the EEG leads. Other sensors may also be placed. A gauze cap will be placed on participants head to protect the leads and keep the participants from moving them. 'Lights out' will occur as close to participants bedtime as possible. ...

title: Early Clonal Dynamics During Venetoclax Treatment for Relapsed or Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
text: [Fase: PHASE2; Estado: RECRUITING] Background: The drug venetoclax treats chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Researchers want to find better treatments for CLL. To do that, they need to learn how the drug affects CLL cancer cells and the immune system. Objective: To learn about genetic changes that happen during treatment of CLL with venetoclax. Eligibility: Adults ages 18 and older with relapsed or refractory CLL after at least 1 prior therapy Design: Participants will be screened under a separate protocol. In Phase 1, participants will get venetoclax free of charge through the NIH. Venetoclax is started at a low dose. The dose will be increased every week until participants reach their maximum tolerable dose. This usually take about 5 weeks. Participants will visit the NIH at least once per week. Visits will be about 4 hours. They may have to stay in the hospital to be observed. In Phase 2, participants will continue to get the drug through their local cancer doctor and their health insurance. Patients will also visit the NIH every 6 months, or if their disease progresses. At the NIH participants will have regular health assessments. These will include physical exams and a review of the medicines they are taking. They will talk about how they are feeling. The study included the following tests: Blood draws CT scans: Participants will lie in a machine that takes pictures of the body (maximum 3 per year) Bone marrow biopsies: A small amount of marrow will be taken out of the participant s hip bone with a needle. Optional lymph node biopsies: A small piece of the participant s tissue will be taken out with a needle. The study will last at least 2 years.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Next Generation CT Reconstruction (NextGenIR)
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] Background: \- Computed Tomography (CT) is a scan that makes detailed pictures of the body. It uses radiation to do that. In 2011, about 85.3 million CT scans were done in the United States. But there is growing concern about the health effects of radiation. There are new and different ways to make CT pictures that use less radiation. Researchers want to learn whether these new methods create images that are similar to images from a traditional CT. Objective: \- To learn if new CT imaging methods with less radiation make images that are similar to traditional ways. Eligibility: \- Adults 18 years of age and older who are scheduled for a CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast. Design: * Researchers will review participants medical records to see if they can be in this study. * Participants may have blood drawn from an arm vein by a needle stick. The blood will be used to make sure they can be in this study and that it is safe for them to have contrast. * During the participants CT scan appointment, one extra scan will be done using low radiation methods. * During a CT scan, the participant lies on a table. A large x-ray machine takes pictures of the body.

title: Novel Genetic Disorders of the Immune System
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] Background: \- The immune system helps the body fight infection and disease. People with immune system problems can get infections, blood disorders, and other health problems. Researchers want to learn more about the immune system, like what causes it to not work properly. Objectives: \- To evaluate people with certain types of immune system disorders. Eligibility: \- Adults and children with an immune disorder or symptoms of one, and their relatives. Some disorders are not included in this study. Design: * Researchers will review participants medical records. * Participants may mail in a blood or saliva sample, or be evaluated at the clinic. At the clinic, they may have a medical history, physical exam, blood tests, and imaging scans (with dye given through a needle in the arm). They may have genetic testing done on a sample of blood, saliva, hair, or nail clipping. * Participants may choose to have a skin biopsy. Up to 2 skin samples will be taken from their arm, back, or other area. A biopsy punch is inserted into the skin and rotated. A small circle of skin is removed. * Participants 10 and older may also choose to have leukapheresis. Blood is taken through a needle in one arm. It passes through a machine that separates the white blood cells. The rest of the blood is returned by needle in the other arm. * Researchers may recommend medicines, but no treatments are being studied. * Participants may be invited to return for visits over several years. At those visits, they may repeat some or all of the above tests. Or they may mail in blood or other samples. They may also send medical records.

title: Advanced Multisensorial System for Automatic Assessment of Neurological Disorders in Smart Spaces-Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (URJC)
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Neurological diseases affect people's cognitive and physical abilities, limiting their functional independence and causing disability, which in many cases, is progressive and degenerative. Being able to perform activities of daily living is a challenge in these pathologies. Currently, different observational tools are administered to assess the degree of functional limitation in basic and instrumental Activities of Daily Living (ADL). However, the assessment must be performed in an ecological and real context to obtain objective information and ensure the most accurate assessment possible. To this end, it is necessary to consider the factors that influence the performance of ADLs and also on the quality of their execution, especially in this population in which the stressful situation of direct observation by an evaluator has a direct influence on the final score. Advanced Multisensorial System for Automatic Assessment of Neurological Disorders in Smart Spaces (NeurEYE) aims to develop technological tools to extract from sensory systems typical of intelligent spaces and with the help of signal processing and machine learning processes based on artificial intelligence, indicators of neurological impairment that influence functional capacity and function/dysfunction components while observing the performance of an activity of daily living. In addition, NeurEYE would provide as a scientific breakthrough the accurate description of subjects' limitations in the controlled assessment environment within the routine patient context. The NeurEye project will allow the clinical validation of a multisensory system that, through the detection of functional limitations in the ADLs of patients with neurological disorder, allows to establish the level of disability of the subjects. In addition, the qualitative and quantitative description of the functional alterations of the person with neurological disorders and, the elimination of the subjective bias of the examiner, will allow the generation of individualized clinical and statistical reports according to sex, activity, etc. that will be clinically useful in the early detection, diagnosis, and adaptation of rehabilitation treatments to the specific functional needs of neurological disorders.

title: Oncological and Perioperative Outcomes of Laparoscopic Versus Robotic Partial Nephrectomy for Treatment of Renal Tumors.
text: [Fase: NA; Estado: COMPLETED] partial nephrectomy offers lower renal function impairment and equivalent oncological survival outcomes compared with radical nephrectomy in those with T1 tumors. As urology has embraced the gradual shift from open to minimally invasive surgery (MIS), PN is being completed more often by laparoscopic and robotic methods . The first laparoscopic transperitoneal partial nephrectomy was reported in 1993 by Winfield, with the retroperitoneal approach introduced 1 year later With advancing robotic technology and the development of the DaVinci system, urologists began to explore the realm of robotic-assisted urologic surgery. In 2004, Gettman et al. published a paper describing their experience with robotic-assisted laparoscopic partial nephrectomy. Moreover, robotic assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) and laparoscopic partial nephrectomy (LPN) seems to be significantly better than OPN in terms of perioperative complications, estimated blood loss and hospital stay. Conversely, transfusion rate, ischemia time, change in estimated glomerular filtration rate and early cancer outcomes are similar between the two approaches. International guidelines recommend the use of both approaches according to the surgeon and patient preferences. so, we are plaining to do the study comparing between RAPN and LPN regarding feasibility and ability of both techniques. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and computer vision, is increasingly used in urology for imaging, pathology, outcome prediction, and surgical video analysis. In surgery, it allows surgical phases, instrument movement, and technical skill to be measured objectively from routine video. In partial nephrectomy, AI has been applied to phase recognition, augmented-reality guidance, and measurement of warm ischemia time (WIT).

title: Protocol for generation, immunophenotyping, and live-cell cytotoxicity analysis of primary human CAR-NK cells using CRISPR-SaCas9 and AAV6.
text: Targeted gene editing enables controlled integration and consistent expression of a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) in natural killer (NK) cells. We present a protocol for homology-directed repair-mediated CAR knockin into the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus of expanded human NK cells using CRISPR-SaCas9 ribonucleoprotein electroporation and AAV6 donor-template delivery. We also detail the phenotypic analysis of CAR-NK cells using a 23-marker flow cytometry panel including CAR detection and describe a live-cell imaging assay to evaluate CAR-mediated and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity kinetics.

title: CD44+ Proximal Tubular Epithelial Cells May Be Involved in Renal Fibrosis and Inflammation via TGF-β Signaling in Hyperuricemic Nephropathy.
text: The prevalence of hyperuricemia (HUA) is continuously increasing and HUA may eventually develop into irreversible hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN). Injured proximal tubule (PT) in the HUA microenvironment plays an important role in the progression of HN. However, the underlying pathological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between HUA kidneys and control groups were screened from bulk RNA sequencing data to identify abnormally activated signaling. Subsequently, PT cell-subtypes related to injury and repair were identified in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Cellular functions of injured PT cells were identified via pseudotime analysis, cell communication analysis, and in silico perturbation. Additionally, spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics analyses were combined to validate the expression correlation of signature genes and the functional changes of PT in HUA kidneys. TGF-β signaling-associated genes were upregulated in HUA kidneys. Injured and repairing PT cell subtypes were identified in HUA kidneys with an increased proportion of the Injured subtype and a decreased proportion of the repairing subtype. Spp1 was identified as a signature gene of PT cells and injured PT cells in HUA kidneys. As the receptor of SPP1, CD44 was specifically upregulated in injured PT. Tgfb1 and Tgfbr1 were more highly expressed in the Injured PT subtypes and exhibited spatial overlap with Spp1 and Cd44. In silico perturbation of Cd44 in the Injured cell-subcluster predicted reduced expression of TGF-β signaling-related genes. Cell communication analysis predicted potential associations between CD44+ PT cells and increased SPP1-CD44 axis signaling via autocrine/paracrine SPP1. These predicted interactions may also be linked to TGF-β-associated signaling and to potential pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic functional programs in fibroblasts, macrophages, and dendritic cells (DCs). Additionally, spatial proteomics supported the high expression of TGF-β signaling-related proteins in PT. Computational analyses suggest that CD44+ PT cells are associated with TGF-β-related signaling and may interact with fibroblasts and immune cells through the SPP1-CD44 axis, representing the candidate cell population in the progression of inflammation and fibrosis in HN.

title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

title: Clinical research resources and researcher-facing query tools: a scoping review of maturity, usability, and implications for oral health.
text: To jointly map data-holding clinical research resources and researcher-facing query tools, assess how far the combined landscape has advanced toward query-ready infrastructure using a novel 4D maturity framework, and interpret implications for oral health. Following JBI scoping review guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting, we searched PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, the ACM Digital Library, and supplementary technical sources. Two reviewers independently screened all records and applied a predefined maturity framework: operational readiness (R), governance and access (G), query-system maturity (Q), and evidence maturity (E) to each retained unit. Of 675 unique records, 58 analytic units were retained: 39 data-holding resources and 19 query tools. The dominant pattern was a maturity-usability mismatch: 25 of 37 resources rated as operationally deployed (R ≥ 3) had no or minimally documented query layers (Q ≤ 1). Query tools showed rapid technical evolution toward NLP- and LLM-assisted interfaces, but validation consistently lagged behind functionality as only 1 tool demonstrated independently documented sustained research use. Oral health lacked advanced query capability and broadly interoperable, governed multi-site infrastructure at the scale seen in general medicine. Governance and operational deployment are more mature than researcher-facing usability across the clinical research data landscape. For oral health, the central gap is not a missing AI layer but the paucity of upstream building blocks (interoperable multi-site resources, governed discovery networks, and openly documented query environments) from which a credible research workbench could be built.

title: Mapping the global landscape of research on primary and secondary headaches from 2000 to 2025: a bibliometric analysis.
text: To map research on primary and secondary headaches, including its interface with dentistry, in PubMed records entered in 2000-2025. PubMed records were retrieved with two strategies based on the International Classification of Headache Disorders and restricted to a validated thematic core; citations came from NIH iCite. Output, citation impact and flows, collaboration, co-citation and bursts of Medical Subject Headings were analyzed. Of 50,825 records, 40,441 formed the core (precision 92.0%; estimated sensitivity 99.2%). Annual output rose from 747 to 2,522 articles (modeled growth 4.0% annually), with a roughly stable MEDLINE share. The United States led production (29.8%) and China grew fastest. Migraine appeared in 68.7% of articles, secondary headaches in 12.2% and tension-type headache in 8.8%; the latter's share declined (odds ratio per decade 0.69; 95% confidence interval 0.65-0.72). Research shifted from triptans to calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) therapies, with bursts in CGRP antagonists, genetics and machine learning. The dental interface (temporomandibular disorders, bruxism, orofacial pain) appeared in 1.3% of articles; only 1.0% of all articles were in dental journals, which received one third of expected citations. Headache research grew with the biomedical literature and turned toward targeted therapies; tension-type headache is underrepresented given its prevalence, and the dental interface was small, with few articles in dental journals and limited uptake. Headache often coexists with temporomandibular disorders and sleep bruxism, yet few studies address dental aspects. The core journals and gaps identified can help dentists and researchers navigate the literature and identify research priorities.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of mortality at candidemia diagnosis: development and external validation across multicentre cohorts.
text: Early identification of candidemia patients at high risk of death may inform clinical management. We aimed to develop and externally validate a clinically interpretable machine learning model to predict 30-day all-cause mortality at candidemia diagnosis. The derivation cohort comprised pooled data from three prospective Spanish cohorts including adults with candidemia. Following benchmarking of seven supervised algorithms, an XGBoost algorithm was developed using nested cross-validation. Discrimination was assessed by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR). Calibration was assessed by calibration plots, intercept and slope. Overall performance was assessed by Brier score and scaled Brier score. Model interpretability was evaluated using Shapley additive explanations values. External validation used an international cohort from the European Confederation of Medical Mycology Candida III study. Among 1,640 patients in the derivation cohort, 476/1,640 (29%) died within 30 days. The final model retained nine predictors of mortality: age, neoplasia, chronic kidney disease, chronic liver disease, recent surgery, septic shock, intensive care unit setting, presumed catheter-related source, and corticosteroid exposure. The derivation AUC-ROC was 0.749 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.723-0.775), AUC-PR 0.562 (95% CI 0.522-0.607), and Brier score 0.171 (95% CI 0.164-0.178). In the external validation cohort (n = 632 patients, 228/632, 36% mortality), AUC-ROC was 0.668 (95% CI 0.628-0.710), AUC-PR 0.515 (95% CI 0.467-0.574), and Brier score 0.218 (95% CI 0.204-0.232). Logistic recalibration improved the Brier score to 0.213 (95% CI 0.203-0.222) without changing discrimination. This multicentre study developed and externally validated a machine-learning model using routinely available clinical variables that may provide a framework for early risk stratification of 30-day mortality in patients with candidemia. External validation showed lower discrimination and the need for recalibration, supporting further local validation before clinical implementation.

title: Development and Application of Deep Learning Models for Case Finding From Pathology Reports in a Hospital-Based Cancer Registry: Algorithm Development and Validation.
text: Few studies have investigated automated case finding in hospital-based cancer registries despite their crucial role in supporting population-based surveillance. In these settings, data completeness is often compromised by referral patterns, yet the influence of weakly supervised learning strategies on model performance remains underexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different supervision approaches (inaccurate, inexact, and report-level labeling) on deep learning model performance for cancer case finding in a hospital-based registry setting and assess model generalizability across patient-level and report-level classification tasks. Hospital-based cancer registry and pathology report data from Songklanagarind Hospital (2005-2023) were used for model development and evaluation. Three labeling approaches were implemented: inaccurate (all reports from patients with cancer labeled positive), inexact (concatenated reports from patients with cancer labeled positive), and report-level (only registrar-annotated tumor-related reports labeled positive). Model performance was evaluated on max-pooled, concatenated, and individual report classification tasks using a simple word embedding model, multilayer perceptron, recurrent neural network, convolutional neural network (CNN), and hierarchical self-attention network architectures. Models trained using weakly supervised labeling achieved the highest performance across patient-level evaluation tasks, and CNN models consistently showed superior performance. While report-level labeling yielded superior accuracy for individual reports, it suffered substantial degradation in patient-level evaluations. This suggests that models trained on curated data overfitted to primary tumor patterns, failing to recognize secondary evidence (eg, metastatic or surveillance findings). Conversely, weakly supervised approaches enabled the detection of patients with cancer via diverse report types. Error analysis revealed that false negatives were primarily driven by insufficient institutional data-specifically, referred patients lacking primary diagnostic reports-rather than algorithmic failure. In this single tertiary referral hospital setting, weakly supervised labeling outperformed report-level human annotation for patient-level case finding, whereas report-level labeling performed best for individual report classification. The CNN architecture achieved the highest or near-highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve in most configurations.

title: Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design.
text: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a transformative therapeutic strategy for eliminating disease-associated proteins, including targets that remain challenging to modulate using conventional occupancy-driven inhibitors. Among TPD approaches, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) exploit the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to induce selective and event-driven degradation of proteins of interest (POIs). Despite rapid advances in PROTAC development, successful translation depends on interconnected determinants, including target degradability, ubiquitin ligase (E3) recruitment, warhead and linker properties, ternary-complex formation, ubiquitination efficiency, intracellular exposure, and pharmacokinetic behavior. This review provides an integrated, mechanism-oriented analysis of these determinants by linking PROTAC design, ubiquitination biology, computational approaches, and clinical development. We examine key principles governing PROTAC-mediated degradation, with emphasis on E3-ligase selection, linker design, ternary-complex geometry and cooperativity, ubiquitin (Ub)-acceptor lysine (Lys) accessibility, ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme (E2)/E3 context, proteasomal engagement, inefficient degradation, and the hook effect. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for degradation-activity prediction, E3-ligase/POI pairing, ligand and linker optimization, ternary-complex modeling, and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) assessment are critically evaluated alongside their technical and translational limitations. Preclinical developments, clinical-stage degraders, emerging TPD modalities, and major barriers to translation are also discussed. We propose an integrated framework linking distinct target ubiquitination patterns, degrader design, ternary-complex geometry, AI-enabled prediction, and pharmacokinetic/clinical constraints, providing a mechanism-informed roadmap for the rational development of next-generation protein degraders and identifying mechanistic bottlenecks and translational priorities across therapeutic settings.

title: From Technical Performance to Clinical Impact: Challenges and Opportunities for AI Modelling of CKD Progression.
text: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, with highly heterogeneous trajectories ranging from long-term stability to rapid progression towards kidney failure and kidney replacement therapy. Accurate prediction of CKD progression is essential to support personalised monitoring, timely therapeutic intensification, nephrology referral, and preparation for advanced kidney care. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) approaches may improve risk stratification by modelling complex, nonlinear, and time-dependent patterns in routinely collected clinical data, electronic health records, and potentially multimodal data sources. Nonetheless, it remains unclear how ready these AI-driven models are for clinical use. This structured narrative review aimed to map the current landscape of AI for predicting CKD progression, assess the robustness and clinical relevance of the evidence, and identify methodological and implementation gaps that must be addressed to translate technical accuracy into clinical impact. This review synthesised 35 studies published between 2020 and 2025 that developed and evaluated models to predict CKD progression. Most studies used retrospective cohort designs and electronic health record data, relying mainly on demographic variables, laboratory measures, comorbidities, and clinical history. Tree-based models, random forests, boosting methods, regression-based approaches, and neural networks were the most commonly investigated methods. Overall, the reviewed models often achieved favourable discriminative performance, as measured by AUROC or C-index. Nevertheless, the evidence base remains limited by substantial heterogeneity in study designs, cohort compositions, prediction targets, time horizons, feature engineering, and validation strategies. External validation was reported in only about one-quarter of studies, while calibration, clinical utility, patient-level uncertainty, and implementation-oriented evaluation were inconsistently addressed. Prediction endpoints were predominantly kidney failure-related. Multimodal data, including imaging, genomics, and social determinants of health, were rarely used, and explainability methods were more often applied for model description than for clinician-facing decision support. AI models show substantial promise for predicting CKD progression, particularly when trained on routinely available clinical data. However, the field remains more advanced in model development than in clinical validation and implementation. Future research should prioritise external and temporal validation, systematic calibration assessment, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis, comparison with established clinical risk scores, clinically meaningful prediction horizons, subgroup and fairness evaluation, patient-level uncertainty estimation, and prospective testing of model-informed care. These steps are essential to move from statistically accurate models to reliable, interpretable, equitable, and actionable tools for CKD management.

title: How AI curates evidence on a contested health topic: a consumer health information quality assessment of generative AI and conventional search responses to Tylenol-autism queries.
text: To assess whether consumer artificial intelligence (AI) platforms assemble systematically different evidence bases on a contested health topic than a clinician-oriented tool and conventional search engines, and whether any differences in source quality, composition, and stance reduce users' capacity for independent evidence evaluation. Sources cited by Google AI Mode, Bing Copilot, Glass.health, and top-ranked organic results from Google and Bing were collected for 4 consumer-style queries on Tylenol (acetaminophen) and autism (October 8-17, 2025). Sources were evaluated using DISCERN, JAMA benchmarks, and Global Quality Score (GQS). Text analysis was performed on AI-generated responses and cited source texts using a keyword dictionary. Consumer AI platforms and the clinician tool assembled non-overlapping evidence bases. Glass.health exclusively cited peer-reviewed literature (100%) and scored higher on DISCERN (55.4 vs 48.4), JAMA (4.0 vs 2.8), and GQS (3.4 vs 2.8) than consumer AI. Consumer AI drew 43.2% of citations from news media, citing peer-reviewed literature at half the rate of conventional search (4.5% vs 9.8%). AI-generated responses averaged one-third the word count of cited sources while referencing scientific evidence less frequently and using denser, graduate-reading-level language. Source assembly, not text synthesis, accounted for the largest quality difference between consumer and clinician AI. Curation systematically substituted secondary journalistic interpretation for primary evidence, reducing the capacity for independent verification and exposure to peer-reviewed literature. Regulations should mandate disclosure of source selection criteria and establish minimum thresholds for peer-reviewed evidence inclusion in health query responses, particularly on widely used consumer-facing platforms.

title: Machine Learning Versus Traditional Methods for Predicting Venous Thromboembolism After Surgery: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
text: Postoperative venous thromboembolism remains a major cause of preventable morbidity after surgery, and established risk scores may perform inconsistently across surgical populations. MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies comparing machine learning with traditional risk models for postoperative venous thromboembolism prediction. Risk-of-bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI. The primary outcome was discrimination measured by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis estimated mean differences versus Caprini with 95% credible intervals. Best and worst-version analyses explored the impact of within-study multiplicity, with subgroup analyses by cancer surgery and procedure type. Eighteen studies including 177 656 validation patients were included. Meta-ensembles showed the largest improvement compared with Caprini in the best-version analysis (mean difference in AUROC, 0.232; 95% credible interval, 0.129-0.334), with a similar finding in the worst-version analysis (0.237; 0.123-0.351). Several other machine learning classes also had higher AUROC estimates than Caprini, whereas most traditional scores and surgeon judgement did not. Geneva showed lower performance than Caprini. Meta-ensembles ranked first overall, while Caprini and Geneva ranked 14th and last, respectively. Meta-ensembles and boosting models had higher AUROC than Caprini in both cancer surgery analyses; in general surgery, no model class showed higher performance than Caprini in the worst-version analysis. Machine learning models, particularly meta-ensembles, showed higher reported discrimination than traditional scores, but evidence remains limited by heterogeneity, inconsistent calibration reporting, sparse decision-analytic evaluation and infrequent external validation. Clinical adoption requires external validation and demonstration of real-world net benefit.

title: Machine learning-derived discordance between predicted mortality risk and valve surgery utilisation in infective endocarditis: a nationwide population-level analysis including injection drug use-associated disease.
text: Infective endocarditis (IE) carries high mortality, and valve surgery is indicated in selected patients on the basis of specific clinical circumstances assessed by a multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team. Predicted mortality risk is not equivalent to surgical indication; nevertheless, how surgical utilisation is distributed across the spectrum of illness severity at the population level has not been described. We used machine learning (ML) to describe population-level variation in valve surgery utilisation across strata of predicted in-hospital mortality risk, with a secondary focus on injection drug use (IDU)-associated IE. We analysed adult hospitalisations with an IE diagnosis code in the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022). Co-primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and valve surgery. Weighted multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with each outcome. Machine learning models (LASSO, random forest, and XGBoost) were trained using demographic, clinical, and hospital characteristics recorded during the hospitalisation, with temporal validation (2016-2020 training; 2021-2022 testing) and supplementary 5-fold cross-validation. Because diagnoses are recorded for the entire hospitalisation, the models were framed as retrospective, discharge-level risk classification rather than prospective prediction. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, and F1 score, and SHAP analysis was used for model interpretability. Among 125,100 IE hospitalisations (weighted ≈ 625,500), in-hospital mortality was 10.1% and the valve surgery rate was 8.3%. In the 2021-2022 temporal test set, the XGBoost mortality model achieved an AUROC of 0.842 (95% CI 0.836-0.848) and an AUPRC of 0.395 (event rate 11.8%), and the surgery model an AUROC of 0.857 (0.850-0.864) and an AUPRC of 0.403 (event rate 8.5%). Observed mortality increased approximately 80-fold across predicted-risk quintiles (Q1: 0.4% to Q5: 35.5%), whereas surgery rates varied only modestly (Q1: 5.6%; Q4: 10.8%; Q5: 9.5%). In SHAP analysis, mortality predictions were most strongly influenced by clinical severity markers (APR-DRG mortality risk, age, APR-DRG severity), whereas surgery predictions were most strongly influenced by age and hospital characteristics (bed size, teaching status, transfer-in), together with arrhythmia. IDU-associated IE (23.3%) had lower adjusted mortality (aOR 0.64, 95% CI 0.62-0.65) and was only weakly associated with surgery after adjustment (aOR 0.97); surgery rates were comparable between IDU and non-IDU hospitalisations at similar predicted risk. Mortality increased from 8.2% (2016) to 11.9% (2022; P-trend < 0.001), while surgery rates remained stable. Findings were unchanged after excluding APR-DRG variables. At the population level, valve surgery utilisation in IE varied little across a wide gradient of predicted in-hospital mortality and was more closely associated with patient age and hospital characteristics than with markers of illness severity. Because administrative data cannot establish surgical indication, operability, or patient preferences, these findings describe variation in utilisation rather than under-treatment of individual patients. IDU status was not a dominant correlate of surgical utilisation once predicted risk was considered. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in clinically detailed cohorts that capture guideline-defined surgical indications. Not applicable.

title: Machine learning-based risk prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with chronic hepatitis B: current evidence and future directions.
text: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and the risk persists despite potent nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. Current surveillance relies on broad clinical categories and conventional risk scores, although HCC risk in CHB is heterogeneous and changes over time. This review summarizes current approaches to HCC risk stratification in CHB, critically appraises machine learning (ML)-based models for individualized prediction, and discusses requirements for clinical implementation. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE from inception to July 1, 2026 for studies that developed or validated an ML-based model for incident HCC in adults with CHB, and appraised the included models with a structured approach informed by PROBAST+AI and TRIPOD+AI. Conventional models are generally static and do not fully capture non-linear relationships, time-updated risk, or multimodal information. ML-based models using clinical, virological, treatment-related, post-seroclearance, and imaging-derived data can refine risk prediction across stages of CHB care. However, most appraised models were at high risk of bias in the analysis domain, and none has undergone prospective clinical validation. Future models should move toward dynamic prediction using longitudinal data and multimodal integration of clinical variables, liver stiffness, imaging, and viral or molecular biomarkers. Key requirements include external validation, calibration, interpretability, fairness, cost-effectiveness, and prospective impact studies. ML-based models may complement conventional risk scores and support individualized surveillance in CHB. Future research should prioritize dynamic, multimodal, externally validated, and clinically implementable systems that improve surveillance decisions and patient outcomes.

title: Direction of apoB/LDL-C Discordance and Systemic Inflammation in U.S. Adults
text: BackgroundApolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. However, some individuals have discordant apoB and LDL-C. We evaluated whether apoB/LDL-C discordance is associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a key marker of systemic inflammation, in a nationally representative sample. Methods and ResultsWe analyzed cross-sectional data of 2226 adults aged 20 years or older from the 2015 to 2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete apoB, LDL-C, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). LDL-C and apoB were converted to survey-weighted z scores, and discordance was the residual of apoB regressed on LDL-C. Participants were classified as apoB-high, LDL-C-high, or concordant (reference). The association of discordance group with elevated hs-CRP (>3 mg/L) was estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes. Discordance was present in 26.4% of adults (13.7% apoB-higher, 12.6% LDL-C-higher). Elevated hs-CRP prevalence differed by discordance group: 47.6% (95% CI, 37.6-57.7) in the apoB-high group versus 20.5% (12.9-28.1) in the LDL-C-high group and 33.6% (29.7-37.4) in the concordant group. Relative to concordant participants, adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP were higher for apoB-high discordance (odds ratio [OR], 1.58; 95% CI, 1.03-2.45) and lower for LDL-C-high discordance (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30-0.78). Similar results were obtained among participants not on statin therapy, with apoB-high discordance demonstrating stronger adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.01-4.04). ConclusionDiscordantly high apoB relative to LDL-C is associated with systemic inflammation in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults.

title: Intersectional inequalities in demand satisfied by modern contraceptive methods among women in sub-Saharan Africa, 1994 to 2024: a multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy
text: BackgroundDemand for family planning satisfied by modern methods is Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 3.7.1, and countries have committed to universal access to family planning by 2030. Inequalities are usually reported one social dimension at a time. This hides how social characteristics combine and leaves open whether programmes should target social groups or strengthen services for all women. We measured intersectional inequalities in demand satisfied by modern methods among women in sub-Saharan Africa over three decades, assessed how well social position discriminates between women, and identified groups left behind. Methods and findingsWe did a preregistered cross-sectional analysis of 139 Demographic and Health Surveys from 38 countries with fieldwork from 1994 to 2024. We included 675,584 women aged 15-49 years with demand for family planning and grouped them into 144 intersectional strata by age, union status, education, household wealth and residence. We fitted multilevel logistic models with random effects for strata and surveys (multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy, MAIHDA) and estimated the variance partition coefficient (VPC), the area under the curve (AUC) and the proportional change in variance (PCV). Weighted demand satisfied rose from 27.5% in 1994-99 to 54.1% in 2018-24. Predicted demand satisfied ranged from 13.2% (95% CI: 11.0 -15.9) among married adolescents with no schooling in the poorest rural households to 68.0% (95% CI: 63.6 - 72.0) among unmarried urban women aged 25-34 years with secondary schooling in the richest households. The strata explained only 6.9% (95% CI: 5.6 - 8.7) of individual variation, with small discriminatory accuracy (AUC = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.63 - 0.66), and a Bayesian model gave a similar VPC (7.0%; 95% credible interval: 5.7 - 8.9). Additive effects explained 95.1% of the between-stratum variance. The VPC fell from 10.1% (95% CI: 8.0 - 12.8) in 1994-99 to 4.5% (95% CI: 3.6 - 5.8) in 2018-24. Five strata of married rural women with no schooling were in the lowest decile in every period. In the latest surveys, married rural women aged 15-24 years with no schooling had lower demand satisfied than other women in 29 of 30 countries (median gap 17.5 percentage points). The 15 most disadvantaged strata held a median 16.4% of unsatisfied demand, so targeting these groups alone would reach about one in six women whose demand is not met. The main limitations are the cross-sectional design, self-reported contraceptive use and the exclusion of 15 early surveys. ConclusionsIntersectional gaps in demand satisfied by modern methods have narrowed in sub-Saharan Africa, and most of the remaining gap between groups is additive. Social position alone discriminates poorly between women, so programmes targeted only by social group would miss most women with unmet need. This supports strengthening universal services. Within universal services, married adolescents and young women with no schooling in poor rural households have been left behind for three decades in almost every country and need priority, country-specific programmes if the 2030 targets are to be met. title: Real-world effectiveness of nirsevimab over three RSV seasons in an integrated health care system: a target trial emulation study
text: Most nirsevimab effectiveness estimates come from test-negative designs, which restrict populations to those seeking healthcare and testing. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness among infants six months post-receipt using a target trial emulation with an estimand aligned to phase 3 trials. We emulated a target trial among infants born from February 2, 2023 through May 30, 2026, using electronic medical records at Kaiser Permanente Georgia. Using a g-computation estimator with Cox models fit separately in nirsevimab recipients and non-recipients, we estimated the cumulative incidence of RSV hospitalization and medically-attended RSV at 30-day intervals through 180 days post-receipt. Among 4,826 infants, nirsevimab reduced the risk of RSV hospitalization by 95% (95% CI: 84% to 98%) and medically-attended RSV by 67% (95% CI: 45% to 80%) at 180 days post-receipt. The number needed to immunize to prevent one case was 147 (95% CI: 94 to 333) for RSV hospitalization and 39 (95% CI: 28 to 68) for medically-attended RSV. Nirsevimab was effective through 180 days post-receipt. This cohort-based emulation avoids conditioning on testing and the restricted generalizability of the test-negative and matching-based designs that dominate the literature. These findings support continued nirsevimab use to protect infants against RSV.

title: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo
text: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed drug delivery, enabling the stabilization and efficient intracellular delivery of nucleic acids. Current LNP platforms, including those used in clinical COVID-19 vaccines, rely on polyethylene glycol (PEG) to stabilize the nanoparticle. However, anti-PEG antibodies are ubiquitous in the population and are a major cause of anaphylaxis and reduced therapeutic efficacy by accelerating the blood clearance of PEGylated products. Here, we report the development of poly(2-oxazoline) (POx) lipids as alternatives. POx polymers are poorly immunogenic and mitigate accelerated blood clearance. Upon varying polymer hydrophilicity and molecular weight, we screened transfection efficiency in multiple cell lines and evaluated top candidates in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that POx-lipids incorporating short hydrophilic oxazoline chains enhance target transfection while mitigating liver expression. These POx-lipids boost expression in key extrahepatic tissues, including lymph nodes and spleen. This marks a notable advancement toward replacing PEG in LNP therapies and provides a clear path to optimizing POx-lipids for targeted vaccine and therapeutic applications.

title: Parallel ZNF598 and GIGYF2 pathways mediate conserved collision dependent mRNA decay with divergent endonucleolytic features
text: SUMMARY Quality control of aberrant mRNAs is essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis. Ribosome collisions caused by translational stalling trigger mRNA surveillance pathways that promote degradation of faulty transcripts. In yeast, two major collision-responsive pathways have been proposed: the Hel2–Cue2 pathway and the Syh1–Xrn1 pathway, yet their functional relationship and conservation in mammals have remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that these two pathways act redundantly to degrade collision-inducing mRNAs in both yeast and mammalian cells. In yeast, we dissect the contribution of Cue2-mediated endonucleolytic cleavage and show that eS7 polyubiquitination–dependent cleavage plays a dominant role in Hel2–Cue2 pathway. In mammals, although the proposed Cue2 homolog N4BP2 is dispensable, we provide the first direct evidence of collision-induced endonucleolytic mRNA cleavage. Together, our findings reveal both conserved and divergent features of ribosome collision–coupled mRNA quality control and expand our understanding of mRNA surveillance and potential therapeutic mRNA implications.

title: LONP-1 deficiency causes dysregulated protein synthesis within mitochondria that is suppressed by mitoribosomal mutations
text: Mitochondrial homeostasis is maintained by molecular chaperones and proteases located within the organelle. The mitochondrial matrix-localized protease LONP-1 degrades oxidatively damaged or misfolded proteins. Importantly, LONP-1 also regulates mitochondrial DNA replication. Here, we show that mutations in C. elegans that impair LONP-1 function cause dysregulation of mitochondrial DNA replication, mitochondrial RNA transcription and protein synthesis within the mitochondrial matrix. LONP-1 deficient worms had reduced levels of oxidative phosphorylation proteins despite increased mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis. Via a forward genetic screen, we identified three mutations that restored mitochondrial function and the rate of development in lonp-1 mutants to levels comparable to those in wildtype worms. Interestingly, all three suppressor mutations were found in genes encoding mitochondrial ribosome proteins. A point mutation in the mitochondrial ribosome protein MRPS-38 restored oxidative phosphorylation in lonp-1 mutant worms. Combined, our results suggest that LONP-1 regulates mitochondrial translation and that suppressor mutations within mrps-38 or mrps-15 can enhance oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly when LONP-1 function is diminished.

title: A multimodal foundation model for molecular and morphologic data in oncology
Spatial transcriptomics for gene discovery identifies Slc13a5 as a modulator of bone mechanoadaptation
text: Bone is a dynamic tissue that continuously adapts its structure in response to mechanical loading, an essential process for maintaining skeletal health. However, this adaptive capacity declines with aging, contributing to increased fragility and fracture risk. Developing therapeutic strategies that preserve or restore bone mechanoadaptation in patients with increased bone fragility requires identifying key molecular regulators of this process. Because mechanoadaptive responses are spatially heterogeneous across bone compartments and loading environments, we applied spatial transcriptomics (GeoMx, NanoString) to characterize gene expression changes induced by mechanical loading in the female murine tibia, focusing on periosteal and bone compartments in regions under tension and compression. Spatial data were validated and cross-compared with previously published bulk RNA-seq and laser-capture microdissection datasets, identifying a set of 12 genes consistently regulated by loading across independent platforms and laboratories. Among these candidates, we selected Slc13a5 for in vivo investigation because it encodes a citrate transporter implicated in bone mineralization and metabolism, yet its role in bone mechanoadaptation remains unknown. Conditional deletion of Slc13a5 in osteolineage cells using Osteocalcin-Cre in female mice significantly increased the loading-induced mineralizing surface in tensile regions compared with Cre- Slc13a5fl/fl littermates. In addition, Slc13a5 cKO mice exhibited lower resorption around the neutral axis after loading compared to controls. Together, these findings identify Slc13a5 as a regulator of bone adaptation in regions experiencing low mechanical stimulation and suggest it as a potential therapeutic target for conditions characterized by impaired mechanoadaptive responses. This study highlights spatial transcriptomics as a powerful gene discovery framework for bone, enabling identification of novel targets to understand mechanisms and develop therapies.

title: Targeting Neutrophil Extracellular Traps to Inhibit Colon Cancer Tumor Necrosis and Metastasis
text: Tumor necrosis is associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) yet is generally viewed as a passive consequence of tumor growth rather than a therapeutic target. We demonstrate that necrosis correlates with metastatic disease in human CRC independently of tumor size. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of primary CRC and colorectal liver metastases revealed that peri-necrotic programs are associated with metastatic progression. Patients with CRC exhibited increased circulating neutrophils, including NET-primed and CD177-low neutrophils with reduced extravasation capacity. Consistent with these findings, intravascular NET aggregates localized adjacent to necrotic regions in human CRC specimens. In a mismatch repair-proficient mouse model of CRC, neutrophil infiltration and NET formation increased during tumor progression, whereas genetic and pharmacologic NET inhibition reduced tumor necrosis, decreased metastasis, and enhanced chemotherapy efficacy. Together, these findings identify NET-driven tumor necrosis as an active promoter of CRC metastasis and support NET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

title: Ferrohydrodynamic Microfluidics for Multiscale Bioparticle Separation and Phenotyping
text: Ferrohydrodynamic microfluidics uses magnetic nanoparticles dispersed in ferrofluids to generate magnetic buoyancy forces for continuous manipulation of diamagnetic particles and magnetically labeled cells. These forces enable separation and phenotyping of cells, extracellular vesicles, and other bioparticles across length scales, although downstream molecular and functional compatibility depends on controlling ferrofluid exposure and residual nanoparticles. This Perspective examines the evolution of ferrofluid-based microfluidics from size-based enrichment toward quantitative physical and molecular phenotyping. We assess key technical and translational challenges, including biocompatibility, scalable and reproducible device architectures, nanoparticle depletion, quality control, and clinical translation. We also define application-specific priorities and discuss how engineered ferrofluids, additive manufacturing, machine learning, and molecular readouts could broaden the versatility of these platforms for precision bioanalysis.

title: Combinatorial mutagenesis of N-terminal sequences reveals expanded stability determinants of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway
text: Although penultimate residues near the N-terminus are known to influence protein stability, their exact contributions in prokaryotes are not well understood. Here, we utilize combinatorial mutagenesis, cell sorting, and next generation sequencing to perform the deepest sequence coverage screen of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway of proteolysis. Our results reinforce the known influence of canonically destabilizing P1 F/L/Y/W/R/K while revealing unexpected effects from P2 residue identities that influence protein stability comparably to P1 identity, such as for P2 Pro (stabilizing), Gly (stabilizing), or Gln (destabilizing). For low stability sequences without P1 F/L/Y/W/R/K, we identify motifs rich in P1 Cys paired with bulky and negatively charged P2-P5 residues. Furthermore, additive stability effects were observed for motifs rich in bulky (destabilizing), acidic (stabilizing), and flexible Gly/Ser (stabilizing) residues. We train a machine learning model to predict the stability of N-terminal sequences, including motifs that break expected stability rules. We find that these data-driven predictions of P2 identity contributions quantitatively correlate with binding energies predicted from computational docking of peptides to N-recognin ClpS. Our work expands the stability determinants of the N-degron pathway with unprecedented granularity, serving as a resource for N-degron identification, understanding, and design.

title: A scalable tumor-vasculature-on-chip for CAR T cell trafficking and efficacy studies
text: Most cellular therapies, like CAR T cells, remain ineffective in solid tumors. This is primarily due to a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), which creates biochemically hostile and often immunosuppressive conditions that limit efficacy of immunotherapies. Besides, cellular therapy efficacy is still often established in traditional 2D cultures that fail to simulate relevant aspects of solid tumor biology. Recent advances in three-dimensional (3D) and organ-on-chip culture systems have provided more physiologically relevant models for immunotherapy testing. These microphysiological systems (MPS) not only offer a 3D environment that alters tumor cell sensitivity to therapy but also enable inclusion of TME components and assessment of processes such as extravasation and infiltration, key steps in CAR T cell activity in vivo. This study focuses on applying an advanced culture technique and further building on the use of a scalable on-chip platform, the OrganoPlate, to grow EpCAM-positive and EpCAM-negative tumor cells in coculture with an endothelial vessel to study EpCAM-targeting CAR T cell migration and killing kinetics. The CAR T cells specifically targeted and killed EpCAM-positive HT-29 tumor cells while EpCAM-negative A375 tumor cells were not affected. In addition, target cell killing was dependent on the ratio between CAR T and tumor cells (E:T ratio) and was enhanced by addition of IL-2. Inflammatory cytokines like INF-γ, TNFα and IL-6 increased overtime in cultures containing CAR T cells. Morphometric analyses of the endothelial compartment showed E:T ratio dependent disruption of endothelial vessels. Additionally, this system was able to distinguish EpCAM ScFv-CD28-CD3z and EpCAM ScFv-TM-4-1BB-CD3z CAR T cells killing abilities and was used for studying the effect of immune checkpoint inhibitors and Temozolomide, a DNA targeting drug, on CAR T cell performance. Altogether, this work adds to the available advanced culture techniques for immunotherapy developers by describing a model that is modular, scalable, and suitable for phenotypic and functional characterization of CAR T cells.

title: Enabling lab autonomy with reward functions and executable workflows
From a single demonstration to a general policy for contact-rich manipulation
text: We present a four-stage Learning from Demonstration (LfD) pipeline that incrementally constructs a general policy for multi-stage contact-rich manipulation from a single human demonstration. The pipeline is built around a crucial inductive bias—environmental constraints—that separates general task structure from hard-to-model instance-specific details. We show that, on top of this inductive bias, simple and well-established components are already sufficient to build an interactive LfD system that generalizes to unseen variations in object pose, local geometry, and contact conditions under real-world uncertainty. We validate the system on seven real-world multi-stage contact-rich manipulation tasks and achieve over 90% success across tasks. These results establish environmental constraints as fundamental building blocks for efficient generalization in learning from demonstration. The project website can be found at https://lfdec.github.io/ .

title: A Systematic Survey on Deep Learning Architectures for Point Cloud Classification and Segmentation
text: Point cloud stands as the most widely adopted format for representing 3D shapes and scenes due to its simplicity and geometric fidelity. However, its inherent unordered and irregular nature, exacerbated by sensor noise and occlusions, introduces unique challenges for machine learning-based methodologies. To combat these issues, diverse strategies have been developed, including converting to a format that has orderliness, extracting local geometry, and permutation-invariant or self-attention-based processing. In this article, our focus is directed toward deep learning models for three fundamental tasks in 3D vision: point cloud classification, part segmentation, and semantic segmentation. We begin by formally defining point cloud data, followed by an in-depth discussion on its structural characteristics. Then, we categorize notable works based on their backbone structure and evaluate their performance on popular benchmarks. Beyond empirical comparison, we offer insights into architectural innovations and limitations. We also outline open challenges and promising future directions for 3D point cloud understanding.

title: AutoSAM: An agentic framework for automating SAM code input-deck construction with multi-modal retrieval augmented generation
Shape-informed cardiac mechanics surrogates in data-scarce regimes via geometric encoding and generative augmentation
text: High-fidelity computational models of cardiac mechanics provide mechanistic insight into the heart function but are computationally prohibitive for routine clinical use. Surrogate models can accelerate simulations, but generalization across diverse anatomies is challenging, particularly in data-scarce settings.
