The available observations support further investigation of C3-targeted renal epithelial cultures, but do not establish a causal requirement for epithelial C3 in serum-containing conditions or protection against clinical antibody-mediated rejection. The absence of rescue, C3-source discrimination and endothelial validation limits mechanistic and translational inference.

title: Oncohematology in the Era of Immunotherapies: The Key Role of the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) Complex.
text: Immunotherapy has transformed the therapeutic landscape of onco-hematology, evolving from historical allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) to modern chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T/NK cell therapies, bispecific antibodies, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. Central to this immunological cross-talk is the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) system, which governs self/non-self-discrimination, alloreactivity, and tumor immune evasion across both classical allografts and novel adoptive cellular platforms. Facing hematological malignancies, ranging from acute leukemias and multiple myeloma to chronic leukemias and lymphomas, clinicians must overcome tumor immune escape while managing treatment-related toxicities and Graft-versus-Host Disease (GvHD). Advances in high-throughput molecular biology techniques, notably Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) and long-read sequencing, have become indispensable for high-resolution HLA matching, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and chimerism analysis. Furthermore, gene-editing strategies (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9) targeting TRAC, B2M, and CIITA, alongside HLA-E engineering and induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology, are driving the development of universal "off-the-shelf" effector platforms that bypass classic HLA barriers. In this review, we provide a conceptual synthesis of immunotherapeutic paradigms in onco-hematology, highlighting the pivotal role of HLA biology and molecular diagnostics in shaping next-generation personalized cellular therapies.

title: Biomimetic magnetic nanocarriers for theranostic CRISPR/Cas9 delivery: targeting WT1 in a murine model of breast cancer.
text: A biomimetic magnetic nanocarrier was developed to facilitate the targeted delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 components to breast cancer cells, with the aim of improving tumor-directed gene delivery and reducing nonspecific distribution to healthy tissues. The effective delivery vector for partial WT1 disruption consists of a superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) core loaded with a genome-editing plasmid. The SPION is wrapped in a red blood cell membrane functionalized with the nuclear- and cancer cell-targeting aptamer AS1411. Findings from cytotoxicity assays and western blot analyses validated the effectiveness of this delivery system. Furthermore, fluorescence imaging and flow cytometry demonstrated enhanced GFP reporter expression in 4T1 cells treated with PSMA compared with the nontargeted formulation, suggesting improved functional plasmid delivery. In vivo investigations revealed substantial tumor-growth inhibition following PSMA administration, while ex vivo fluorescence imaging showed enhanced tumor-associated GFP reporter signals compared with the nontargeted formulation. Moreover, the diagnostic potential of the synthesized SPION-CRISPR/Cas9 plasmid/membrane/aptamer complex was evaluated using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which revealed enhanced contrast at the tumor site. Overall, this platform demonstrates potential for tumor-directed plasmid delivery and MRI-based imaging, although further studies are required to establish reproducible WT1-editing efficiency, long-term safety, and therapeutic specificity.

title: Systematic clustering alignment and feature characterization for single-cell omics using ACE-OF-Clust.
text: Clustering is widely used to identify cell types in cellular-resolution transcriptomic data, including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST). Mixed-membership clustering assigns fractional memberships across clusters and captures continuous variation beyond hard clustering, but integrating and interpreting results from either approach is complicated by the "clustering alignment problem," which arises from label switching, multi-modality, and differences in model settings (including differing numbers of clusters). We introduce ACE-OF-Clust, enabling a four-step workflow for single-cell clustering: multiple clustering, clustering alignment, model comparison, and identification of informative features. ACE-OF-Clust introduces direct comparison of clustering solutions, assesses consistency against annotations, and leverages feature-level clustering profiles to prioritize genes discriminating among cell types, as well as to evaluate how gene sets contribute to clustering patterns. We demonstrate its utility using PBMC scRNA-seq data, breast cancer and mouse embryo ST data, and single-cell multi-omic data. ACE-OF-Clust quantifies cross-omic clustering variability and suggests putative cross-omic regulatory links. Overall, ACE-OF-Clust increases the interpretability, flexibility, and robustness of single-cell clustering, providing a scalable tool for studying cellular heterogeneity and gene expression dynamics.

title: Computational Prediction of Elbasvir as a Theoretical Candidate for PFOS-Associated Gut and Skin Shared Pathologies.
text: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently co-occur along the gut-skin axis, yet the systemic triggers, particularly environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals like perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate network toxicology and single-cell multi-omics to propose a computational framework for the shared molecular signatures of PFOS-driven AD and IBD comorbidity. Utilizing large-scale clinical transcriptomic cohorts and machine learning, we computationally predicted the transcription factor MYC as a potential core pathological hub. Single-cell transcriptomics and in silico virtual perturbation models revealed that aberrant MYC activation is highly restricted to barrier-forming cells: epidermal keratinocytes and intestinal mucosal progenitors. This spatially specific dysregulation not only compromises epithelial structural integrity but also reshapes local chemotactic networks, driving macrophage pro-inflammatory polarization and immune imbalance. To translate these findings, high-throughput drug repurposing screening and 200 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations identified the antiviral drug Elbasvir as a stable, high-affinity MYC inhibitor. Collectively, our work proposes a single-cell spatial pathology of environment-driven shared pathologies across the gut-skin axis and provides a theoretical pharmacological strategy to intervene in systemic inflammatory networks.

title: Spatial organization of immunosuppressive niches is associated with immune exclusion in ETMR.
text: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) is a rare and highly aggressive malignant pediatric brain tumor with limited treatments. The spatial organization of the ETMR immune microenvironment remains poorly understood, limiting our understanding of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance. We defined the spatial organization of ETMR using spatial transcriptomics across 11 samples from 9 patients, integrated with independent publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Immune cells were largely excluded from the tumor core, while the peritumoral border formed an immunosuppressive niche enriched for B-cells and M2-like macrophages. These cells exhibited conserved transcriptional programs associated with gliosis, extracellular matrix generation, immune suppression, and cellular exhaustion. At this interface, the CD74-MIF signaling axis was enriched, suggesting a possible coordinated mechanism underlying peritumoral macrophage and regulatory B-cell abundance. Integration with the ETMR developmental continuum further revealed spatial covariation between tumor developmental states and immune and stromal features. Multilayered rosettes, a histopathological hallmark of ETMR, showed spatially confined interferon-responsive, immune-associated transcriptional programs, enriched for type I and II interferon signaling and antigen-processing pathways. This suggests that despite global immune exclusion, localized regions of interferon-responsive and immune-associated transcriptional activity persist within the tumor. These findings define a compartmentalized spatial immune architecture in ETMR characterized by relative immune depletion in tumor-rich regions, immunoregulatory and stroma-associated programs at selected tumor interfaces, and localized interferon-responsive transcriptional activity within rosette-associated regions. This spatial framework provides a basis for future mechanistic studies of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance in ETMR. Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) is a rare brain cancer in children, with few good treatments. Immunotherapy might help. But first, we need to know why the immune system does not fight these tumors on its own. We used a tool called “spatial transcriptomics” to see which cells are present in tumors. Immune cells are mostly missing in the tumor center and gathered at the edge. A signaling pathway called CD74-MIF appeared at the tumor edge with immune cells that form a barrier. Immune signals called interferons were active in the tumor signature structures known as multilayered rosettes. ETMR contains signals that block and support the immune attack. These findings could help find immunotherapies that target the tumor's weakness.

title: Emerging Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics: From Multi-Kingdom Interactions to Genetic Variation and Population Diversity.
text: Plants are composed of highly specialized cell types. Their identity, location, and interactions collectively determine their development, environmental responses, and evolutionary adaptation. The emergence of single-cell/nuclear technologies has transformed plant biology by enabling the study of gene expression at cellular resolution, while spatial transcriptomics preserve the developmental and spatial context. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the current experimental and computational landscape of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in plants. We discuss the strengths, limitations, and applications of available technologies, ranging from transcriptomics at cell level to high-resolution spatial platforms, as well as recent advances in bioinformatics analysis, data integration, and community resources. Beyond methodological advances, we highlight how these technologies are redefining our understanding of plant development, responses to abiotic stress, and interactions among different kingdoms, by revealing dynamic cellular states, regulatory networks, and spatially organized biological processes that remain inaccessible to bulk analyses. We discuss the emerging integration of single-cell approaches with population genomics, evolutionary biology, and genetic demultiplexing, which opens up new avenues for identifying the cellular basis of natural variation and adaptive evolution.

title: AI-Assisted PROTAC Design for Cancer Therapy: An Evidence-to-Decision Framework for Designer, Connector and Predictor Roles.
text: AI methods are used in proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) discovery for candidate generation, ternary-complex modelling and property prediction. These tasks are organised here into Designer, Connector and Predictor roles to examine how computational outputs can inform experimental decisions in cancer drug discovery. Published studies connect selected computationally generated compounds to biological testing and show how new measurements can inform chemical optimisation and property-model refinement. Case studies of linker modifications and PKMYT1 stereoisomers illustrate discrepancies between binding and cellular degradation. Further preclinical and clinical findings show why target depletion must be interpreted alongside pathway suppression, tissue exposure and tolerability. The analysis identifies measurements that could distinguish competing explanations and guide changes to candidate chemistry, structural hypotheses, prediction models or experimental conditions. Predictive performance depends on chemical and biological context, so validation needs to reflect the compounds, targets and endpoints encountered in the intended application. Exposure-response models can help interpret pharmacological findings when supported by relevant tissue and pathway measurements. Clinical outcomes are also distinguished from evidence of AI involvement in individual candidates. Current evidence supports specific connections between computation and experiment. Prospective comparisons are needed to determine whether coordinating these methods improves candidate selection and pharmacological outcomes.

title: Single-sequence, structure-free allosteric residue prediction with protein language models.
text: Large language models trained on protein sequences learn general coevolutionary relationships at scale, which contain useful structural and functional information. We show that attention maps, matrices of learned pairwise relationships between residues, include information about allostery. This enables prediction of allosteric relationships with no task-specific training, requiring a single input sequence and specified active-site residues, without structural information. Attention maps outperform established structure-based and sequence coevolution-based models across a benchmark of 109 allosteric proteins. In the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, a G-protein coupled receptor, attention maps correlate more strongly with experimental alanine-scanning measurements of allosteric effects on signaling than these comparators. Language model attention also guides efficient, low-throughput experimental discovery of putative allosteric residues in the protease DPP4 and residues coupled to the known allosteric pathway in ACE2. These results enable and demonstrate allosteric relationship prediction in a zero-shot, single-sequence, structure-free manner. We provide this method in the AlloGator web interface.

title: Molecular recognition and dynamic behaviour of diosmin as a putative inhibitor of Plasmodium falciparum.
text: Malaria remains a leading global public health problem, mainly because of the spread of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains, which underscores the need for antimalarials directed at alternative metabolic routes. The present study combined sequence conservation analysis, structure-based virtual screening, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and experimental evaluation to identify candidate inhibitors of P. falciparum bifunctional farnesyl/geranylgeranyl diphosphate synthase (PfFPPS/GGPPS). Comparison of the AlphaFold-derived model with the experimentally determined structure (PDB ID: 9NSR) gave a global Cα root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 0.524 Å and a docking-region RMSD of 0.347 Å. Alignment of sequences from three Plasmodium species confirmed complete conservation of 11 of the 13 docking-site residues examined. The lowest-energy apo conformation, selected from a 100 ns MD simulation by free energy landscape (FEL) analysis, was used for screening. Screening of 1,247 natural plant compounds identified Diosmin, Hesperidin, Sanguinarine and Narirutin as candidate binders, with docking energies of - 9.3, - 9.2, - 9.0 and - 8.7 kcal/mol, respectively, compared with - 7.7 kcal/mol for the reference compound A1B0W. Two independent 500 ns MD simulations of each complex revealed ligand-dependent conformational behaviour, with Diosmin showing protein Cα and ligand RMSDs of 4.95 ± 0.66 Å and 4.75 ± 0.50 Å. Experimental testing against P. falciparum 3D7 showed concentration-dependent growth inhibition by Diosmin, rising from 26.33% at 50 nM to 69.86% at 1000 nM, whereas chloroquine produced 69.75% inhibition at 100 nM. Collectively, these findings identify Diosmin as a moderately active antiplasmodial candidate warranting further investigation, although direct inhibition of PfFPPS/GGPPS remains to be experimentally established.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Coumarin Sulfamates as PxGSS1 Inhibitors in Plutella xylostella.
text: Glucosinolate sulfatases (GSSs) enable the diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella, to evade crucifer defenses by desulfating glucosinolates. In this study, 20 coumarin sulfamates (D1-D20) were designed, synthesized, and evaluated against recombinant P. xylostella glucosinolate sulfatase 1 (PxGSS1). D18 exhibited the strongest inhibition (IC50 = 4.38 mg/L). Although D18 and D19 had nearly identical cLogP values and similar predicted docking energies, their distinct binding poses suggested that ligand geometry may influence inhibition. On flowering Chinese cabbage leaves, D18 caused limited acute mortality but significantly reduced larval growth, pupal weight, pupation, adult emergence, and fecundity; no significant developmental effects occurred on a glucosinolate-free artificial diet. LC-MS/MS revealed tissue-specific redistribution of 4MSOB, desulfo-4MSOB, and 4MSOB-ITC, including elevated 4MSOB in the gut and integument and enrichment of 4MSOB-related metabolites in frass. These findings identify D18 as a promising lead associated with altered GSS-mediated glucosinolate metabolism.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Herbicidal Activity of Coumarin-3-Acetamide Derivatives as Potential Transketolase Inhibitors.
text: Transketolase (TKL; EC 2.2.1.1) has been confirmed to be a promising new herbicide target. In this study, two series of the coumarin-based compounds 12a-12j and 13a-13m were designed and synthesized based on TKL as the new target. Among them, compound 12c could significantly inhibit the activity of SvTKL (IC50: 0.96 μmol/L) in vitro. Notably, compound 12c exhibited inhibitory effects of over 90% against D. sanguinalis and A. retroflexus higher than those of the positive control (inhibition < 80%) at 375 g a.i./ ha via the pot spraying method. Additionally, compound 12c exhibited good safety (injury rate <10%) for wheat and maize at 375 g a.i./ha. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation studies indicated that compound 12c has a strong binding ability and dynamic stability with SvTKL. Furthermore, ARG598 may contribute to the stabilization of 12c within the SvTKL active pocket. These findings establish coumarin-fusaric acid derivatives as promising leads for new herbicide development.

title: Rational Design of Benzofuran-Linked Isatin Derivatives as MTDLs Targeting MAO-B and Cholinesterases: Synthesis, in silico Insights, and Neuroprotection Studies.
text: Neurodegenerative disorders are multifactorial diseases associated with oxid active stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurotransmitter imbalance, leading to progressive neuronal loss. Since monoamine oxidase-B (MAO-B) contributes to dopamine metabolism and reactive oxygen species generation, it represents an attractive therapeutic target for anti-neurodegenerative drug discovery. This study aimed to develop novel benzofuran-isatin hybrids within a multitarget-directed ligand (MTDL) strategy to achieve selective MAO-B inhibition combined with cholinesterase inhibitory and neuroprotective activities. Twelve target compounds were synthesized and characterized using 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and LRMS analyses. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for MAO-A and MAO-B inhibition, while the most promising candidate was further investigated for inhibition kinetics, cholinesterase inhibitory activity, and neuroprotective effects against Aβ1-42-induced toxicity in SH-SY5Y cells. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in silico ADME prediction were also performed. The synthesized compounds displayed weak-to-moderate MAO-A inhibition (IC50 = 2.56 to >40 μM) and potent MAO-B inhibition (IC50 = 0.016-2.65 μM) with excellent isoform selectivity. The 7-methyl derivatives 7e and 7k emerged as the most potent MAO-B inhibitors, displaying IC50 values of 0.016 and 0.073 μM with selectivity indices of 852.50 and 547.96, respectively. Kinetic studies demonstrated that compound 7e acts as a competitive MAO-B inhibitor (KI = 0.012 μM). Furthermore, 7e exhibited potent AChE inhibition (IC50 = 0.091 μM), comparable to donepezil, together with moderate BuChE inhibition and significant neuroprotective activity against Aβ1-42-induced toxicity in SH-SY5Y cells. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported favorable and stable binding of the active compounds within the MAO-B and AChE active sites. In addition, in silico ADME prediction suggested acceptable drug-likeness and CNS-related pharmacokinetic properties. These findings identify benzofuran-isatin hybrids, particularly compound 7e, as promising multifunctional candidates for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders. Future studies should focus on in vivo validation of compound 7e, including its pharmacokinetic behavior, brain exposure, safety, and therapeutic efficacy in relevant models of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Neurodegenerative diseases are complex disorders in which nerve cells gradually lose their normal function and eventually die. Because several biological processes contribute to these diseases, medicines that can act on more than one disease-related pathway may offer greater therapeutic benefits. In this study, we designed and synthesized a new group of compounds combining two chemical structures, benzofuran and isatin, with the aim of producing multifunctional agents against neurodegeneration. The new compounds were particularly effective at blocking monoamine oxidase-B, an enzyme involved in the breakdown of dopamine and the production of harmful reactive oxygen species in the brain. The most promising compound, 7e, also effectively inhibited acetylcholinesterase, an enzyme involved in the loss of an important brain chemical required for memory and learning. In addition, selected compounds protected neuronal cells against damage caused by amyloid-beta, a protein strongly associated with Alzheimer’s disease. Computer-based studies further supported the ability of these compounds to interact effectively with their intended biological targets. These findings highlight compound 7e as a promising multifunctional candidate for further investigation in the development of treatments for neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Drug Development: Recent Advances and Emerging Applications.
text: Drug research, formulation development, manufacturing, quality control, and pharmacovigilance are just a few areas of the pharmaceutical industry that have undergone a paradigm shift with the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI). The numerous ways that AI-driven technologies impact each stage of the pharmaceutical life cycle are examined in this comprehensive analysis. One subfield of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) that stands out is deep learning (DL), which uses artificial neural networks (ANNs) to find intricate patterns and relationships in massive datasets by simulating the structure of the human brain. These methods have produced state-of-the-art results in fields such as speech detection, natural language understanding, image recognition, pharmacophore selection, and protein targeting. The manuscript discusses how data analytics, machine learning algorithms, and predictive modelling can be used to improve Pharmaceutical formulation development throughout its life cycle. This critical review provides important insights into the changing dynamics of drug development through AI-driven innovation by outlining the latest developments and patents.

title: Targeting the Intrinsically Disordered N-Terminal Domain of the Prion Protein: A New Frontier for Antiprion Therapeutics.
text: Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions have long been considered challenging pharmacological targets because they lack stable 3D structures and well-defined binding pockets. Nevertheless, advances in structural biology, biophysics, and computational drug discovery have demonstrated that their dynamic conformational ensembles can be selectively targeted. The cellular prion protein (PrPC) exemplifies this emerging paradigm. Although antiprion strategies have traditionally focused on its structured C-terminal domain, the intrinsically disordered N-terminal region plays essential roles in metal ions homeostasis, neuroprotective signaling, membrane interactions, and prion propagation. In this review, we summarize and examine the physiological and synthetic ligands that bind to the PrPC N-terminal domain or fragments thereof whose interactions have been characterized at the molecular level using biochemical and biophysical approaches. We discuss the molecular determinants of ligand recognition, the structural and functional consequences of binding, and their therapeutic implications. By integrating current structural, biophysical, and pharmacological evidence, this review aims to define the structural principles governing the selective targeting of the intrinsically disordered N-terminal region of PrPC, and to provide a framework for the rational development of novel antiprion therapeutics.

title: Task-aware conditional diffusion model for EMG artifact removal in single-channel EEG.
text: Electroencephalography (EEG) is highly susceptible to electromyography (EMG) artifacts, which can obscure task-relevant neural oscillations and degrade downstream analysis. Existing denoising methods usually treat EEG as task-agnostic signals and may attenuate physiologically meaningful rhythms during artifact removal. This study aims to develop a task-aware single-channel EEG denoising framework that suppresses EMG artifacts while preserving task-dependent neural oscillatory characteristics. We propose TaskEEGDiT, a task-conditioned diffusion framework for EMG artifact removal. The model introduces task-wise spectral prototypes as conditioning signals to guide denoising toward task-relevant spectral distributions, while the noisy EEG is used as a sample-specific reference to constrain the reverse diffusion process and enable deterministic reconstruction. TimeMixer is adopted as the noise prediction backbone to capture non-stationary temporal dynamics and multi-scale dependencies. A multi-constraint joint loss further combines denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) noise prediction, encoder-based temporal content preservation, and power spectral density (PSD)-based spectral style alignment. Experiments on motor imagery EEG and sleep EEG datasets show that TaskEEGDiT outperforms tuned baseline models and a task-conditioned DSATCN variant across correlation coefficient, signal-to-noise ratio, spectral-domain relative root mean square error, and time-domain relative root mean square error. TaskEEGDiT achieves SNRs of 13.841 dB and 15.781 dB on the motor imagery and sleep EEG datasets, respectively, improving over DSATCN (task-conditioned) by 2.177 dB and 2.433 dB. Additional analyses across signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels, task conditions, and sleep EEG subjects support robustness, while real-recording results provide preliminary evidence of applicability. With 10-step Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) accelerated sampling, inference time is reduced to 345.684 ms per 2-s EEG segment. TaskEEGDiT demonstrates that task-wise spectral prototype conditioned diffusion modeling can improve EMG artifact removal while limiting alterations to task-relevant EEG spectral characteristics, supporting faster-than-real-time EEG denoising for online brain-computer interface and neurophysiological monitoring scenarios.

title: Precision fermentation at scale: engineering economically resilient hosts.
text: Precision fermentation (PF) offers sustainable production of food ingredients, yet inconsistent scale-up and poor economics hinder its use in bulk foods. We propose economic robustness as a central engineering goal: the ability of a PF process to meet predefined commercial targets despite variability in strain performance, bioreactor conditions, feedstock costs, market demands, or regulatory requirements. We outline how scale-down systems, computational fluid dynamics, and multi-omics can link process conditions to cellular responses. We discuss strategies to improve multi-stress tolerance, population stability, productive lifespan, protein secretion, and regulatory compliance. Finally, we explore how AI-guided strain engineering, protein language models, and digital twins could integrate these strategies into predictive, economics-aware design-build-test-learn cycles, enabling affordable and scalable PF-based bulk foods manufacturing.

title: What is learned with scale? The transformative power of knowledge-enriched pangenomics.
text: The massive drop in the cost of DNA sequencing in the late 2000s led to a rapid increase in the availability of whole-genome sequences for a wide variety of microbial organisms. Today, hundreds of thousands of genome sequences exist for strains of select species. These large, steadily growing data sets demand scalable data analytics to elucidate the diversity encoded in these genomes and their phenotypic implications. Knowledge-enriched pangenomics provides a formalization of knowledge that can be used to address this challenge by moving beyond simple gene catalogs toward the creation of mechanistic, genome-scale computational models capable of simulating strain-specific phenotypes. Such studies have grown to the 104 genome scale for several microorganisms and demonstrated that new lessons continue to be extracted as the number of genomes used to form pangenomes grows. This minireview outlines what has been learned and forecasts future results likely to be gained from further increases in scale. By providing mechanistic, chemistry-grounded explanations rather than associative correlations, knowledge-enriched pangenomics complements-rather than competes with-modern artificial intelligence approaches.

title: ​mRNA-based Medical Countermeasures for CBRN threats: Current Status and Research Priorities.
text: Medical countermeasures (MCM) for chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats have relied on recombinant protein therapeutics and monoclonal antibodies, which are constrained by slow, costly, and difficult-to-scale manufacturing. mRNA platforms offer a potentially faster and more scalable route to vaccines, therapeutic enzymes, antibodies, and other biologics against CBRN threats, but introduce their own translational barriers, including cold-chain logistics, dose-response uncertainty, and organ-specific delivery. This review evaluates the current status of mRNA-based MCMs organized around the three core CBRN threat pillars, chemical, biological, and radiological/nuclear, using chemical defense bioscavengers, a nerve agent MCM with the most mature mechanistic foundation but the least translation to mRNA-based formats, as an anchor case. Within each pillar we distinguish clinically evaluated approaches from preclinical proof-of-concept studies and from conceptual extensions for which no mRNA-specific data yet exist, and we critically assess translational feasibility and field-deployment barriers rather than only cataloguing potential applications. We close with cross-cutting research gaps in RNA stability, dosing, organ-targeted delivery, and distributed field manufacturing that must be addressed before mRNA MCMs can be fielded.

title: Engineered extracellular vesicles as next-generation platforms for mRNA therapeutics delivery.
text: mRNA has emerged as a star molecule in pharmaceutical development, demonstrating immense potential for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer, neurological disorders, genetic diseases, and infectious diseases. It has played a particularly pivotal role in COVID-19 prevention. However, the clinical translation of mRNA therapeutics is significantly hampered by its inherent instability, low cellular permeability, and poor targeting specificity. Consequently, the development of efficient mRNA delivery systems represents a paramount challenge for its biomedical application. Conventional delivery platforms, as exemplified by lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), offer advantages including mature manufacturing processes and broad clinical adoption. Nevertheless, they still face limitations such as suboptimal delivery efficiency and biosafety concerns requiring further improvement. Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, microvesicles, and apoptotic bodies, have emerged as highly promising mRNA delivery vectors. This is attributed to their low immunogenicity, favorable biosafety profile, intrinsic homing effect-based targeting capability, and amenability to engineering modifications. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in EV-mediated mRNA delivery, detailing strategies for mRNA loading into EVs, approaches for achieving targeted mRNA delivery using EVs, and the therapeutic applications of EV-encapsulated mRNA. The synthesis of this knowledge aims to provide insights to advance the clinical implementation of mRNA-based therapeutics.

title: Combinatorial synthesis of novel polycations for mRNA delivery via Ugi 4-component polymerisation.
text: RNA therapeutics offer solutions to treat previously undruggable diseases, but successful RNA delivery requires efficient and safe vectors. Cationic polymers provide one technology platform for this delivery, however, despite many current materials in this class showing promise when tested in cells, none have yet progressed to the clinic. Existing commercially available polymers evaluated for RNA delivery have either limited structural variety or poorly addressable functionality, which means that tuning of pharmaceutical properties is difficult. In order to control better some parameters of key importance for RNA delivery, such as assembly with nucleic acids, internalisation into target cells and degradation after payload release, new chemistries and structures are needed. Multicomponent polymerisations provide a means to access easily highly functionalised materials, thus here we report the use of Ugi 4-component polymerisation to synthesise a range of cationic polyamides. We demonstrate a facile synthetic route to a diverse polymer library which, when screened for in vitro transfection with mRNA, showed several polymer structures with high potency in selected cell lines.

title: Digital Solutions for Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases in International air Travel: A Scoping Review.
text: International air travel significantly contributes to the global spread of infectious diseases, prompting the rapid deployment of digital systems for border health security in response to recent epidemics. However, evidence on digital systems characteristics, maturity, and implementation remains fragmented. To systematically map and synthesize the characteristics, functions, maturity, and reported impacts of digital systems used for infectious-disease control in international air-travel settings. We performed a scoping review based on the framework developed by Arksey and O'Malley, further enhanced by Levac and colleagues, and adhered to the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines. A comprehensive search was conducted across scientific databases to identify English-language studies published from 2006 to 2025 that described, implemented, or evaluated digital systems related to infectious-disease prevention and control in airports, air-border settings, or among international air travelers. The collected data were analyzed thematically to identify and classify different management approaches, along with their defining features and implementation challenges. Twenty-eight studies were included. Most systems were implemented directly at airports or air-border settings (71.4%), while others were indirectly related through modelling tools, epidemic-intelligence platforms, digital credentialing systems, or traveler-facing applications (28.6%). The largest proportion of studies originated from the World Health Organization (WHO) Western Pacific Region (46.4%), and COVID-19 was the predominant disease focus (50%). Six categories of digital systems were identified. Systems implemented at national or operational scale represented a minority but showed the clearest evidence of real-world utility, particularly for improving workflow efficiency, traveler follow-up, and information linkage across border-health processes. However, many systems remained prototypes or pilot implementations, and evidence was more often operational or technical than epidemiological. Digital systems have become important tools for infectious-disease control in international air-travel and border-health contexts. Their greatest benefits were observed when embedded within coordinated public-health infrastructures that enabled timely data sharing and decision-making. However, many systems remain fragmented, insufficiently validated, or constrained by interoperability, privacy, equity, and user-adoption challenges.

title: Bridging the data quality gap? The 'Biotechnology Data Quality Accelerator' proposed in the EU Biotech Act at the crossroads of EHDS, GDPR, and AI innovation.
text: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into health biotechnology has generated acute demand for large volumes of high-quality, curated, and annotated health datasets-a demand that the EU's existing digital regulatory framework is structurally ill-equipped to address. While the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) addresses data quality indirectly through the accuracy principle, which functions as a data subject rights mechanism rather than a substantive quality standard, the European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation focuses on data access and interoperability rather than curation, and the AI Act imposes a substantive quality standard on high-risk systems at the development stage, yet leaves the underlying curation process unaddressed. This 'data quality gap' carries particular strategic and patient safety implications for the EU's health biotechnology sector. Against this backdrop, this article critically examines the 'biotechnology data quality accelerator' (BDQA) mechanism introduced by the proposed EU Biotech Act, the first dedicated EU legislative attempt to govern health data curation as a task of public interest. Through doctrinal legal analysis, the article identifies three significant legal tensions in the BDQA mechanism's design and offers targeted legislative recommendations: its public interest characterization and interplay with GDPR legal bases; the legal status of 'enhanced data' and its friction with the EHDS access regime; and the accountability implications of the Commission's power to define BDQA processing modalities.

title: Integrating personal health records into clinical pharmacy practice: A scoping review of pharmacists' roles.
text: Personal health records (PHRs) enhance patient engagement by allowing individuals to manage their health data, including medications, laboratory results, and treatment plans. Despite increasing PHR adoption, the role of pharmacists in PHR-based interventions remains underexplored. This scoping review aimed to characterize how PHRs have been used in pharmacy practice and the roles pharmacists have played in PHR-facilitated patient care. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria, 9 conducted in the United States and 1 in China. Since 2020, application-based PHR platforms have become more prominent, particularly among patients with chronic conditions. The predominant PHR type was a hospital-integrated patient portal incorporating reminders and secure messaging. Across studies, pharmacists contributed to clinical reviews, therapeutic drug monitoring, adverse drug reaction (ADR) management, medication reconciliation, and patient education. Recent research highlighted increasing use of patient-reported outcomes, with a focus on adverse drug events, adherence, and pharmacist-patient communication. This review found that PHRs have been used in pharmacy practice to support medication safety, optimize therapeutic outcomes, and promote patient-centered care. Standardizing pharmacist-led interventions and addressing barriers such as interoperability, patient engagement, and digital literacy are critical next steps for integrating PHRs into clinical pharmacy practice.

title: Predictive capability for tooth agenesis based on two-dimensional frontal facial photographic measurements using machine learning algorithms.
text: Previous research shows that nonsyndromic permanent tooth agenesis is linked with other craniofacial alterations. This study evaluated the ability of machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict nonsyndromic permanent tooth agenesis (excluding third molars) based on two-dimensional frontal facial photographic measurements. A cross-sectional observational study included a sex- and age-balanced sample of 524 participants: 175 individuals with tooth agenesis and 349 controls. Frontal facial images were obtained with a standardized dental photographic protocol. Seven linear facial measurements were extracted from images using ImageJ software, with calibration based on interpupillary distance. Six ML models were used: logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, artificial neural networks, AdaBoost, and k-nearest neighbors. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), precision, sensitivity, specificity, and Matthews correlation coefficient. Among the evaluated models, the artificial neural network showed the best performance (AUC = 0.784; accuracy = 0.736), followed by the logistic regression model (AUC = 0.774; accuracy = 0.725). Predictive importance analysis identified zygion-zygion, exocanthion-exocanthion, and endocanthion-endocanthion as the most predictive variables. ML models based on facial measurements from standardized two-dimensional frontal photographs showed moderate discriminative ability for tooth agenesis. These models are not intended to replace clinical or radiographic examination but may be explored as adjunctive tools for preliminary risk stratification. External validation is required before clinical application.

title: Dynamic risk of kidney allograft rejection and the prognostic value of Banff phenotypes: a time-varying cohort study in an Asian population.
Artificial intelligence and causation: from prediction to causal inference in biomedical research.
text: To distinguish what dental artificial intelligence (AI) models demonstrate from what their findings are claimed to mean, and to offer a framework for matching each claim to the evidence required to support it. AI studies in dentistry report sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve: measures of agreement between model outputs and a reference standard. Yet verbs such as predict, detect, identify, and explain are used interchangeably, and outputs are often read as identifying modifiable causes or as evidence of clinical benefit. Using the causal hierarchy of association, intervention, and counterfactual reasoning, this review separates description, prediction, causal effects of interventions, and individual counterfactuals. Directed acyclic graphs illustrate how confounding by indication can make an effective treatment appear harmful in a predictive model. The review summarizes the identification conditions that causal claims require (exchangeability, positivity, consistency) and where AI can legitimately contribute: measurement, nuisance-function estimation, heterogeneous treatment effects, and hypothesis-generating causal discovery. Model-explanation methods describe how a fitted model behaves, not how patients would respond to intervention. A published caries-detection model illustrates the evidence needed to move from diagnostic accuracy to claims about clinician decisions and patient outcomes. Most AI models developed for prediction operate at the association level. Model complexity and dataset size cannot substitute for a defined intervention, an appropriate design, and defensible identification assumptions. Dental AI accuracy studies show agreement with a reference standard, not that using the tool improves decisions or patient outcomes. Such claims require comparative evaluation of AI-assisted care.

title: Differential scanning calorimetry and artificial intelligence for analytical profiling of disease-related plasma thermograms.
text: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) is a systems-level thermodynamic tool for probing disease-related changes in complex biological fluids, yet clinical translation is hindered by challenges in thermogram interpretation, reproducibility, and data integration. DSC captures heat capacity transitions from multistate protein unfolding, reflecting collective stability landscapes of the plasma proteome. Pathological conditions can induce reproducible thermogram distortions, suggesting their utility as ensemble biomarkers beyond conventional scalar descriptors. Recent advances in ultrasensitive and microfluidic DSC have improved stability and reduced sample needs, while artificial intelligence enables extraction of distributed calorimetric features beyond melting temperature and enthalpy. Machine learning strategies-including statistical, kernel-based, deep learning, and physics-informed frameworks-help identify informative thermodynamic patterns. This review integrates thermodynamic principles, data-driven analytics, and clinical studies to assess DSC's capabilities and limitations. We further propose practical standardization and minimum-reporting frameworks for DSC acquisition, preprocessing, AI model development, and validation to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability. Persistent issues such as inter-laboratory variability, cohort heterogeneity, small datasets, and regulatory hurdles continue to restrict routine use. Overall, combining DSC with AI offers a promising analytical framework for extracting clinically meaningful thermodynamic insights and advancing disease characterization.

title: Biological augmentation of electronic health records through estimation of patient proteomes.
text: High-dimensional proteomic profiling can improve clinical risk prediction and provide insight into disease biology, but routine acquisition of omic data at population scale remains impractical. We developed Real-world AI-based Biomarker Inference Technology (RABIT), a machine learning framework that biologically augments electronic health records (EHRs) by projecting longitudinal clinical histories into a high-dimensional proteomic representation space learned from paired EHR and plasma proteomics. RABIT was trained using patients with paired EHRs and measured plasma proteomics and externally validated in an independent cohort with paired data. RABIT profiles showed broad concordance with measured protein expression and more closely resembled measured proteomics than their input EHR. Incorporating these biologically augmented representations improved 5-year disease onset prediction across 14 conditions (n = 449,223; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 33.7%) and generalized to an external cohort (n = 1,038,419; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 70.3%). RABIT profiles reproduced clinically meaningful organ-specific biological changes in response to aging and further outperformed models built from comprehensive established clinical predictors in prediction of chronic kidney disease progression, major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Last, RABIT enabled biological signatures derived from small discovery cohorts to be extended to population-scale clinical datasets, generating clinically relevant hypotheses linking cytomegalovirus-associated immune states to variation in brain tumor outcomes. Together, these results demonstrate that biological augmentation of EHRs can enable molecularly informed clinical prediction and hypothesis generation at population scale.

title: Large Language Model Performance in Structured Data Extraction From Neurosurgical Electronic Health Records: Comparative Benchmark Study.
text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to extract information from electronic health records (EHRs). Given the rapid pace of LLM development, robust scenario-specific benchmarks are essential to evaluate clinical usefulness and support safe deployment. This study aimed to compare contemporary LLMs for structured data extraction from real neurosurgical EHRs written in Czech. In a prospective single-center cohort, 172 hospitalized patients provided informed consent for the use of anonymized EHRs. For each patient, predefined records were collected and concatenated. Ground truth for 35 data points was established by dual extraction with consensus. A standardized prompt requesting JSON output was submitted to 19 LLMs. The primary outcome was overall accuracy; secondary outcomes were category-level accuracy and the proportion of complete machine-readable outputs. A total of 6264 documents were collected (median 33, IQR 25-41 per patient). Ground truth was established with 92.6% initial interrater agreement before consensus. Several models produced complete JSON outputs for 100% of cases (Claude 4.1 Opus, Grok 4, and Gemini 2.5 Flash); GPT-4.1 (DeepSearch) and GPT-5 completed 99.4%. The highest accuracy was achieved by GPT-4.1 (87.6%), followed by GPT-4.5 (85.6%), Claude 4.1 (84.8%), and Grok 4 (84.2%). Accuracy declined by data type: binary (up to 95%), numeric (~89%), multiple-choice (~75%), and short text (~78%). Current LLMs can reliably extract structured clinical information from full, non-English EHRs, while older or smaller models show major limitations. A hybrid workflow-automated extraction with targeted validation-appears practical for research use.

title: Evaluating Human and AI-Based Triage Performance in the Emergency Department: Real-World Cohort Study.
text: Emergency departments (EDs) depend on rapid, reliable triage for patient safety and flow. The Manchester Triage System (MTS) is widely implemented but exhibits known interrater variability. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as potential decision-support tools for triage and early assessment, yet real-world comparative evaluations remain scarce. This study aimed to compare clinician and LLM performance on ED triage accuracy, specialty assignment, diagnostic recommendations, and admission prediction in a real-world cohort. In a retrospective cohort study, 305 walk-in ED encounters at a German tertiary-care hospital were analyzed. A nurse performed real-time MTS-assessment and initial specialty assignment at presentation. Each anonymized case was independently evaluated by 4 physicians and 12 LLMs from 4 providers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Mistral). Triage agreement was assessed against 2 reference standards: a consensus human label (ground-truth 1 [GT1]) and real-time nurse-assigned MTS-triage (ground-truth 2 [GT2]). For human raters, a leave-one-out variant of GT1 (LOO-GT1) assessed incorporation bias. The primary statistic was quadratic-weighted Cohen κ (unweighted κ reported alongside). Secondary outcomes were directional triage errors (over- or undertriage, |Δ|≤1), specialty top-1 accuracy, per-case precision, recall, F1-score of recommended diagnostics, and admission prediction (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value [PPV], and negative predictive value [NPV]). Median age was 45 (IQR 31-62) years; 188 (61.6%) patients were male; admission rate was 20.1% (56/278). Against GT1, human-rater (physicians and nurse) accuracy ranged 0.59-0.83 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.60-0.88; unweighted κ 0.35-0.74), and LLM accuracy 0.35-0.70 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.46-0.72; unweighted κ 0.11-0.53). Under LOO-GT1, human-rater weighted κ fell to 0.48-0.81. Only 1 clinician (Doctor 1, weighted κ 0.81) retained agreement clearly above any LLM, while 3 LLMs (Gemini-3.5-flash=0.72, GPT-5.5=0.69, and GPT-5=0.66) exceeded the LOO-corrected agreement of the remaining 4 human raters. One-off agreement exceeded 86% for all raters and models. Vs GT1, overtriage ranged 6%-56% and undertriage 6%-36%. Vs GT2, corresponding ranges were 11%-62% and 5%-30%. Against the study specialty reference, physician specialty-assignment accuracy ranged 0.88-0.93 and LLM accuracy 0.62-0.80. Against the operational triage-pathway specialty assignment, the corresponding ranges were 0.81-0.82 and 0.57-0.75. Model diagnostic recommendation F1-scores ranged 0.55-0.69. Admission prediction demonstrated high sensitivity (0.73-0.95) and NPV (0.90-0.96), but modest PPV (0.25-0.41). In a real-world ED cohort, 1 clinician (Doctor 1, a specialist physician) had the highest urgency agreement point estimate under both GT1 and LOO-GT1. Under LOO-GT1, 3 contemporary LLMs reached agreement that exceeded that of the other 4 clinicians. For specialty assignment, all clinicians remained clearly ahead of the best LLM. LLMs showed strong sensitivity and high NPV for admission prediction, but modest PPV precludes autonomous use. Because both reference standards are empirical rather than outcome-anchored gold standards, findings represent agreement against expert consensus and routine practice rather than an absolute correctness benchmark, and support a complementary, human-in-the-loop role for LLM-based decision-support in ED triage and early assessment.

title: Prediction Models for Frailty in People Living with HIV: Systematic Review.
text: Frailty is increasingly prevalent among people living with HIV, who experience earlier onset and a higher burden of frailty than the general population. Prediction models that identify people living with HIV at risk of future frailty could enable timely, targeted intervention. However, the evidence on prediction models developed specifically for frailty in people living with HIV has not yet been systematically evaluated. This review aims to systematically identify and critically appraise multivariable prediction models for the future occurrence of frailty in people living with HIV and to assess and summarize their methodological quality and predictive performance. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, ProQuest, and Chinese databases (SinoMed, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP) from inception to July 24, 2026. Studies that developed or validated any multivariable statistical or machine-learning prediction model for frailty in people living with HIV were eligible. Title and abstract screening, full-text evaluation, data extraction (Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies [CHARMS]), and risk-of-bias and applicability assessment (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool [PROBAST]) were conducted independently in duplicate. The search identified 2523 records (initial search: 2205; updated search: 318); 137 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and only 1 study met all inclusion criteria. Frail RISC-HIV (Frailty Risk in the Short-Term for Care of People with HIV) was developed in the Centers for AIDS Research Network of Integrated Clinical Systems (CNICS) cohort (n=4680; training n=3170; validation n=1510) using Bayesian model averaging and LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) regression combined with Cox proportional-hazards models to predict incident frailty within 2 years. The model comprised 8 predictors (baseline frailty score, depressive symptomatology [Patient Health Questionnaire-7], prescribed antidepressants, current illicit opioid use, current marijuana use, current antiretroviral therapy, age, and sex) and achieved acceptable discrimination in the validation set (Harrell C=0.76, 95% CI 0.73-0.79), with a sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 61% at a 5% risk threshold; calibration under-predicted the observed risk (predicted 7.9% vs observed 14.7% in the validation set). PROBAST assessment rated the study at high overall risk of bias, driven primarily by the analysis domain. To our knowledge, no external validation of the model was identified, and TRIPOD (Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis) reporting was incomplete. Quantitative synthesis was not feasible. The evidence base for frailty prediction in people living with HIV currently comprises a single, internally validated model that has not yet been externally validated. This critical evidence gap underscores an urgent need for further model development and rigorous external validation in diverse settings, with standardized frailty definitions and reporting in accordance with TRIPOD.

title: Developing and Externally Validating Machine Learning Models to Forecast Short-Term Risk of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.
text: To develop and externally validate supervised machine learning models using routinely collected ICU electronic health record (EHR) data to predict short-term onset of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) before clinical diagnosis. Prospective observational cohort study with temporal model development and external validation. ICUs. Mechanically ventilated adults in a prospective observational cohort (Successful Clinical Response In Pneumonia Therapy [SCRIPT]) who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) for suspected pneumonia and had BAL-confirmed adjudicated VAP or adjudicated non-VAP status (n = 507). External validation in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV) included mechanically ventilated patients with greater than or equal to 48 hours of continuous invasive ventilation (n = 2681). Additional evaluation was performed in participants from the Inhaled Amikacin vs. Placebo to Prevent Ventilator Associated Pneumonia (AMIKINHAL) randomized trial evaluating inhaled amikacin for VAP prevention, using centrally adjudicated VAP outcomes. None. We extracted 36 day-level clinical features (vital signs, ventilator settings, laboratory values, inflammatory markers, and support devices) from the EHR and trained models to predict VAP within 3, 5, or 7 days before BAL-confirmed diagnosis. Unsupervised clustering identified physiologic states enriched for VAP-labeled days. In internal testing, the best performance reached an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.866 for predicting VAP within 7 days and 0.843 for predicting VAP within 5 days. Predicted risk increased over the days preceding VAP among patients who developed VAP, while remaining low among non-VAP patients. On external validation in MIMIC-IV, the best model achieved an AUROC of 0.817 for predicting VAP within 5 days. Performance was poor in AMIKINHAL, where only nine of 36 features were available. Across models, influential predictors included ventilator duration and mechanics (e.g., positive end-expiratory pressure), platelet count, and inflammatory markers. Machine learning models trained on day-level structured ICU data with BAL-confirmed adjudicated labels predicted VAP up to 7 days before clinical diagnosis with strong discrimination and generalized to an external health system when key features were available, supporting future prospective real-time evaluation.

title: When the Judge Is an LLM: An Oncologist and a Language Model Evaluator Disagree on Responses to Inpatient Oncology Consultations-A Retrospective Blinded Study.
text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly tested as aids for oncology consultation and, increasingly, as graders of such outputs ("LLM-as-a-judge"). We assessed whether an LLM judge and an oncologist reach comparable conclusions on real oncology documentation. For 108 consecutive inpatient oncology consultations at a tertiary centre, the oncologist's original note and responses generated by Gemini and ChatGPT were scored by a medical oncologist and an LLM judge (Claude Opus 5), both blinded to source labels, using a nine-domain rubric (0-45). The oncologist separated the three sources by ≤1.6 points (Kendall's W = 0.082), whereas the LLM judge scored the two models 9.8 and 13.4 points above the oncologists' notes (W = 0.772). Agreement was poor overall (ICC(2,1) = 0.167) and within each source (0.003-0.235). Between-evaluator differences were 10.5 points for oncologist notes versus 1.1 and -1.2 points for model responses (distribution-free interaction p < 0.001). LLM-judge scores, but not oncologist scores, increased with response length, including among oncologists' notes (ρ = 0.56). Safety flags were assigned at different rates and overlapped no more than expected by chance. In oncology consultation research, evaluator choice can determine study conclusions; no single evaluator, human or LLM, should serve as sole assessor without calibration against independent expert judgement.

title: Beyond Mutations: A Seven-CpG DNA Methylation Signature for Predicting HRD in MMRd Colorectal Cancer.
text: We previously identified a high level of molecular heterogeneity within mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) colorectal cancer (CRC). Despite MMRd CRC being typically considered suitable for immunotherapy, only less than half of the metastatic CRC (mCRC) patients achieve complete remission. Thus, the search for identifying new therapeutic targets has become extremely urgent. The use of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) has revolutionized the treatment of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) cancer; however, the HRD prevalence in CRC remains unclear. Here, we conducted an integrated analysis of genomic and methylation profiles from a cohort of Chinese MMRd CRC tumors. We successfully developed a novel DNA methylation signature that can effectively stratify MMRd tumors based on their HRD status. The findings suggest that within the MMRd CRC subgroup, more than half of tumors exhibit a concomitant HRD phenotype characterized by hypermethylation. The newly developed methylation-based classifier showed high performance in predicting HRD, offering a promising molecular tool for refining patient stratification. This study highlights the epigenetic heterogeneity of MMRd CRC and proposes a novel, methylation-based signature for identifying tumors with HRD, which may have implications for therapeutic strategies targeting DNA repair vulnerabilities.

title: Construction of a clinical prediction model for the risk of iatrogenic vertical root fracture using multiple clinical indicators.
text: Vertical root fracture (VRF) complicates endodontically treated teeth, often leading to extraction. We developed a diagnostic prediction model for VRF using a retrospective cohort of 80 patients. Three machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, random forest, and LASSO) were used to identify key predictors. As all predictors were ascertained at the evaluation visit, the resulting model is diagnostic rather than prognostic, estimating the probability that a tooth presenting for re-evaluation already harbors a VRF. We evaluated the model via bootstrap internal validation and three-tiered external validation in an independent cohort (n = 130). Intracanal medication, time interval, and the absence of post emerged as consensus predictors. The model demonstrated strong internal discrimination (optimism-corrected AUC = 0.795, 95% confidence interval: 0.703-0.890) and excellent calibration, yielding a risk score ranging from 0 to 5. In the external cohort, locked-model validation achieved an AUC of 0.621, model refit 0.711, and transportability assessment using conceptual proxies 0.756. This model supports risk communication and shared decision-making during re-evaluation for suspected VRF.

title: Therapy Performance Predicts Functional Recovery After Stroke.
text: Early prediction of post-stroke recovery is important for guiding personalized rehabilitation and optimizing care planning. However, existing prediction approaches often overlook therapy intensity and patient engagement during post-stroke rehabilitation. Deriving therapy performance metrics (TPMs) from clinical notes and evaluate their utility in predicting functional discharge outcomes on the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), and Berg Balance Scale (BBS). Electronic medical records from 42 individuals undergoing inpatient stroke rehabilitation were mined to extract TPMs describing therapy exposure, walking distance, treadmill use, and stair practice. TPMs were evaluated across inpatient time-points to compare distributions between participants who met or did not meet established clinical thresholds for each functional outcome and to assess associations with discharge scores. TPMs were integrated into machine learning (ML) models along with patient demographics and sensor-derived gait features collected at IRF admission. TPMs differentiate patients with clinically meaningful improvements as early as 5-7 days post-admission and were strongly associated with discharge outcomes (R2 = .64-.78, P < .001). Incorporating TPMs into ML models improved 6MWT performance (R2 increased from .30 to .63, reduced prediction error by ~25 m) relative to baseline models without TPMs. Importantly, ML models using TPMs enabled early outcome prediction for non-ambulatory patients, a group often excluded from gait-based predictive approaches. TPMs provide early markers of recovery and enhance the prediction of discharge outcomes, particularly for patients who are non-ambulatory at admission. Leveraging structured information from routine therapy documentation may enable dynamic, near real-time recovery prediction to support data-driven rehabilitation and care planning after stroke. Therapy Performance Predicts Post-Stroke RecoveryRecovering the ability to walk and keep balance is an important goal for many people during post-stroke rehabilitation. Clinicians use standardized tests to measure recovery, but these tests provide only snapshots of a patient's recovery. Information recorded during physical therapy may provide a more continuous picture of how a patient is recovering. In this study, we explored if information written in physical therapy notes could help monitor recovery and predict discharge abilities from inpatient rehabilitation. We developed therapy performance metrics (TPMs) to describe aspects of therapy such as walking distance, treadmill activity, stair practice, and therapy exposure. We examined how these measures related to walking speed, walking endurance, and balance at discharge. We also evaluated TPMs at different times during rehabilitation to determine how early they could provide useful information about recovery. We then used TPMs into machine learning models to predict discharge walking and balance abilities. TPM were added to admission data and allowed predictions to be updated as rehabilitation progressed. Models incorporating TPMs also showed less bias across patients with different recovery trajectories. The results suggest that TPMs may provide a valuable way to track recovery throughout inpatient stroke rehabilitation. In the future, the automatic extraction of these measures from clinical notes could help clinicians update predictions, discuss progress with patients, set individualized goals, and adapt rehabilitation plans as recovery unfolds.

title: ETS1 as a Candidate Biomarker for Sepsis‑Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Multi‑Omics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
text: This multi‑omics study aimed to screen candidate molecules associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis‑associated ARDS, and provide preliminary biological evidence for risk‑stratification research. Public transcriptomic datasets were used for differential‑gene analysis, WGCNA, lung‑tissue‑expression filtering and multi‑algorithm machine‑learning screening. We performed transcriptome sequencing on peripheral blood samples from our exploratory single‑center cohort including 22 sepsis patients and 10 healthy volunteers to verify gene dysregulation in sepsis vs healthy status. Associations between gene expression and established ARDS among sepsis patients were assessed using the public dataset GSE32707 only. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data, functional enrichment and literature mining were applied to explore potential molecular mechanisms. Twenty‑seven candidate genes related to septic lung injury were obtained. ETS1 emerged as a hub gene with high model contribution across machine‑learning and SHAP interpretability analyses. In our clinical cohort, ETS1 was significantly down‑regulated in sepsis patients compared with healthy controls. Analysis of the public GSE32707 dataset further suggested that ETS1 exhibited stepwise reduction from healthy controls, through uncomplicated sepsis, to sepsis complicated with ARDS. Single‑cell analysis demonstrated that ETS1 was predominantly expressed in NK cells, T cells and B‑cells, implying potential roles in immune‑homeostasis regulation. Our machine‑learning models achieved high classification performance for discriminating sepsis from healthy volunteers. However, this classification task cannot directly predict incident ARDS among sepsis patients. In this hypothesis‑generating observational multi‑omics study, reduced ETS1 expression was correlated with sepsis and further decreased in patients with established sepsis‑associated ARDS in one public dataset. ETS1 represents a candidate correlative biomarker for sepsis risk stratification. Further large multi‑center cohorts, cell‑composition correction and functional wet‑lab experiments are required to validate whether ETS1 can support ARDS early‑warning or serve as a therapeutic target for septic lung injury.

title: Dairy-derived bioactive peptides in the regulation of obesity and type 2 diabetes: engineered production strategies, mechanisms and translational challenges.
text: Obesity and type 2 diabetes are interrelated metabolic disorders and pose growing socioeconomic and clinical burdens. Although current pharmacotherapies, such as metformin and orlistat, are widely used, their long-term effectiveness may be constrained by side effects, poor compliance, and incomplete glycemic control in some patients. Hence, interest in food-derived peptides as sustainable dietary interventions for metabolic health has increased. Casein and whey proteins can generate peptides with potential anti-obesity and anti-diabetic activities by modulating digestive enzymes, incretin signaling, insulin sensitivity, and inflammation. However, evidence is predominantly from in vitro and animal studies, with limited human validation. Their clinical translation is further limited by bitterness, gastrointestinal instability, low bioavailability, and batch-to-batch variability. This review summarizes recent advances in peptide production, including fermentation, enzymatic hydrolysis, and synergistic production, and highlights mechanistic and translational challenges. The integration of AI and machine learning with advanced fermentation and enzymatic hydrolysis has, been reported to increase peptide yield and diversity. Engineering solutions, such as peptide self-assembly, nanoliposomes, nanofibers, and double-emulsion microencapsulation, may enhance peptide stability and delivery. Future research should prioritize AI-driven peptide discovery and improved delivery systems to enhance gastrointestinal stability and bioavailability, alongside rigorous standardized clinical trials to facilitate clinical translation of dairy-derived peptides.

title: Antibiotic prescribing and resistance beyond hospital surveillance networks in India
text: Hospital-based networks provide much of Indias antimicrobial resistance surveillance evidence, but community-facing data on both prescribing and resistance remain limited. We analysed 2.78 million prescription-validated antibiotic records and 155,764 microbiology samples from Tata 1mg, a digital healthcare platform, during 2023-2025. We assessed prescribing composition and resistance trends, and explored ecological prescribing-resistance associations using merged monthly series. Access antibiotics accounted for 28.7% of records, compared with 47.0% for Watch and 11.9% for Not Recommended antibiotics. Across 25 eligible states and union territories, Access shares ranged from 16.1% to 38.0%. Urine comprised 93.9% of samples. Among urinary Escherichia coli isolates, resistance was 4.9% to nitrofurantoin and amikacin, compared with 53.6% to ceftriaxone and 57.0% to ciprofloxacin. Exploratory prescribing-resistance associations varied by organism and antibiotic. These findings identify stewardship priorities within a digitally mediated care pathway and illustrate the complementary value of routinely collected pharmacy and laboratory data for surveillance beyond hospital-centred networks.

title: Bivariate Multiscale Sample Entropy of Frontoparietal-Subgenual ACC Dynamics in Depression During Accelerated TMS at 7 T
text: ObjectiveTo examine whether longitudinal changes in frontoparietal (FP)-subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) joint temporal complexity differ between sgACC hemispheres in patients undergoing accelerated TMS (aTMS) and untreated healthy controls. MethodsTwenty-four patients with current depressive episodes and fifteen healthy controls underwent 7T resting-state fMRI at baseline and follow-up. Patients received aTMS localized to the left DLPFC using Beam-F3. The same bilateral FP time series was paired separately with left and right sgACC time series. Bivariate multiscale sample entropy (bMSE) across scale factors a1-a10 was summarized by trapezoidal integration as a complexity index (bMSE-CI). The primary test was the Group x Time x sgACC Hemisphere interaction in a mixed repeated- measures ANOVA. Scale-specific interactions and clinical Spearman correlations were evaluated with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction. Change scores were follow-up minus baseline. ResultsThe bMSE-CI Group x Time x Hemisphere interaction was significant (F(1,37) = 6.043, p = 0.0188, partial 2 = 0.140). Mean left/right bMSE-CI changes were -0.286/+0.124 in patients and +0.323/+0.112 in controls. Of ten scale-specific three-way interactions, only a2 survived FDR correction (q = 0.0435). No baseline or change-score bMSE-MADRS association survived the specified FDR corrections. A random-intercept-only mixed-model sensitivity analysis did not reach statistical significance for the three-way interaction (p = 0.0718). ConclusionFP-sgACC joint temporal complexity showed hemisphere-dependent longitudinal differences between patients undergoing aTMS and healthy controls. These exploratory findings motivate further evaluation of bMSE as a candidate measure of longitudinal neural change in depression. Independent replication, more precise reliability estimates, and prospective validation of clinical relevance are needed.

title: An fMRI Phenotype of Reward in Effort Expenditure in the VTA and Dorsal Raphe: A Longitudinal Study of Depression under Escitalopram Treatment
text: Anhedonia and motivational impairment are central features of major depressive disorder, yet the neural processes linking reward information processing to sustained goal-directed behaviour remain insufficiently understood. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we examined representations of reward levels during sustained effort expenditure (a construct in the RDoC framework) as a distinct component of reward processing in depressive patients under escitalopram treatment. Twenty-eight unmedicated patients with a current depressive episode and forty-three healthy control participants underwent fMRI scanning at two time points three weeks apart; patients started escitalopram immediately after the first measurement. Across participants, sustained effort expenditure engaged midbrain reward circuitry (ventral tegmental area, VTA), even in the absence of immediate reinforcement. Here, we observed a reward level x session x patient group interaction, driven by larger activity in patients after treatment. A targeted analysis also revealed changes in activity of the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) in patients. By isolating neural mechanisms supporting sustained goal-directed behaviour, the study identifies novel and clinically relevant imaging phenotypes of reward processing and their change after three weeks of treatment, representing a potential pathway of escitalopram treatment in depression.

title: Association of mRNA COVID-19 vaccination with overall survival in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: a retrospective cohort analysis.
text: BackgroundA retrospective study in Nature recently reported improved overall survival (OS) when COVID-19 mRNA vaccination was administered around initiation of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Whether this association depends on vaccination timing relative to ICI treatment remains unclear. MethodsWe conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of patients receiving palliative-intent ICI therapy at a UK tertiary cancer centre between October 2014 and December 2025. Two vaccination exposure definitions were evaluated: (1) vaccination from 100 days before to 100 days after the first ICI cycle (initial window); and (2) vaccination from 100 days before the first ICI cycle to 100 days after the final ICI cycle (extended window). Multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, treatment line and year of ICI initiation, with the baseline hazard stratified by tumour group. Landmark, time-varying, pre-ICI, active vaccinated comparator and calendar-restricted analyses were performed. ResultsAmong 2,054 patients, 493 (24.0%) received [≥]1 COVID-19 vaccination. In the initial fixed-window analysis, mRNA vaccination was not significantly associated with OS (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.60-1.06; p=0.123). No significant association was observed in day-100 landmark, initial time-varying or pre-ICI analyses. The active vaccinated comparator analysis was also non-significant. In the extended fixed-window analysis, longer OS was associated with mRNA (HR 0.59; 95% CI 0.46-0.76; p<0.001) and adenoviral-vector vaccination (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.51-0.83; p<0.001). The mRNA association was attenuated in calendar-restricted analyses and was non-significant in the supportive time-varying analysis (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.66-1.04; p=0.099). ConclusionsSurvival associations with COVID-19 mRNA vaccination varied according to exposure definition and analytic handling of vaccination timing. The strong association observed in the extended fixed-window analysis was attenuated in calendar-restricted and supportive time-varying analyses. Prospective studies are required to determine whether COVID-19 mRNA vaccination at specific time points during ICI therapy influences clinical outcomes. HighlightsO_LIInitial fixed-window mRNA vaccination was not significantly associated with overall survival. C_LIO_LIExtended fixed-window analyses showed survival associations that were attenuated in time-varying analyses. C_LIO_LILandmark, pre-ICI and active vaccinated comparator analyses were non-significant. C_LIO_LIProspective studies are required to assess causality and tumour-specific effects. C_LI

title: Impact of wildfire-related fine particulate matter on tuberculosis notifications in Brazil: a nationwide panel study, 2003-2023
